I've been looking forward to yet another good Numi tea flavor. This is a blend of chocolate with vanilla flavors.  I personally drink the Dry Desert Lime and the Jasmine.  I am the only person in my family who likes the Dry Desert Lime though.  One time was enough for everyone else.  So a more user friendly flavor, like this one, is much appreciated.As far as the chocolate flavor, no one is going to say, "Oh, chocolate," when they taste it.  It is a lot subtler than that.  The same is true of the vanilla.  These are undertones to the full bodied tea taste instead.It tastes great, either hot or cold.  I even drink it at room temperature.I've tried it out on my mother-in-law.  She generally does NOT like the Numi teas, finding them too weird.  However, this is the first Numi tea I've tried on her where she drank the whole thing and said she liked it.There is another great painting on the box as the female half owner of Numi uses the teas to paint. Her paintings are reproduced on the boxes which is a very nice touch.

column9: Pleasant, but you only get one cup of tea per bag
column10: Chocolate Puerh is a good cup of tea.  It is certainly different, with the chocolate in it, but not what I would characterize as a truly excellent tea. Since good-quality puerh black tea has a rich complexity of earthly flavors, it makes me wonder why Numi decided to dress it up with chocolate and spices.  I discovered puerh tea at a wonderful tea shop in Xi'an, China, and this just is not the same thing...maybe I was just expecting something different.Pros:1. I wouldn't call this a sit-and-savor-it kind of tea, but it's pleasant.  It reminds me of a mild chai tea.2. It doesn't seem to get bitter as it cools down.3. It's organic, and comes from sustainably harvested wild tea trees.4.  The chocolate and spices are nicely balanced, and there is no need to add milk or sugar.Cons:1. The directions don't state the yield of the tea bag, or even how much water to use.2. The directions state to pour boiling water over the tea bag.  I was taught that water for good quality tea should be very hot, but not boiling.  So why are they telling me to put boiling water on it?3. The directions also do not say anything about re-steeping.  I found that the teabag only was useful for one 8 oz. cup of tea, which I steeped for four minutes (directions say to steep it from 3 - 5 minutes).  I tried re-steeping it, and the resulting brew was very bland.4.  Top quality puerh tea generally is more robust than this tea.  At one cup per bag, it seems a bit pricey for what you get.Overall conclusions:  It's very pleasant, but not earth-shaking.

I'm usually a strictly black tea drinker - I don't need anything too fancy in the morning. After trying Numi's Chocolate Puerh, it's going to be hard to go back to basics. It has a great chocolate flavor which blends perfectly with the flavor of the tea. It is rich, but not overpowering - drinks great with or without milk. Great way to start the morning, or equally good as a nightcap before bed. Definitely worth trying.

I am a huge chocolate fan. And, though coffee is my morning beverage of choice, I also drink a fair amount of tea. This tea feels a bit richer than average tea, but I wouldn't say it tastes very chocolatey. The over-riding flavor is black tea. Adding a splash of milk and a bit of honey enhances the subtle hint of chocolate.

Pros:- Has chocolate in it- Organic- Very differentCons:- You really cant taste any chocolate- Taste is earthy as described...which tastes earthy with spice- "Nourish & Energize" are the last adjectives I would use when describing how I feel after drinking the tea.I drink about 2-3 cups of tea a day, and sadly this is one tea I do not look forward to drinking.  I have let other people tried it, and they all too agreed that "energize" was one of the last words they would use to describe the tea.However, due to the tea being very different, it does add something "different" for my collection.  You could call it almost a love hate relationship.To sum up this tea: It tries to be something it isn't. (relating to every word used to describe the tea on its box)
A surprisingly lightly flavored tea with a great chocolate aftertaste.  Adding a little milk and honey to the hot tea did enhance the flavor.

This tea is really different. I taste chocolate if I think about it, don't notice the orange, cinnamon or vanilla at all and find the nutmeg to be the strongest flavor. Take the word "strongest" with a grain of salt....I found this tea to be very watery with little body. Perhaps I added too much water - I used about 8 ounces. I even just left the bag in the mug, hoping that if it steeped longer the flavors would intensify. No luck. Even my favorite tea, Stash White Christmas, which is made with white tea, has more body than this. I can make that in my 12 ounce mug and still have a good cup of tea. I don't see myself ever reordering this tea; it's just too strange a flavor and too weak for my taste. 2 stars.After further review I've found that just 2 drops of stevia made a difference in the flavor; made it more palatable. I also gave the teabag a good squeeze and that helped slightly. I raise my rating to 2.5 stars, rounded to 3.

Don't know how helpful this review will be, since I'm giving two points of view -- my own, and that of a family member. One person in the family enjoyed the tea. He thought it was good with some coconut creamer and a bit of sucanat sugar, and found it nicely chocolatey.I on the other hand, found it pretty bland, and hardly tasted the chocolate. Like another reviewer commented, I was underwhelmed.The other person in my family and I both agree on one thing, however, if you're expecting something like "a cup of hot cocoa", you will be disappointed.

I like the tea, but it's not only chocolate and puerh, it does have roobios red tea in it and i think nutmeg and cinnamon, so it tastes kinda like a chai mix with puerh mix with red mix with slight cocoa flavor...it's ok..but by far not that great and not the my favorite.

column9: I enjoy this - no cream or sugar required!
column10: I'll apologize up front that I'm no good at describing subtle tastes and aromas...but I'm drinking a cup as I type this to help me out.  :)I normally put some type of sweetener into tea, but I think that this is good just by itself - that's not unprecented, but it's pretty rare for me.  It has sufficient taste to it to keep me interested without sweetener, and it's not bitter (at least when steeped for 2.5 minutes).This has a hint of spice, IMO.  It's quite enjoyable.  Regarding the "chocolate" in the name, I honestly can't taste any at all...zero, zip.  The directions say to stir the cup as the chocolate might settle, but I still don't taste any.  Perhaps that's one of those subtle tastes that I'm not picking up on, but on the chance that you're like me, don't expect any chocolate flavor.Lack of chocolate aside, I like this a lot.  Overall, I enjoy this tea and recommend it.

This tea is healthy and extremely tasty.  It is so satisfying sometimes I just have a couple of cups of hot chocolate puerh for breakfast and I don't need any food.  This is good mixed with magnolia puerh.  One tea bag of each to a tea/coffee mug and you can fill it up to three times and it will retain the robust flavor.

I'm a bit sensitive to the acids in black tea, but I'm trying to watch my sugar intake, so I don't want to sweeten it. This means that I find many black teas to be too harsh. Numi's Chocolate Puerh, however, is ideal for me. The very mild notes of vanilla, chocolate, and spices don't in any way overwhelm the black tea. Instead, they mellow and complement it. The result is a perfect cup of tea that makes it worth spending the extra for Numi. Even though, yes, the price tag does make me wince.

column9: Delicious, a bit subtle, but wonderful for blending with other teas
column10: Chocolate and tea are not the most obvious combination, and yet this tea provides a soothing, harmonious experience that seems like the most natural thing in the world. The chocolate flavor isn't terribly strong, but the subtlety of it is part of the charm and what makes it work so well as a mid-afternoon or evening indulgence. Drink a cup of this tea slowly instead of snacking on a chocolate bar, and you may find that you're more relaxed, happier, and relieved at having saved calories for some other indulgence.And here's a hint: try combining this tea with another flavor. I sometimes brew a small pot of tea using a bag of this and a bag of The Republic of Tea's Strawberry Chocolate tea to really emphasize the chocolate flavor and add that delicious strawberry essence into the mix. The possibilities are pretty much endless, and this product makes a great base for a lot of happy experiments.
I love all sorts of tea but was unfamiliar with Puerh teas.I would not call this my "favorite" but it is definitely good.  A nice change of pace from my usual black and green teas.

column9: Pretty good tea, coming from a tea plebian.
column10: Yes, I am a tea plebian.  I do not have multi-million dollar tea brewing pharaphrenalia, nor do I import loose tea from the Huangshan Mountain in China.  I do occasionally enjoy a simple cup of tea, usually brewed out of a bag, in a cup with some boiling water.  Nice and simple.  That being said, this is pretty good tea.  A little weak for my tastes but definitely with a plesant chocolate/vanilla flavor.  I can't say that I notice a big difference when compared to standard comparable store-bought teas.  It does smell very nice and makes a good after-dinner treat.

column9: Good in concept, flawed in execution
column10: The description on the box sounded wonderful; hints of chocolate, vanilla, orange peel, cinnamon, and nutmeg, but I found the actual product to be rather flawed.  The tea leaves look far from the full leaves mentioned on the box, and there was also a fair amount of sedimentation from the bag.Moreover, the vanilla was extremely subtle, and I couldn't taste the chocolate or orange peel.  There was however a lot of cinnamon and nutmeg, which overpowered the other spices.  It tasted like a cinnamon tea, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but it is if you're marketing it a blend of spices.

column9: So far, everyone that I've had try it likes it...a lot!
column10: Being an avid tea drinker, I simply couldn't pass up this Numi tea.  Now, I'm no connoisseur of things chocolate, but, seeing as I've never tried a chocolate tea, I thought it'd have a more potent taste.This tea is black, but with just the right hint of sweetness, mostly a sort of velvety chocolate, if you will.  All I added was a spoonful of sugar per cup, and I immediately recommended this tea to co-workers and family--and they enjoyed it as well!A great tea for tea enthusiasts or not (as my family member doesn't really drink much tea).

I have to admit that I'm not much of a tea drinker.  Most of the time I stick to coffee, but I'm trying to kick the habit (at least a little bit!).  I've been looking for a tea that will give me the same satisfaction as a nice hot cup of black coffee.  Numi Organic Chocolate Puerh just might be the one.  Normally I wouldn't put chocolate and tea together, but the result is quite satisfying.  The chocolate taste isn't overpowering, but instead gives the tea a subtle and earthy flavor.  In fact, a hot cup of this tea satisfies my late night sweet tooth.  I can't wait to try it with a cookie.

This is a very interesting product. It definitely is not a typical tea. It has a lot of un-tea flavor (chocolate and subtle spicing). Very good when you want a bit of a chocolate fix. Might be especially good on a cold winter day with some milk to make it seem creamy likely hot chocolate. Big tea bags too! Lots of flavor here. Try it, you might like it!

This is a delicious tea with a nice blend of natural chocolate. The flavor of tea predominates, with the addition of a touch of chocolate and a hint of vanilla; it sounds like a weird combination, but works out rather well. The chocolate adds just a tad of weight to the flavor without making it taste at all thick. The taste worked well for me both with and without sweetener; but I think if you normally use sugar or other sweetener in your tea, as I do, you'll probably still want to do so.The packaging, as noted in the product description, is recycled; and this is altogether a product that will appeal to consumers with a conscience, whether it be with regard to what they put into their bodies, how they impact the environment, or how they affect the farmers. Regarding the packaging, each teabag is enclosed in its own biodegradable packet and has a tiny slit to help the consumer open it easily. I think the box, which is rather close in size to roughly similar items on the grocery shelves (Celestial Seasonings, Bigelow teas, etc.), is a little large to contain only 16 tea bags.

Puerh tea is normally a traditional Chinese tea that has been aged and fermented. The teas are commonly sold in shaped bricks of compacted leaves.  The Yunnan region in China is well known to be a source of this tea.  This tea can often be found in varying vintages and sold according to a particular tree.  A one hundred year old tree can produce a flavor complexity different than a 50 year old tree.  Believe it or not, there are tea connoisseurs that can recognize the flavor profile from a particular tree.Numi tea brings to the mainstream US consumer market the looseleaf bagged sampling of this tea known for generations in China.  The tea has a mellower, rounded taste due to its aging and fermentation.  They have also added hints of spice so that you have subtle hints of chocolate, cinnamon, nutmeg, etc.  It is not overwhelming in spice like many of the other "spiced" tea, but much more subtle.  It does not hit you over the head with spice notes like when you go into a department store during Christmas season.  But don't let the chocolate throw you off.  There is almost no discernible chocolate flavor, it is more of a scent.  If you enjoy black tea and want a bit more of a flavor and scent profile but find the mandarin spice or chai spice too overpowering, I strongly recommend this tea for you.

column9: Agree with other reviews - inconsistent quality
column10: It's hard to review this tea because each bag I've steeped has been like a whole different experience... one was smooth and flavorful, another weak, and still another bitter.  Nothing's changing in my process except the tea bags!  Perhaps I just got a bad batch, but I cannot in good conscience recommend this product.

I liked this tea a lot. It is indeed chocolate-y tasting, as long as it's sweetened. I liked the almost dessert-like flavor. If you don't like sweetened tea, be forewarned--I thought it tasted odd without.

I have to confess that I'm a real fan of Numi teas. I haven't tried one yet that I haven't really enjoyed, and the Chocolate Puerh is the latest on my list of must-have teas.As teas go, I think this is really somewhere between a tea and a chai. The ingredients are puerh tea, cocoa powder, vanilla, theo chocolate cocoa nibs, rooibos, orange peel, nutmeg, and cinnamon. All organic, of course!The first think I noticed when I opened the foil wrapper was the cocoa smell. Mmm. First scent was good. I steeped the tea for about 4 minutes (they suggest 3-5 minutes) and took a sip. The flavor is definitely tea, but there's the deep undercurrent of cocoa reminiscent of holiday baking and childhood treats. I think the rooibos and orange peel add a nice sweetness and slight citrus to the mix, and the cinnamon doesn't overpower the rest of the ingredients. Numi does a good job of balancing flavors.The tea bag wrapper says "velvety & vanilla," and the tea does have a somewhat heftier mouthfeel than a regular cup of tea, probably because of the cocoa. I could drink this every day, but I'll probably savor it a couple of times a week as an after-lunch treat. If you like tea and chocolate, this is definitely worth a try.

I shared this product with a person in my office who drinks tea daily.  (I'm a big coffee drinker, so I don't drink tea every day.)My initial impression was that while this tea smelled good once the bag was opened, the tea itself had almost no aroma once brewed and the tea didn't have much flavor either.  I thought that perhaps I had not brewed it long enough even though I had brewed it a full 5 minutes (the manufacturer recommends brewing 3-5 minutes), so I threw the bag back in my cup of tea.  Despite leaving the bag in the cup as I finished drinking the tea, the tea never got much flavor as far as I was concerned.  Then again I'm used to drinking really strong coffee, so I thought that perhaps my taste buds were simply used to a stronger flavor.Enter my co-worker.  I specifically did not tell her my impression of the tea because I wanted her unbiased opinion.  She was excited by the description of the tea on the box and brewed a cup for herself as she normally does every morning at the beginning of the work day.  She just stopped by my desk to give me her feedback.  Her main description of the tea was "bland."  She said it did not taste bad, but that it did not have much flavor.  In other words, her perception of this tea matched mine.  She further added that she would not buy this tea.  She didn't even want the rest of the box from me, so I'm simply going to put it out in our lunchroom in the hopes that perhaps some people where I work will enjoy it.  Who knows -- maybe this tea will impress at least one of my coworkers and they'll decide to purchase this tea.  I know I wouldn't.
Chocolate Puerh:  Complex and rich flavors, it's a solid tea and might be my personal favorite of their Puerh line.

I love this tea! It tastes good. :) It's a nice, smooth black tea with a touch of chocolate flavor. It doesn't need sugar.I am not a tea expert. I don't drink Lipton tea at all ever. I only drink Earl Grey black tea on a very cold, wet day when I'm exhausted from over work. That's why I'm glad to find this tea. Sometimes I need some caffeine but want a nice mellow flavor. Numi Organic Puerh with chocolate tea is perfect for me.

This tea is infused with cocoa to give it a light chocolate flavor. I am really enjoying the tea, but before I buy another box, I plan to try infusing cocoa with loose leaf tea myself to see if I can get a stronger chocolate flavor from it. It does have a nice, light taste to it. It's a great tea to drink mid morning.
I am an avid tea drinker and i must say this is AMAZING!!!!!!!!  Perfect blend of flavors!  I will probably be going through a box a week.
By far my favorite tea... and the shipping is incredibly fast.  The chocolate flavors are subtle and very pleasant, plus it is a healthy drink!Highly recommended.

I love the taste of this tea and the energy kick is a bonus for me.  It is a nice pick me up in the morning without the gittery sensation I often get with coffee.  Chocolate is not the main taste I get in this tea so if you want a powerful chocolate flavor this tea may not be for you.  It is more balanced of all of the flavors which is just what I wanted.  My husband who is a coffee guy loves this tea as well. So glad I took a chance and tried this tea.
What a wonderful earthy flavor! Chocolate taste is very subtle, soft, and compared with pu-erh, creates a combination of flavors that is a real treat!

This is the first tea that I've had where I did not feel the need to add any sweetener whatsoever...no honey, sugar, cream, nothing!  I noticed many reviewers were unimpressed by the lack of chocolate flavor, but Numi never claims that this is hot chocolate.  It has a subtle, yet definite chocolate essence, and tastes wonderful whether it is hot or cold.  My favorite thing to do is drink tea while it's piping hot, and then whatever I don't have time to drink, I refrigerate and drink later with my meal.  This tea is perfect for that, and makes a nice (and healthy) alternative to a cold soda.  Numi, you hit it out of the ballpark with this one, and I will continue to drink and serve this tea for years to come!

Maybe I got a bad bag (possible, considering the other reviews), but this tea is pretty underwhelming.  This is my first experience with a chocolate tea, so I don't know what to expect, but I found this had a faint smell of chocolate and a very watery, very faint sweet taste--what that specific taste is, I couldn't say.  Will be trying yerba mate next and am hoping for a better experience.

column9: Too good to get a 3 rating, but not good enough to earn a 4 rating...
column10: I had really high hopes for this tea. When it arrived in the mail I immediately opened up a pack and made some tea. It's not really what I expected. I thought it would have a slightly lighter and more chocolaty flavor. Don't get me wrong, its still a good drink. I think there's a little too much nutmeg that kind of throws it off. I would definitely urge people to give it a try because it is pretty good and has a distinct flavor

"Numi's vision is to inspire well-being of mind, body, and spirit through the simple art of tea."  That's an awful lot for a tea to take on, but you have to give them credit for setting such a goal!  I can't say I was spiritually transformed by this tasty chocolate tea, but I can say it was soothing and pretty yummy.  There is enough chocolate and vanilla bean taste to satisfy a small chocolate craving, but not enough to make this tea sweet - at all.  It's a good way to have a small treat with hints of chocolate to end the day so you can avoid caloric damage from real chocolate treats.  I am not such a tea aficionado that I can comment on the tea quality beyond the fact that it is clearly not Lipton and this company is into image and producing a quality product.I go with 4 stars because, while tasty, this flavor is really not my - wait for it - cup of tea (sorry).

Chocolate tea ? What a concept - two fabulous drinks in one cup.  Ah, but it might not be such a great idea as chocolate with coffee, because the "green" flavor of tea does not harmonize with the warm flavor of chocolate.  It's not bad, it's just not great.Other Numi products are better.

Let me start by saying I generally LOVE Numi teas and own a lot of them!  I've bought several of their "sampler" packs and enjoy the variety of flavors they offer.That being said, this is NOT one of my favorites!  In all fairness, I think maybe I just don't LIKE chocolate and tea together, because I also tried Trader Joe's brand of chocolate tea and thought it was nasty stuff.  I wouldn't say this is NASTY but it's certainly nothing I would actually purchase again.I like chai tea, and this sort of reminds me of it, but the chocolate notes in it just seem out of place to me - and I LOVE my chocolate!  Just not in tea, I guess.  I'll stick with their Earl Grey and Moonlight Spice, two of my all-time favorites in the Numi lineup!5-24-10 - I am updating my review!  My favorite restaurant serves Numi teas, and I decided to have some after dinner.  I asked the server which one she preferred, and she pulled the packet of Chocolate Puerh out of the box of assorted teas - she said, however, that it really needed cream and sugar to be GOOD!  So I took her advice, added a good splash of half & half and a packet of Splenda and you know - she was RIGHT!  It WAS good and just the right "dessert" after a big meal.I'm glad I didn't throw out or give away the box I had - I dug around in the cupboard and found it and have been enjoying it at home ever since.  I do use heavy cream at home, which gives it an ever richer mouth-feel.  I will probably buy another box when this one is done.

column9: If you like the taste of Chai you will love this.
column10: This is a very enjoyable tea. A nice smooth taste with a touch of chai to it. I did not find a chocolate taste to it. But it is still very good.

column9: Smooth, chocolatey tea, with a high price tag
column10: I am truly more of a coffee drinker, but I do enjoy tea sometimes. I have found that I really enjoy teas that have a chocolate flavor. They seem more rich and satisfying to me. One I had been enjoying is this one:Good Earth Cocoa Chai, Black Tea, Cocoa And Spice, 18 Count Tea Bags, 1.43-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)It is good, and you could somewhat compare it with the one I am reviewing today.This one, the Numi tea, is even better. Richer, smoother and more full-flavored. I had company last weekend and several of my guests tried some and everyone wanted to take an extra teabag home. That said, it is very expensive compared to other chocolate teas, like the Good Earth brand. About 3 times as much per bag, comparing with the Good Earth subscribe & save price!I would not purchase this for every day, but it is definitely gift-worthy if you have tea lovers on your gift list this Christmas and want to get them something special. Even the box is lovely and special looking. I will be ordering some more for gifts, as well as some to keep around specifically for company. (I may have to hide it to keep it from disappearing in between company visits!). I can't afford it for everyday use--I'll probably keep buying the Good Earth for that--but this one will still have a place on my shopping list.

column9: If you like the delicate flavor of tea, look elsewhere.
column10: Since I like tea and I love dark chocolate, I thought I would give this Chocolate Puerh tea a try.  I didn't know what to expect based on the description, but it was not at all what I would have liked it to be.Although I do regularly partake in some truly fine teas from Mighty Leaf, both loose and bagged, I don't consider myself an expert or a tea snob, but I do know what I like.  Properly filtered, clean water is important if you want to taste the tea and not whatever is in your water so I use water filtered by a PUR pitcher for making tea.  I also use a glass cup, so no undesireable flavor is introduced there.When I brewed my first cup, the first thing that came to mind is that it has a nice aroma, but it wasn't the aroma of tea... it was the aroma of weak cocoa.  I tried some without any type of sweetener and my impression was that the cocoa powder completely overwhelmed the flavor of the tea leaves.  It kind of tasted like a weak, bitter chocolate drink to me.  I've eaten raw cocoa nibs in the past and it reminded me of that... not at all pleasant since cocoa nibs are bitter.  I decided to add sugar to the tea to see if that would improve the flavor at least to the point where I would enjoy it and luckily it did.  My impression of the sweetened Chocolate Puerh was that it tasted just like a base for chai tea without the chai spices or the milk.  It's pleasant, but not at all like most of the flavored teas I've had in the past, the majority of which still retained some tea notes, whereas this tea does not.  Over the coming days, I brewed more of it and I came away with the same impression each time.  While I like it with sugar, I was not thrilled with it or blown away by it.  I'm not going to come home and crave a cup of this as opposed to say, a cup of Mighty Leaf Organic Earl Grey or Mighty Leaf Vanilla Bean, both of which are truly excellent flavored teas.Overall, this is not a tea I would order again.  Although it is okay, it just doesn't taste like tea as the cocoa completely masks the flavor of the underlying tea leaves and unlike a good chai tea, it does it in a way where the overall flavor isn't strong enough to satisfy or entice.  I feel like the brew is not quite like tea and its not quite cocoa and its not a chai.  Its stuck in the mediocre middle somewhere and what it does offer is just not desirable enough for me to want a more of it in the future.

I was skeptical about this product - chocolate tea? How would that work?  I was very pleasantly surprised by this sophisticated tea.  First you taste a nicely spiced black tea, then subtly you begin to experience the chocolate taste. I liked it because the chocolate did not overwhelm the spicy tea flavors, but complemented them in an unexpected way. This is a unique tea to enjoy especially during the cold months. And it goes great with cookies!

After ordering this tea, I thought, "What was I thinking?" but I'm glad that I did order it. Trying to describe this tea is kind of like trying to describe Coca-Cola to someone that has never had it. There are definitely flavors of cocoa and nutmeg, but this isn't like drinking watered down cocoa.  While the flavors in this tea are familiar in themselves, the combination is unique and definitely worth a try.  I'm sorry that I can't better describe this tea....the Coke analogy kept running through my head as I thought about what I would write.  I do recommend this tea as an experience of something new and different.

Numi tea tends to be good tea, as a general rule.  This tea is a nice addition to Numi's repertoire.  It's a hearty tea, the kind that coffee drinkers would also likely enjoy.  The addition of the chocolate is a nice touch as it stands up well to the bold flavor of the puerh.  The cinnamon and nutmeg lend a warming effect to the tea and the combination brought to mind sitting in front of a warm fire during the holiday season.  There is some orange peel in the blend as well, but I didn't find the flavor of it to be noticeable.I drank my first cup black and found it quite enjoyable.  It was mildly sweet, thanks to the chocolate, but not overwhelmingly so.  The cinnamon created a sort of tingly sensation.  The second time around, I added two teaspoons of turbinado sugar and a splash of milk and found it equally enjoyable, though I don't really think the sweetener is necessary.  Still, the milk gave it a more velvety feel and the sugar brought out more of the chocolate taste and toned the cinnamon down a bit as well.  This is definitely one of those teas that can justifiably called "dessert in a cup".

I had to look up Puerh (from Wiki: Puerh tea (pronounced POO-urr) or Bolay tea is a type of tea made from a "large leaf" variety of the tea plant Camellia sinensis and named after Pu'er county near Simao, Yunnan, China).  It has a good balance of flavors, a little bit sweet so I'm assuming not calorie free.  The company is very "green" using recycled and biodegradable papers in their packaging and tea bags.  Also supporting fair trade with the tea farmers.  All around a good product from an upright company.
A very enjoyable cup of tea.  The chocolate is not over powering with a nice scent, backed up by the orange peel, nutmeg and cinnamon ingredients.

column9: Tasty way to try Puerh tea
column10: I want to say off the bat that I'm not a fan of Puerh tea - the types I've tried so far have been very strong, with a heavy mushroom flavor, even when brewed lightly. "Earthy" is a word that's frequently used to describe Puerh.  Takes some getting used to, at the very least.  But Numi's chocolately version of Puerh is a big improvement - just as it's described on the box, it has a "velvety and vanilla" flavor - it's still a medium strong flavored tea, but the flavorings make it very palatable.It's best brewed with boiling water, for about 5 minutes, to get a deep chocolate flavor (and be prepared to stir occasionally while you drink it, so you can keep blending the chocolate, which can settle a bit at the bottom of the cup).I've also tried the loose version of this tea, and it is a bit stronger than the bagged version.I give this 4 stars mainly for reasons of personal taste, since I'm not 100% enthusiastic about Puerh in general, apart from this particular brand.  Also for those not in the know, Puerh can also have a bit of a "cleansing" effect (in terms of your digestive tract), so be aware this is probably not a tea you would want to drink in mass quantities on a daily basis. But as an occasional treat, or as a "dessert" tea, it's perfect.

So very different and definitely worth a try ... a pleasant experience awaits. Upon opening the first packet, I fell in love with this tea. I didn't even need to steep it to know it's a keeper. So glad I gave it a try.

I am smitten with this tea. First, the packaging is lovely. The design of the box, the fonts used...everything ids flawless and inviting.On to the actual TEA. I never expected a tea that had vanilla and chocolate as the main flavors to be this perfect, but it is. The chocolate is more of a hint, not like a thick uber-sweet chocolate taste. Just enough of a hint to set the tea apart from other more spicey flavors.I give this tea a HUGE thumbs up. Add it to you tea library and enjoy!

Wow! This is such a different type of tea experience. I like it plain but it is really yummy with some soy/almond milk and agave nector or other sweetener. It's Cacao flavor, not chocolate which gives it a different kind of taste. It doesn't taste too sweet at all, it's full bodied and satisfying. It feels so comforting to drink! The only improvements would be chai spice flavorings instead of the vanilla. Still, overall delish!

column9: Very mild, choc/vanilla almost chi tea (mild hot cocoa w/stevia & milk)
column10: First off, to understand my palate, I, growing up, until I became an adult, LIVED on candy. To lose weight, I still ate processed low-fat food. It wasn't until 10 years ago, I was told how evil processed food was & how it effects the body & finally re-developed a taste for natural foods/herbs. I stopped fast food, dairy, artificial anything, then even all foods that contain table sugar. I still have a killer sweet tooth like any kid & the only thing that helps me stay good is my IBS.On that note, I dislike tea & coffee, but like hot cocoa & loved Chai tea w/healthy dose of milk/sugar from years past, so gave this a shot.I seeped the tea for the full 5 min., even squeezing the bag w/my spoon during & using I think 7 oz. of water (which I think maybe too much & 5 oz. is probably best). Without adding anything, this tasted pleasant, but very mild & watery. I could taste the chocolate & vanilla faintly when I concentrated, but nothing sharp, no taste of strong spices either, which was a letdown as I love nutmeg & cinnamon.I added only MOST of a packet of Sweetleaf (non-artificial Stevia leaf) & it really helped bring out the chocolate & vanilla to give it a more robust, admitting also nicely sweetened taste. Even with my sweet tooth & dislike of tea, I would have been overall happy with this.I added 1 tablespoon of 2% milk (non-organic unfortunately, nor any soy milk in the house) to the stevia sweetened tea & it's got a nice full body taste. It tastes like a thinner, lightly sweetened hot cocoa & instead of slowly sipping, I gulped it down happily.I tried using only 1 tbsp of milk & no stevia, but if had to choose, stevia brought out the flavor more.I tried adding a slight tap of cinnamon & nutmeg to the tea, but even with the milk, it overpower the tea blend.

I usually like to drink tea (and coffee) straight-up, and while this had a good strong tea flavor, the chocolate and spices were barely there.  After reading other reviews, I tried steeping for only 4 minutes and adding a splash of milk, which improved the overall flavor, but again it tasted like tea with a sweet-spicy scent, not "chocolate-flavored" tea.

I've tried both the Numi "Chocolate Puerh" and "Magnolia Puerh" teas.  Both are excellent quality.  The flavors are distinct, not overpowering, and enjoyable.These teas are enjoyable with just a touch of agave to sweeten the cup.  The flavor is pleasant without any need to be enhanced or covered up by anything else.  A touch of lemon juice also works well.  And a dash of vitamin C can be used in harmony with this tea.I do agree with the instructions to not let it steep too long, in fact a good full flavor is obtained at the low end of their recommended steeping times.I like what they have written on the box about being high quality and healthy.  It is nice to not find "artificial flavors" added.  This company appears to really care about producing a good product and protecting the environment.

column9: Where is the tea, where is the flavor?
column10: The description is so mouth watering that I did not hesitate to buy it. It smells great, but that's about it; I tried to brew it as the package says, with hotter water, steeping more time, less time... whatever: feels like I'm drinking hot water with a vague spicy taste.... quite disappointing - expensive experiment!

column9: The best thing about it was the name .."Chocolate Puehr" *giggle*
column10: This was OK, it has kind of an odd flavour but then again I am not known for either flavored tea or organic products. It's a nice little substitute for hot chocolate or coffee.

column9: Medium Strength Tea with Great Mix of Flavors
column10: I have a group of teas that I alternate between depending upon my mood. This tea fills a void I didn't realize exists in my favorites -- chocolate tea. This is a medium body tea -- not weak and not strong. It has absolutely no harsh bitter aftertaste and I brewed it at different time intervals, and no bitterness appeared. I followed the package recommendations to steep for 3-5 minutes, and ignored the boiling water directions and just used very hot water to steep the bag. At three minutes it was a bit too weak, but it seemed just right at five minutes. I left the bag in the cup and let the tea cool down to see if it would become too strong or lose its smoothness as it cooled -- it did neither. The results seemed to hold firm at the five minute mark. I often use tea in cooking but this tea would not work for that purpose -- it isn't strong enough to impart flavor as an ingredient in other dishes. The tea is organic and Kosher, and 1% of sales benefit social, environmental and sustainable causes.There is a lovely pronounced chocolate flavor in the background that oddly enough works perfectly with the black tea. There are much milder hints of cinnamon, orange and nutmeg that also help to create the tea's special blend. And, although the chocolate isn't strong enough to cause me to skip dessert, it might do in a pinch. I will definitely add this tea to my list of favorites -- it is that good. And, I would definitely curl up with a cup of Chocolate Puerh to sip and savor on a rainy day.

This Numi Chocolate Puerh tea is truly original, at least for me. I have never had a cocoa infused tea before and certainly nothing as rich as this tea. I'm eager to try other flavors after tasting this one.The tea is smoother and fuller bodied than the average tea, a bit more like coffee, but still a tad lighter. It has a very chocolate/cinnamon flavor much like a gourmet dark chocolate bar.There is also the claim that this tea is good for you. I certainly can't attest to being healthier after drinking it, but the flavor is wonderful so I will continue to enjoy it and hope for additional health benefits.Unique, organic, and tasty, with cool environmentally sound packaging, too. Highly recommended!

This is absolutely the best tea I've ever had. Seriously. I'm a lifelong tea drinker and have tried many, many types and brands of tea, and this is, was, love at first sip. I'm hoping Numi will do a bulk version.
I had tasted the chocolate flavor at a tea I went to, and loved it. The tea I ordered from Amazon had a funny taste, and did not meet my expectations.

I had really enjoyed a sample I'd received, so I think it's possible that the product I ultimately ordered from Amazon should have been better.  If quality control is so inconsistent, I guess I wouldn't take a chance again.  I guess either something went wrong in the recipe, or in the filling of the tea bags at the factory, or maybe it was stored too long in the wrong conditions, because the product was really weak.  Too bad.
Love tea, love chocolate.  Together...not so much.  The chocolate flavor was too weak and there was a strange chalkiness to the drink.  A real disappointment.

column9: Pleasant... but nothing to get excited about
column10: Numi Organic Chocolate Pureh makes a nice cup of tea and it is good to know organic methods were employed in its production. There is not much chocolate or vanilla flavor, it has a sort of a non-descript brown herbal mugginess. I tried putting milk in it because that is how I enjoy black tea, but it was not a good fit. Maybe sugar would give it some zing, but I don't want to start putting sugar in my tea.

You would never know this was a tea from the taste -- it tastes like the world's thinnest water-based hot chocolate.  This might be a good choice if you want the taste of chocolate without a lot of calories.  But there is no way to tell how many calories, or how much caffeine, since there is no nutrition label.  All in all, there is not much reason to drink this beverage.

I was expecting a really spectacular cup of tea after reading the product description.  The tea was ok, but I would not buy it again.I felt the tea had a gritty aftertaste to it.  The chocolate flavor was extremely subtle and hard to taste.And even though the box touts its green nature, the tea bags came sealed in foil packages (not recyclable).  The box also mentions that the bags are compostable, but most tea bags I've encountered are compostable.

column9: Really Weak Tea made me Really Nauseous
column10: I tried this Numi Chocolate Puerh tea four times and was disappointed and left with a very upset stomach. I used a big mug and the taste was barely detectable, it did however have a pleasant aroma of cinnamon with an ever so slight scent of vanilla. I then tried it in a smaller cup with the same results, barely any taste to it. I then tried it in a tiny 6 oz tea cup and it still really had no flavor other then a slight taste of cinnamon in hot water. Very weak tea with awful side effects of extreme nausea. Not sure if this was from the acid in it or something else, maybe the cinnamon. I can't recommend this on any level, it is weak and tasteless with awful side effects at least for me.  I love plain Rooibos and I will stick to that.

My wife and I both love this Tea! She is the more picky about her tea, between the 2 of us. If she likes it than it must really be good since she has tried a great many different kinds and can be considered a connoisseur.Personally, I prefer to drink my teas plain with no sugar or other additions. This tea tastes great plain. The very subtle chocolatey aftertaste is very pleasant. I tried adding just a bit of sugar, as an experiment, and it's still quite good that way too.Based on my experience, I find the Numi Organic Tea to be of high quality and can definately recommend it to tea drinkers everywhere.

I LOVE this tea! It has such a rich, deep flavor to it. It's hard for me to drink any other tea now, they all seem thin, watery, shallow in taste compared to Numi's Chocolate Puerh.I truly look forward to my daily cup and enjoy every sip!

You'd think with "Chocolate" and "Velvety and Vanilla" in the name of this tea that you're in for a real treat. Don't be fooled. There is some kind of spice added that makes this tea taste like Indian food. I like Indian food, don't get me wrong, but I don't want it's flavors in my tea.

column9: I know what you're thinking... chocolate tea???
column10: Yes, I thought the same thing: chocolate tea??? Amazon Vine provided a free sample box and I could not be more happy in taking this gigantic leap into the unknown. Ok, ok, so it's only tea - not that much of a leap (leaf?);) Bottomline: Numi has produced yet another 5-star product that both tea lovers *and* chocolate lovers will surely enjoy. The deep, smooth, chocolaty flavor + aroma will have you clicking the "subscribe and save" button regularly!

I'm reluctant to leave a review for this product. I feel like I found some gold and I don't want to share it.A health oriented product in a chemical free can. A fraction of the price than I can get it locally. And FREE delivery.Shhh. Don't tell anyone.Thanks Amazon and Eden.

I don't eat many prepared foods, so I rarely have quick options on hand when I need them.  Enter this chili.  I got a great deal with subscribe and save, and made the commitment of 12 cans, having never tried this product.  When I finally did, I found it good but bland.  I threw it in a saucepan with a little extra water, tomato paste, and three different kinds of chiles.  I like a LOT more spice and flavor in my chili and I didn't mind adding to my preferences.  That aside, you can tell the ingredients are good quality and healthy, which makes the taste adjustment worthwhile to me.  It's a good pantry staple and I'll eventually eat them all, but will then probably try something new.  I'd LOVE a really, really hot variety.

Am new to gluten free foods. My husband says that gluten must be really flavorful because he had not experienced any tasty gluten free foods. BUT, this chili is flavorful and has wonderful texture. He approves of this chili and I absolutely love it.I have used this chili in a few ways. I add it to: scrambled eggs, red pepper soup, chips and cheese. The chili is great all by itself too.

column9: I really like this one, just one flaw
column10: Taste is great! I was surprised how much I liked this flavor. My one and only complaint (besides it not being free) is that the two types of mushrooms in this product are NOT organic. Everything else is, just not the mushrooms - only reason I gave it 4 instead of 5 stars. I am on the fence if I will reorder....  :(

I love Eden products especially for the fact they use bpa free cans and they are gluten free. Might need a little cayenne pepper or added seasoning for those who are used to msg crap filled products. My delivery was fast but 4 cans were dented pretty bad. Not too big of a deal cause I can just cook em up this week but I was hoping to store these for longer periods of time. All in all I give it 4 stars.

column9: Worst thing I have ever eaten!
column10: I read the great reviews this product got and was encouraged to try it, but when I did I could barely finish a bite.  It has a horrible bitter taste that lingered.  I would like to return for a refund but the site says it is not returnable.  Not happy at all as I am now stuck with 11 unopened cans of the stuff.  Maybe I'll give it to a food bank and somebody else might like it.

This is hands-down the best Oatmeal I have ever eaten, and I've tried McCann's, Quaker steel cut, our local organic, everything! It cooks in 4 minutes in the microwave (be SURE to stir it thoroughly after one minute to avoid clumping), and does NOT develop that sticky/gluey texture that all other oatmeal seems to have--now I finally understand that Scots' obsession with oatmeal for breakfast!

I bought this as a themed Christmas gift for my mother. She loved it!! The recipe for morning oatmeal was wonderful. It has just enough texture. She and I both will be ordering more in the future. It arrived on time and secured in a plastic bag to protect it from moisture.

I heard about this oatmeal on Dr. Oz as a "sleep" product.  I tried it and while it didn't keep me sleeping any longer than I normally do (about 45 minutes to 1.5 hours), it was filling and tastes good.  I would definitely recommend this product to others.

Most folks here in the Pacific Northwest prefer extra dark espresso roasts, but I love the mild, non-acidic, medium roasts served in the German and Austrian restaurants I frequented while traveling on business in the 1980s. I've tried just about every medium roast on the market, particularly after Safeway stopped carrying Dallmayr a year or so ago, but everything tastes bitter in comparison. Dallmayr is also very finely ground, which is important good coffee from drip coffee makers. I'd buy the larger 17-ounce size (a 30 cents per serving savings, I believe) but the 8.8 ounce fits perfectly in my special coffee tin.

It has been almost 20 years to enjoy this coffee. It is hard to tell which one is the best coffee because of different taste for everyone, but it is the best coffee to me that I have ever had until now. It is very smooth from the beginning to the end of the last moment. I also like to drink it even if it became cold because it still smooth to drink when I compare with other brands. I also noticed the taste could be different when I make it with different water. E.g. purified water or tab water... I hope that anyone who is insterested in to try different coffee than local store will enjoy it.

We love this coffee! Rich flavor without bitterness and one interesting thing we discovered, the longer the coffee sits in the pot, the richer the taste with no bitterness. It does not bother my stomach. I no longer buy any other coffee.

This is the best coffee you will ever taste.  Prepared properly, it offers a smooth brew, with no acidic edge.  If you've had coffee at a German restaurant here in America, you've probably had Dallmayr.
this is without a doubt the best coffee you will ever taste.  i know........frank
I LOVE THIS COFFEE !!! It is very smooth, full bodied, with a hint of caramel flavor.

I bought a small package from a local store because it was sitting with all the other luxury coffees like Kona or Blue Mountain, but for a quarter of the cost.  I hope I don't make that mistake again. I use a french press to make my coffee and my favorite coffees come from Kenya, Ethiopia and Hawaii. Maybe I got a bad batch, maybe I am doing something wrong, or my tastes are different, but this coffee tasted weak and lifeless. Thinking I just made it too weak, I used more coffee the next time.  I got some of the flavor I was looking for but it was overpowered by an acidic flavor.  So I cut it with milk and it improved, but it still just doesn't taste how I think a fine coffee should.  I shouldn't have to go through all that to get a drinkable cuppa joe. Yes this coffee is not very bitter, but removing an entire element of flavor from this coffee just ruined it.  I like very dark chocolate because of all the different interesting flavors, fruity, spicy, sweet, and it's slightly bitter- but in a good way.  That is how coffee should be.  This coffee is like milk chocolate. It is overly simple, hardly bitter and some people are bound to like it that way.  To me, it lacks the flavor I look for.

I recently tried Dallmayr prodomo. I typically like German coffee (Jacobs, Tchibo, even Aldi "German Roast") but something seems "off" on this Dallmayr. Black with just a bit of Splenda results in an odd, possibly acidic, taste that's hard to describe. Adding a bit of Half and Half which seems to make it taste more like "regular" coffee, but I don't normally do that with any of the other coffees I drink. I bought the coffee locally, and it was more than year from its freshness date, so I'm just going to avoid this variety in the future.

Not everyone has the same expectations for smoked fish.  Some people prefer it smoked to a crisp; other people prefer smoked fish that is nearly raw.  The folks at Seabear seem to have found a good, in between, place.I've used this product several times and have always enjoyed it.  The salmon is smokey and flavorful, flakey, firm, and tasty.  The salmon ships in foils pouches, each containing a couple of ounces of salmon oil.  You can pour it down the drain if you prefer a drier fish (but that's a lot of good omega-3 fatty acids to waste).  Used in salmon pasta with a little olive oil, sundried tomatoes, and a little black pepper (let it sit over night in the fridge for the flavors to mix) it is a summer favorite.  If you like your smoked salmon moderately moist, yet firm, Seabear is a good choice.

I've ordered this a few times for myself and as gifts, and it's always appreciated. Having lived in the Pacific Northwest for a few years, I get that "deja vu" feeling whenever I eat salmon smoked the way SeaBear does theirs. Very flavorful and a heavenly snack to accompany your favorite whiskey.
I've sent this assortment to my dad twice, and he absolutely loves it. Says it's the best smoked salmon he ever had. I highly recommend it.

column9: Great price for a great product
column10: I have this product delivered to my Dad every two months.  He loves it!  He has tried to find it or something similar on the open market in Los Angeles, and just unable to find the same prime quality.  Once he mailed me the packaging.  I thought he was sharing.  NOT!  He wanted me to see how nicely the product was packaged!  I'm glad I finally found something that he really looks forward to receiving.
We have this delivered to us every other month. We love all three selections, but the Soho is our personal favorite. We highly recommend. A little pricey, but we cannot find smoked salmon locally.

column9: This salmon is a tremendous treat!
column10: Fresh, good color, wonderful taste.  We've eaten the salmon several times this year, and love it!
I admit the salmon is out of my price range, but now and then I treat myself. It is pure Alaska, keeps forever, and is so tender. I am a bagels and lox person, but there are many recipes included.

column4: notAyesperson "Always in search of good books"
column10: Nice company, will answer your emails.This fish is ok. Kind of pricey, not that decadent.  I'm not sure I would purchase this again.  Similar to canned tuna in texture and presentation.
Great tasting salmon trio. The only reason why I gave it four-stars is because it was slightly salty for my taste. Would recommend it to anyone.

Since moving to the Northwest, we wanted gifts for friends and families that reflect our new lifestyle.  The trio of smoked salmon is perfect.  I keep some around for visitors also.  It doesn't have to be refrigerated, the salmon is very good, and the 3 pack makes it great for a couple of visitors or open more than one box for a crowd.  Put out some cream cheese, crackers and the fish and you are the best hostess in town.  Be sure to pat the fish with paper towels before serving or it is very wet.

This sample pack was great! I ordered it for my finance as a valentines gift, and he was very pleased. The steaks were large and thick and the flavor was excellent.  The box came quickly as advertised and we will be ordering this again.
What else do I need to say - it was a gift for my father and both he and my mother loved it. I will be ordering it again in the future.

column9: Tased like canned salmon, expensive canned salmon!
column10: There was little to no taste difference in the 3 fish. Very flaky and dry with NO smoked flavor. The fish in all the pouches were crushed and almost to a mush. I WOULD NOT BUY AGAIN.
Probably the Best Brand of Smoked Salmon I ever had. really enjoyed the taste and freshness of the fish. You wont be disappointed in this brand for sure.

Every year I order some smoked salmon for my dad, and this has been, by far, the best yet. Not at all dry like some we have gotten. The trio gives you three types so you can see which you like better if you aren't sure. I will be ordering SeaBear again!

column9: " S M O K E D......S A L M O N ".....I S.....N O T.....A L W A Y S....." L O X '.
column10: Many people, trying to be and sound more sophisticated, substitute the words "smoked salmon" for the word "lox".  Having eaten the "SEA BEAR SMOKED SALMON TRIO", herein being reviewed, (and the literature that comes with it), I have learnt that, whilst all "lox" IS smoked salmon, not all "smoked salmon" is lox. (SeaBear DOES offer a nice, large package of "lox"....and calls it "lox", and illustrates it, in the advertising flyer that comes with the "Smoked Salmon Trio").  But the fish within the "Smoked Salmon Trio" is NOT "lox". The fish here is dryish, and very salty.  "Lox", on the other hand, must go through additional preparation, for it is far more moist than the dryish fish within the "Smoked Salmon Trio".  I have seen, (in the "Cabelas" catalogue), "Lox" described as 'buttery'....which it truly is.  For those who are interested, "Lox" also is usually certified kosher -- whilst the fish within the "Smoked Salmon Trio" is not.The smoked salmon within the "Smoked Salmon Trio", is, as I have said, very dry and salty.  However, all bones have been removed, (although the skin remains).  This fish also will keep on a shelf!  It need NOT be refrigerated until opened.The three types of smoked salmon within have very little taste variation to me.  Yes, there is a TINY bit of difference....but not enough to excite my taste buds.  And salmon -- right from cans, especially the top brands and varieties -- right from the supermarket or on Amazon, taste almost the same to me, at a far lesser price.The literature that comes with this set of three smoked salmon varieties is interesting and informative, as is the history of "SeaBear" foods, which is also given.  This company obviously takes great pride in providing good salmon and other products to its customers, and strives to be the best it can be.  I would advise them, however, to emphasize, even more, the difference between "smoked salmon" and "lox" in ALL its literature, and in the package description of ALL its products. Knowing whether "Dry" smokedsalmon, or "buttery", or "lox"-type smoked salmon, is in a package, would be a great help to those who, like me, sometimes get their syntax and meanings confused, betwixt the two.SUMMARY:  Will NOT Buy This Product Again.  (But hopefully, the "Lox" they sell will be available in smaller quantities! : ),

This is far too overpriced, you get three small filets that have a terrible smell to them, almost like day old tuna.  It works out to about 12 dollars for a 6 oz salmon filet that really isn't even good. You can get it fresh, minus the horrible smell and not already precooked.  To be perfectly honest, a can of bumblebee tuna would be better than this and it would cost you 35 less dollars, I only purchased it by mistake and the seller immediately hit the shipping soon button and would not stop shipment even after request.  Worst transaction I've had on Amazon to date.I couldn't even stomach to taste it, that's how bad the smell was, huge waste of money, just go to the store and get a filet yourself, cheaper and better quality.
This is real earth friendy food that is good for health and preserves the species of good salmon just like the Native Indians did. Respect, Wisdome and Honer

This is a fairly salty (which can be expected from smoked products)fairly dryish solid slab of salmon. I couldn't decide how to use it so it ended up in an omelet and I guess the rest will go into salmon salad.
I had these on several Jet Blue flights and just had to have them. I am not a big potato chip person but these are delicious.
I had these chips on a recent Jet Blue flight and they were incredible!!!!  Very low in fat, but delicious.  I highly recommend these chips and will be purchasing them off Amazon!

The normal price for these chips is just too high to justify on a regular basis, so it is one of the many items I have on my shopping list so I can keep track of prices and scope out when it goes on sale. I got lucky on these recently, at about half off, during the warehouse sale for the box of 12 so I jumped on it.These blue chips, not dyed, just made from Blue potatoes, are such a treat. They are crisper and somehow heartier than your normal chip and, like almost all Terra Chips, are just deliciously made.I've grown blue potatoes in my garden. They tend to be much smaller so the chips also are smaller. You certainly don't need nearly as many to get your salty crisp fix than you do of your regular chip.These arrived double boxed and in perfect shape. New chips with expiration date the same as the chips in the store so not an issue there. It may seem strange buying groceries at Amazon, but I had to say, this was convenient, smartly priced and well worth it!

I had never heard of these potato chips or blue potato chips for that matter before Dr Oz recommended them on his tv program.He raves about them because he says they contain anthocyanins which in his words,help you to lose weight by tricking your body into wanting to be thin.Besides being healthy,these chips are really delicious!They're bursting with flavor!I have already converted a couple of people into naturally blue potato chip fans.They are also not fried,but they do contain some oil.If you like potato chips,you will love these!
Looked like a dark roast which I'm not fond of but turned out to have a wonderful flavor and aroma! I went through it in no time!

This is a very flavorful blend.  I thought it would be bitter when I saw how dark it was, but it is not bitter, but has a robust, smooth flavor and aroma.  I love the fact that it is fair traded and organic.  Good bargain.
It is definitely stale and burned. All three bags. Unless you think that French Roast is supposed to taste like charcoal.Chuck Full Of Nuts would be the closest comparable brand.

I just finished up my first bag of this coffee, it's great. I normally buy Starbucks Breakfast Blend, just so you know for comparisons purpose-but I am switching to this brand. It's just the perfect blend for me, smooth but strong enough to wake me up.

I really hate to give this coffee a bad review, especially after seeing all of the positive reviews, but it was pretty terrible.  I hate that I got three bags of it and will take it into the office where we drink any generic coffee that's on sale.  I make my coffee in a french press to preserve the oils.  There are no oils in this coffee.  It's basically colored water.
good coffee for a french press.make it as strong or lite as you like it
My husband loved this coffee.  It was fresh and delicious.  I love the fact that it is organic and fair trade!
I started to drink only decaf, so my hubby gets to drink this.  Up until the switch, I made this along with my decaf for a 1/2 & 1/2 brew.  It was yummy and I was happy that it is also organic!
We liked the reviews and realized the wisdom of organic coffee...so tried it.We love it! Very smooth and flavorful.
Just made my first batch and am very pleased. Nice French roast taste but mild. I was surprised how quickly the beans ground to a very fine grain size. Maybe I'll hold the button down for less time.

I have this product on Subscribe & Save which makes it the most economical organic coffee I know of that also tastes good. It does tend to brew light (I have the typical drip coffee maker) and I noticed that if I grind it a little too finely it can have a bitter edge, but that might be more a user issue than a coffee bean issue. I love the aroma of a freshly opened bag. Taster's notes say "citrus & butterscotch" and I have to agree because, without reading that, I noticed caramel-y notes on my first sip. It also says the coffee is "bright & balanced". I've gone through several bags and the taste and character is consistent.I am still looking for a Fair Trade (possibly locally sourced? might be asking for too much in the coffee industry), Organically Grown coffee that has consistent, exceptional taste, and I am still open to suggestions. In the meantime, however, I am very happy with my current Pick (pardon the pun!).

This isn't the best coffee I've ever had, but for sitting on an Amazon shelf for who knows how long, and then being shipped out to the consumer at a sum cost of $16-$20/30 oz, it's an amazing coffee.  Definitely a French roast, but not a burnt French roast; it doesn't taste like the roast is hiding anything in the beans.  It drip brews up full bodied, smooth and rich - exactly what an every day breakfast blend should be.  The organic label is a bonus, but it's not the reason I buy this.
This is a robust dark roast coffee. My husband and I are coffee snobs and we love this coffee. It is so smooth and never bitter.

After trying so many varieties of coffee, I've finally found the perfect coffee for me.  It has great body, aroma, not bitter,just smooth to drink.  I specially love it using my espresso maker.  Well worth the search. I have this on auto shipment.

column9: Comforting is right on the mark,
column10: I'm not really a Republic of Tea drinker - normally. I have found this comfort and joy tea to be remarkably comforting. The tea consists of cinnamon, cloves, licorice root and apple pieces. I think it's the licorice root that really makes this tea. It is an extremely soothing tea, easy on the tummy.Each flavor comes through very delicately, nothing is too overpowering in this cup of tea.

I love love love this tea. It is amazing!!! I actually bought it as a gift for someone this year & ended up getting some of it as well. Shipping was great, had it in time for the holidays!!! It's too bad it only comes around once a year, I would drink it all year round! :)  It would be even better if they had it in loose leaf. I did not see that option, only the pod option.
For a busy mom with a ton of kids, these crackers are a life-saver in the area of on the go snacks.

column9: WARNING! Keebler announced "precationary hold" for Salmonella!
column10: I recieved an email from the FDA stating that Keebler has placed a "precautionary hold" on these crackers because of the salmonella outbreak associated with peanut butter. You can look up the info on Keebler's website.

Anybody who has ever had "Dynamite shrimp" from PF Changs or "Bang Bang Shrimp" from Bonefish Grill is familiar with this sauce. It is the same stuff. Very spicy, so have plenty of beer around you. lol.

This shrimp sauce is now one of my favorite things.  I love the spicy taste of the sauce and it actually provides the right amount of "kick" without being too spicy.  I tried it for the first time at a party I hosted and it was a big hit.  Reminds me so much of the Bang Bang Shrimp I have whenever I visit Bonefish Grill.  This is a keeper for me and my family.

I don't know if the taste is identical to the sauce used to make the Bang-Bang Shrimp at Bonefish but it doesn't matter.  This sauce has good heat and flavor.  I can make my own but now that we've found this, why bother.
This is a great sauce, can be used on Salmon, chicken and even hamburgers!  I love it and have used it on all of the above its really great!

Dinni's Select Spicy Shrimp Sauce, 12-Ounce Bottles (Pack of 3)BINGO! Finally last year I got a Gift Pack containing 1 jar each of Dinni's Spicy Shrimp Sauce, Honey Mustard and Italian Herb Vinaigrette. All these products made a believer out of me. These is no difference that I could tell in Shrimp I cooked with Dinni's Spicy Shrimp Sauce and the one I eat at Bonefish. Amongst the 3 product each one was better than the other.I have ordered several times since then from Amazon. There are some products Amazon does not carry, which I buy from Dinni's website, and always the company includes a free jar as repeat customer appreciation. The free stuff is not mentioned on Dinni's site hence I was surprised the first time. Every product I have tasted is simply Amazing. I don't understand why Amazon does not carry all of them.We throw several parties every year. I always wanted to serve the Bonefish  Bang Bang Shrimp, but it is not practical, so I started searching the web to find a exact recipe, the first one I tried was the one which had lots of good reviews, it called for; Mayonnaise, Thai Sweet & Hot Chili Sauce. After 3 hours shopping and trying to purchase hard to find ingredients and another hour in the kitchen, the result was very disappointing. The shrimp turned out to be miles apart from Bonefish's Shrimp. Don't get me wrong the shrimp was OK if you are not looking for the Bonefish Taste, but defiantly it was not a knockoff.

This shrimp sauce is AMAZING!  My entire family loves Bang Bang Shrimp at the Bonefish grill, this sauce helps us re-create it at home.  Although I have a recipe, I have a quick version that is delicious too.  I prepare popcorn shrimp in the oven.  When it's done, I pour the popcorn shrimp over shredded lettuce, then I pour the shrimp sauce over that.  My whole family LOVES it! It's quick and a crowd-pleaser!  I love it so much, I ordered it for several of my friends for Christmas.  You won't go wrong ordering this sauce!  Plus, the company is great to work with too.  They sent me a free bottle of an Italian marinade that is yummy too!

column9: As close to Bone Fish Bang Bang as you can get
column10: My husband and I are Bone Fish Bang Bang Shrimp nuts!  We order it often.  I am a recipe hound and am always looking for copy cat recipes and this is it.  I read up on one of the recipe sites about this sauce being as close as you can get to the real thing.  Of course Bone Fish will not give out its recipe, however this is close.  There is a recipe on line that is pretty close and then we toss this sauce...delicious.  Great product!  The sauce is great on other items as well.  FYI its got a kick.

I think this horchata is just as tasty as ones I've had in mexican restaurants.  The nice thing about this product is that it lacks hydrogenated oils, artificial sweeteners, and dairy products which I have found in some powder mixes and concentrates. It's a little sweeter than I thought it would be, but normally my horchata from restaurants has ice so maybe I'm used to a more dilute flavor.  Adding a bit of water helped cut the sweetness and allows me to extend my yummy horchata a little further.The ingredients in this product are: Filtered Water, Brown Rice (Partially Milled), Dehydrated Cane Juice, Expeller Pressed High Oleic Safflower Oil, and/or Canola Oil, Rice Flour, Natural Flavors, Spice, Carageenan.An 8 oz serving contains 160 calories, 25 calories from fat.  4 Servings per Container.  Total Fat 2.5g (4% RDA), Saturated Fat 0g, Trans Fat 0g, Polyunsaturated Fat 2g, Monounsaturated Fat 0.5g, Cholesterol 0g, Sodium 5mg (0% RDA), 80mg Potassium (2% RDA), Total Carbohydrate 32g (11%RDA), Sugars 18g, Protein 1g, 4% RDA Calcium, 2% RDA Iron.FYI, the packaging indicates that this product should not be used as an infant formula and to consult your child's doctor for use with children under age 5.I have found this drink at my Whole Foods Market if you are interested in trying it before buying 6 boxes.  It was 2. 69, so only a bit more expensive than Amazon.

Having never tried horchata before this, I can't really compare it to other brands.  It is a rice-based drink with a hint of cinnamon.  Serve it cold/over crushed ice. It's refreshing with a spicy meal. Lactose and gluten free.

column9: Very yummy with cereal for those who can't process milk.
column10: I have tried both of the other Rice Dream flavors, vanilla and original. This one came in the 32 ounce size so I thought I would give it a try. It makes a high fiber bowl of cereal a taste treat. It's a mild cinnamon taste. It's like the difference between oatmeal plain and oatmeal with cinnamon. And thanks to it being lactose free, no bloating and no tummy troubles.

I keep ordering this and draining the boxes one after the other until I have none. This will be my fourth order and it absolutely won't be my last. Keep this cold in the back of the fridge and add some ice... so good. That said, sometimes I don't even bother with a glass, let alone ice. Other times I thin it with some water to extend the goodness.It tastes creamy, but the texture is thin. It's sweet, but not too sweet to drink down like it were water. The only problem here is that I have no desire to moderate my consumption of this stuff. I want it to come in gallon containers and I want to treat it as a replacement for water. Of course, at 32 ounces per each of the six containers, that gets costly. It's also good mixed with coke for a Pepsi and Milk replacement (no, really.)
AFTER ENJOYING THIS DRINK IN CALIFORNIA I WAS HAPPY TO FIND IT WITH YOU. A REFRESHING CHANGE.
This drink is great chilled or warm. My kids love it, sure I will reorder.

column9: Better than orange juice, Coca Cola and Mountain Dew combined
column10: Better than orange juice, Coca Cola and Mountain Dew combined (not together, just of any other drink I've had since milk as a kid).I decided to cut back dairy, bread and red meat for my 80 something Mom and I (including store pizza, cheese and such).  I've been ordering boxes of aseptic Soy and Almond milks looking for some good flavor, variation and low price; combining flavors with soy and whey proteins in a blender for a daily protein shake as a nutritional supplement - as recommended for her by her doctor.(The protein has helped my senior Mom recover badly needed lower body strength, and actually our high blood pressure problems have disappeared. She is mentally sharper.)...Looking at prices and availability through my Amazon prime account the horchata sounded interesting enough to try - Amazon prime because I don't think I would want any grocery goods shipping more than a day or so. In fact I prefer to order up when a product is temporarily out of stock so that there is a better chance it has not been sitting in their warehouse very long.While all of the flavors of other products have been ok; even great when combined and mixed with other flavors (bananas, yogurt, (mint)-chocolate, misc. fruits and flavors) the horchata is delicious right out of the box - the delivered case had a ruptured box leaking into the shipping box (and delivery truck) and I drank a glass poured off straight - yea, I'm kinda gross sometimes.It was like the long ago taste of cinnamon toast without the toast (and loads of added sugar and butter).So I use the horchata alone for some of the soy and whey protein shakes (with a little Guar gum to thicken it maybe) and no ice needed with the boxes in the fridge.It makes up a little for pizzas and stuff. I think this is the start of something special...

I ordered this product in Sept. 2010.  I enjoyed this product very much.  I was introduced to Horchata through my aide who is from El Salvador.  I went to a BBQ and they had me try it.  I loved it so much I searched online and found this.  The first couple of boxes were excellent.  I have 1 open container in the fridge now.  I went to have some and it seems as though it fermented or just plain went bad.  I looked on the container and the best by date says  May 2011.  I have like 2 containers left, not open.  I'm afraid to try them.

column9: Going through this quicker than I expected!
column10: I got this because I thought it would take me too long to get through 12 cartons of rice milk. I was wrong, it's been less than a week and I'm already on my 3rd carton. This stuff is great.  If you like rice milk, this will be a nice twist. I've used it in recipes as a replacement for milk (Coffee Cake) and it turned out great!
Definitely recommend this product, the taste it is just as I remember it brings back memories from my childhood, very flavorful, my whole family enjoys having a glass of agua de horchata.
I fell in love with Horchata out in portland on food trucks. This is as close as i can find. Costs $4 a carton locally. Shelf stable tetra pack.. Ready to drink, light cinnamon flavor.

column9: Had it in a restaurant, now I have it at home.
column10: I have recently been looking for a different drink (trying to get away from boring old soda pop) and a friend suggested Horchata at a local mexican restaurant.  Nearly every day I've been going through drive through near work to get my horchata fix...but nothing in the local city I live in.  A quick Amazon search and the click of a button...now I can have my new favorite drink at home too!

I've been drinking this like water I love the taste!  I pour it over some crushed ice, and I can just down it.  My husband on the other hand HATES the taste of rice, and he didn't like this either. (it has a rice taste) So if you love the taste of rice, you'll love this for sure.

column9: Great treat for my 5 year old
column10: My son loves getting horchata at our favorite Mexican restaurant and so finding this product was fantastic. The more easily found Kern's, while tasty too, has more sweetener (corn syrup, yuck) as well as artificial flavors and has to be kept refrigerated even before you open it, unlike this product. This is healthier, tastes better and so dang cool to have delivered to the door. Yay Rice Dream!

I'm not crazy about this product. It's nowhere near as good as the horchata I get at my favorite Mexican restaurants. I think it lacks flavor; it definitely needs more cinnamon. Also, it's quite sweet. It should be poured over a large glass of ice to water it down. I still do enjoy this product somewhat, especially after adding more cinnamon. It's just not ideal, especially because the extra cinnamon doesn't incorporate well. I think I'm going to try blending it with ice and extra cinnamon to see how it turns out.

I decided to try and find a horchata that tasted like the kind I'd drink when growing up in San Diego. So far, this has been the furthest from it. This product has a chalky, almost dry taste to it. It's not awful, but not the taste I was expecting. There is an aftertaste that seems like flour or some other similar flavor. Obviously, liking the flavor is subjective, but I will not be purchasing this brand again. When Amazon has it in stock, the Klass brand horchata is my preference so far.
Thes GREAT Haribo Gummi Rasberries are THE BEST. If you haven't tried them I suggest you try some. THEY ARE "GREAT".

column9: My wife and I love these
column10: My wife and I love these. I bought these for her christmas stocking and they lasted about a day. Delicious.

I was very happy to see that I could order just the blueberry tea like the tin that came with my iced tea maker, it's the first blueberry tea I've tried and I love it. I ordered the 4 pack tins and I will for sure order it again!!

Ohhhh maaaan.... Yup, I think this is hands-down one of the most indulgent, chocolatey, and SINFULLY delicious breakfast treats I think I've ever had! (And I've had quite a few!)This pancake mix is over-the-top in the best way you can imagine: super rich chocolate taste, hearty texture, and tons of white chocolate chips! <<<AWESOME There's no imitation anything in this stuff, you can tell by the taste. All of the ingredients are PACKED with flavor and they all work together, too. (The white chocolate chips blend with the chocolate (cocoa?) blends with the whole wheat flour they use for a hugely delicious taste! It's funny how my roommates always think I'm the "star chef" whenever I break this out at the breakfast table... XDI make this stuff, Jack & Jason's Pancake & Waffle Mix - Blueberry - Case of 6, and Jack & Jason's Pancake & Waffle Mix - Banana Walnut - Case of 6 all the time...but I keep coming back to Double Chocolate--it's just SO GOOD!!! Only problem is sharing with my roomies!!!

To begin with, I am no expert in the field, and I have pretty limited range of experience. That being said, I love Glenmorangie Original. It has wonderful aroma and complex flavors. I don't know all the proper lingo, I'm afraid, but it has sweetness and smokiness and a little citrus, maybe? It is light and not peaty. The finish is long and lovely. When you roll this whiskey around your mouth a bit, the "mouth feel" is very rich and pleasant. This is a far more complex drink than American or Canadian whiskeys and a bit richer than Glenlivet, the Scotch I met first.

My hubby and I love our large cup of coffee in the mornings but we hate that we have to pour cold creamer into our just made Tassimo cup of hot joe, so now we add the t- dis creamer and our coffee is hot and creamy. We love the creamer.

Received Monday, only 1 slightly dented can. had it for lunch yesterday right out of can with a butter and kraft mayo dip. Not one bad spot or tuff leaf, delicious.
