I've read several other similar stories so I'll keep it short. Not every Pod is bad, but enough are bad that I've cancelled my Subscribe and save order. I don't want to keep dealing with the brewing problems. The few pods that have worked actually made great tasting coffee. We purchased the medium roast and the decaf, same issues with both.

column9: Nice cup of decaf; defective k-cups
column10: The Brooklyn Bean Decaf Breakfast Blend is a fine-tasting, mellow cup of coffee.  My personal favorite decaf has always been Timothy's Colombian, but this is a nice, slightly milder alternative.  In fact, I couldn't tell you which of the two I like more.One strange issue - all the cups I've brewed up so far (we have a Keurig B70 Platinum) have brewed very slowly.  There might be an issue with the internal filter not allowing the water to move through quick enough.  No explosions or overflows, but not that great if you're in a hurry.UPDATE: Explosion time!  Don't you hate it when you get a cupful of grounds?  Don't think I'll be buying these again.  Oh well.

Like trying new coffee in my Keurig so I purchased the Boardwalk blend.  Love the taste of the coffee but as with other reviewers some of them what I will call exploded in the brewer.  This left quite a mess to clean up. Even though this happened will order another flavor of this coffee as I love the coffee.I will amend my review after receiving a box of the Cyclone Blend.  I have brewed 12-15 cups without any problems at all.  The company has apparently solved the problem they were having  with the k cups. As I stated previously I love the coffee.  After trying the Cyclone blend I've decided that this is the blend for me.  Will continue to purchase the coffee not only for the flavor but also the cost.

column9: Your taste buds will thank you!
column10: I was pleased to win a sampler box of Brooklyn Bean Roastery's eight most popular varieties (2 of each) in a contest promotion, and I can't say enough wonderful things about this ambitious new company's offerings.  From what I read here in early reviews, they got off to a shaky start with quality control in the manufacturing of the K-cups, but rest assured that I experienced no problems whatsoever.  The quality of the coffee is top notch, and the blend variety is mesmerizing.  It's SO good, in fact, that it's really hard to pick favorites, which is why I think that the most brilliant thing Brooklyn Bean could do, is offer a VARIETY PACK!  After all, not every one wants the same exact coffee, cup after cup.  Variety is what makes life interesting, does it not?Brooklyn Bridge Blend was the first one I tried, and my personal favorite.  It's a delightful medium roast that delights any time of day or evening, with just the right balance of body and flavor.  If I had to choose one coffee to drink for the rest of my life, THIS would be the one.Breakfast Blend paled in comparison, being a light roasted coffee, and initially not a standout for me.  But, my wife thought it was stellar, and could easily be a daily, easy-drinking morning favorite, even though she usually prefers darker, stronger roasts.Their Colombian is by far the BEST Colombian I have ever had, very complex in taste with sweet and nutty undertones.  Start your day with this, and you'll have a happy day.French Roast is usually not high on my list, but Brooklyn's is astounding!  It doesn't display the bitterness that I usually find with other French Roasts, and makes an excellent dark roast after dinner coffee.Boardwalk Blend is a medium roast, extra bold, that is best made in a larger size cup, 10 or 12 oz, and is also excellent over ice!  It won't knock you out, because it's not overwhelming in any one character, but it's a pleasant, drinkable blend.Corner Donut Shop is unique, in that it's not like any other company's "donut shop" blends for the Keurig type machines.  The flavor is a bit more subtle, and compliments pastries, pies, donuts (of course) any time of day.  This is a relaxing coffee, not one to shake you up, which is a good thing sometimes.  Think of it as the "comfort food" of coffees.  Medium roast, extra bold, make this in a larger size cup, also.Cyclone, named for the iconic Coney Island roller coaster, is a kick in the pants coffee.  Strong, bold, daring and a thrill-ride of complex, intense flavors, circling your palette, with each sip being a new thrill ride.  Yes, you'll want to ride again!  My wife has called this the "Guinness of coffees", with chocolaty undertones and full-bodied texture.  Definitely make this in a larger cup, being both a dark roast and an extra bold cup.A Brooklyn uniqueness, Fuhgeddaboudit, is another dark roast extra bold blend that leaves no doubt in your mind that you're drinking a cup of COFFEE!  This will wake you up out of a coma, folks!  Only in New York could they possibly come up with something this brash, cosmopolitan and interesting.I rarely drink decaf, but would like to try BB's, and feel the same about flavored coffees, like their Maple, Hazelnut and Vanilla offerings.  But, in short, we're so fond of Brooklyn Bean coffees, all of them so far, that it really is a tough choice to shop for a 36 count box of any one blend.  This is why it would be astounding, if they offered for sale, variety packs!  Keep up the great work, Brooklyn, I predict that this will soon be the #1 K-cup coffee on the planet!
This coffee is excellent!  Not to strong, not to weak when made as an 8 oz.cup.  It is by far one of the best values for Kcup coffee lovers.  Enjoy Life, Drink it up!

This review is for French roastWith a pinch of dark brown sugar make it tastes the way i like.This Kcup is lighter than regular brand only 11g(others 14-16g)Made with thin plastic cup & foil.The label is cute, bold enough for me & cheaper than others brand.

Updated Review 4/30/2012 -First shipment had multiple failures of the K-Cups, similar to many other reviewers.BBR sent a replacement order.  The brewing performance was improved - one of the first eight passed through some grounds, but not a total blowout.  Found I had to brew a smaller cup than normal for acceptable flavor, and even so the coffee had a certain 'hollowness'.  Not sure if it was just weak coffee, or the result of their filter system.
Absolutely awful. Would be good maybe if your cup wasn't full of coffee grounds and only get 1/4 a cup of coffee. I will never buy again.

Fuhgeddaboutit (or as I like to call it "unspellable") is a really good dark brew.  Considering it's price it's about to become a staple.  Cyclone and the French Roast are pretty good dark brews also.  I'm unqualified to comment on the lighter roasts.What I like most is the company.  I wrote a review on k-cups I didn't even purchase and Brooklyn reached out to me in an attempt to make it up to me; as if I was an actual customer, not a lot of companies would do that.  They sent me a sampler pack.  I'm very impressed with both Fuhgeddaboutit and the company. So today I go to Amazon to purchase a box and they are sold out.  What a cruel twist.

Maybe we're just used to stronger blends, but this one tastes pretty bland and weak to us. Honestly it quickly became one of the least popular items on the k-cup carousel in our house. For this price level, you can definitely do much better with the San Francisco Bay k-cups, which are cheaper and better.

column9: Worth another try!  Update to previous reviews.
column10: Tried this coffee based pretty much on the assumed introductory price.  I was a little skeptical about trying this product based on the reviews, due to the explosion issues.  Reviewers didn't rave on the taste too much however.  So after receiving these cups, I gave one a whirl, and had no problems brewing it.  I did notice that the box that they were packaged in could use some (might I say) environmental saving upgrades, and the box itself was a bit rough shod.  Also I examined a few of the K-cups and there seems to be a vacuum issue with them.  Some looked as if they were ready to blow up right in my hand, as they were so full of air, or whatever it is inside them, they were like a balloon that when over blown with air, it could explode in your face at any second.  The others seemed like they had no air or nitrogen or what ever inside. Cups could be squished and squeezed and the foil top would just waffle back and forth.  So that seems to be another quality control issue, with the vacuum packing and sealing process. Perhaps that may lead to the product quality itself once made in the cup.  I really don't think I have had the same consistent taste with one of these cup yet.  My first cup was rather weak, as in it tasted like I had run twice as much water through it than I should have.  Really had a watered down taste.  The following few cups weren't much different.  I am using a controlled amount of water, but the consistency of the coffee that gets filtered into the cup seemed to be all over the place.  There have been a couple of cups that seemed to be almost "just right" but still on the weak side, given this is supposed to be a medium roast.  I mean, I've had medium blends that taste like French Roast, but this I would really have to classify as a very light roast.Too light for me, so I'm sure if I re-order, I'll try a stronger blend.That being said, I think these guys at Brooklyn Roasting Co. are on the right track, and I do hope they can find a way to keep the price down.  If so, and assuming I can find the right roast for me, I might stick with them for a while.  If the price goes up, where it's tooth to tooth with the big boys, I'm afraid the big boys will win me out.Update 8/15/12. Well, just when I thought this problem with exploding cups was solved...BOOOOM!!! Coffee grounds everywhere!  YES, It happened to me.  *I'm trying to insert a photo, if I can figure that out. I'm pretty confident though that this will be my last purchase of these Brooklyn k cups.  It's one thing to have a passion to go after a piece of the K cup Pie, but if you can't do it right, don't do it at all.  This company (based on several buyers and reviews, even before I happened on to these "cheaper" cups) had plenty of chances to get it right.*Apparently Amazon or this company will not allow additional photos, as I tried to post an image of the exploded cup sitting in my machine.  My guess is they would have far too many photos of the dastardly messes.Update 9/03/12.  Ok, Based on the fact that this company is serious about hanging in there, and making things right with their customers, I am giving these guys another "college try".  After the exploding cup, they very graciously sent me replacement cups.  I did not ask that they be replaced, or demanded that they redeem themselves, I merely reported the problem, along with a photo, and next thing I knew, they were asking me for more info, about the product that I had, and then told me they would send some replacements. Again, I did not solicit these, but a few days later, a very generous offering was delivered to me.  I am really excited to try out all of the other flavors now, as the sent a sample box of several different flavors.  My wife and I have already tried a couple of the new flavors and so far they were quite good.  My wife really liked the Vanilla blend, and wants me to order a box of that alone.  I had the french roast, and thought it was pretty good as well.  The cups performed nicely and I'm looking forward to trying all of the others.So I suppose that as I am always willing to give things another shot, I really think that this company is truly trying to deliver a great product, and is doing the right thing by taking care of it's customers, one cup at a time.The only thing I'm still a little skeptical about is the pricing seems to be creeping up, closer to that of the big brothers in the business.  I was really hoping that they could keep them below .50 cents a cup, but are already surpassing that.  Pricing will be they main drive factor for me if these cups provide consistent and equally good or better coffee to that of the original players.All that being said, I'm upgrading the star factor.  Thanks Brooklyn for taking care of me.  That was unexpected, but very welcome!

This coffee was about the worst coffee I have ever had. It left a bitter taste in my mouth, and had no smoothness.  After reading the description(before ordering) it sounded wonderful. Whoever wrote it should get a reward for fiction.

I bought the fuhgeddaboudit cups, and the coffee is great, a very dark and flavorful roast with no bitter aftertaste. The k-cups themselves, however, have a tendency to explode, leaving a watery, coffeee-ground laden mess everywhere. The problem is the plastic on the bottom of the cup, it's either too thick, or a different material from most other k-cups. When you close the machine, the needle that is supposed to pierce the bottom of the cup sometimes fails to pierce the cup, but rather causes it to indent. The top needle has no problem piercing the top foil. The result is similar to trying to rinse the left over peanut butter out of a measuring spoon by putting it under the faucet running full blast. There is an easy way to prevent this from happening - if you manually push down the k-cup when you put it in the machine and make sure you feel the pop of the needle piercing the cup, you won't have any problems.That being said, the coffee is very good - will buy again.

I wanted to try a new coffee company and found Brooklyn coffee on Amazon. I have tried almost all the Kcups out there and I prefer extra bold type coffee. The Brooklyn extra bold coffee was strong, but not too strong, and had a full bodied aroma and flavor which I really appreciated. The box design is pretty cute as the flap opens up to become a dispenser.I was concerned when I read the reviews about the Kcups exploding/imploding but I am happy to report that I have had no issues brewing the Kcups in the Keurig machine. Hopefully, future reviewers can confirm that the quality control issues are in the past for Brooklyn Kcups. I liked the coffee and will buy another box soon.

I find this coffee a little bit too mild for me. Perhaps others will like it fine. I haven't had any of the problems with coffee grounds that others have mentioned. OK, so my review wasn't looooong enough so I'll add this last sentence for no real reason.

This coffee isn't anything special.  I would compare it to Timothy's Breakfast Blend.  But I purchased it for about 55.5 cents per cup, and for that price, this is good coffee.  If you're looking to save money, this is a solid choice.

column9: close as a k-cup will get to a Starbucks
column10: Strong with a lot of personality and flavor. This is as close as a k-cup will get to a Starbucks cup of coffee. 30% cheaper than regular k-cups makes this an easy choice.

column9: I guess I am in the minority
column10: I preordered this item in March. I was on vacation when it arrived so it took awhile for me to use the first one. I ordered the Donut Shop, a decaf and Fuhgeddaboudit. I will say the donut shop was a disappointment, but i LOVEEE fugeddaboudit. I normally use either starbucks or newman''s and the flavor is so rich with brooklyn bean. I just happened to stumble upon the review and I am surprised at the negative ones. ( at least for this flavor)

This coffee is.. well.. THE BEANS!We received a sampler pack from this Brooklyn Bean, and were amazed with the quality, taste and overall service from this company!Our first sample pack never made it to us.. But they were awesome enough to SPEEDILY send us another one within a few DAYS!My husband is a "STRONG" guy- who likes his coffee straight up.. Dark, rich and all alone (no creamer or sugars.. just black!). He enjoyed the darker blends.While myself, Am a light & sweet kind of gal, and the milder blends provided a great flavor that complimented my french vanilla creamer perfectly!Overall, we LOVED our box, and are quickly running low! Thank goodness we have Amazon Prime, and can order this in a jiff when we order again!This is certainly going to overtake our kcup storage rack now!STRONGLY RECOMMEND!! :)

I recently tried this coffee after winning a sampler pack from their facebook page. Breakfast blend was the 1st that I tried and it was by far my favorite! Would definately recommend them to anyone and I love the company itself as well. They are a great customer based company!

I shared the sample pack with my tam mates at work.  I heard nothing but great comments from everyone.  We did not have any failures with the product and I consider it one that we will put into purchase rotation not only here in the office, but at home as well!  Keep up the delicious work!

Brooklyn Bean Roastery coffee is delicious and energizing; not only do my parents always ask for a cup when I pull the k-cups out of the cabinet, but my siblings do too! It appeals to both young and old with its delicious blend of flavor and assortment.

My friend recieved a box of free sample brooklyn bean coffee,she wanted me to try it so she brought me over a couple k-cups.I gotta say it was soooo good,she likes the dark roast,I like the medium roast(it was all good though).I would recommend this coffee to all my friends,and I pretty much drink coffee day and night.Thanks Brooklyn Bean Roastery

I have tried all of the Medium Roast K-cups as I am not a big fan of the Dark and/or Bold Roasts. I really enjoyed all of the ones that I tried. I had 1 that exploded, but it was not too bad, I caught it right away and got it cleaned up. I look forward to trying the flavored varieties one day. Thank you Brooklyn Bean!

if you like a good dark coffee like I do, brooklyn bean roastery, cyclone is a product for you! all of the companies coffees are delicious, but this 1 is tops in my book for dark, bold blend! I have even asked my grocery store to start carrying it! not 1 problem with exploding cups!

Brooklyn Bean Roastery Coffee, Brooklyn Bridge Blend, Single Serve Cup for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, 36-Count  ALL of Brooklyns coffee is the best i have ever had i tried samples of it and ended up buying a box of 36 they are far better then any other k cup makers i have tried and i have tried alot i am coffee aholic i recommend them to everyone

column9: Great tasting coffee with a few grounds.
column10: To be honest, I had never heard of this brand till I won a contest and they sent me a free sample box to try and was shocked when I received a box of 16 cups. Great start to a sample pack and of course I had to dive right in and start testing the different flavors. Every single one I have tried except the french roast (not my style) was great. They all had full body flavor and a great taste. The only downfall I would say is that I ending up getting coffee grounds in most the cups which is why I only gave 4 stars but if that was fixed it would be a 5 star product. As someone else mentioned that they seem to brew slower than normal, it was a great experience (minus the grinds). Thank you Brooklyn Roasters!

column9: great product and happy to support it
column10: We use this coffee at work and I like it better than almost all the other brands. It works well, tastes good. Packaging is fun. Plus I'm happy to support a small company and encourage others to do the same!Rebecca
I usually don't drink dark coffee, or write reviews for it. This coffee has so much flavor without the bitterness (i do use half & half with sugar). I really enjoyed it, and was surprised!

I am on auto ship and my 2nd box sb arriving soon.  No problems with the first box and the taste is pretty good on these.  They must have worked out their initial issues as my kcups all worked flawlessly.

I was very pleased with this coffee, cyclone was a full bodied coffee, but not bitter. I had no pod issues like some posted with any of the pods I received .The coffe was very tasty and I would definitely buy again. I have not had one I haven't liked yet and I've tried several flavors

column9: Really clean flavor - delicious hot or cold.
column10: I won a sampler pack from a Brooklyn Bean Rostery promotion. Having never heard of them but being a gourmet coffee lover, I was delighted to try them. The flavor of the cyclone is intense. So carmelly (is that a word?) and very rich. I loved it! Perfect with a light pastry in the morning.The breakfast blend was super good both hot and cold. I brewed a standard hot cup on my keurig and poured it over ice with a little creamer. It was absolutely delicious.I'm not quite done the pack but am definitely impressed! These aren't your typical bitter starbucks or overpriced Gloria Jeans. The best compairson I have found are the Emeril K-cups, and although being in the Delta I'm a fan of rich chicory coffee (the only thing I can find missing from the BBR selection) these are a better every day blend.Happy drinking! :)

To be honest, I ordered this because of the price, but I have to say we haven't had any really bad experiences.  We've gone through two 36 packs at this point, and once or twice there's been some grounds in the brew - a slightly better record than Gloria Jeans'.  No sign of off-popping lids or anything like that.Flavor-wise it's a good medium roast that doesn't taste watery on the high setting.  I think it's better than anything of Gloria Jeans, and compares favorably to those 'morning blend' sorts of things you get from Green Mountain or Newman's Own.  I just wish they offered a hazelnut blend.Update July 30 -At this point I should probably raise my rating to five (or even six) stars - you just can't beat the quality of these K-cups at the current price point, which is incredible.  If Brooklyn Bean DOES bring in a hazelnut blend I'll HAVE to go up a star - though my tastebuds still yearn for the IMHO now wildly overpriced Van Houtten blends...Anyway, we've now tried the Corner Donut Shop, Boardwalk Blend, and Colombian K-cups with nary an exploding pod.  Irritatingly my wife preferred the Boardwalk blend, which is now discontinued, but the other two have been just as good as their Green Mountain, Newman's, or Timothy's equivalent, and are a much better brew than those San Francisco Bay pods which are weak on the high setting.  I've tried A LOT of the different brands out there - some are pretty good, but at this time you can't beat Brooklyn's price/quality ratio.Update August 25 -I sometimes have to revise my reviews, so here we go: I still like this stuff and will continue my subscriptions - but we HAVE had a couple problems.  I DO mean a couple - we have had two pods bleed grounds heavily, and one sort of jammed somehow - hot water backed up in the pod, only a half-cup poured through, and when I took out the pod I was almost scalded.  However we've gone through half-a-dozen boxes of Boardwalk, Donut Shop, and Colombian, so I'd say the odds are pretty good.  There's still no sign of any "exploding pods."
This is one of my favorite Keurig cup flavors, I first tried it at a Co-workers house and I had to get some!
I think this coffee tastes great and would buy it again. Next time I will try a different blend. I especially enjoy supporting a local company.

I am really enjoying this coffee. It tastes excellent, was nicely priced and the company has gone out of their way to provide excellent customer service after some initial problems.I am going to get this monthly on subscribe and save and I do recommend it now. the brooklyn bridge and breakfast blend are very nice!

I just got a Keurig and was browsing through the endless options of kcups when I found this fun brand, Brooklyn Bean Roastery! I actually tried these on a whim because the brand name and images were so appealing. Thank goodness I did! I love the donut shop kcups! They are perfect for my morning coffee, full of flavor with out being too strong.I highly recommend you give this one a try! I can't wait to try some of their other kcup choices too.

Let me preface this review by saying I drink iced coffee on the "4" setting of my cuisanart.  I liked this coffees flavor and the aroma a lot! It had my whole kitchen scented delicious (which is rare with a k cup and is one of the only things I miss about more traditional brewing).  The only down fall was that there was loose grinds in the packaging and they seemed to leak a little during brewing.  Maybe I am not as picky as others, but the flavor & cost far outweighed that small leakage.

I frequently drink the Nantucket blend, and thought I would give the Brooklyn Bridge Blend a try, based on favorable comparisons. While the price is better, the quality is not. I found that I could only use the medium cup size on my machine or the coffee was too weak for my liking. This was not a problem with the Nantucket blend, so simply based on serving size, the savings go out the window.The flavor (for a medium size) is good and it compares favorably with Nantucket and some other blends I have tried. However, as a number of other reviewers have noted, the cup brews VERY slowly, and in fact, my machine stops about 50% of the time and pauses for up to a minute before the cycle resumes. Additionally, I get grounds in my cup about 50% of the time, from just a few to "pour the cup out and try again". Nothing explosive like one of your reviewers, thank goodness.Because of the inconsistency, it is, as I said, like going to Vegas. It was worth a try, but I will not buy this brand again.
I bought this to try since it was new - or at least I had never heard of it.  it has become my favorite. there is no bitter aftertaste that many of the coffees have.  i really like it!

I have to admit, being from Little-Italy New York, I originally bought it for the name "Fuhgeddaboutit" only to find that it's a great coffee.If you like strong coffee (like I do) this is for you. Taste great and a good morning "wake-up".

column9: Excellent coffee at a reasonable price
column10: I have tried the Columbian k-cup and must say it is the best I have found to date, I have owned my Keurig brewer for about 1 yr and have found Brooklyn Bean coffees to have good verity and reasonable price. Customer service is excellent.

column9: very weak coffee was extremely disappointed
column10: The name of this Kcup sounds better than it tastes.  I had contacted the company and told them that the coffee was not strong enough and tasted like colored water. would not buy again

While the taste of this coffee is good, for some reason, it tends to clog in the brewing process.  I've used it in 3 different brewers with the same problem.  To prevent this problem, the K-cup has to be shaken immediately prior to brewing.  Perhaps the coffee is ground too fine and is getting packed down as the water is being pressed through the K-cup.  I probably wouldn't buy this brand again.

This coffee I would not purchase again.  It just did not tickle my taste buds.  It had a flavor and strength I did not find to my liking.  I am very fickled when it comes to my morning coffee, and this one just did not do it for me.

column9: 3.0 out of 5 stars I am a Starbucks extra Bold Roast kind of girl, so keep that in mind
column10: I am reviewing all the flavours in my variety pack in the hopes of finding one I like.  I am pretty picky on coffee, and k cups, so you may notice my reviews are similar (mainly because I am doing the exact same thing to each cup, in the hopes of finding one that is similar and cheaper to what I usually like.I made Fuggedaboutdit,  as I usually make my K-cups (I drink Van Houtte Eclipse almost every morning) and used a 6 ounce cup of water. I don't use sugar and do use coffee cream.It smelled good, but when I poured cream in, went super white almost immediately, which usually means the k cup is not going to be a strong enough taste for me.  I did not pour it out, but still feel like I have not had a cup of coffee yet today. Too weak for me on six ounce setting.My 16 year old son made Cyclone and he liked it but he told me I would not.Maple sleigh- i dont normally like flavoured coffee, but the flavour was alright.  Same problem with the coffee being too weak, even on a 6 ounce setting.That said, I am sure someone who is not as into very strong coffee as me, will like it. It's not bad, or anything, its just I am a Starbucks extra bold kind of girl, so remember that when you read my reviews. Interesting though that two of my favourite K cups (other than double black diamond) are Caribou regular (I don't like the mahogany which is supposed to be stronger tasting) and the Eclipse, both of which are sort of medium smooth coffees. Looking forward to trying and reviewing some more.  I did not buy the cups on Amazon, but have started reviewing things on Amazon, whether I buy them here or not.  Its not like you can try things in an online store, and I am a very regular amazon.com and .ca customer for other items, so I am motivated to review things so as not to be disappointed when I am shopping.  The more of us who do this review thing on all products, the better.

I have no idea how they taste as the first 3 exploded.  What a mess to clean up.  I phoned Amazon immediately and they were wonderful. They refunded my money and I threw the kcups away. I don't even want to try these things again as I don't need the mess to clean up. If I  wanted the mess, I would use the my kcup which doesn't ooze the grounds all over the place but you have to  deal with the grounds in the dispenser. I can't believe they  are still selling these things without perfecting them.  btw, I had the decaf if that helps anyone.

I've tried a few different varieties of the Brooklyn Bean Roasts and so far have been happy with all of them - I got them at a great Subscribe and Save price, but it looks like it's no longer offered as a S&S item.  Still a good product at a good price though

I have tried a few kinds of coffee by this maker through variety boxes.  I just don't like it as much as I like other brands.  I tend to like a starbucks, caribou etc so maybe these just aren't strong enough for me

we loved the taste of this blend and the price was very reasonable. The only problem was that about 1 in 5 kcups leaked grounds when using. They also raised the price about 4 dollars a box recently which makes it about the same, as better known brands

This coffee is very good, the first couple of cups brewed fine. Some of these k-cups the inside paper filter does not touch the bottom so when put into the brewer the paper filter is not punctured and the water can not pass thru it fast enough and it overflows. Tested other brands of k-cups and they work fine so it is not my machine.
I had hoped this would compare to Starbucks Pike's Roast; however we couldn't drink it and neither could several friends we gave it to.

column9: Bad K cups - Leaves grounds in coffee - everyone bad
column10: Bad K cups - Leaves grounds in coffee - everyone bad and had to throw them away. Will not buy this item again.

This is a good tasting medium roast coffee.  However, we have had trouble with grounds coming out of the cup during brewing. Thus creating a cup of coffee with grounds floating on the top.  Not my idea of a fresh brewed cup of coffee.  It happens randomly, not every cup.  I'm not sure what the problem is. It seems like some of the cups are not sealed properly or something.  We do not have this problem with other brands using the same brewer.

I want to like these k-cups.  Although the flavor is a little on the weak side, I enjoy it.  What I didn't enjoy was the grinds ending up in the cup.  There is something off with the foil on the top of the cups.  A lot of the cups already had grinds on them when I opened the box.  It seemed that I ended up with grinds in the majority of the cups I brewed.  Would like to order again, but not if I have to deal with the same issues.

I was hoping for more from this company, someone to take on behemoth GMCR. The coffee is weaker than most GMCR blends and the taste is average. It's not terrble,  but not a wonderful experience like Barista Italian roast, detrich's french roast or Caribou blend. I also got their French roast to compare and again it was average and weaker. I had to go 2oz less to get the consistency of both the same. It is cheaper, but for 14 cents more I can  get a great cup of coffee. I found that these are not quite what I am looking for, but are great for company who doesn't expect too much but likes a good cup of coffee. I still want to try Fogetaboutit and see how it compares.

I am rather torn about these K-Cups. The taste of the coffee is very good; actually one of my favorites. (Even better than Dunkin Donuts, which has always been my go-to coffee). That being said, as has been pointed out before, the quality of the physical k-cups is lacking.When I first opened the box there were coffee grounds everywhere. Upon looking closer, I noticed that the foil tops of two of the cups were not aligned with the plastic bottom and so there was an open slot for the coffee to come out. After rinsing the k-cups off and brewing some though, I discovered that it actually tasted really good; though there seems to always be coffee grounds at the bottom of my cup.To be honest, I still dont know if I will be ordering these again or not; on one hand they taste really good, but on the other its very frustrating to have had the cups break open before they even get to me, and depending on how many are broken it slowly drives up the price per cup.Update: 8/16/12This is really a great company that cares about the quality of their product. After the bad first batch, and being contacted by a company representative, I received samples that brewed perfectly and tasted delicious. Will definitely buy this brand again!

I tried this coffee because the price simply can not be beat.  We are not coffee experts by any means but we love a good solid brew.  The coffee has the right balance of strength with a mellow aftertone.  The only thing that I have found less than stellar is the exploding cups.  In a batch of 36 we've had 9 explode on us.  When you look at the cost per cup that's coffee that is lost plus the time spent having to thoroughly clean the machine.  Hopefully the exploding cup issue has been resolved.

I purchased these kcups to use with my Cuisinart Keurig maker.  While the product tastes good, it repeatedly causes brewing problems with the cuisinart, either stopping its function completely or causing it to overflow.  Would not recommend for use with Cuisinart makers.

column9: Less than satisfactory.  I gave the Brooklyn K-Cups away as a gift.  I will not buy this particular brand again.
column10: Brooklyn "French Roast" K-Cup Coffee is not one of my favorites. It's not awful.  It's okay if you're in a "pinch" and it's the only pod you have.  I ended up giving my entire box to a friend.  I wasn't a fan.  There was nothing special or memorable about the taste.  I won't buy it again and I won't recommend it.

I have to say that I have tried 3 varieties of Brooklyn Beans coffees, and I love all the flavors that I have tried.  That being said, now the negative, I hate grounds in my coffee.  All the varieties seem to leave more grounds in the cup than the Green Mountain cups, the decaf experience was extremely bad. I will not buy more decaf until I am confident the manufacturing issues have been fixed.  I purchased a box of the decaf cups from Amazon on 5/14/12.  I am not a frequent drinker of decaf and have not had more than a couple of cups before this weekend, when I brewed 2 of the decaf.  One clogged in my machine producing only a half cup of undrinkable coffee, a mess in my machine and on the counter.  The second one produced a cup with many grounds, and had to be strained before drinking.  Please fix the manufacturing Brooklyn Beans!Brooklyn Light Roast Bean Roastery Decaffeinated Coffee, Breakfast Blend, Single Serve Cup for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, 36-Count

column9: 2 Stars for good taste when it works
column10: I am disappointed in this product.  After reading the reviews about the pods not working and the followups from the company saying the problem was fixed I thought we'd give them a try.  Guess what, 1 out of 4 of our k-cups didn't work.  Either they pop or they leak which both make a mess.  When they work they taste good but the faulty cups and the mess take away all the savings.  Buy at your own risk.

The coffee has good taste but the kcups are defective. Over half will not puncture bottom hole due to collapse of holder or they puncture the filter inside and you get grounds in the coffee cup. Fix this problem and they would be fine..

We really like the flavor of this coffee. The only problem is that a few of the K-cups have been defective; allowing a bunch of grounds to get down into the cup. This ruins the cup and at $.60+ per cup is a bit annoying. They should have better quality control. It seems like the filter inside the cup gives way.

Despite several reviews that said these K-cups sometimes explode we decided to purchase them anyway. The coffee is delicious there's no doubt about that, but you can only have a cup of coffee when there is actually coffee inside the k-cup. We've had a few that were completely empty. Just foil lid over plastic cup, that's it. Great coffee, but apparently poor quality control.

Good flavor but they still have not solved their packaging problem.  I would say that 15 to 20% of the cups leak and leave a lot of grounds in the cup. If they would solve this problem the flavor and value would easily top 4 stars.

column9: Not as bad as some reviews.
column10: I tried a box of 36 and found the coffee to be pretty good and well worth the price.  However, I also experienced a problem with 4 of the K-Cups.  They didn't explode but they did leak grounds into the cup.  I will probably wait to see if they can really solve their quality problems before I even think of ordering again.
I am disappointed in this product.  I love the taste of the coffee but the issue with grounds coming out and blocking the water flow has made the product unusable.
Coffee blend is fairly good. However three empty K cups out of 36 is pathetic. K cups are too pricey for this kind of nonsense.

I was hesitant to purchase this product, based on other reviews addressing issues with a manufacturer defect; however, I placed the order anyway and was very disappointed to find that several of the k-cups caused a very nasty, gritty substance to come out of the k-cup when making coffee. I had to use four k-cups before I was able to finally get an actual cup of coffee. Once I finally was able to make a true cup of coffee, the taste was pretty good (why I am giving two stars versus one star). I must've gotten an older batch of the k-cups because they apparently explode in the keurig machine if the top of the k-cup is flat instead of bubbled. I had to throw away over half of my package and needless to say, I will not be wasting my hard-earned money on these k-cups in the future. It's a shame, because for the price and the taste, it seemed like a good deal. It was very inconvenient to have to clean my keurig machine after the k-cups exploded. I have ordered other name brand k-cups (I.e. donut shop, green mountain, Gloria jeans, timothy's, etc) and I've never had an issue with their k-cups exploding in my keurig machine. I thought their manufacturing defect was resolved, but appartently it has not been resolved.

column9: Taste= Great, Stability= Not so much
column10: I held off on ordering this product due to some of the manufacturing problems they had. Seems i should have waited a little bit longer.I order the Cyclone because i like a strong coffee but not so strong that you cannot taste the flavor. The product was dead on when it came to flavor. taste, great strength, really made a great cup of coffee, but then the astounding packaging failure.Went to make a cup last night and walked away. All of a sudden i was smelling the wonderful aroma throughout my living room. My thought was 'Man this is a great smelling cup of coffee." it never occurred to me that i normally cannot smell my coffee brewing that far away. Then i went to get my cup and noticed that the coffee was all over my counter. Seems the foil top had a severe malfunction and spewed coffee all over the place.So in review, Great cup of coffee when it works, I hope they get the manufacturing problems fixed because this is something i would love to try again.

column9: Things just seem wrong about it
column10: With Black Tiger off the "subscribe and save" program (and its recent huge price increase) I was looking for a replacement and tried the Cyclone blend.  I wanted to like it, but couldn't.  I have a B70. It takes considerably longer to brew (I haven't had any leakage problems though).  There are grounds in the coffee and the flavor seems "papery" The strength does seem good and comparable to Black Tiger.

column9: The first one I tried leaked spectacularily ~!
column10: I ordered 72 Cyclone and Fuhgeddaboudit K cups . I had read the reviews about leaking K cups and read the manufacturer's response that this issue was resolved .  On that I assumption I placed my order and received them today (June 05/12) . I was really annoyed that the first one I tried leaked all over the place. Once I got one to work, I found I really enjoyed the coffee. I am unsure if I will order these again. I guess I will wait and see how many duds I get out of box ~!

UPDATE 6/18/2012 THE ORIGINAL PACKAGING DESIGN HAS INDEED BEEN FIXED.  I Highly recommend their coffees. No more "Coffee Shop" brand for me...ONLY Brooklyn Roastery Brands.Like others have mentioned here coffee is quite good....WHEN THE K CUPS Work.  I have a box of 30 recieved the end of May ...so far 50 % of the Kcups either clogged up my Keurig, or shot out coffee all over the counter-top or give you a cup of coffee grinds. When you put one of these KCups in the machine..it may or may not work. Very poor packaging standards.

All of these K-cups had defective tops.  When I tried to use them the blew out and coffee went everywhere except into my cup.  What a mess!  Since food items cannot be returned, Amazon was kind enough to refund my money.  Greatly appreciated...

While the coffee is at least under the $.50 a cup barrier ( with subscribe and save ) it pretty well failed in its comparison to Green Mountain's Dark Magic. First off , when the box arrived and was opened coffee grounds spilled all over the table. Upon inspection , 5 of the k cups had faulty foil and had come off in the box. The box itself was not damaged in any way and was packaged well by Amazon so I'm not sure what type of quality control goes into the product. Anyway , i figured if it at least measured up taste wise like it said I probably would have given them another try. Unfortunately , the taste was not even close!! While its not necessarily a bad cup of coffee , it compares more to the Folgers Columbian k-cups my wife drinks. It tastes more of a medium roast and is not very strong . In my opinion , it would make an ok secondary cup once you have had your morning powerhouse to get you started , it just didn't measure up to its claims of Dark Magic comparison or its quality control on its products.

Being born and bred in Brooklyn but now living upstate NY, of course we had to try this product.  Short and sweet, the coffee is good but the packaging is horrible, every two to three cups comes loaded with grinds.  Don't plan to order again.  Gave two stars only because few cups without the grinds were good.  We now put a tea strainer on the cup when brewing.PM - just heard from a friend who also ordered coffee a short time after we did.  I had written to see if they had any problems and they did not so I felt I needed to be fair and come back to edit my post to include their comment.  We both agree, however, that the coffee is good.6/11/12:  I know I am not the only only customer who had communication with Brooklyn Bean Roastery and I admire the fact that in true Brooklyn style, they stepped up, admitted there was a problem then made good and ensured it was corrected.  However, I am rewriting this review based ON THE COFFEE not the fact that the manufacturer replaced my original order and included some samples of the other blends.  As I said in my original review, the coffee was good without the grinds, now not having to deal with straining the coffee, we are truly enjoying it and have decided to replace our usual breakfast blend with BBR's Breakfast Blend.  We have been very pleased with all the samplers tasted.  Thank you for for giving us the opportunity to change our minds and truly enjoy the coffee.  BBR Rocks!

so far have used 12 of these k cups for making coffee, 3 of the cups the grinds shot out of the cup all over the machine, seems to be a manufacturing quality control issue. the coffee doesn't drain out of the bottom, but shoots back out of the top. the other 9 k cups worked as designed.

We tried this coffee and enjoyed the taste, bold. However the filter in the k-cup does not work at least half the time.  About half of the cups I have used emptied the coffee grounds into the cup of coffee instead of staying in the k-cup.  Really not what you want first thing in the morning.

When you put these cups in the Kuerig the plastic is so flimsy instead of piercing a hole in the bottom to drain the coffee, the plastic is bent. So the water goes into the k-cup overflows out into your coffee cup, coffee grounds and all. I've tried to pierce a hole myself to no avail. I Wasted $17!!!! Don't waste YOUR money.
these are horrible! there are always grounds in the bottom, it doesn't fill the cup, horrible packaging and inconsistent performance! DO NOT BUY!

[Update: Brooklyn Beans sent me a new box - as you can see in the comments below. 1 out of 24 cups was not sealed. I have now learned to squeeze the k-cup just slightly to see if the foil lid responds to the light pressure. If it bulges just a little, the lid is good. If it is loose, I pull the lid off and brew it in My K-Cup coffee filter so at least the coffee is not wasted. The coffee is very good. My favorite was Brooklyn Bridge Blend. But all of it was fresh and tasty. ]7 out of 36 cups are not sealed. I do not think the box was compressed in shipping causing some of the cups to burst. No cups were crunched. The BB box looks fine - undented. It was inside an Amazon box which also looked fine - all still-puffy airpillows inside. There was loose coffee in both boxes and coffee dust on  the k-cups and airpillows.The k-cups that have a good lid  look roughly made to me. The logo printing doesn't line up with the top of the cups. The edges of the foil is rough. Where the foil is sealed on the cup the foil feels bumpy... like loose coffee was not cleaned off the cup before the foil was applied.I haven't made any coffee yet. I will up date this review when I do tomorrow morning... but right now, already 7 cups down, I am not impressed.I rarely write bad reviews, but I do not want anyone else to be disappointed like I am right now.

We wanted a treat for our Coton de Tulear that was good nutritionally and healthy at the same time...Vitality Chicken Breast strips definitely is all that and more. These 100% cage-free real chicken breast treats contain no by-products, hormones, antibiotics, BHA/BHT, fillers or artificial flavors and are high in protein and low in fat so you can be sure you are giving your dog a healthy, digestible treat.

I stopped buying this product after I realized it was made in china. My jack russel threw up a few times and I couldn't figure out why until I read the government warning about made in china chicken jerkey. I would warn anyone to stay away from this.
My dog cant get enuff of these. I stored 3 packs in my garage and a mouse got into one bag..it ate them all! store in a closet in ur kitchen or in a sealed metal can lol

This sauce was incredible. Like, I loved the way it tasted on my shrimp, and I can't stop adding it to my seafood. It's citrusy, slightly tangy, and just sweet enough to make the flavor pop. I suggest it!

I guess it depends on your taste! I happen to like potato based soups. I think it's great. I prefer it over the "no salt added" version. Dont care too much for the other Health Valley soups. If you dont know if you'll like it, buy one can at the supermarktet before getting the entire pack.

My son has allergies to milk, wheat, peanuts, almonds.  I have allergies to soy.  This is a great soup for the both of us.  I cook up some potatoes to make the soup last longer.  We do like the taste.  I appreciate the convenience.  Since we are limited on what we can eat, I appreciate this Health Valley Organic option, and the price of 12 cans for $28.98 plus the 15% off with Subscribe & Save makes it even better.  Only once I got these cans for 10 cents less, but that was in February 2009 during a sale on this item plus the once-monthly additional 10% off for customers at the local health food store.

Okay, I have tried several of this company's products and they are fair.  However, this one was shockingly bad.  The flavor was not just bland.  It was repulsive.  It was disturbing to imagine this is something people actually enjoy. I have given up on it.  I have decided to not eat the other cans.  I cannot in good faith give it to others.
It's tastes great and is made without eggs.  This is very helpful for anyone with an allergy to eggs and unable to eat mayo.

I have had major problems finding this salad dressing in any local markets in my area and was going to give up till I thought of Amazon as a source.  Boy am I glad I did.  It's really easy to order and it comes right to my door.  The price is reasonable as well.

This is my favorite dressing ever...unfortunately, I cannot find it anywhere in Massachusetts! I fell in love with it where I grew up, in Indiana, and was very upset when I couldn't find it out here. I was thrilled to be able to buy it on Amazon! Unfortunately, the expiration date on the bottles did not go far enough to get me through all 6 bottles. It is amazing on taco salads :)

column9: Best Dressing You Can't Find at Your Local Grocery Store
column10: I rediscovered this wonderful dressing in Ohio while visiting relatives.  I haven't been able to find it in a store anywhere else, so I went in with a coworker to buy a six pack.  Another coworker tried it, and now she wants to go in with us when we buy more!  It has a wonderful cucumber essence without overpowering the ranch dressing.
I was so happy to final get my Cucumber dressing.  The stores in our area use to carry it and then just stop.Now if could just fine Sugar Free Tang that would be great.
If you like your soup hot and spicy this is the soup for you then!!! Also there are plenty of noodles!!! Not much of a lobster taste but soup really clears thr Sinuses!!!!!!

I'm in Iraq and I get super tired of making chow hall funs just to get crappy food. I ordered these because I really wanted to try them and share them with others at my site. They came in the nick of time and are sooooo yummy - just the right spice and fills me up in one trip.

This ramen reminded me of the Nong Shim Seafood ramen somewhat. It's not to spicy and the seaweed does not dominate like it does in the nong shim seafood ramen. The cup is larger than a typical ramen bowl and is plenty for an entire meal. I'm not sure if it is just me..but i really didn't taste any "Lobster" flavor. All in all its a good ramen that is not too overbearing.

column9: Love, love, love them!  These are the best!
column10: I've switched awhile back to kamut and spelt grains,,,,with all my food allergy problems, I thought it was a good idea,  Plus, I like them,,,,,,as well if not better than wheat and corn anyway,  So I was thrilled to discover the Suzie line of products,,,are so good,  Healthy and yummy,  I've been purchasing the kamut puffed cakes by the case for awhile now,  But yesterday I got in my first case of the spelt,,,and I like them better than the kamut, much to my surprise, They have a little more flavor,,,,are a little more filling and more substantial,  I love them,,,,,,now I wish I hadn't just purchased TWO cases of the kamut,,,,,instead had purchased the spelt,,but I will polish off all of them in time,  Since it is advised to rotate your foods when you have allergies what I am doing is pairing these up with one of my numerous kinds of nut butter,,,,and it's a terrific, healthy protein meal,

These are pretty good. They are whole-grain spelt and are fairly low-carb so they can help you lose some weight and they have helped me. Kind of crunchy when you need something like that. I'm glad I found them.

I recently started eating these and the kamut ones since my bread company went out of business. Pacific Bakery. I need single grain foods, plain due to allergies and a rotational plan to reduce more allergies. This is perfect as it is just organic spelt and sea salt.I did suggest to the company they seal the packages better.Much better price than buying at Whole Foods. They are fairly far from me.Would be nice to buy a partial case.

column9: Biscotti - who would have ever thought they could be HEALTHY!
column10: Wow - I thought I was eating a good old fashioned italian biscuit - packed with Almonds, sweet - DELISCIOUS! Then I realized - I was also getting all that extra protein and nowhere near as many calories or carbs! What a find! The holidays weren't that bad for my diet after all! Great job!

column9: progressive nutirition with actual focus on pet health
column10: I read a book once written by a cardiologist and nutritionist. It was on pet nutirition. In it they describe the best pet food ingredients and the ones to avoid. This product almost line for line includes the foods these authors recommend for high nutritional value.Love the no carb concept. With this food the aging, low energy, small breed dog I have went from pudgy to a proper weight effortlessly.

We were curious to try this salt based upon an article we read in a health magazine. The "rotten eggs" smell was, of course, a concern, but we opted to try it anyway.Let it be known that the smell is exactly as described, as well as the taste when sample straight out of the packaging. However, once added to a dish and cooked (even sprinkled on veggies), the sulfur-like aroma and flavor changes into a subtle and interesting result for your palate.At first, I thought this might be one of those seasonings only for special dishes..but we tried it on some basics (other than adding to veggies). We added it to a crack-peppered hummus...and it rocks!Experiment and you'll find that it is an eggcellent salt!

I bought this salt because i heard it was the secret ingredient for making a Tofu Scramble. Boy were they right! The slightly sulfurous taste/smell of this salt really made our scrambled Tofu taste just like eggs. It's in a powdered form, so it distributed evenly amongst the Tofu. I am very pleased with this product.
Perfect for tofu scramble or eggless egg salads. The product is as good as company claims, reasonably priced and user friendly zip bag containers and fast delivery.
GREAT SALT AND IS HEALTHY IF USED IN CORRECT QUANTITYS.  IT'S THE ONLY SALT WE USE.

I ordered this because my girlfriend and I enjoy trying unusual foods. Based on everything I'd read, I expected a strong, unpleasant smell and very sulfurous taste. I was pleasantly surprised when I dipped a finger in the salt and tasted a rich, creamy egg in my mouth! We tried this on sauteed green peppers with balsamic vinegar, and it was absolutely delicious. I would recommend putting it on any savory dish. I couldn't be happier with the purchase.

This stuff really makes a difference to any tofu "egg" dish. My family actually prefers scrambled tofu and tofu based "egg-salad" over the same made with real eggs, however, the black salt steps it up a notch. It definitely gives the tofu a more egg like flavor. I have never used this product for anything else before, however, in a vegan kitchen, I think it's a must have for anything "eggy".

The smell is awful, but this salt works wonders in a myriad of dishes. Sprinkle some of this on your tofu and you will never miss eating eggs. Add a bit to various Indian dishes and other spices and you have a party going on in your mouth! By far buying this was cheaper than other black salts I have seen on Amazon. You actually get more for your money with this one. Packaging is secure and it reseals without having to transfer it to another container. Glad to have finally made this purchase.

Ujinotsuyu's genmaicha is one of my favorite packaged teas. It has a rich, strong, and full taste. Delicious, warming, nourishing tea for a chilly day. This product is a bagged mixture of green tea and little bits of toasted rice. When brewed, you get tea that has a sort of cozy, toasty, nutty flavor to it. It's really pleasant to sip on a blustery autumn day! Some tips: green tea is more delicate than black, so use water that is slightly cooled from boiling--not at boiling temperature--as you would with an herbal tea. Also, this tea, IMHO, is best left unsweetened; the sugar would mask the delicate green tea flavor and the nuttiness of the toasted rice. Brew it for about 3-5 minutes, although (unlike with black tea) you won't end up with an undrinkably bitter brew if left in longer.Also, as noted before--this is tea, NOT soup. The rice is enclosed in the bag with the tea leaves. It lends flavor, not substance.

These pine nuts are a product of China.  Had I known that I would NOT have purchased them.Why?  These Chinese pine nuts leave a distinctive and extremely unpleasant metallic flavor on the tongue which lasts for as long as two weeks depending on how many are eaten.Being a raw foodie, I use a lot of pine nuts in my raw food preparation, so it didn't take long for me to isolate the food which was causing the terrible, disagreeable reaction on my palate.  The nuts are expensive and I thought I was getting a good value with Azar but as it turns out, since the Azar Chinese pine nuts are not edible for me, they were a tremendous waste.Perhaps not every body will have the same reaction as I but I thought I must still flag a warning about Chinese pine nuts.I should add finally that I do NOT have any problems with domestic pine nuts or Italian pignolias and I much prefer them, especially if they are organically grown.  The flavor of USA and Italian grown pinenuts is far superior.  The metallic issue seems to come up with Chinese pine nuts only.

"Pignolia" generally refers to pine nuts from the Stone Pine.  The nuts from this tree are superior in their taste and health benefits to other pine nuts.  The packaging here seems intended to make the buyer think they're getting Italian Stone Pine nuts, but they're not; they're Chinese pine nuts, which tend to be blander in taste and to have fewer health benefits.

column9: Yummy for GF if you modify it a bit
column10: I usually let the noodles cook a bit longer, since rice noodles can be kind of tough.  I add the two tablespoons of butter (or a bit more), a smidgen more than 1/4 cup milk, and about a 1/2 to 3/4 cup of shredded cheddar cheese.  I put some salt and pepper on it and it is much better than the original mix and takes about the same amount of time.I like the idea of adding a bit of spice to it as well and will try that next time.This cannot be compared to the Kraft mix (and I loved that as much as anybody), but if you have to eat gluten free, this is a good substitute when you add some more flavor to it.

column9: Annie's makes GREAT gluten free mac & cheese
column10: I have reviewed several gluten free products and this is the best gluten free mac & cheese I have found.  I found this at my local health food store, about the only place I shop now that I have to eat gluten free, and loved it.  When I saw it on Amazon by the case (and $10 off to boot) I was excited.  Annie's also makes frozen, microwaveable mac & cheese that is *very* good...it really just depends on whether you are used to the frozen/baked kind or the kind out of a box.  It seems that Annie's makes a great line of products and I would try any of them.Great product and I appreciate Amazon stocking quality, good tasting gluten free items like this.

column9: Getting to enjoy a childhood favourite...despite the adult allergy!
column10: At 33, I was hit with a sudden-onset (over the course of a month) wheat intolerance. I've always loved good food, have become an accomplished cook, and mostly cook from scratch. But...good ol' Kraft Mac & Cheese has been a childhood favourite that I've never stopped loving. When the wheat intolerance came along, I thought I'd never get to enjoy my occasional Mac fix again, but then I stumbled across this! It's received some criticism in other reviews here, but my guess they come mostly from people who don't have to eat wheat-free and either (a) aren't used to the slightly different flavour of the foods or (b) don't know how to prepare these foods properly (ie the cooking times/what to look for when preparing rice pasta), with the necessary tweaking. I thought this was delicious, worked well without a lot of doctoring, and was as close to my childhood favourite as I ever thought I'd get again. If you're like me, & thought you'd never get to enjoy that old Mac & Cheese standby, you'll love this!

I don't have a gluten intolerance - just trying to cut back on the intake of wheat/gluten...and sugar, but that's another story;) so my body feels less bloated, unhealthy and lethargic due to wheat.  With that said, I do know the differences in taste between wheat pastas, rice, quinoa, corn...etc.  Personally, I have come to love the taste of non-wheat pastas over wheat, with the exception of corn flour, which isn't similar enough to wheat to fool my taste buds.  Annie's does a fantastic job with this rice flour product, giving it a consistency and flavor akin to Kraft mac and cheese.  What makes this better is the cheese, which tastes far yummier than any boxed mac & cheese I have ever had.  Also, it's real cheese, with as few bizarre ingredients as possible.For those who like to see ingredients, here is a comparison (and please note I am not a nutritionist - just writing a friendly review:):Kraft Mac & Cheese:Cheese sauce mix ingredients: whey (milk protein), milk protein concentrate, milk, milkfat and cheese culture, salt, sodium tripolyphosphate, sodium phosphate and calcium phosphate, Yellow 5 and Yellow 6, citric acid, lactic acid and enzymes.Annie's Rice Pasta & Cheddar: cheddar cheese (cultured pasturized milk, salt, non-animal enzymes), whey, buttermilk, salt, cream, natural flavor, natural sodium phosphate, annatto extract for natural color.*wiki annatto extract: Annatto coloring is produced from the reddish pericarp or pulp which surrounds the seed of the achiote (Bixa orellana L.). It is used in many natural cheeses (e.g., Cheddar, Red Leicester, Gouda (cheese) and Brie), margarine, butter, rice, smoked fish, and custard powder.Annie's also has less sodium and sugars, which I am grateful for.Also, Annie's does make another rice pasta mac and cheese - it's a deluxe box.  This is what I would compare to Velveeta - for you lovers out there.  It's the ooey gooey cheese that is thicker.  Personally, I detest Velveeta, so the deluxe isn't as awesome as the simple Rice Pasta & Cheddar.  But the deluxe IS better than macaroni with Velveeta because the consistency of the cheese isn't ridiculous overbearing and throat-clogging as Velveeta.  I swear, I always felt like I would suffocate eating that stuff!I definitely recommend this product to those with allergies, and intolerance, or those like myself who are looking for ways to significantly reduce heat intake.  My entire family has now switched from Kraft over to this product (and they didn't do it for health reasons - they simply prefer the taste!)It's a bit more pricey, I'll give you that.  But for a hint - do check Target occasionally.  They sell Annie's pastas and some amazing organic bunny fruit snacks - all of which go on sale quite often (I just purchased Rice Pasta & Cheddar for $1 a box!)  If only the prices were always so kind;)

This is the perfect comfort food for those of us who cannot eat gluten. I let the water (along with olive oil and salt)  come to a rolling boil, dropped in the noodles, stirred until it came back to a rolling boil, and let it go for ten minutes stirring occasionally. I drained the noodles. While they were draining, I mixed 1/4 cup water, some butter, and the sauce packet in the pan until blended. I then tossed the noodles into the sauce and mixed. Perfection. It was just like Kraft, only way better. In fact, it was so good, I ate the entire box in one sitting. I ate it again the next day. This is becoming an addiction.

My son developed gluten intolerance at 16.  He knows what food is supposed to taste like.  This is his favorite pasta.  I'm very happy Amazon makes it easy for families with celiacs to find "normal" tasting food.

column9: Tastes great with a few simple added ingredients:)
column10: This mac & cheese isn't terrific following the box instructions. HOWEVER, if you follow these simple instructions I promise you will LOVE it and you and your kids will gobble it up!  Cook noodles according to package instructions and set aside.  Melt 2 tbs butter in the still warm pot then add boxed cheese powder mix, 1/2 cup shredded mild chedder cheese, and the milk (keep the milk out because you may want to add more).  Stir these all together over very low heat until they've combined and have the consistency of creamy velveeta cheese.  Add the noodles and stir.  If it seems dry at all just add a little more milk (not too much or it will get soupy).  ENJOY!

Very tasty! Much better than that other brand with their "improved flavor" that is inedible now. If you're lazy like me, you can add the cheese powder directly to the buttered pasta. Just stir in slowly and it won't clump. Perfect with a dash of cayenne and paprika.

My kids love mac and cheese, but they are a pretty picky eater. If it doesn't taste good they will not even touch the food. After the first try of this mac and cheese, they keep asking for more. It's very rich, and you can tell the cheese is real cheddar. It's very easy to prepare. The kids don't have the patience to wait, so if you want to make the kids happy and cook something easy. Go with this.

I'm a big Annie's fan, and they tend to cater to special diets, so when I started a gluten-free diet I knew they would have something at the store.  I was impressed by the texture and flavor, and very pleased to still have a familiar box in my pantry.  Here are some things to remember when preparing gluten-free mac and cheese: boil the noodles for substantially longer, and be sure to stir constantly.  If you cook them long enough, they will take on a texture very similar to traditional macaroni -- it just takes longer and the noodles end up comically large.  (I actually thought of this as a plus for a comfort food.)  The noodles are especially prone to becoming a brick if you don't stir regularly.One last thing with regard to the cheese sauce: I always use margarine/butter.  The box says it's optional, but it's really about as optional as if you were making Kraft mac and cheese.  You need margarine/butter for flavor and creaminess.  I found the cheese to be up to snuff when prepared this way.

We put my son on a gluten free diet after he was diagnosed with autism. He has issues with texture of foods and eats very few foods because of this. Kraft mac-n-cheese used to be a favorite of his, but after going gluten free, we decided to try this substitute even though other gluten free pastas were terrible. To our surprise (with slight modification) HE LOVES THIS! I add slightly less milk and put a big scoop of butter in, also cook the noodles a little bit longer so they are tender. Honestly (and I am not gluten free), I like these better than "the real thing"!

column9: For GF - you can't get any better!
column10: My 4 year old has Celiac disease. As most toddlers do - she lived on Mac&Cheese! I was sad for her. We tried almost every brand I could buy at the grocery store, Trader Joes (in California), Whole Foods, Namaste, Mrs Leepers Mac&Cheese, and all we could find online at the Gluten Free Mall. I tell you - most brands are so gross I spit it out. This was the only brand that was actually good. I actually would eat it with my daughter and was happy with it. We live in Denver so we have to cook it for 18 minutes, so that sort of sucks, but it is worth it. We have an "easy lunch" again and it is a real treat for her. Thank you Annie's! I am so happy...

One of my biggest concerns when told I was gluten intolerant was the possible exclusion of comfort food. Let me tell you, this is almost as good as Kraft Mac & Cheese dinner (mind you, the concession) ...The transition in diet was made much easier when I discovered Annie's product. Not only is it Gluten free, but I can make it with my own Lactose-free milk! I can't say I've been easy to adjust to my new diet, but Annie's makes it so much more bearable. I'm down to 3 times a week with this, but I'd easily consume it more. ...Don't know if they do, but if they offered other pastas, I'd be happy to try them with my own sauce!

My husband and I do not usually eat packaged food, but we did need something for those evenings we were too tired to cook.  With my husband being gluten intolerant, we found no quick meals at any nearby markets. When I saw the gluten free mac and cheese, I was really pleased.  I ordered a package, and found it had real cheese.  When we first ate it, we were pleased with the taste and quality. We will continue to buy it

I've eaten this product for years due to a wheat allergy.  I loved it so much that I convinced my non-gluten sensitive friends to eat it (and they love it).  For years, I ate it at least once per week.... until this last batch.I'm not sure what is different but this batch of pasta makes me very sick.  I wasn't sure it was the pasta.  The first time I cooked it, I blamed the broccoli I added.  The next time, I must have undercooked the chicken.  The next time, it was the pepper flakes' fault.  Then, the added garlic.  While working through the pack of 12, I eventually developed an aversion to it from getting so sick and started eating it only once per month.The last few times... again, sick.  So, today, I tried it just the pasta and water, nothing else... and sure enough, VERY sick.  I won't get descriptive but I am suddenly very, very sensitive to something in the pasta. I am 100% certain it is the pasta since I become sick within hours of eating it.  I am also positive I have never, not in years of regular consumption, had this type of reaction before this batch.  I just wanted to put it out there in case anyone else has a similar reaction to whatever has changed.I scanned the boxes, just now, to make sure I accidentally didn't get shipped a gluten case and noticed that this is new packaging.  So, maybe they changed the recipe with the colors/art on their box.  Either way, I won't be eating this again and it's a shame b/c it was such a versatile tool in an otherwise limited cross section of gluten free foods that my "typical" friends will eat.

column9: love this subscription if that is what it is called
column10: this is a very convenient and economical way to keep my family gluten-free. Until these products become more widespread, prices are high so this amazon subscription comes at a good price and is convenient to receive in the mail on a regular basis.

column9: Best GF boxed mac n cheese
column10: This is the best brand of boxed GF mac and cheese you can buy at this time. We have tried at least 4 and none come close to Annie's.In my opinion the cheese sauce is not the greatest in the world, but it is what it is. Apparently you can buy the Kraft cheese powder separately and it is gluten free and we have tried that but our kids did not enjoy it as much as the Annie's sauce. So maybe the taste is a subjective issue. You could probably do better making your own cheese sauce and buying bulk gluten free elbow noodles, but then you would be defeated the purpose of buying boxed mac n cheese wouldn't you?I always wait until they have it for <$2 a box and buy a bunch to store.

I'm relatively new to being gluten free, but still wanted a pasta to eat.  I have made some from scratch that are great, but that's not something I always have the time to do.The noodles cook up very consistently, the texture is pretty close to the 'real' thing.  The packet of cheese flavoring that comes with it is not stellar.  After I add in some cheddar cheese, Parmesan cheese, and some spices  it tasted pretty good.  This will work great when I'm short on time.

column9: My son's favorite macaroni and cheese!
column10: This is by far my son's favorite mac and cheese. We have tried many different gluten free brands and this one has the best flavor and texture. We buy it by the case at Amazon.

You pay for what you get.  This costs more than regular kraft but it is worht it.  It has a Great taste. My friend uses it because of her gluten-free diet, but I really like it also. You can hardly tell the difference. I sometimes use the noodles in other macroni receipes also. I think this is the best store bought stuff you can buy in this category.

My daughter always loved Annie's products and has enjoyed them since age 1.  Now she has been diagnosed with wheat and egg allergies, we absolutely depend on items like these for the times when cooking is a tough situation.  Annie's is delicious and the rice noodles, when cooked to the full time recommended, are fantastic--I just add another 1/4 cup of grated cheddar along with the sauce (after the noodles have been drained), and cook over low heat until the sauce has thickened up.  A little bit of pepper on top, and it's great all by itself.  Don't forget you can always normalize this more by adding chopped heated tender ham, chopped fully-cooked hotdogs, or some thawed peas.  I totally recommend the subscribe and save every 3 months to save money, rather than having to buy this at the few grocery or health food stores who have it at a much higher price.  You just can't beat the free shipping too.The kids I serve this to (when we have company) and my nephew devour this.  They don't notice any difference and tell me it's the best mac and cheese they've ever had.

Annie's rice pasta has a firm, toothsome texture that semolina pasta can't match, and the cheese is mildly sweet and tangy (the instructions say the cheese will stand up without butter, but use it anyway to cut minor Cheetos-like overtones).  Though pricy, it is nutritionally rich and has a good flavor, unlike regular macaroni, which is mostly filler and serves to deliver the cheese.This product has the advantage of being gluten-free, but even if you're not on a restricted diet, I recommend it.  Both healthy and tasty, it's a step up from the garbage that got most of us through college.  You need to eat less of it to feel full, thus offsetting the greater price, and it's so tasty that you need to eat WAY less of it to have your taste buds satisfied.  Savings, nutrition, and good flavor... what more could you ask for?

column9: I honestly just bought this for the noodles!
column10: My daughter has a wheat allergy so to satisfy her mac and cheese craving I simply boil some brown rice elbow macaroni and use the cheese package mix out of the Kraft mac and cheese box, discarding the noodles. You can't taste a difference. According to the cheese sauce ingredients supplied by Kraft, the sauce mixture itself does not contain wheat, just the noodles.

column9: Too yummy to be gluten free!
column10: This gluten free Mac and Cheese is the best I have had in the 6 years since going gluten free. My kids who eat "regular" food love it too!

Love this mac n cheese. So creamy and cheesy. Kids will love it. Closest to Kraft you can get, But healthier. I add a little milk and butter and then whisk the cheese a little before adding the pasta. Gluten free heaven.

After many flops we tried Annie's Gluten Free Mac & Cheese and it's an instant winner.  My little one declared it delicious, with the right color and consistency.  It does need a bit of salt to perk it up, but that is easily rectified.Thanks to Annie's for making GF mac & cheese easy and tasty!

Delicious deal, the serving sizes are a little smaller than normal mac n cheese, so it will really only feed 2 kids. I added some other gluten free noodles from the pantry in to make it go a little farther and I always add extra cheddar to the sauce. Overall I'm happy I invested in it!

I bought this to eat as a birthday treat, I am undergoing the "gluten challenge" pending Celiac diagnosis but did not want to be sick on my birthday so I skipped a day of eating gluten foods (after the tests are performed I am forced to be gluten free for life anyway, I am confirmed gluten intolerant whether or not it is full on Celiac disease). This macaroni surprised me, I had the expectation that gluten free food wouldn't really taste like food at all. The al dente texture of the pasta was awesome, I had expected it to be even mushier than regular macaroni sometimes gets and it wasn't at all. The cheese sauce was just as good as the regular Annie's (my fav!). The only thing about it I don't like is that the rice noodles don't have much flavor of their own at all and they stick together a bit worse than wheat pasta does, but it is what it is. I knew it wouldn't have that yummy wheat taste but it was still a little disappointing. I gave it four stars because yes, I'll eat it again, but it needs a little something extra in the cheese packet to counter the blandness of rice noodles.
I've been gluten free for a while and have tried countless different boxed mac n cheeses. Annie's is by far the best, and the closest to Kraft.

This Mac and cheese is great, especially if you cannot have the regular kind. This is the first rice pasta we have tried and it was every bit as good as Annie's regular Mac and cheese. I actually thought it was better because the noodles in this one are bigger. I added a little shredded cheddar but I have always done that to any Mac and cheese. My 13 month old loved this and my 4 1/2 year old, who adores Mac and cheese, ate 2 servings. Thanks Annie's for allowing my family to have Mac and cheese again!

column9: Good Gluten Free Mac N Cheese
column10: My youngest son is on a gluten free diet and loves mac-n-cheese. Everyone in the family eats this and enjoys it. While I like the idea of being able to stock up by purchasing 12 boxes at the time, I can save $1 per box at my local big box store. For now I'll continue to purchase it elsewhere.

column9: Annie's Gluten Free Mac - Good Stuff!
column10: We really like this stuff.  Even my non-gluten free fiance likes it!  We highly recommend Annie's gluten free mac & cheese!
I really missed pasta after going gluten free. I came across this product and decided to give it a try. It's really good! My family likes it too!

I got this because I have celiacs and as a result am incredibly sensitive to gluten. This is very safe and I had no negative side effects at all. It's also very easy to make and it's delicious. I loved this! I will definitely be buying this again and recommend it for anything who's forced to be on a gluten-free diet but loves the taste of mac and cheese. It's delicious.
