Of course, they cooled while we finished making the soup, but pouring the hot soup over the noodles brought them back to temperature quickly.The second recipe is sort of a seafood scampi with noodles.  I have a pretty good idea that the noodles will be nice in that dish, but I will update this review after we have made it in a day or two.The package has 7 ounces of product.  Looking at the nutritional statement, the serving size is 2 ounces, so the package says it contains 3.5 servings.  While it would have been more convenient to have an even number of servings, I found that using 3 ounces of uncooked noodles was plenty for two servings of soup.  Why 7 ounces?  This product is made in Singapore, and the package contains 200 grams, which happens to be about 7 ounces.  The Singaporean package design did not consider the US standards for serving sizes.Rice noodles (of any kind) do not have a lot of distinctive flavor; their flavor is very mild.  Therefore it is not easy to declare this as "delicious", but they are nice, and we enjoyed them.  Rice noodles do a fine job of taking on the flavors you put with them - in our case, Myanmar Mohinga soup.  The texture, especially with my brief cooking, was very pleasant.Some noodles we buy at the local Chinese market (which are NOT whole grain) are arranged in serving-size bundles in the package, making it very convenient to take out the desired number of servings.  These come as one hunk of noodles.  One suggestion I would make for improving this product is to make them into serving-size bunches, because pulling out odd lots causes them to snap and fly all over, and so I do not have to use a diet scale to measure serving sizes.

column9: Vermicelli, Celiac Disease and recipes, oh my!
column10: Preparation: This was super simple with this product. With Traditional Mai Fun you need to soak it for 10 minutes in very hot water. This product just needs to be soaked in water at room temperature for a few minutes to soften and be ready to eat. The texture is very  chewy and I did add extra cooking liquid to allow it to steam. After soaking and steaming the vermicelli still did a decent job holding it's shape.Texture : My kids did not really like the texture of the vermicelli and prefer the Tinkyada pasta and noodles. I actually think the texture mimics Mai Fun very well and if you enjoy a Mai Fun stir fry this would be excellent. The rice/sago texture really does not make it a good substiture for pasta.Flavor: Nice clean rice based flavor. It picked up the flavor of the cooking liquid very nicely.Recipes on the package : The instructions on these are pretty vague. There is no ingredient list or amounts in the recipes. The instructions tell you, as an example, to "prepare a clear soup stock with anchovies, soybeans, salt and sugar; mix a variety of vegetables strips in oyster and soya sauce with the stock, add blanched brown rice vermicelli, toss and simmer until cooked." If you can soar with a recipe like this, go for it. If not, I'd look online for stir fry recipes using Mai Fun. Note also that the recipe stated that you should use 'blanched' noodles, while the preparation instructions for the noodles state that you soak them in room temperature water! I found that the soaking at room temperature worked fine but you do need more than a minute for the noodles to soften. I think that the recipe is a little 'lost in translation' but the product is still a good one if you can find a better recipe for it.Is it REALLY Gluten Free? : If you're living with Celiac disease your criteria for what makes something 'gluten free' is often a very strict one. I've learned to trust many of the items that are made in the US and labeled Gluten free as long as the allergy information does not say that it is made on equipment shared with wheat products. The packaging on this item does not say anything regarding shared equipment and the same Singapore based brand also produces wheat flour and wheat starch. Except for the Gluten free label up front and the ingredient list (Brown Rice, Sago Starch and water) there is no further explanation of it's gluten free status. My child with celiac is not super reactive to trace amounts of gluten but, if you are, this may be something to consider.I did call the East Coast distributors but was unable to get an answer for the shared equipment question. I will email the manufacturers and update this review if I get an answer. Unless I can determine for sure that the factory uses dedicated gluten free equipment we will, unfortunately, not be using this product again.

column9: Quick but more processed and less tasty than other forms of brown rice
column10: I ordered this because I like whole grains and brown rice, but now that I've tried it out it strikes me more as a fairly highly processed food. On the plus side it's convenient, made from brown rice, super quick to prepare, and versatile enough to be used with either Asian or Italian-style sauces, which supply most of the flavor to what you eat. On the minus side, anything you can cook like this in almost no time has been altered--or processed--significantly from its original whole-grain state and consequently will tend to have a higher glycemic index, fewer nutrients, and less taste. It's like the difference between brown rice and brown Minute Rice or old-fashioned oats and instant oatmeal.These noodles are so bland, air-spun, and taste-free that they hardly seemed like real food to me. I also didn't like that they're not organic and come from Singapore as I'd rather eat American-grown food for environmental, nutritional, and economic reasons. I doubt I'll be ordering them again, though they're probably healthier than most white flour ramen-type products and certainly convenient to use.

column9: Great gluten-free product and super-fast cooking!
column10: I am gluten intolerant, but have not taken to most gluten-free pastas. I have several boxes of rice spaghetti that I just can't manage to eat because it is so underwhelming. The rice pastas I've tried fall apart when cooked; you need to watch them especially carefully, and even if you get them off the heat at the right time, they aren't great leftovers. Like soy milk or turkey bacon, rice pasta is usually entirely disappointing if you are expecting the "real thing".What I love most about the Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli is that it does not fall apart. This is not just a function of not boiling it (though that's excellent); I think it's something about how it's made as well. It has substance.Update:The cooking instructions on the bag are feeble. Here's what I suggest most people do:1. Boil water and add salt, as you normally would with pasta. 4 quarts is probably about the right size, though I use a 6-quart pot as my generic pasta pot, so that's what I used.2. Add the noodles; stir.3. You can even turn the heat off at that point, though you can also wait a minute or two with the heat on. Do not leave them soaking in water for too long; rice pasta tends to dissolve. (I have not tried this with these particular noodles yet.) Two or three minutes is all you need for the cooking time.They are really great noodles.Here's the rest of my original review:I cooked my sample package in the microwave with chicken broth. Cook a minute, stir, repeat. (This could be more streamlined, but I was trying to maintain a high noodle to broth ratio, thus the need to keep the noodle moist in not really enough broth.) I added salt, pepper, and parmesan, but of course there are many options once you have the substrate.Pros:1. Can cook in liquid in a microwave, almost like ramen (not quite that easily). Or just soften in a bowl of water to be cooked with other things in a frying pan, as per the directions.2. Maintains its structure, even as leftoversCons:1. I agree with others that it doesn't have much flavor, but I think that's if you compare it to wheat pasta, and if you are gluten intolerant, that's not an option. Update! I think it's because of the salt. When most of us cook pasta, we put salt in the water, and the cooking methods suggested on the package do not add salt.Other:1. These are much finer noodles than what I think of as vermicelli, finer than angel hair. Which is great in that it enables the no-heat softening. So this is just a heads up in case you're expecting noodles that are a bit thicker than a spaghetti.Alternative product:I just tried notta pasta vermicelli, and it's also good, but different. Notta Pasta Rice Vermicelli, 8.8-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6) It's not made from brown rice, it's a larger package (despite the weights, it makes about twice as much as this, though the overall price/meal is comparable, I think. The notta pasta has you boil it for 2-3 minutes and that worked well. The notta also comes in boxes, not bags, so it seems to stay in tact in the package better. But the box is surprisingly hard to open.I am going to try Peacock again, and try boiling it. (Which worked, see above.)I am now getting the Peacock via subscribe and save, and very happy with that.

Believe it or not, this pasta does not need to be boiled in water!  All you do is soak it in regular tap water and then cook it as desired.  We had ours with pesto, so we put the pasta in a saute pan, covered it with water and let it soak for approx 2 minutes.  Then we poured the water down the drain, added our pesto sauce along with about a cup of water (you'll be able to tell how much water you need to add, if any) and heated it in the pan for a couple minutes - that was it.  The vermicelli was almost exactly like regular pasta, only a tiny bit chewier.  I would definitely buy this to keep on hand when we want pasta fast, without having to wait for a pot of water to boil.My only complaint is that the instructions on the package were very vague.  There are two recipes on the back, but they don't give amounts for anything - not even the amount of water to soak the pasta in.  You'll kind of have to keep checking things as you go along.

I have always been a huge fan of rice vermicelli, in Asian foods. The only setback is that most rice vermicelli is made from processed, refined flour. Hence, the carbohydrates are simple - not complex. This means that the carbohydrate is converted to sugar in your system, and it induces in your system a feeling of "crash and burn." Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli is made from complex carbohydrates. This means your body will process and convert the nutrients, more sustainably.A great recipe for these noodles is very simple and incredibly satisfying. Sautee one onion with 2-3 cloves of garlic, with a tablespoon of grape seed oil. Cook until golden brown, add 1/4 of a head of red cabbage, soy sauce, peanut butter and minced ginger. Add tofu and water softened vermicelli (soak for one minute prior to adding to recipe). Cook until all ingredients are soft. Serve warm with a cup of oolong tea on the side. Delicious.

I received a 7 oz. package of the product, which advertises that it is gluten-free, fat free cholesterol free and contains no preservatives.  Ingredients listed on the back are: Brown Rice, Sago Starch and Water.  The manufacturer is Chye Choon Foods Private Limited, Singapore.  Serving size is 2 oz. (56 gm) and there are 3.5 servings per package.  Calories per serving are 209, 7 of which are from fat - few enough fat calories to be considered fat-free, evidently.The instructions say to soften brown rice vermicelli in water at room temperature for 1 minute prior to cooking.  That's it for basic preparation instructions.There are two recipes included:BROWN RICE VERMICELLI IN AGLIO OLIO STYLE tells you to soften the vermicelli, heat olive oil and garlic over medium heat in a frying pan, add in red chili, flat parsley and assorted seafood together with the vermicelli, stir well, remove from heat and serve with grated cheese.BROWN RICE VERMICELLI WITH VEGETABLE STRIPS instructs you to prepare a clear soup stock with anchovies, soybeans, salt and sugar, mix a variety of vegetable strips in oyster and soya sauce with the stock in a large non-stick pot, add blanched brown rice vermicelli, toss the mixture occasionally and simmer until cooked, garnish with spring onion and serve.WHAT WE DID: We lightly browned some garlic in oil, using a large frying pan.  Added a package of Wegman's Asian Slaw (cabbage, celery and carrots) and a bottle of Wegman's Vegetable Simmer Sauce. Soaked the vermicelli in room temperature water as directed.  Added the softened vermicelli to the pan, tossed it around and heated it.  Salt and pepper.  Serve.  It was pretty good.

When it has come down to each of us, we need to find better in the way we eat and also cook. For Peacock, they definitely have made some very strong grains and rice foods. That comes in well with their Brown Rice Vermicelli. It is simple and easy to cook, but also tastes pretty goos with just about anything you add with it, whether it is chicken, vegetables, or beef. I was surprised at how good it tastes. It flows well with the others brands of rice makers like Uncle Ben's and Success. I would give this a try and give Peacock a piece on your plate, and keep in mind for your foods.Price: BTaste: BOverall: B

I'm pretty easy going about noodles. And I like my pasta with no fuss. So I was disappointed with these Brown Rice Vermicelli. Following the packaged instructions, the  noodles came out so al dente they tased like crunchy hair or easter grass. No one in my family liked them. I ended up eating mine on top of my fried rice like a garnish, but frankly they were just too hard. Only after the noodles had sat uneaten in the bowl in a sink filled with soapy dish water, did these noodles actually soften up to a reasonable texture. So my advice?- soak 'em longer than the package says.I also have to say the instructions weren't that good. Its really hard to mess up noodles... But these yes... It is possible.Overall, I can't recommend this product. I like my pasta fuss-free, and this was a high maintenance low mileage generic tasting stuff. I've had better- and a lot less fuss too.

I have loved "Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli, 7-Ounce Packages"(I am assuming at that age they might have been another brand but they were the vermicelli) since childhood.  I loved watching the waiter get a wok full of hot olive oil, adding veggies and various meats(whichever you chose) and throw these noodles into the hot mixture....poof...they were little bird nests with yummy food inside.I did this at home with  "Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli, 7-Ounce Packages" with crab, orange, cilantro, Vidalia onion sliced very thin and threw in the noodles...Poof, I was back to childhood.Delicious after being tossed a bit with a slice of lime.Wonderful choice I made and I will make it again.  They are incredibly healthy so tasty and good for you....how can you miss?

I would never recommend this item. I made it tonight with some vegetables and it pretty much ruined dinner. The taste is very bland (unlike other brown rice pasta that I've had) and the noodles are so small that they seem to divide and conquer the plate and completely take over. These are thinner than regular vermicelli and probably should just be labeled as an Asian brown rice noodle instead of trying to be an Italian vermicelli noodle. If you're seeking a brown rice noodle that tastes good and has substance to it, this isn't it. Try Tinkyada instead.
I tried this product with a stir fry my spouse prepared for me and found it quite tasty and easy to prepare.  If you like Asian food you can't go wrong with this.

The instructions on the back of this product were obviously a struggle to write in English and not clear.  The product itself has no flavoring other than what you add.  Rice pastas are notoriously difficult to cook as they will dissolve into a glob if not cooked correctly.  Since I am experienced with cooking them, I figured out despite the incorrect instructions how to prepare this and that the flavoring was up to me to add.  You don't soak it for over a minute in cool water, then drain it, then stir it into a hot, non-stick skillet, with plenty of olive oil or oil of your choice that you've already cooked your peppers, garlic, onion, whatever you want to flavor it with.  Keep some broth handy to add into the vermicelli as you are cooking it which it will absorb  rapidly.  Don't leave it!  This will be a short process when you start cooking it.  Be careful stirring it or it will break up into little sticks.  Actually, a package of Rice A Roni, is a lot easier to cook than this!

column9: Meh - better rice noodles & GF options out there
column10: We're Gluten Free, so we eat rice noodles on a regular basis. Whenever I see a new brand come along I usually give it a try and most of the time they aren't as good as Tinkyada Tinkyada Brown Rice Pasta, Spaghetti, Organic, 12-Ounce (Pack of 6), and this product is no different.First off, I never follow the instructions on noodles - I cook them all the same way I was taught by my mother...boil the water, put them all in with a bit of salt (oil optional) and test them until the right texture is achieved. I did the same with these - I'm not up for soaking, or  boiling water, putting in noodles then letting it sit off the burner for "x" amount of time or any of that. So, that may make a difference. Anyways...Many of the noodles were broken, so be aware of that if ordering vs. picking them out yourself in a store. I personally don't like noodles so thin - they are harder to work with and to me just don't contribute much to the overall meal. However, I do like the really thin rice noodles used for Pad Thai, Pho and dishes such as that and they cook super quick as well! My favorite of those are: GLUTEN FREE Vietnamese Brown Rice Noodles with Organic Green Tea - JUST NOODLES, 8.6 oz, 4 SERVINGS per box (Pack of 6) These are very long and skinny, cook really quick, and an be used like spaghetti noodles or in any way you might want to use noodles. I suggest you buy those instead.My suggestion is to go with Tinkyada noodles for any type of "regular" noodle dishes you need, and the Just Noodles GLUTEN FREE Vietnamese Brown Rice Noodles with Organic Green Tea - JUST NOODLES, 8.6 oz, 4 SERVINGS per box (Pack of 6) whenever you need super quick cooking noodles or for Asian, Thai, etc. type dishes. I think they're tastier, have a much better texture, they're easy to cook and overall I like them better.
These noodles are fine and a bit textured when cooked. That is because it is brown rice. It would be good for a gluten-free diet. White rice noodles are more bland in flavor.

I love to make stir-fry veggies, and I almost always have them with brown rice, so I was excited to have the chance to try this noodle product made from brown rice. As soon as I got the product, my son and I put together a terrific dish with this! After reading the two recipes on the back, here is what we improvised: Chop up half a small cabbage, an onion, two cloves of garlic, two stalks of celery, a red bell pepper and a few small portabella mushrooms. Saute in about a Tablespoon of olive oil. Soak the noodles for a minute or so. Add the noodles to the mix. Add one small can of chopped anchovies, along with the oil from the can. My son put lots of red pepper (cayenne) in, and I thought it would be too much, but it was actually delicious in it. We had a package of portabella mushroom soup in the fridge, so I added about a third cup of that for flavor and moisture. With this package of Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli, a little imagination we concocted a delicious hot dinner dish. The only thing I would have added if I had some would have been some seafood--such as scallops and/or shrimp. Bits of chicken would have worked nicely, too. It was quite filling and satisying. I will probably get more of this brown rice vermicelli to keep on hand for quick dishes.

I am giving it 3 stars as being Korean and my husband Italian we love any form of pasta. I personally love vermicelli. The 7 oz bag gave in a box a size you could fit a mass volume of toilet paper in or 6 containers of laundry detergent. I can't review this product in a fair way as when I opened the overly large box and grabbed the vermicelli, it was completely in little bits. There would be no way to even try and strain this product after being cooked. there were no large intact pieces. I would not order this from amazon as this is not the first time they have had poor packaging.

column9: Brown Rice Vermicelli Not for Us
column10: The brown rice vermicelli may be fine for specific uses but not for the general use we had in mind.  It simply does not fit in with our meal types.

column9: Fast, yummy, and good for you, but the packaging could use some work.
column10: I very much enjoyed this vermicelli.  I've never had this type of noodle before, but I love how quick to prepare it is and how well it soaks up the sauce you put it in.  Its very tasty and pretty healthy to boot.The main problem I have with it is the packaging gives you NO clue how to prepare it.  Its very vague.  I figured it out after looking up stuff online.  I'm sure if you're used to using vermicelli this kind of thing won't bother you.  But I had never used it before, and some tips for a guy like me would've been appreciated.

A high quality product which is super easy to prepare, and can be used like a pasta. Brown rice is a great source for carbohydrates. Cholesterol free, gluten free and fat free, soak for one minute and the vermicelli is ready for cooking - pan frying or adding to soup. I use vermicelli along with shredded bbq pork or shrimp and mushrooms as fillings for summer rolls too.Also try their brown rice spaghetti. Perfect if you're looking for gluten-free pasta.

These noodles are truly worth having on hand to use to throw together a quick meal.  The way I used them?  I had a jar of simmer sauce, and some frozen seafood mix.  Defrosted the seafood (I already had it defrosted but you can do it in cold water in 20-30 minutes), sauteed it for 3-4 minutes, added the simmer sauce and let it simmer for about 10 minutes.  Meanwhile, I softened the noodles in room temperature water for 1 minute (per the package directions) and then added the noodles for the last few minutes of the simmer time.  All told, the meal took less than 15 minutes to prepare and was so delicious everyone wanted to go back for more (although there was only enough for one serving each for my family of four).The noodles themselves couldn't be simpler - just brown rice, starch and water.  I love that they are made from brown rice.  It not only gives them a little better texture but makes them easier to work with than white noodles.Definitely will purchase again and recommend to anyone.

column9: okay but not as healthy as it appears
column10: I am always looking for healthier, whole grain versions of foods I enjoy.  Unfortunately, these Peacock brand noodles are yet another food masquerading as healthy.  The product title in big letters on the front says "Brown Rice Vermicelli", making the consumer think "this is made with brown rice, so it should be a healthy choice".  But the first indication that it is not is when looking at the fiber content on the nutrition facts - only 0.6g per 2oz serving.  Then onto the ingredients list to see why so low... contains brown rice, sago starch and water.  The sago starch comes from palms and must not have much (if any) fiber.The Annie Chun's Maifun Brown Rice Noodles (sold on Amazon and in my local healthy grocer) has become one of my staples and is my frame of reference when comparing to the Peacock brand.  The Annie Chun's product is made with 100% whole grain, with ingredients brown rice flour and water.  Per 2oz serving, it has 4g fiber and pretty much the same calories and other nutrients as the Peacock brand.If you do try this Peacock brand noodles and have not used rice noodles before, you will need to seek guidance elsewhere on preparation.  As others have pointed out, the Peacock package gives almost no directions on how to prepare the product, aside from a brief mention in the recipes (in the header text it does say that they are "easy-to-cook" but does not say how).  It also contains a very strange recipe for rice noodles: Aglio Olio style - this is an Italian recipe for noodles with olive oil/garlic/sprinkled with grated cheese that I think would not be very tasty.  The second recipe appears to be for a soup with veggie strips.  Neither recipe gives amounts or much direction.  In comparison, the Annie Chun's package gives clear, specific directions on rice noodle preparation and two recipes.I use rice noodles = maifun = rice sticks = sometimes called vermicelli for making the Vietnamese salad "bun tofu", to serve with stir-fried veggies or in lettuce rolls.  They can also be used in spring rolls/egg rolls.  When cooking with thin rice noodles, be careful not to oversoak/overcook/overmix or they tend to disintegrate.  Asian rice noodle vermicelli (maifun) are not the same as Italian vermicelli and are not readily interchangeable.  If making an Italian recipe, the best results would be expected from Italian pasta and not maifun.A few final notes...  Both Peacock and Annie Chun's brown rice noodles are gluten free.  The Peacock is made in Singapore and the Annie Chun's in Thailand.  The Peacock noodles do taste fine (kind of bland), but so do the Annie Chun's.  At this time, they are both approximately the same price.  Peacock come in an plastic bag with some noodle crushage upon shipping; Annie Chun's are perfect upon removal from their cellophane bag in a box.  Overall, I highly recommend the Annie Chun's Maifun as a healthier option over the Peacock brand.  On a related note, the Annie Chun's soba and brown rice pad thai noodles are also excellent.Rating for this product: 2.5 stars rounded down to 2 stars.

My local Trader Joe's has a similar product so I was anxious to see how this would stack up.  It is very easy to make and perfect for the health conscious person who desires an alternative to rice or potatoes.I added shrimp to my dish and it was outstanding.  The flavor was very tasty and the product was bold versus getting over cooked.  It is a good base for consumers looking to build a nice entree for your seafood, poultry, pork or even beef.  Of course, for vegetarians you can also build a nice side dish because it is very easy to prepare.

The instructions on this package were atrocious.  They didn't make sense, and I couldn't figure out how much water to use.  Needless to say, they didn't turn out well.  I suspect the product itself is decent, but I would need better directions or many more packages with which to experiment, to determine that for certain.

To prepare these, I soak them for 3-4 minutes in hot water. Then drain the noodles before sauteing them.My family loves them. They are nearly as quick as ramen and we like the texture and flavor a lot more. I sauteed them in olive oil with canned chicken breast, lots of garlic and some oregano and served them with cheese. The packages say 3.5 servings, but that worked out to 4 lunch sized portions.Pros and Cons, some of what is a pro for my family may be a con for other families and people:Little flavor- also a con, they pick up other flavors very well. They do need other flavors though because they are very bland on their own.Fast- Really fast. Using cooked shrimp, or other cooked meat and frozen small veggies like peas, you could have a meal ready in under 10 minutes.Size- also a con, if you have a family of 4, one package is just enough noodles. If you're only cooking for yourself, or for a couple, it may be too much, and it doesn't break down easily into smaller amounts. They don't keep well once "cooked".We don't have gluten-restricted dietary concerns in my family, but these are gluten free if that is an issue. The picky eater in our family declared these were delicious.Tomorrow I plan to try them with shrimp, temari, garlic, ginger and mushrooms. I can see these being the base for a lot of quick meals.

Peacock's All Natural Brown Rice Vermicelli is useful if you want to make a really quick stir fry, and it also has a recipe for soup on the back of the package I want to try (with some modifications). I modified the "Brown Rice Vermicelli in Aglio Olio style" recipe (also on the package) by adding broccoli, pea pods and some other vegetables, and it was a fast and nutritious complete meal.The ingredients listed are simply brown rice, sago starch (a starch which is extracted from the pith of tropical palms), and water. What it gains in convenience and speed, it somewhat loses in flavor. I found it slightly "starchy" in texture, but with the right seasoning, vegetables, and seafood or  finely sliced meat, it's a good item to keep in your pantry for quick and easy meals.It's also good for people like me on "limited diets." Pasta is a "no no" on my very restricted regimen, but this Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli is a great way to "have my pasta and eat it too." Calories are 209 for a 2 Oz. portion (approximately 3.5 servings per bag). I'm going to enjoy experimenting with recipes where I can use this product.

column9: Each 7 ounce package makes a nice meal or two with additional ingredients
column10: Each individual 7-ounce package of Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli comes with preparation instructions and two simple recipes, and contains enough vermicelli to make meals for up to two people.  I usually combine vermicelli with any two or three of the following: diced pork, shrimp, tofu, chicken, shiitake mushroom, and / or green vegetables.  Add soy sauce and other condiments when you pan cook them, or if you prefer to make soup, just add chicken broth and bring them to boil. Either way, you only have to soak the vermicelli in water at room temperature for about a minute before you start cooking.

Not good at all. The vermicelle has absolutly no flavor on it's own what so ever. It's more of a filler for a dish. I soaked it for a minute in room temp water like it said, then put the olive oil & the garlic in the pan as directed, heated it & added my sliced peppers & shrimp, then added the vermicelli as directed. It was like a paste & NO, I didn't over cook it. Very angry as it made the rest of the dish awful so I wasted my time as well as my electric cooking it & all the other ingredients I had put into it. I would personnally NEVER buy this & if someone gave it to me I'd throw it out, as I did. Lucky for me I had other actual rice to cook to use for my remaining ingredients as I did a small amount instead of cooking all of it together just in case I didn't like it. I was able to pick out the shrimps & the peppers to save them. Those items aren't cheap to buy. You may feel differently about it but I can't imagine why since it has zero flavor.

column9: Not Soft Enough For My Taste
column10: There are 2 recipes / preparation methods on the back of the package, so I tried these 2 ways:1. Stir FryThe package suggests olive oil, parsley, peppers, seafood & cheese Italian style. I don't have any olive oil, so I substituted Sesame oil & also cilantro for the parsley & went Asian style. The noodles were hard as rocks. I did pre soak.2. SoupI don't have any soup stock laying around either, so again after the recommended pre soak, I prepared the noodles in an Indian curry with lots of sauce. They were much better this way, but still too tough for my taste.I have eaten similar noodles at Vietnamese restaurants, & I did like them. I am also quite familiar of & approving of Brown Rice Noodles & Whole Wheat Noodles; my problem with these is the texture.It is possible that Olive Oil is REQUIRED; if that is the case, it should have been made more clear on the packaging.If you like your stir fry somewhat cement like, or your soup noodles chewy these are for you. If not....................One last unexpected comment: the uncooked noodles have become my boy kitty's favorite toy of the moment! He found a couple on the floor last night & had a blast stalking & torturing them before eating them!

column9: May be worthwhile for those intolerant to gluten
column10: Taste is OK; texture is something like straw. It might respond to cooking the same as angel-hair pasta; but then again, maybe not: the instructions for preparation are not helpful in this regard, which is too bad for a relatively unfamiliar product not described in most cookbooks.The package does not re-seal or re-close; however, it contains only about 3 servings, so would usually be used up all at once anyway.Aside from providing a gluten-free food for those who need it, this mis-named "vermicelli" (angel-hair, more like) is healthful from the standpoint that it incorporates brown rice rather than over-processed wheat (or white rice, for that matter); however, similar health benefits, for the majority of people who are not gluten-intolerant could also be achieved in a whole-wheat product.With better packaging and instructions, I could give this a mild recommendation for the general consumer; as it stands, it's only for those who must avoid gluten.

column9: Good taste but high in salt
column10: If you're in a pinch for a side dish or you're a struggling student and need something tasty at a good price then this is for you, but if you are looking for something healthy then the sodium here should scare you away

column9: Good but not great - and NOT a purely brown rice product
column10: It's a bit hard to rate something as bland as rice vermicelli, but here goes.  It had to be soaked before cooking, but cooked up nicely.  It has little inherent taste of its own, but works nicely with any number of other ingredients, providing nice variety.  Would we go out looking for this or buy a case at a time?  Not really.  But if we found it locally, we might buy a bag to have on hand from time to time - just not worth the price as a main food product.  It is not something we'd likely use a lot of the time.  As the title says, it's a moderately good product, just not great.  Another reviewer hit it badly for no taste - I would not have expected a substantial taste, just more of a different variety of additional food product that goes with whatever else is mixed in with it.  It will take on the flavor of whatever it's cooked with - it is NOT a stand-alone food.One note: it isn't worth the money.  At Amazon's price, this is selling for more than $5.00/pound yet it's not even a pure brown rice product, as one might think from the packaging.  Fortunately, due to dietary restrictions I've got, I read labels.  Read the label on this one.  It's got SOME brown rice in it....
This is my new fave rice vermicelli - since I purchased this case, I've cooked it virtually daily with homemade asian stock, chopped veggies & seasonings - it's perfect!Go for it!

I found Peacock's Brown Rice Vermicelli to be a fun alternative to rice in stir frys (it's rice but in noodle form).I only have two complaints:1) The directions for preparing them are poor. The bag says that the noodles only need to be soaked in water for 1 to 2 minutes, but I found that they needed at least 5 in order to be soft enough to combine with whatever else I was cooking.2) The noodles come in two large clumps. If you don't want to cook with an entire clump, you need to break it appart -- especially problematic when you only want to cook with a third or a quarter of a clump. It would be more useful if they came in many small clumps.Besides those qualms, I'd still recommend them.

This is very quick and easy to make and there is never really ever just one way of preparting vermicelli or anything else for that matter.A brown rice version is slightly healthier and great for those of us whose staple consists of rice.  3.5 servings per bag, 209 calories, 47.1 g carbs, .6 g fiber, and 3.2 g per serving.

The package said they don't need to be pre-soaked, but after reading other reviews, I decided that was the best route to go.  Pres-soaked for a few minutes, then I cooked with them, and they turned out pretty well.  Not sure if I would buy these (I ordered these through Vine), but they were good try try.  Added stir fried veggies and shrimp to them.

The package said that you must pre-soak the noodles for five minutes (or whatever length of time it was) before boiling the noodles. Not necessary. My wife and I, on two occasions, just dumped some into boiling water, kept an eye on it, drained them after a period or time, and ate them.They were fine. They were not earth-shatteringly delicious, but then again many things that comes in bags are not. It was good, fine, adequate, serviceable, non-regrettable and I'll leave it at that.The instructions on the back are rather odd though. It gave me the impression that there are a limited number of recipes/dishes with which you can make these noodles, most involving top-of-the-line seafood. Again, unnecessary fuss. I think we had this with some plain Jane vegetables and seasoning. Turned out to be a nice dinner. I don't think my kids liked it, but that's kids for you.ADDITIONAL NOTE: I found the bag, so here's the nutritional information -Serving size: 56gm (2oz)Serving size per container: 3.5Calories: 209Total Fat: 0.8g (Saturated fat: 0.3g, no trans fats)Sodium: 2.4mgPotassium: 3.3mgTotal Carbohydrates: 47.1g (Fiber: 0.6g, Sugars: 2.2g, Protein: 3.2g)DAILY VALUES: Vitamin C = 0.3%Calcium = 1.4%Iron = 3.2%No vitamin AIngredients: Brown rice, sago starch and water

I cooked it according to directions, and had it with chicken and vegetables, and it wasn't too bad.  My husband wasn't a huge fan, but he's pretty picky.  I liked it okay.  It's definitely something different, but I don't think it will become a staple in our pantry.

My mother must eat a gluten free diet so when I saw this item I was very intrigued. Some gluten free products have an off texture. I followed the recipe suggestion on the bag and it came out delicious. One tip: after cooking & until serving place wet papertoweling on top of noodles to keep from drying out.

To begin, I have to state that the package is deceiving. I was pleasantly surprised at just how many noodles fit in one package. It was much more noodles than expected. As for the taste of the noodles, it was pretty good. I prepared the noodles with a Thai curry sauce, and the flavors worked well together. My only complaint is that the noodles were incredibly thin. The texture is kind of awkward in your mouth, as it feels as if you are eating thick hair. Having said that, it wasn't a major issue, and I quickly became accustomed to the texture. Overall this brown rice vermicelli is a good choice if you are looking for a healthier alternative to traditional noodles.

Vermicelli rice noodles are always a great addition to soup or stir-fry.  This is my first brown rice vermicelli and it fairly similar to white rice vermicelli.  The main differences were the taste and consistency.  The taste is more flavorful and slightly nutty, like brown rice.  The consistency was less pleasing however.  This whole grain vermicelli feels tougher and denser than it's more processed counterpart, as you would expect if you've had whole wheat pasta.Preparing Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli is exceedingly simple.  The directions on the bag say to soak for 1 minute in cool water.  I like to use salty broth because they will soak up the flavor of the broth.  If you are eating them in soup, you are done and simply add the noodles to the soup; no cooking is needed.  For stir-fry's you'll want to toss them in a hot wok with your sauce or oil for a minute or two.  If you crisp them up, the consistency is less noticeable.

column9: pretty good option for quick GF meals
column10: We soaked the noodles and then used them in a stir fry.  The good:  the noodles were quick and easy to prepare, and definitely different from plain rice.  The texture reminded me a bit of straw, and there was no noticeable flavor, but it did work as an interesting "base" for our veggies and seasonings.

Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli is a nice alternative to regular pasta. It will take me some time to get use to this product, but it is not bad.  Would love to try it with some other receipes.  I recommend this product to individuals who like to try new things and experiment with new recipes.

column9: Not bad for an amateur cook
column10: I was skeptical after reading the reviews here if I should try to cook this with some expensive Newman's Own tomato and garlic sauce. I soaked it for one minute then put it in a deep skilet and put 3/4 of a jar of tomato sauce on it and cooked until hot. It turned out good. It takes on the flavor of whatever your spices are, I suppose. It probably would have done even better if I had put the entire jar in it.

column9: Pretty good for a rice pasta
column10: The first time I tried this brown rice vermicelli I was less than impressed.  It has such a fine texture and I cooked it like I would regular flour pasta in water.  I thought it was tastless and not good.  The next time I prepared it I read the package which tells you to soak it in room temp water for a minute or so before cooking.  It also has a couple of recipe ideas.  I soaked the pasta for a minute (or 3) and it didn't really seem to soften it any but I'm sure it must have helped.  Then, based on the recipes provided, I put it in a large skillet with some Asian and basalmic oil and stirred it around.  It wasn't softening as quickly I I thought so I added a little water and put a lid on it for just a minute.  Perfect!  It came out soft and had absorbed the flavors beautifully.  It made a great addition to my Asian grilled Redfish.  The texture was smooth and soft, not gritty nor gummy.  I'd recommend this product to my friends who are alergic to gluten as well as those who want a healthier alternative to pasta.

column9: Tastes fine, but strands are incredibly thin and preparation method is too mysterious
column10: Let me preface this review by stating that I have never prepared vermicelli before.  That being said, I took the pack and started to boil water, figuring this stuff (which is hard and brittle out of the bag) was prepared like pasta.  When I looked at the pack for a cooking time, I didn't find any, just the following statement: "Soak vermicelli for one minute at room temperature before cooking."  Otherwise, no cooking instructions whatsoever.  Well, I soaked the stuff at room temperature for a minute and it was still hard, brittle and not especially edible, so I tossed it into the boiling water for two or three minutes and it softened up.  So I drained out the water and discovered that the bag of vermicelli was now like a soft ball of vermicelli twine that I had to cut up to eat.  I mixed the vermicelli with grated parmesan cheese and garlic sauteed in olive oil, then added some spicy chili sauce.  Overall, it ultimately tasted good, but it wasn't up to Thai restaurant caliber.  The packaging should be more explicit about how to prepare the vermicelli.

I was very satisfied with this texture of this product. Being gluten free, I know that it can be hard to find pastas that hold up well to boiling and other preparations. This held up well and had a good, slightly nutty, flavor. I used this in vegetable sushi and in a broth based soup, both were very good and I will be looking for more of this product.

I got one package of Peacock Brown rice Vermicelli free from the Amazon Vine program, in exchange for writing a review of the product.I thought this product would be a healthy way to eat pasta, and it reminded me of Asian rice noodles when I removed it from the packet.  We like brown rice and try to eat whole grain pasta, to add complex carbohydrates to our diets.I soaked it for a minute as directed, then added it to a hot wok, along with sesame oil, shrimp, chopped green onion, precooked chopped bok choy, a little soy sauce and ginger.  I tossed it gently for a minute and thought perhaps it would soften up a bit with the oil and heat, but all it did was turn into a clumpy glob.  We did manage to eat some of it, and pick out the shrimp and vegetables, but none of my family liked this product at all.  It was basically tasteless in addition to being gummy.I've never seen any type of noodle go from crunchy and breaking into pieces, to a gummy wad of glue so fast!I won't be buying this product in the future.

These noodles were perfect for our family when we were on a gluten free, dairy free diet.  Its hard sometimes to locate noodles and other items on this diet and when you do, they don't always taste that great.  I found this product very simple to prepare and a great option for recipes I use for dinner.  The bag I received was a 7 ounce bag, which isn't very big.  Looking at the product description, this is a pack of 12, not just one bag.  The size is perfect for a family meal.  I'm not a huge fan of brown rice, so the taste was a little blah, but for gluten free noodles - it was ok.

I never had a brown rice vermicelli before but these noodles were not a disappointment. They were delicious. This is a product I would probably buy after Receiving from Vine. It was good quality and it didn't need much extra to make it taste good, it stood on it's own, even plain, just put a little olive oil and garlic and you got a great meal and you don't even have to really boil the noodles.It's not something I'd eat everday but as far as taste and quality i'd give it about a 4.5. Also easy preparation. Highly Recommended.

column9: Tastes vaguely of cardboard, and the noodles went soggy fast
column10: First off, these are skinny, skinny noodles, more slender than normal wheat vermicelli, and as such much more delicate. The bag they came in did nothing to keep them from shattering in shipping, and every time I picked up the package I felt like I was breaking them more.Definitely read the directions when you go to prepare them. They say to soak for one minute and then basically just heat them up in whatever dish you're making. They need pretty much zero cooking, so would be great for making fast or on-the-go meals.But for dinners where you are home and happy to wait, other rice noodles are better. These have a slightly dingy flavor, probably from the fact that they're made of brown rice, and get soggy and pasty super fast. They ended up soaking up so much water that they tasted watery and made my Asian-inspired sauce taste bland. I'm used to cooking Asian rice noodles since we try to eat gluten-free, and while these aren't the worst I have tried, I'd prefer most brands over this one.I'll give it three stars for the fact that if I were to make my own instant ramen to take somewhere, this would def. be the brand I'd choose as they don't really need to cook like other brands do.

column9: Accidentally soaked the whole package...and was able to cook the rest the next day.
column10: My daughter was helping me make lettuce wraps and she soaked the entire bag of noodles before I could tell her I only wanted to use half.  We drained and refrigerated them, thinking they would most likely be mush by the time I got around to using them.  The next day, they were still firm and ready to use with no ill effects from being wet an excessive amount of time.  And, BTW, they were really good in the lettuce wraps!  We didn't have bean threads, so we decided to substitute these noodles instead.  Everyone raved over the recipe...it's highly seasoned, and the noodles absorbed all that good seasoning.  Yum!
I enjoyed the product.  It was tasty and easy to fix.  Add a little bit of chicken and you have a meal.  I liked the fact the product was gluten free.

I used these noodles in soup, to make it stretch further.  The noodles didn't have much of a taste on their own, because they soaked up the broth around them and tasted good.  They went nice as a filler in soup, but I have yet to make them by themselves. I'm not much of a pasta person, so I thought soup was a good use for the vermicelli noodles.

column9: better than yo' mama's traditional pasta
column10: So, I thought this would be REALLY hard to make/use with my cooking. I was DEAD. WRONG. This is SUCH a tasty and enjoyable "dish," or rather, it makes for a great dish. When you cook it - I'd HIGHLY recommend using a skillet, although I suppose one could use a wok - it picks up the flavour of the other foods around it and the seasoning just cooks into the noodle, whether you add it in after the noodles are in the skillet, or whether the seasoning from the meat (or I suppose tofu - though I've not yet tried it with tofu) seeps into the noodle. The noodle itself you only really have to soak for a minute or two to soften them, drain the "noodle," and then throw it in the skillet with your meats and/or veggies.There are two suggested recipes that are on the back of the package for which one can use the vermicelli. The one I based my trial off of was the seafood, but I didn't have seafood, so I just used a chicken breast that I seasoned (with garlic powder and [Mexican] chili powder - seasoned to taste preference) and cooked in a skillet. Instead of olive oil, I tried coconut oil - since a friend had recommended using that and gave me a sample - and BOTH using the coconut oil to cook the chicken AND cook the veggies and vermicelli made it taste FABULOUS! *And I am NOT a fan of coconut at all.The recipe doesn't specifically call for much but chili pepper (if memory serves correct,) HOWEVER, you can add whatever you want in, I'd suggest adding it in with the garlic (or just have the veggies without the garlic) cooking over medium heat for a short bit before adding in the vermicelli and meat of choice (for now, I'd strongly suggest chicken.) Or, you can just have the veggies and vermicelli.However you choose to cook it, ANYONE will love it! I cooked some for a dear friend of mine when she was feeling sick and didn't want to eat anything, and she ate it and liked it - well, maybe she loved it, but I wouldn't know since she didn't express it directly - and was VERY appreciative that I shared. I also made it another time for a friend of mine who is borderline celliac; she could ACTUALLY eat it! She LOVED it and was so thrilled that I had found something else that was gluten-free and complimented me on "always finding great-tasting, gluten-free food." Anyone from any walk of life or dietary problems can eat it and enjoy it. Best part? You can mix and match the seasoning and other add-in items you so wish to cook it with.I'd HIGHLY recommend it and honestly, I would hands-down buy more of this the next chance I get!*The whole package roughly makes 4 or 5 adult servings....depending upon how big the portions are.

First off the noodles get very broken up from the packaging (probably the shipping and handling), so you wind up with nearly a quarter of a bag at the bottom in small pieces, the other problem is that they just do not have much flavor and they do not offer a great texture to the meal.  I tried to make these with some teriyaki and chicken stock, and they came out mushy and flavorless, they do not seem to absorb and flavor from the dish and they get soggy like and do not hold up after cooking.  I frequently enjoy making noodle dishes and have never had noodles that came out so bland and textureless as these did, even when cooked with intense flavor items.  I much prefer Maifun Rice Sticks, and will probably stick to them for future entrees.Maybe in certain dishes you can make use of these noodles, but for the meals that I like, I will have to continue to use Rice Sticks and Chinese Noodles.  My only other flaw with these noodles is that they get crushed in their packaging, and causes for the majority of the noodles to be broken at the bottom of the bag.

These are some of the best noodles I've ever tried. I loved them a lot, and I really love noodles!I think that the brown rice is why they're so delicious, because they seem more substantial, and they seem like they have more taste than other noodles. They would work as part of a very fancy meal, or they'd be a great addition to any dish. They tasted delicious. They didn't taste 'healthy.'Pros:+Delicious noodles+Can be part of a very deluxe meal+For thin noodles, they keep their shape and hold a good texture very wellCons:-Each package doesn't have a ton of noodles in every package

I used these noodles to make a gluten free "cup o soup".  They cooked super fast in chicken broth and tasted great.  I had no issues with them making the broth too starchy.  Though this was a review item provided to me via Vine, I would not hesitate to purchase this product to use in my gluten free cooking.  They are very thin, so you'd definitely need the whole package for a meal.  However, if you're cooking for one, half a package was adequate for my needs.

i'm a big fan of asian cooking, and enjoy experimenting with various types of noodles for various meals (soups, stir fry, etc.).  these noodles are a nice addition to that mix, have a pleasing taste and cook easily.  highly recommended for your various cooking needs.

column9: Easy to prepare but not much flavor
column10: This product is very easy to prepare - soak in water then add to stir fry / veggies / meat... but there is not much flavor - even plain brown rice has a little flavor to it.  This product tastes like they processed the rice so much that they squeezed out all the flavor and left only the outer film of the rice to roll into noodles.  We mixed these noodles with sauteed veggies and shrimp with sesame oil, soy sauce, garlic salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes but still needed to add more to get a decent flavor.  Once we did, they were fine and the meal tasted good.

I love brown rice and I love trying new foods so when I saw that they came out with a brown rice vermicelli, I knew that I had to get my hands on it. I cooked it up for dinner one night with some veggies and stir fry chicken and I have to say I was pretty disappointed. While the package makes it seem like the product will be light and fluffy, the actual vermicelli was pretty heavy and also like whole wheat angel hair pasta. Now, I love my rice sticky but there's a difference between sticky and glumpy...this was glumpy. I had my partner try it just to make sure that it wasn't just me and she said that she found it to be almost slimy. I added tons of veggies and spices and yet it seems like there was no taste. I have tried this recipe before on brown rice and it's exceptional so I knew it wasn't the recipe I used. I saved the leftovers to have for lunch the next day but when I heated it up, the noodles just got more lumpy and stuck together.Overall, I don't think I had a great experience with this product. While the first couple of bites were okay, the rest of the meal was a let down.

I have never made this type of noddle before.Although I have made Brown Rice pasta before.It is easy to over-cook Rice pasta, and then its mushy.I like that this is Brown Rice, which is healthier then white rice.This Peacock brown rice does not have any gluten in it,which is a realplus for people that have to eat Gluten free, as my Son does.All rice pasta is Gluten Free, and All Pasta is fat and cholesterol free.I soaked the pasta for a few minutes in hot water. Drain, saute in Olive Oil & Organic coconut oil. Seasoned with  allot of Garlic, Herbes De Provence, Onions, sliced Crimmi Mushrooms, Red bell pepper,a little Sea Salt, Lemon Pepper, then added fresh cooked ocean Salmon..What can I say, it was tasteful, not too dry, and very good..If anyone usually cooks white pasta, the brown rice has a different texture to it.

I have to admit I have never cooked with rice noodles before but have liked them in Thai dishes in restaurants.  I followed the directions for soaking the noodles prior to cooking with them but the noodles remained hard.  I did not care for the recipes on the package so created a stir fry out of ingredients I had on hand.  Needed to add a lot more liquid to the dish as I was cooking to get the noodles to have the texture of noodles instead of pretzels.  We liked the finished product OK but I would be leary of trying these again without cooking guidance from someone else who has used them.

My family found this to be a nice change from traditional pasta.  And still quite different from having regular brown rice.  The strands are very thin, and the cooking directions are vague, so we initially overcooked the vermicelli resulting in a too soft texture.  But this was easily corrected.  Nice with regular spagetti sauce, for a variation on the usual spagetti, or try with with Asian sauces.  Really good with seasame oil.

I made a Thai curry dish and needed something to go with it for dinner.  Usually I make brown rice.  However, I was anxious to try brown rice noodles.  These are perfect.  I let it sit in a bowl with warm water for several minutes and later added the softened noodles to the curry dish.  The texture was perfect and tasted great.  I will definitely purchase again in the future

column9: The texture is strange. They don't cook as quickly as they say.
column10: Honestly, I've tried very few rice pastas, but this one wouldn't win me over.  The texture was rough and grainy, even after 5 minutes of soaking in very hot water.  The directions said to warm them for 1 minute in "warm" water (no temperature indicated).  We did over 5 minutes in water at 120 degrees to no avail. The noodles were still pretty chewy and has a slightly grainy, raw-ish feel even heavily immersed in coconut milk broth.  Wouldn't buy again, especially for the price.

column9: Dreadful Product that Ruined a Previously Flawless Recipe
column10: We tried this product with a favorite family recipe.  I followed the instructions for preparing the vermicelli (soak in room temperature water) before tossing it in with the various ingredients which were not very different from the two recipes on the back of the package.The end result was dreadful.  So bad that one person couldn't even swallow because the texture of the noodles was off-putting.  This is a recipe we've used with different types of pasta--everything from rice noodles, egg noodles, whole wheat, low carb.  This is the first and only time we hated the end result.Hugely disappointing there are two good things I can say about the product:1) The packaging opens very easily2) You get a lot of vermicelli from what seems to be a small packageOf course, what's the point of having a lot of something you don't want to eat?  And if I'd known how really bad the end result would turn out to be, I'd probably have left it in the package, no matter how easy it was for me to open.

I have tried many types of noodles and vermicellies and this one by far the best one. It is very easy to prepare (only took me about 20 minutes to get my meal ready). The season is just enough, not too light, not to salty. And did I mention that it tastes awesome? The only drawback is that it's kind of dry. But if you have it with some sauce, it would not be a problem.

These noodles cooked literally in about 2 minutes, very nice and easy. They were a good flavor and texture, not rubbery at all. I put them with some veggie chicken and alfredo sauce and it paired really well. It is a big amount, and would be hard to break up or keep for leftovers, so I recommend waiting until you have a few people to feed before using it.This is a great alternative to other kinds of noodles, they are much more nutritious with the same flavor. I did not brown mine (as you are supposed to do with vermicelli, I found out), and they tasted just fine.

I love to eat the skinny little rice noodles in Chinese take-out meals. I had not been adventurous enough to try making the same thing at home. Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli gave me an opportunity to do that. I combined the vermicelli with Green Giants' Valley Fresh Steamers Asian Style Medley, a pound of peeled frozen shrimp and some simple seasonings. Prep time was less than 20 minutes for four generous servings and the dish was delicious. I will use this product to make a quick meal for unexpected guests. (They'll wonder where I've hidden the take-out boxes.)
We cooked this with pork chops.  It has a good flavor and texture - it compares well with other good-quality vermicellis.

column9: Rice noodles for fun and profit
column10: Ok, the title doesn't make much sense, but there isn't much to say about rice noodles.  I had hoped these had more of the earthy taste of brown rice but were just as flavorless as the white rice varieties.  That's not bad as rice noodles tend to be a binder for a dish rather than the focus.  Rice noodles rehydrate quickly in dishes making them versatile for last minute meals.The packing for these was disappointing.  Instead of a cardboard box, these were packed in a poly bag and had significant breakage during transit.  Additionally, the noodles were in one big lump instead of multiple smaller conglomerations thus making it hard not to cook the whole bag.Overall a nice choice for those looking for something a bit healthier and try to avoid overly processed products.

I followed the package directions and was pleasantly surprised. My family enjoyed the taste and I enjoyed the fast, easy way to prepare it. In this day and age of gluten issues, it is nice to use a product made of brown rice. This is also a very versatile product, and the directions gives you many different ideas. Truly you can complement it with almost any source of protein or veggies.

column9: A quick gluten free good choice
column10: A dear friend of mine is on a gluten free diet, so I opted to try the sample of Peacock brand Brown Rice Vermicelli for her sake. She has tried lots of various gluten free vermicellis and has been disappointed by most.I've never cooked vermicelli in my life, let alone a rice vermicelli, so this was going to be a big experiment for us both.The package states it will make 3.5 servings, and they are right on the mark with that - full, deep soupbowl servings. There are two recipes on the back of the bag, both of which were enticing, but I didn't have all the ingredients for either, so I used what I had - grapeola oil and butter, minced garlic, roasted red pepper, and some sauvignon blanc, with fresh grated parmesan to sprinkle over.The only problem I had, due to lack of experience, was that I paid attention to the brief directions on the bag which said to "soften brown rice vermicelli in water at room temperature for 1 minute prior to cooking." I did this, and that's how the sauvignon blanc got quickly added to the frying pan after adding the noodles. They were still too hard and dry. In the future I would heat up some broth to just below simmer, then add the noodles for a minute - this way they would soften better and pick up additional flavor.However, my white wine rescue was successful, and although the vermicelli was a little chewy, it held and mixed the flavors very well. My friend said they were the best rice noodles she has come across yet, and she has tried a lot of different varieties. Because they cook up so quickly, she could grab a healthy meal with these noodles (and a few ingredients) before caving in to something bad for her digestion. She urged me to bring the bag to our nearest grocery store to see if they can find it and stock it for her.I was really pleased to have found yet one more healthy gluten free food item to support her well-being.

This is a good non-gluten noodle. It held up well in cooking and can certainly substitute for wheat noodles for those who must, or simply want to, use something with no gluten in it. The noodles have no flavor of their own; none. They take on the taste of what they are cooked with. The package is also generous in quantity despite the 7 oz weight. I was cooking only for myself to test trial this for Amazon so I simply broke off a handful. One package would make me many lunches. I had it with stir fried bok choi and spinach and mushrooms with curry  but it would easily also go in an Italian direction. All in all, a good product that does what it says it does. But it does not substitute for the flavor of traditional wheat noodles. There is just no flavor of its own at all. That is why I gave it 4 stars rather than 5. Aside from that it is an excellent product.

column9: A product in need of a better label
column10: Before I used this product in a recipe, I read a lot of reviews here since there is not a lot on the bag. And from the negative reviews and complaints about hard noodles, what directions that are on the bag do not seem very helpful. So I went to the positive reviews and looked for guidance there.My conclusion? Ignore the soaking instruction of one minute in room temp. water. Try hot or boiling water, for a couple of minutes, stirring to separate them. Then all was well.I used them in a shrimp and vegetable soup and added them at the very end, cooking a little more until I felt they were done for my taste.That being said, I still had a couple of issues with these. The noodle are very, very, very thin. Thinner than I would like.Also, the packaging, in a bag, does not provide adequate protection and a great deal of the noodle were broken to tiny, tiny pieces. Ok, for a soup I guess, but in say, a stir fry, no.I looked at other brands in the store today and they all used a much stronger package to protect the very delicate noodles.So not at all sure I would buy these again.

I liked this vermicelli - fast to cook and great in noodle salads and for really fast meals. As it's made with brown rice it was more apt for rice noodle dishes than for Italian vermicelli dishes, which is fine by me.While this is quite good, there are better packaged alternatives with larger amounts for lower prices. Shop smart, but if you want to try something different this isn't a bad option.

column9: Change of pace from American pasta
column10: When I ordered this, I thought I was getting vermicelli. It is more like asian spaghetti. I used this in chicken stir-fry and it was tasty. Some reviewers said they acted like glass noodles but mine batch was more like pasta. It was quick to make, so I made it last after I finished the meat and vegetables. When I want a change from rice, I would use this product.

I tried these noodles as part of a stir-fried vegetable and noodle dish last night. I was improvising a bit since I had never used this type of noodle before, but I was quite pleased with the results. The noodles take only a few minutes to cook right there in the frying pan, they taste good, and they really absorb the flavor of any sauces you put in the pan. I used some soy sauce and Sriracha Hot Chili Sauce to make a nice spicy, flavorful dish. Again, the flavor of the sauce really does permeate the noodles, and it does so pretty evenly as long as you stir it well when you're cooking.One thing to note is that the package says they should be soaked in room temperature water for one minute before cooking. The noodles will *not* be ready to eat at that time. Some other reviewers seem to have been confused by this part of the directions on the packaging, and I will agree that the instructions could have been clearer. If you do soak them beforehand as directed, they should cook very quickly.My basic process for cooking these was as follows:1) Stir fry some vegetables in large pan with a bit of oil.2) Add soy sauce or other sauces as desired.3) Add the noodles along with a little bit of water and stir until all of the water is absorbed.4) Keep adding water, a little at a time, until the noodles are as soft as you like them.The "add water" step does create a little bit of trial and error, but it seemed to work out all right. By combining some vegetables, sauce, and these noodles, I was able to make a delicious meal.

column9: Solid Core Product, But Far From Healthy and Tasty
column10: I am a huge fan of Italian cooking, as my slightly larger waistline will attest to, as I love to experiment with new ingredients and the Peacock "Vermicelli" (closer to Angel Hair, really) seemed like an interesting place to start anew.Unfortunately, my first experiment was in the heat of the moment with 20 minutes on the clock and I needed a quick bite before going to work.  Thanks to the small noodle size I was able to quickly cook the 'vermicelli' and mix it with blue cheese to make a quick meal.  It was a good meal that kept me full till I got home from work, which is good given my evening job keeps me on my feet for most of the night.My next experiment involved my usual spaghetti sauce al la fuente, which consists of me sauteing ground turkey in Taco Bell mild sauce with chopped pepper and Texas Pete (gives it a zesty tangy taste but neutralizes the Hispanic spices to it still tastes Italian), a very spicy but lovely sauce.  The noodles, given their gluten-free rice taste, was a very interesting mixture with my sauce as it tastes... well, bland.  In my experience, gluten-free products are typically very bland and require a literal grocery list of spices and herbs to give them any kind of flavor.  This is not necessarily a bad thing as my spices and mixtures seem to remedy the blandness, but the credit goes to my sauce and not the core product.Then there's the texture; it's literally like straw as it is super dry and very stringy.  Even after utilizing sea salt in the boiling water (tap water in North Dakota is notoriously bad) and using butter to dampen the noodles they still had a straw-like texture and a bland taste.  By the time I got them to taste good and feel better I had added enough extra ingredients, primarily butter, to nullify their health benefits.  It literally became a "happy heart attack meal," a term I typically reserve for anything served at Hardy's or Jack-in-the-Box.And don't think the fat and gluten-free labels make this thing healthy.  The 'vermicelli' are nothing but carbs and lots of them.  My mother, being a diet and nutrition expert, proved to me that noodles can be low in carbs and very low fat by purchasing certain pre-made packages that were found in the freezer at the local grocery store.  Not quite sure what they were called, but at the same cost per package as these, I will certainly go that route.All in all, the vermicelli was OK, albeit super bland, no texture, and a crap ton of carbs.  There are better solutions out there for less.

I regularly eat brown rice and whole wheat pasta so I was interested to see how this would taste.The first thing I noticed was that it was very thin and it resembled oriental translucent cellophane noodles. I soaked the whole pack in warm water for a minute and then made a large batch of soup with it. It didn't take long to cook but the long strands did shatter into one-to-two inch pieces. I tasted the noodles before adding seasoning and it doesn't have any distinguishing taste. But on the other side, it is like Tofu, in that it takes on the taste of the seasonings and sauce that you use with it.Would I buy it again? No. It's too expensive for what you get. But I might consider it if I was gluten intolerant.

My wife and I tried this out last night. She's a diabetic, so brown rice is supposed to be better for her than white. We had the vermicelli with some well seasoned pieces of beef.My wife thought the vermicelli was OK; her only real comment on it.Personally, I am not fond of brown rice. At least when I have had it, it seems drier than white rice. I had the same experience with the vermicelli here, expect where the beef we added to it was in contact with it, then it was softer and tasty.I also prefer vermicelli that is not quite as fine as the product here.All this being said, the product was OK. If you like brown rice, you might even like it very much.

Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli 7 ounce packAt first, I didn't know what Vermicelli was, let alone how to cook and serve it.  *Mother always said there would be Days like this...* :There are probably millions of ways to prepare Vermicelli, but I like to keep things simple -- especially since this would be my first time with Vermicelli.  So, for this review, I took out a large pot, added an envelope of dry soup mix ( Lipton Recipe Secrets, Savory Herb with Garlic ), 7 cups of water, lots of my favorite spices, a bit of salt, a tablespoon of real butter and a can of drained mixed vegetables.Brought the mixture to a boil -- lowered temp to medium.  Drained the water from the soaking (the instructions, on the package, suggest one soak Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli for a minute in water that is room temp. ) Vermicelli, and added it to the pot.  Gave the mixture a couple of stirs with a wooden spoon, and in about 3 minutes (that's all, the time, it took) all was done, smelling good and ready to serve.  :)I presented this wonderful little dinner with oven toasted garlic bread, a few large pitted black olives, a variety of cheese wedges and Wine of choice.Fast and Easy!The Brown Rice Vermicelli did not stick / clump, together or become gluey-- either cooking, or after being served, the color of the cooked product was aesthetically pleasing ( especially with the colorful, mixed vegetables ), and will probably look appetizing served on most any color or patterned dinnerware.Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli was a  Huge Hit, at my home! Everyone wanted seconds! Bon Appétit! 'nuf said.  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2012
Easy to work with.  Soak in water and done.  No need to boil water. The kitchen will say cool in this 90 plus heat.

I am sorry to be doing this; I hate giving poor reviews to products. I cooked this up last night into a horrible mush.  First of all, the cooking directions are vague at best, so I just cooked it the way one normally cooks pasta, only I cooked it for a very short amount of time, because the pasta strands are so thin.Even for boiling it for less than 5 minutes, it cooked up into a mushy gunk.  Well, I ate it.  I was hungry.  One of the worst pasta meals of my life.  In all honesty, I cannot recommend this pasta.

column9: Good Stuff If You Like Angel Hair Pasta
column10: A couple of reviewers had some criticisms of this rice product, but I just don't understand them. It's a good product. If you like angel hair pasta then there isn't anything to dislike about it or the packaging. I thought I'd try it but realized I didn't care much for angel hair pasta. But that isn't a criticism of the rice itself.

I love brown rice, I love rice noodles and I love vermicelli so I figured this product would be something I'd really enjoy.I'm disappointed.  The noodles are bland and straw like.  As others have noted the instructions/recipe on package are lacking in depth and clarity.  Just soaking doesn't create a nice pasta texture, but actually cooking them turns them into clumpy/mushy mess.  If you are looking for a gluten free substitute for wheat pasta to soak up the flavors of a great sauce this might work for you.

Since I really enjoy rice noodles and I love brown rice, Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli seemed like a natural hit. Definitely not.Using the fry method of preparation, I followed the recipe on the package and the noodles came out tough and tasteless. They didn't absorb the flavors of the other items in the dish (I substituted scallops for shrimp), and the texture (mouth feel) was an unpleasant, rubbery blob.Not giving up, I tried the soup directions, using chicken stock and green onions. Again, no flavor. A mouth full of Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli is like a mouth full of nothing, but it has calories. It did not absorb the flavor of the stock or onions, but in the soup the texture was more palatable.Before this, I wouldn't have guessed that there was a food that had absolutely no taste characteristics. Water is more flavorful than Peacock Brown Rice Vermicelli and has a much more pleasant texture (and I don't particularly like water).

The back of the package gives recipes that are not soup based, which is pretty out of the norm for my experience with gluten free vermicelli style noodles.  I decided to give it a try by tossing the noodles with garlic, pesto, and sun-dried tomatoes. The result was mush.  The noodles had no ability to stand up to cooking and had little to no taste.Bottom line: I would not buy these noodles. They may be OK in a soup, but I won't be spending the money to find out.

I probably would have liked these better had I not followed the directions on the package.  I've had quite a lot of brown rice pasta, and this one was fairly neutral, flavor-wise.  It generally took on the flavor of what I cooked with it.  The texture was bothersome.  Again, had I cooked them more in water and NOT followed the directions on the package, the texture may have been better.  As it was, after soaking them for the requisite minute, they came out like straw.  It only went downhill when I put them in the skillet.  They began to breakdown to mush immediately.  There are other brown rice pasta products, even very fine ones such as this one, (Annie Chun's Maifun comes to mind) that will hold up to cooking and handling.  From a gluten-free standpoint this pasta is a thoughtful gesture.  That's about all it has going for it.  I don't recommend it at all.

Peacock's Brown Rice Vermicelli is a fairly decent gluten-free substitute for pan-fried noodles.  They're a bit bland on their own, but with the proper sauce and other ingredients, makes a good central dish.  1 star off for being slightly less than tasty leaves these at 4 stars.Calling this true vermicelli is a bit of a misnomer; these are very, very thin noodles that are not really capable of being boiled.  Instead, they're best pan-fried, and do soak up the flavor of whatever you end up putting in with them.  I ended up using a variety of veggies, some olive oil, and a bit of cheese, and they worked out quite fine.On their own, they're definitely blander than your average pasta, but as a gluten-free substitute they're not awful by any means.  I'd still recommend Mrs. Leeper's Corn Pasta for those looking for a more pasta-type dish, but these aren't the worst thing to have in your cupboard for the more specialized cook.  4 stars.

I have never liked any brown pasta, and have always avoided vermicelli (because of its tendency to soggily clump together) so I was doubtful about these noodles. They are from Singapore so I tested by finally making Singapore Rice Noodles, one of my favourite dishes. It mixes shrimp, squid and barbecued pork with veggies in an unusual curry AND chili sauce, and very much requires vermicelli.The recipe said to soak the noodles in warm water for 4-5 minutes; the packet said 1 minute. After one minute they were still stiff, so I let them sit for five, then dumped them into a colander and left them for twenty minutes. (Not usually a good idea, especially with vermicelli.)Came time to add them to the wok, they were still perfectly springy and al dente, delightful to eat. They also tasted really good, though the recipe I was using wasn't subtle in any way, so most of their flavour was buried.What particularly delights me is that vermicelli has now been added to my repertoire; I'll shortly be ordering more of these.

column9: Very nice addition to my pantry and table
column10: I grew up enjoying Rice A Roni and it's vermicelli/rice mix. I've never heard of a Brown Rice Vermicelli so when this was offered, I jumped at the chance to give it a go. I just made a package of it and must say, I'm very pleased with both the taste and texture. Very simple to make a nice and healthy meal: I tried these plain to get a feel for their taste/texture, which was pleasantly nutty.
