Then, I put the Pesto/Sundried Tomato Sauce with Sauteed Shrimp I had made for it, mixed it together, and it turned out to be a stunning tasting and simple meal to pull together. I'll be adding this to my master grocery list app, for sure. It's nice to have something different than just rice or pasta for dinner. :)

These are really good vermicelli noodles, which are made out of brown rice.  They are very thin, and they taste really good.  This is gluten-free; therefore it is excellent for those people who are allergic to flour (wheat).  I am not allergic to flour, but I am just saying that it is good for those who are.  These can be used like regular pasta.I received mine today, and I was so excited about trying it.  I immediately cooked some of it; in fact, it was my dinner tonight.  I ate it with a can of tomatoes, just like I would have eaten regular pasta noodles.  It was really good and tasty.  And I loved the texture.There are so many different ways in which this brown rice vermicelli can be done.  I ate it with a can of tomatoes, but I am just thinking about all the things in which a person can do with it.  It can be eaten plain, or it can be made into Italian dishes, or into Asian dishes.  I am just thinking:  these noodles would be good in a skillet with broccoli florets and baby corns, slivered almonds or orange/lemon flavor.This is a product of Singapore.  I really enjoyed these noodles tonight, and I look forward to tomorrow.  I'll make it a different way tomorrow, probably something Asian.I highly recommend these noodles, whether or not you are allergic to flour.

I was disappointed, to say the least, in this product. When I prepared it, I ended up with a sticky mass. The package directions don't give much in the way of directions for cooking--just two different recipes. I obviously overcooked the product. It was such a gummy mess that I had to throw it away. I would not try it again unless the package directions were much more specific about how to use it.

column9: Makes a perfect little boring & virtuous meal
column10: What I'm about to describe is totally not what a normal person would do with this brown rice vermicelli (angel hair pasta) but whoever said I was normal!  It's certainly not anything like the nice pictures on the bag suggest, which is a stir-fry.  Now, THAT would be great and there are two nice recipes on the bag.  Here's what I did:  I soaked about half the bag in water and let it sit for a while.  Then I emptied a 32-ounce carton of Trader Joe low-sodium chicken broth into a large bowl, added the soaked vermicelli, and microwaved it until it was very hot.  Ate a nice little quick dinner.  I loved it.  The ingredients are (1) brown rice (2) sago starch (3) water.  Sodium is 2.4 mg per serving, sugar is 2.2g, fiber is practically zero at 0.6g.  Total carb which I don't care about but seems high but I don't know is 47.1g.  Made in Singapore.  Sure wish it were made in the USA.  Not an exciting meal but it was a quick and sometimes quick is key.  I gave it a 5 not because it was so fabulous in and of itself but because it was so simple to add to soup to have a filling meal with such little effort or thinking.  This would work with other soups, too, of course.  Next time I'll have it with Trader Joe low-sodium tomato soup and it'll be just as good a quick little meal if not better.

column9: With a few modifications to prep directions, these were pretty good.
column10: This is fairly easy to fix.  Soak it in warm water for a minute, then stir fry with veggies and oil.  Doing it that way, I found it way too dry (a lot like straw), but after adding a cup of water, they softened up (although a bit too much).  If I try these again, I'll add a bit less water.While these noodles lacked much taste of their own, They nicely soaked up the flavor of the Prima Taste Rendang Curry Sauce Kit.  I fixed the Rendang according to package directions, then this bag of vermicelli, then I mixed it all together.  It made for a tasty dish.  While these weren't quite as firm as wheat pasta, it served its purposed quite nicely.I like that this pasta is healthy, and that it doesn't have gluten is a plus for those with gluten intolerance.

Vermicelli is a quick cook item that traditionally was only as offered in a white pasta. While the brown rice is not as tasty, for the most part you really can't tell the difference. I tried this product in two separate dishes. Once as an alternative to spaghetti. And the other as part of a Mediterranean rice dishand both came out great! You are getting a lot of product in this package. The downside, sort of, is the instructions says you put the product in room temperature water. That did not work out for me. I had to boil water and cook for about 4-5 minutes to get it to the spaghetti like consistency I wanted to use it for. It's a great healthier alternative to white pasta.

column9: Good vermicelli, but cooking instructions are incorrect
column10: My wife made a traditional dish using these brown rice vermicelli, and it turned out quite good. Noodle strands were separate (not mushy) and taste wasn't any different from regular rice vermicelli.My wife mentioned that if the vermicelli was cooked exactly as instructed on the package, noodles would come out too dry and hard. She said sha had to add some (about half a cup) more water during the preparation of the dish. That made the noodles soft enough, but still not mushy.I recommend this product considering the health benefit of brown rice and the taste.

This is a fair product that I probably would not buy again. We stir-fried it up with chicken, veggies, and some soy sauce. It was a really good meal and if you need something to add substance to your meal that is healthy and gluten-free, this product is great for that. If you are not use to diet food or don't have to watch out for gluten-free products, I don't think you will like it. The noodles are dry, and taste rather bland.

I made a chicken and vegetable stir-fry in my wok and then added the vermicelli to make a delicious asian dish. It was easy to prepare and tasted much better than the white vermicelli I was used to using and a whole lot more healthier. I am thinking of using this with a little parmasan and herbed oil and gilled chicken with brocolli for another tasty and heathy meal.

Since my sister is a diabetic we try things that say free of flour, good fiber and good taste.  This product fills the bill as long as you serve with a flavorful sauce and veggies plus meat of choice.  It does have a better mouth feel if cooked slightly longer and was great as leftovers after sitting in the sauce.I have made the soup with these noodles too and it was very good as long as the broth carried the flavor.

column9: Toss in a nice olive oil with tomato and basil
column10: Nice very thin angel hair pasta! Haven't had this since I went gluten free!Needs a little something something for flavor.  Cooks FAST. Like, superfast!  Gotta watch the pot and don't forget to soak it first.  (I didn't the first time and it was fine, but not as spectacular as it could be).Totally worth a try!

I just purchased this product through Amazon. I have thus far only tried one dish--rice-a-roni. I found a recipe online and tried it out. Of course, my disappointment with the dish may be because of the recipe, so do keep that in mind.Main point? The rice-a-roni was very bland. Again, perhaps the recipe. But it did not inspire me to look at the brown rice vermicelli as a great ingredient. I have, however, a few additional recipes that I intend to use. Perhaps those will be more satisfying.So, this evaluation of the product is still "in process."

This is a great product if you re trying to avoid gluten. I like brown rice and that's probably why I like the taste of this vermicelli. The prep instruction could have been better, but otherwise the packaging was good. I found that soaking the noodles for about 15 minutes in warm water was best--giving them a softer texture. I may try parboiling them. These noodles work best with oriental seasonings and sauces. Obviously too delicate to stand up to heavy Italian sauces. I used Franks Sweet Pepper sauce with shrimp and oriental veggies and it was delicious!

Thankfully it is getting easier to find great tasting gluten free products. we have two members of our family who can't eat gluten due to medical issues so we have to shop with that in mind. Many gluten-free offerings taste dodgy or "off" but this product is an exception. We had this for dinner last night and it was great. We served it with shrimp and tomato sauce and everyone loved it. We will definitely get this brand again next time we have a chance.

I had to soak this for at least 8-10 minutes before it became tender enough to use in the cooking process.  I do love rice noodles and cook them up regularly, they are usually thicker so this is a nice alternative if you wish to make a more delicate dish. These were ok in texture but a bit gummy if over cooked in sauce. I made a black bean and pepper dish which was good as a side. Nice sized bag for 2 people for main dish or you can use twice for side dishes.

The instructions on this package state that it needs to be soaked in luke warm water for 1 minute before serving.  I was skeptical this would work and should have listened to my gut.  After 1 minute soaking it tasted like uncooked pasta  I left it to soak for 10 minutes with no improvement.  Other rice noodles I've worked with need to be either cooked for a few minutes or soaked in hot water, which I definitely would have tried if I hadn't used it all with the first method (I only had one bag to sample).  So buyer beware that the cooking instructions are wrong.Otherwise it seemed like it would be a good product if it were properly prepared.  Peacock should do a little taste testing and redo the instructions and they would probably have a great product.

I used this cake as a base for a charity sale right after the Christmas holidays.  I cored the center making the cake into a large bowl.  I filled the center with a zaballione custard.  We sliced the cake into 24 pieces.  It was a beautiful thing.  Even with all the hundreds of other items available. all this cake was sold in about 10 minutes.  The cake was fresh, well-packed, and very flavorful.  I highly recommend this item.
this 2 lb. cake has excellent texture, consistancy, fiber content, moisture, flavor and does not lose its freshness during storage time while in use.
Closer to cake like, than bread like. Moist and tasty, but the Bellino brand gave you two of the 2 lb panettone cakes for the same price. I have purchased the Bellino again. It was great.

column9: Panettone Cake should be an all year round product not just for Christmas!
column10: I've tried a number of different Panettone products and this one is excellent.A break on shipping charges would be welcomed. The 5 cakes which I ordered arrived in good time and in great shape. Thank you. Almost time for a reorder!

Delicious to smell, delicious to taste. This tea brings the invigorating taste of mint with the healthy benefits of green tea.While this is loose tea it is not, however, whole leaf. I did not have a problem with my infuser catching the tea but others might need a finer infuser.Excellent tin with a plastic cap under the top. I will definitely buy this again.

...but it's thin mint tea! I'm not into the chocolately-mint taste. Also, the packaging was a little weird. The tin was nice but had a sticker label placed over the original label. Who knows what's going on there...

column9: Princella yams now stringy, no longer good
column10: I have purchased Princella brand sweet potatoes/yams for years because I could always count on their quality.Not any more.There were stringy, cotton-like sweet potato "threads" all through the can.  I tried chewing them with the sweet potatoes but that didn't work because the threads were left after the sweet potato was chewed and swallowed.It was like trying to eat a washcloth.  It made me gag.I am really disappointed.I don't think I will purchase them again.

Fireballs are the only candy worth eating.  That's why I ordered this 5 pound container.  What I received was the standard hexagonal, 200 count container sold all over amazon for a little lower price.  The original package label indicates 3 lbs 15 oz, which is accurate (confirmed using my shipping scale).  Bottom line, fireballs rule, but you can find this same package for cheaper.Atomic Fireballs: 5LBS

The fireballs are much smaller than they appear.  In other words, they are not the usual size of fireball - they are miniatures.  Not what I expected - never would have ordered had I known they were so small.

column9: These are the small Fireballs, not the large ones.
column10: I have nearly finished my container of Ferrera Pan atomic fireballs, and ordered this package to refill it.  The package arrived, and to my disappointment, these were the small size fireballs, and not the larger size shipped with the candy jar container.These are the same firey hot cinnamon candies provided in the container, but it would be nice if the product specifications clearly stated that they were the smaller of the two sizes.Other than that, they're great.

I just received my HUGE bag of candy!  I forgot how great these things were.  I placed my order late Saturday night at 10:45 PM and my package got here Wednesday at 12:45 PM.  I used regular shipping and I am quite impressed and how fast this order was completed.  I will use this vendor again.  I got what I ordered although I didn't expect the bag to be SO big.  :)

column9: Atomic Fireballs:Greeaattt!Atomic Fire Balls. They wereexactlywaht the doctor ordered.
column10: The Atomic Fire Balls I ordered from Ferrara were exactly what I was looking for after finding "Sams" had disconued carrying them in bulk.
Great fireballs.....very hot! They are the small ones but they are perfect. I'll be ordering these again and again. Pretty decent price for all you get!

I am blown away at just how fast I received my shipment of atomic fireballs.  I placed my order in the early morning hours of wed 9/21/11.  Not only did my order ship within hours but here it is 2 days later and I already have my shipment!  WAY TO GO, will definitely order again!

column9: Looking for the old school Trident Bubble Gum
column10: I live in Panama City Beach, Fl and was wondering if anyone knew where I can score some of the old school Trident Bubble Gum. I've chewed this kind for about 10 yrs so I'm a huge fan. The new ones on the shelves is like chewing gum now...you can't blow bubbles with it and it falls apart after 2 hrs. I'm tempted to buy through Amazon but I don't want to buy a 12pk of crap bubble gum flavored chewing gum. HELP!!!

column9: Coffee lover -- but it has to be decaf
column10: I discovered Cafe Bustelo when vacationing in Flordia.  Good decaf is hard to find, and this is really great decaf. It's called expresso (but not as dark), fine ground, and the taste is  full bodied.  It's not available where I live, so I'm really glad that Amazon stocks it.

I have been drinking Cafe Bustelo for a couple years, upon the recommendation of an ex-barista friend of mine. It appeals to me on two levels: 1) incredible richness of flavor (even the decaf) 2) darned cheap.I use a wide variety of beans for my coffee and espresso, some expensive ($15 a 10oz can) -- but Bustelo is up in my top two (alongside Illy).  It is always a mile down the street at the supermarket when I need it at a cheap $4.00.  Amazing crema when you make espresso.  Great for a super strong iced coffee.  Also wonderful in a French press.You really can't go wrong.Specifically, Bustelo Decaf if top-notch.  I struggle with insomnia, therefore I avoid caffeine after noon-time.  But, I want my double-shot when I get home from work.  Bustelo Decaf is my after-work grind of choice!Works amazingly in my Breville Roma Espresso Machine --see review if you are looking for a great, inexpensive machine.Check out my food blog [...]

Every single person who loves a rich, complex, full-bodied coffee (not the "morning blend" types) has said they LOVE my coffee, even those who insist they don't like decaf coffee.  I only drink decaf, and this is hands-down the very best I've ever tasted anywhere.  Biggest problem for me is that it raises the bar, and I rarely enjoy coffee anywhere else but at home!Even though it's called espresso, I use this as others use regular coffee (one scoop/tablespoon per cup) in a drip coffeemaker... YUM!Glad to see Amazon offering it in case it becomes impossible to find locally (it can be hard sometimes - seems I'm not the only one in love with it who buys several cans at at time).  But be aware that they're charging a premium here and you should be able to find it for under $4.00/can in your grocery store IF they carry it.  Check in the Spanish/Mexican section if it's not in the regular coffee section...

I think this is a good decaf for the price. That said, it's not great. I've had better decaf, just not at this price. I bought the four-pack because I love the regular Cafe Bustelo but my supermarket didn't carry the decaf. The decaf is not up to the standard of the regular, but it's good, and who can afford to pay $12+ per pound for the really good stuff all the time? Not moi.

I had purchased one can of decaf esspresso and when I needed it again it was discontinued due to lack of sales. I checked everywhere and thought let's try Amazon,I always have good luck there. Surely enough there it was and it was a pack of four for 20 something anyway it was a great price. now I can have my cafe con leche whenever the whim strikes because I know I will find it again on Amazon.

column9: Rich flavor - you won't believe it's decaf
column10: Very nice flavor - rich, but not bitter. It is ground very fine, which makes it a good choice if you have a Senseo. It's more full-bodied than Mellita (my other favorite ground decaf) but slightly more acidic. Oh the other hand, it is priced better (I get it at Wegmans for a very nice price).Highly recommend if you like rich-tasting decaf.

If you like the flavor of cardboard, then you will like this because that's what it tastes like. I like coffees that are strong flavored...this is not it as it has little flavor at all.  I guess the saying is true..."You get what you pay for" price is cheap and it tastes cheap.  I'm sorry I bought it.  Please contact me if you would like one opened can and one sealed can and I'll give it to you for free.  Actually, I wouldn't want to give this to a homeless person because I'd hate to put them through the unpleasant taste.  Surprising to see some people said they like it.  Wish I could have agreed with them.  Opened one of the cans, it didn't even leave an aroma which was my first clue that it would probably not even have a pleasant taste.  Then I tried several varied amounts in the brewing process thinking that eventually I would get a decent tasting cup of coffee.....NO SUCH LUCK!!! I ordered based on the other reviews here on Amazon.  Worst coffee I've ever tasted and comes close to the taste of coffee aboard some NAVY ships where the coffee has been brewing for about 5 hours or more.  I strongly recommend others to avoid this brand and try something else.I normally like to use whole beans and ground them myself...this is the first step to making truly flavorful coffee. If you use paper filters, let a cup of water run through them then empty the carafe and then put your freshly ground beans in the filter and brew. This process takes out the mill-dust that all paper filters have in them which will taint the flavor of the coffee if you don't do this process. As for store brand coffee, I would recommend the selection at Kroger called Spotlight or the other called Private Select. A good non generic store brand coffee is Community Coffee. If you are fortunate to have a Central Market grocery store near you, try the fine selection of whole bean coffees.

I recently bought a sno-cone machine to help me cut back on calories yet cool me off when the weather heats up over 100 degrees outside. To save even more calories, I wanted to use sugar-free syrups. I have tried the Back to Basics Sugar-free syrups and they are pretty watered down tasting. I was pleasantly surprised how sweet and tasty the Jelly Belly Sugar-Free Apple was! I am in love and will be buying the 3 pack next time to save money.
Kids love the syrup but you can get it at Bed Bath & Beyond for $2.99.  We have also tried blue raspberry and green apple.  Nice thick syrup.

We recently bought a snow cone machine for my daughter.  I wanted to join in the fun, but I have been on a low-carb diet for almost 2 years.  I noticed there were a number of manufacturers making sugar-free snow cone syrups, but I chose Jelly Belly because I assumed that they would make a great-tasting syrup.  I was not dissappointed.  This one tasted as good as I have ever tasted a sugar-free product.  I have since ordered several other of their sugar-free flavors.  Thank you Jelly Belly.

column9: Ack! Did they not test this flavor?
column10: I bought Very Cherry and Berry Blue from a local retailer and they were horrible.  I tried the Cherry twice and the Berry once before I dumped them in the sink and refilled the bottles with home brew syrup made with Kool-Aid.  Don't waste money on this, especially at this price.
Do not buy the sugar free versions! They impart a strong chemical after taste. Kids hated it and never finished the snowballs.

Its OK. It tasted more like sugar than pina colada :( i was a lit bit dissapointed. maybe because it was sugar free so it wasnt as tasty or good as I have expected it. But it really tasted like watery sugar.
I tried the product since I can no longer eat sugar thinking it would be a good substitute. It tasted too heavy and too sweet I did not enjoy the product and will not purchase again.

In a word,  HORRIBLE.  This stuff no more tastes like Apples then do my hiking shoes.  This stuff is nasty, it has a sweet chemical-like taste that is just yucky.  Can I say anymore about how I dislike the taste of this overpriced product?  How anyone could buy this stuff more than once is beyond me.
You can get the exact same product at Wal Mart for 2.50 why would anyone pay almost 13.00 dollars for snow cone syrup?....crazy!

This coffee is awesome! The first time I drank it, my friend & I giggled for 2 to 3 hours. This stuff has got more caffeine than any energy drink on the market today. I've tried most of them & this coffee truly lives up to its name! Beware of the after effects... I definitly crashed after the caffeine wore off!

WOW is all I can say, after drinking this coffee I was UP and READY to GO !!!!  Perfect for shift-workers who need to stay awake.  Bold flavor, dark roast, full strength you will not need to add an espresso shot with you afternoon coffee craving.  The world just does not move fast enough after you have a cup of this coffee.  Enjoy ;)

column4: Mommy of Cuties M & Z "Mom of Twins"
column9: ~*~*~My Girls LOVE these, PERFECT SIZE for Little Fingers~*~*~
column10: When we first started giving these to our daughters we had to keep a very close eye on them(as with any solid food) because sometimes they would start choking and we would have to stick our fingers in their mouths and get these out.These do 'dissolve' pretty easily but your baby may take a little getting used to eating them like mine did. But in no time they knew how to eat these with OUT choking. I think at first they were just trying to swallow them before they got wet and 'dissolved'.We have bought Walmart Store Brand & these Gerber Puffs. Walmart Brand is Good but Gerber brand is GREAT! The Gerber Puffs are bigger making them easier for tiny fingers to pick them up, yet they are still a small enough size for them to eat. Walmart Brand have a lot of broken pieces so many of the pieces are tiny and my girls can't pick them up to eat them, I don't know that I have ever found a broken Gerber piece. I think Gerber stays fresh longer, it seems not too long after I open a Walmart Brand they are stale feeling.Since I have twins we go through these fast so we've found it much cheaper to order them in bulk.These keep my girls happy while my husband and I eat or get things done. Even if I have just fed my girls, if they see us eating they will have a fit. We put some puffs on their walker or high chair trays and they are Happy again. We even pour these in their play pen & they don't even make a mess. At a restaurant if my girls are getting fussy, we'll keep giving them puffs and they are happy. We give them puffs while we are heating their food, if not they'll normally throw fits until we are feeding them.We've tried the Gerber flavors: Bananna, Strawberry/Apple, Apple Cinnamon & my girls love them all.

Our little grandson loves his Gerber Sweet Potato Puffs. Sprinkle some on the table before him and he'll immediately start grabbing for them and putting them in his mouth. I like that they dissolve so readily, making them a safe non-choking hazard. The taste is actually pretty good though to me they taste more like orange than sweet potato.My only complaint, and it's not a major one, is that there is more sugar in the puffs than sweet potato. Yet, with only one gram of sugar in a half cup serving, this minor sin is forgivable.

I hesitated to buy this item, becuase its Ingredients include a little bit sugar..I don't like sugar products. If my baby get used to eating sugar, then he will try to eat sweet things.Anyway.. He likes it. :)
Puff are what I call Baby Crack. They aren't bad for your kid and is always a quick and easy snack. This flavor isn't our favorite but still one my son enjoys.
This is a perfect food for a baby who is stating on finger food.  Easy to hold and disolves in mouth.Gerber Graduates Sweet Potato Puffs, 1.48-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 6)

I got them at Wall-Mart for $1.83 a box. With subscribe & save would have cost me $2.38. Now, don't get me wrong, I love S&S, I signed up for a lot of things, but buyer beware, price is not as competitive as we're accostumed with S&S.
They taste great, even my 13 year old likes them.Easy to pick up, My 8 month old is learning to self feedDissolve quickly in the mouth, I like ALL of the Gerber puffs!

I wasn't sure how sweet potato flavored puffs would go over, but my son loves these. I started giving these to him around age 6 months, and the star shape seemed to be pretty easy for him to pick up. He also loves the banana and apple cinnamon flavors, too.

Our 11-month-old boy is teething and starting on solid foods. We've been giving him more and more solids for a number of months now. You'd be amazed at the things he loves to eat, such as french fries for example. In any case, my wife found Gerber's Graduates in a variety of forms and the boy seems to like them all to one degree or another.One of the varieties our boy likes is the Graduates puffs. They come in several flavors and the present ones we have are the apple-cinnamon. Previously we had some banana-flavored ones. In any case, the  specific flavor seems to make little difference. The little puffs are about 3/8 inch across and are star shaped. We give them to the boy one at a time, which gets somewhat tiresome. So, we place a small handful on his high-chair tray now and then. He attempts to get them all in his hand and then put them all in his mouth at the same time. What are you gonna do? He seems to like chewing them up, as best as he can, and we've had no problems with him choking or anything like that. It's a good product, but we, and the boy, prefer the Cheeto-like larger crunchies.Gary Peterson.

column9: I'm 21, but I eat them for myself. They're delicious!!
column10: I'm 21, but these are great snacks even for adults! I first tried them when my nephew was a toddler. My sister got him these all the time because he loved them. She told me "Try one for yourself. They're really good" so I did. They melt in your mouth within seconds, so this is great for toddlers and babies who can't chew very well yet. As for myself, I'm a constant snacker, so these are a great alternative for me so I don't gain weight. They have vitamin E, Zinc, Iron, and Calcium in them. This is great nutrition for your toddler or baby ... and myself as well I suppose haha.So far I have only tried Strawberry apple and banana. They truly do taste like their flavors they say they are. This is another reason it is a great snack for your little ones. It'll help cause a much easier transition from these to the real thing (real strawberries, apples, and bananas I mean).I highly recommend this product. It's great =)

I place order on 25 June 12 . But this snack expire on 18 sep 12.I order about 200-300 bottle of Gerber Graduate!I got only 2 mounth and a bit left for this flavor!!!!!!!!!!!!Poor!!!!!!Why you do with your royal costumer like this.I pay you a lot every mounth!Bad sale.If it almost expire just keep it away or send it to the bin.Don't give it to me.Waste of money!

Whoever said these are only for babies. I LIKE EM TOO! They're perfect for small munchies like me. Not too sweet and its whole grain. It doesn't really make me bloat like other natural food. But this, is delicious!
Puffs of strawberry apple flavor is the best food, open the can smell a hint of strawberry flavor, each puff of a shallow pink.The baby's favorite.

column9: Strengths than banana smell, no strawberries Apple delicious
column10: This cream puffs taste is very light, unusual taste, can not tell what that smell is.Best to eat or thanks to a strawberry apple.Strawberry puff of apple flavor is best to eat.

PROS-great to start as finger foods (easier than cheerios to pick up and eat)-dissolves quickly (less of a choking hazard)-baby loves them!CONS-stains!  As the baby drools on his hands or loses a half-eaten puff, it leaves a bright orange stain on clothing, rugs, etc.  Not easy to get out, and a lot of the other flavors are more neutral colored and do not stain as much as the sweet potato.  The last thing I want to do is have to wash his highchair cover and straps, rugs, clothes, etc because of bright orange stains all around.-cheaper versions available (ie, at Target they have their own brands)-does have sugar (I wish they can make a low or non-sugar version, because I'm pretty sure the baby will still eat them.  Why add unnecessary sugar into everything?)I started with the Gerber sweet potato, but I'll be sticking to the Target blueberry (because it's cheaper and doesn't stain)

We just started finger food but my baby still can't hold these puffs as they're very small she likes them but I agree that the apple one  has a very strong taste I think sweet potatoes are the best!in general it's a great and healthy snack

column9: My daughter loves these, a nice snack
column10: My daughter loves this product.  It is a nice snack and even when she was younger it seemed as though she had an okay time eating it.  I am also pleased with this line of products as a whole.  Also, while this is more expensive than generic brands, I know that my daughter preferred this to the Target brand item.
my 10mo daughter loves these little puffs. and i love that they just melt in her mouth and it doesnt make much crumbs. will buy this again.
My son loves these for self feeding and it's a good snack on the road, in the car or whenever you go to a restuarant and need to keep them busy. My son loves them, and even I do!
Great Puffs, babies love them, want to eat them all the time, distracts my son all the time especially if we go out the puffs keep him busy for a long time

My baby girl loves this little puff.  She's very attachy and she gets scared when I walk just a few feet away from her but if she has this on her hand she does not care if I am standing far from her.  She always finish her puffs before she goes back to whatever she's doing or watch.  This is even a great snack for adult, my sister and I both love this fruit puff.  The banana flavor is my favorite.BTW, where's the free prime shipping Amazon?
My son loves these and I love them too because they dissolve quickly and are an easy snack to take anywhere.

column9: Kid loves these and so do I
column10: My 1yo loves these and I like them two.  They are tasty.  The peach and the sweet potato ones are great

These puffs are great for a snack for my toddler. He loves all the flavors of these, but banana most of all. My husband and I even tried one ourselves to see what they were like. In my opinion, the banana aroma is much stronger than the flavoring. It's not a bad thing, there's just a very strong aroma of bananas when you open the container, so if I hadn't tried these myself, I would assume my son is getting a flavor (sugar) overload. That is NOT the case. There is just enough flavoring to make these good. My husband (who HATES fruit of any kind and refuses to eat it) actually said these weren't bad. Coming from him, that's a huge compliment.

i should have tried this flavor before buying bulk here.  my daughter loves puffs in general and she really liked the sweet potato ones we got before this one.  but the apple cinnamon flavor is a little too 'artificial' and strong. instead of grabbing them by the handful, she doesn't seem too interested to eat these..

My son has developmental delays, and these little puffs help with his fine motor skills. AND they taste good! I signed up for Amazon's subscribe and save and get 6 cans at a time. It saves me from running to the store to get them every week. They are also cheaper from Amazon with this program. The sweet potato flavor is sweet, but not too sweet. We've also tried the banana which has a "real" taste to it, rather than an artificial one.

Love these.  Not messy.  Not bad for baby.  Melt in his mouth. And come in plenty of flavors! Others have complained about not selling variety packs.  My son goes through them so fast that it is worth it buy a couple sets!
yummy, but not really much cheaper then walmart. my 7 month old LOVES them and will eat them all day long, perfect because they disolve so quickly he won't choke.

I got them when on sale so better price than off-brands. They taste great my daughter loves them. Toddler must have! Get the off-brand though like parentschoice or up and up if not on sale though cuz they are the same thing taste just the same just not as pretty packaging.

My baby (13 months) loves this flavor of Gerber Puffs. The flavor is mild and the texture is really easy for her to chew now. I've actually been giving my baby Puffs since she was about 5 months old and had no teeth. We've tried and approved of Strawberry+Apple, Banana, Sweet Potato and of course this one. We also tried and dislike Apple cinnamon (too sweet) and Cherry (too tart).

I bought this package for our 10 month old to practice self feeding and to have an easy snack on hand when traveling.  They are a step up from plain ol' cheerios!  She loves them and they melt quickly in her mouth.  The price was great with Amazon Mom and Subscribe and Save.

My 2 year old and my 8 month old both love these. I wish there were more calories in these but they are yummy and perfect for toddlers learning to feed themselves. Dissolves very quickly. The sweet potato and peach flavour are my favorites. :)

column9: Puffs Are Great For Early Self-Feeders.
column10: These little snacks are wonderful for little ones learning to self feed. They almost instantly melt in your mouth and I feel that under supervision pose very little choking risk. I had tried many things before these, from Cheerios to Nilla Wafers (crushed up) and nothing was even worth comparing to these puffs.  The sweet potato flavor is also very tasty, and my little one eats them up as fast as I let her!

My daughter officially gives these 5 stars - she just loves them.  These were her first finger food, and they remain her favorite.  I'll add my own 5 stars because they're an easy, convenient snack, and unlike Cheerios, they don't make a mess when the child is just learning to eat (the Cheerios were dribbling out of her mouth and onto her clothes); I suspect it's because the fruit puffs dissolve more quickly.  I'm not crazy about the price - 1.48 oz. isn't exactly a huge amount - but on the other hand, I don't give her that many, so a canister lasts a few weeks (vs. the recommended six servings).  Giving it in smaller quantities should also alleviate concerns about sugar in the product (sugar is the fifth ingredient in the banana puffs).

column9: good flavor, melts in her mouth
column10: When my baby got too big to eat mashed sweet potato--and didn't have teeth to eat it otherwise--I started giving her these. She loved the taste and the texture was crunchy enough to soothe her teething gums while still being soft enough to dissolve easily in her mouth. They're also a really great finger food. I put some in her tray and she'll eat as many as she wants and drop the rest on the floor, which we pick up and put in the bird feeder. Incidentally, the birds enjoy them too :)

my toddler loves them,they are convenient,perfect for sitters house or on the go,and my boy likes all of them.walmart has them under 3 a canister i think.i usually get them there.my star review is based o how much sugar they have.i prefer to give my kid flavored cheerios,they have less sugar and better on price,they just don't melt in your mouth or come in a convenient can.besides the sugar and price,i love them.but i do pretty much use all of the gerber toddler stuff for on the go,and  when i am home i try to use a different sub,like cereal,yogurt or what ever the mainproduct is for that specific gerber item.my dad and babysitter pretty much love to have these on hand for mess free convenience though.

This is a good idea, and they dissolve quickly for babies new to food. But if a partially slobbered on one falls out of the baby's mouth and onto clothing it leaves a stain that proves impossible to remove. The puffs have a bit of an orange coating on them, it must contain food coloring. I've tried organic puffs and they don't leave any stains.

I bought these because I like the idea of a veggie flavor over a fruit flavor.  They really are delicious, but they are very sweet.  They taste a lot like a kids cereal (which they kind of are).  I prefer the Plum and Happy Baby ones because they have half the sugar, and my 11 month old doesn't mind.  If I try to mix the low sugar ones with the Gerber, she will go for the Gerber.  If you don't care about the sugar increase (it is really small), these are tasty and your child will eat them.  If you care about sugar, go with Happy Baby.

column9: A good choice for new crunchers and munchers!
column10: I was pretty wild about these for awhile when my little guy started eating solid food; they dissolve easily and he has fun picking them up. If I put a bunch in his tray, he'll try to shovel them in, but if I put one at a time down he'll pick them up with a thumb and finger. He's fun to watch, learning new things.I do worry about the added sugar, so I've been holding back a little on these lately, offering them less often and giving him Cheerios instead. The Gerber/Nestle corn crunchies are a little up in the sodium, too. Kid snacks don't need that stuff, really, so I'm looking for alternatives, but I think these will still be around at our house for awhile; everything in moderation. :)

We used this as a first finger food with our twins and broke them into even smaller pieces.  Our babies had lots of teeth by 8 months, so they were able to chew.  The puffs melt down when sucked on, so it's a great first "real food" for the little ones.  The sweet potato is not "too sweet" as most of the other flavors are.  Even my older kids (ages 5 and 7) like to snack on these.  I never go anywhere in the car without them.  The star shape seems to be easier for the babies to get to their own mouths when just learning to self feed.
My son loves these. He practices his finger food skills on these and asks for more when I only give him a few at a time. He stuck them in his mouth second by second :)
It would be tremendously helpful to know the expiration dates of these food items... or is it written somewhere and i've missed it? thanks

This is certainly one of the best products from Gerber of all the ones I have used till now and I have used quite a few of them. My daughter is 10 months old and she totally loves it :) They dissolve easily in the mouth and thats the best thing about them. The flavours are also delicious! I totally recommed this product for every mom who wants to begin to teach their kid how to start having food by themselves.
I love these. My daughter goes crazy for them. I have to make her stop from eating them all at one time.

First, I don't have any children. In my mid 20's I bought Puffs for myself to snack on when I get hungry because the whole container has 150 Calories.It's very tasty and if I was a kid I would definitely want these. They melt in your mouth.

column9: Very delicious flavor, the cream puffs with spices
column10: Bananas taste very delicious cream puffs, after the openings have a very strong taste of the banana flavor, the taste is very light. The shape of a box in his pocket contained plum puffs, filled with very full.Amount to enough.Delicious strawberry apple.

I love all the Gerber Puff varieties and so does my son. I was eager to try the Sweet Potato to see how he would like them. He loves them!!! All was well until I removed him from his high chair and saw orange spots everywhere. He is learning to self feed and drools quite a bit so I when he was grabbing at them with his wet hands some of the puffs on the tray got wet. When I went to clean off the tray the puffs came off but everywhere there was a wet puff I now have an orange stain. I wouldn't be so mad of there was some kind of warning on the jar but I can't find one. I am really glad he was shirtless or I can't imagine what his clothes would look like.

I was going to buy this product here at Amazon but when I found it at my local supermarket on sale for $2.99 (as opposed to $8.75 per package here on Amazon), I bought it.  In short, this is a great product.  Overall, it has a very good flavor and did not notice any of that artificial or tinny after taste that some do.As stated above, I found this on sale.  Its regular shelf price was $3.99.  So, where the $34.98 (for 4 packages) comes from, I have no idea.  It is, also, really economical and "green" minded.  Each little tub, reconstituted as suggested on the package, yields 3 1/2 cups of stock.  That is one ounce short of 2 cans of broth from the grocery store and 4 ounces short of one of those 32 ounce cartons.  So, one little 4-tub package represents almost 8(!) cans (at 37 1/2 cents per can) or 4 packages (at 75 cents per package) and taking up a small fraction of the shelf space.  What is better is that this is stock, not broth.  So, there is a more complex flavor profile.  Also, I am thinking of taking them from my pantry and keeping them in my freezer in an effort to extend their shelf life.  Bravo Knorr!!

column9: Great Product But Cheaper In Local Supermarkets
column10: This is an excellent product to use in soups, stews, chili, gravies, etc. However, it only costs $3.79 in my local supermarket.
Everyone should have a pack of this in their pantry. It gives all your foods that slow cooked flavor we all love. I am so in love with it. I use it all the time.
All four of these had "sell by" dates which had (recently) expired.  I cannot recommend this to anyone who can't use them immediately.

column9: Good for a snack! (Not just for baby)
column10: I picked these up today and thought I would try them out for myself, since I don't have a baby.  They are pretty good, a lot of apple flavor with a nice texture.  I enjoyed them and plan to purchase more to use as a great snack.

These are very good. As an adult I use them as a fruit snack.  I can't believe that someone is charging 49.99 for an 8 pack!  That is over $6 a package!  They are under $3 in the local grocery store.If Amazon offers them in the future at a reasonable price I will order them but not from some outfit gouging people!

While they aren't my favorite fruits, I do enjoy bananas and I keep them on hand because I love to add them to my smoothies (I usually add a heaping teaspoon or two of Matcha to all my smoothies too).This matcha has a delicious banana-y flavor that isn't too sweet.  The sweetness is from the fruit flavor and the Matcha itself, but it doesn't taste candy sweet, at least, not to me ... although it does smell like banana candy when you first open the package and all the while during preparation.  But, I don't get that sort of taste from the Matcha and that's a good thing, at least in my opinion.The matcha does taste a little different with the banana flavoring.  The normal vegetative tones of the matcha meld with the flavor of the banana ... the fruity notes of the banana ... in such a way that the vegetal notes seem to disappear and become more fruity.  The lovely, creamy, buttery tones are still there, and it still tastes like Matcha... but it's not veggie or grassy tasting like some Matcha can taste.I like!

This is one of those matcha that you will want to have around for the kids, their friends, and when you want to make smoothies, or have a sweet treat. Its not my favorite from Red Leaf but its not bad at all it just reminds me of circus peanuts. Do you remember those things? Sort of like slightly hardened dried out marshmallow like candies. We used to get them at the dime store. Remember when we had "dime stores" ... haha anyway I do enjoy this tea - takes me back to the good ol days, and really where they all THAT good? Oh well the point is - this is some good stuff and I do like it but its more of a banana candy like flavor rather than fresh ripe banana but at the same time I just don't know how natural of a banana flavor one could possibly get - I don't know if I have ever had a better banana flavor in a tea or anything else for that matter that was not a banana itself. I think that banana flavored things always tend to have that slightly strange flavor to it.Now, this is where things get really good ... I mixed my banana matcha with macadamia nut matcha to make a banana nut like matcha and it was excellent! Made a smoothie out of it that way too! It was QUITE yummy!

column9: My fussy puppy loves Chef Michael
column10: Our rescue dog is a terrier mix named Gaffney.  She is marked like a baby cow (black and white splotches).She has always been very picky about food.  Chef Michael's canned food and dry food are all she will eat,except for treats and whatever my husband and I are eating.

column9: weird smell, but cats ate it
column10: This product, and other flavors from this brand, had a strange chemical smell. But my cats didn't seem to mind and went ahead and ate it.  But I won't be getting this brand again, it just smelled like there might have been some chemical contaminant or something.  Hopefully I wasn't imagining things and knocking this brand for no reason, but I'm not chancing my cat's kidneys :) So two stars vs. one in case it's all in my head (nose) and becaue the cats did eat it.
Bought this for a gift. Tried one of the chocolate bars and it was hard and seemed like it was old. Did not like it.
Great product dogs love it, stays fresh, good for health, all natural I am very happy with how long this stays fresh as well. Smells good.
This treat is great, my 2 adult Maltese love them.  All I have to do is shake the can and they come running. I now buy cans to send home with the new parents of the pups.

I rarely eat red meat, but was looking for a snack-sized product to add some protein to my lunches.I sampled every variety of beef jerky I could get my hands on, then found these at a local outdoor store.This product is far superior in flavor, consistency, and ingredients (nothing artificial) to every type of jerky I tried.

column9: Great stuff, not really hot though
column10: The Tanka Bites (Spicy Pepper) are different than jerky:No MSG and no nitrates commonly found in "processed" meats, no corn syrup, no gluten binder, no high fructose corn sugar or even corn sugar, no raw sugar. My understanding is this makes the product compatible with the "Paleo" diet (so I'm assuming they can not claim this without testing or licensing of that trademark).If you're more interested in the "sustainable" aspects, well, it's buffalo... which is usually farmed more sustain-ably than factory beef. As mentioned above it doesn't contain corn by products.If you pause at the price, well, you are paying for a product that has none of the cost saving shortcuts found in the mass produced stuff.How's the taste?Well, they're very moist - no rawhide pulling against your teeth experience.On the balance these are sweet and tart.There's mild heat from the peppers, but the peppers are used sparingly.I was a little let down... the "hot" on the packaging, and the habanero + jalapeno ingredients led me to believe it WAS hot.I've had hot beef jerky before and this doesn't even come close... I'd say this is medium spicy.I'll still order these again - they're good - but they need to remove the "hot" claim from the packaging (and save it for a future product that really IS hot).

I really love these.  It just feels healthier while eating than mainstream jerky bites.  They would be a staple in my cabinet if they were not so expensive.  So when I do buy them it is for a treat.  The kids like them too.
Good choice for healthy protein, satisfying and delicious. Interesting sweet and spicy taste! Portable protein for on the go energy!
Wish I  liked it more.  Very good ingredients listed.  But it's wayyyy too sweet for me, which ditracts drom the flavor of the meat itself

I've been trying to avoid gluten and be more soy free, and I Tanka Bites is one of the few snacks out there that fills this need, while also delivering a good amount of protein.I'm not generally a fan of cranberries, but in this case, it works pretty well. In terms of quantity/price, this is a better deal than the jerky sticks so this is where I would go.

This is a great low calorie snack. I didn't find the Tanka Bites to be that spicy.  Then again, I love spicy food so maybe it's just me. Also, I love that it's an American product, supports Native American entrepreneurs and comes from grass fed buffalo (not feed lot confined and fed). I'll definitely be ordering again.
This is the sort of jerky a back-sliding vegetarian could love; lean buffalo, raised in the wild, no chemicals, cranberries...not too salty. OK, I've decided, this stuff is great!!
I've cut out carbs from diet and find it difficult to find something healthy and sustains me. Tanka Bites are delicious and they are not very spicy at all.
Bought these because they are up front with the nutrition label and I have to watch my salt intake. Tried one package and loved them! Taking these on my upcoming backpacking trip.
These are tasty with a nice bite.  The cranberry takes the edge off the spice.  However, too expensive. There are other healthy options.
My boyfriends and I both loves Tanka Bites.  We follow the Paleo lifestyle, and these are a perfect, protein-based snack!

This is made of processed meat. As you bite into it, fat leaks off of it. Going to anonymously "forget" it at work.I've bought about 1,000. products of Amazon. And this is my first review.  It's THAT bad! Shipping and such was fine though...
Very good product.  Excellent in salads and to cook.  Much lighter and less acidic than vinegar.  My only concern is shelf life.

Somethng new for me in the bar. Learned about this tpye product on the History Channel. Plan to experiment with different cocktails. Use in place of lime juice, lemon juice and/or sweet and sour.Plan to buy more.

column4: Gail E aka the Stitch 'n Frog
column10: I was ready to begin making my own chili powder mix, until we got this and tried it.  It's excellent, just tried it out yesterday and highly reccomend it.

Never had a problem with this brand. i use alot of chile powder to make my own no salt seasonings and this does the trick for the price.  easy to store plastic shaker bottle, slender enough for easy grip.

I recently bought this tone's chili powder because I thought it was something you had to order nline, I ended up paying @20 with the shipping and then was at our local Sam's Club and bought the same thing with no shipping for $4.99!!!

I make lots of homemade salad dressings.  When the recipe calls for wine vinegar or balsamic vinegar, I use this Chianti Red Wine Vinegar. Most wine vinegar is either too sharp or watery.  Most balsamic vinegar is too sweet for my taste.  I have been using this particular brand for years.  The most reliable source is through Amazon.com. I hope Dal Raccoloto never stops making this stuff!

I used this product to create Tandoori chiken - which I marinated in yoghurt and this paste, and then cooked it on the barbeque for maximum flavour. I have always used Sharwoods Medium Tandoori Paste, however I could not find this product in the USA.  I tried Pataks Tandoori paste, and it was nice, but definitely not as good as the Sharwoods Paste or the Sharwoods Tandoori Curry Powder.Use Pataks if you cant find the Sharwoods equivalent.Craig from Melbourne, Australia.

I really do like this product.  The only reason why I gave it a 4 star is because it contains RED #40.  I truely wish that Patak's would jump on the natural/organic band-wagon and drop the red 40, then it would be PERFECT!  Until I do find a tandoori paste without added color, I will continue to use this one.

Pataks is the definitive Indian sauce base, when you don't want to make from scratch.  The overall rating here would be far better were it not skewed by the idiotic reviews.  Complaining that there's artificial coloring or quibbling that the color is too orange???  Get real!  Someone says it doesn't have the "classic" flavor.  That's utter rubbish!  Unless you have your own Tandoori oven, you can only make Tandoori with marinades like this.  Just add this to your yogurt base.  It's easy, delicious and authentic.  Of course it gets 5 stars!
This tastes very good - but has A LOT of un-needed food coloring in it, so I won't be buying it again.
Pataks Tandoori Paste is wonderful on chicken and a quick and easy way to make a delicious and healthy dinner.  Also, keep in mind that Pataks has other similar products that are equally yummy.
The title says it all.And to top it off, the color isn't right either.It's more of a chili color, rather than red.

column9: Difficult to use in colder seasons
column10: I love coconut....so thought I would love Manna.  However, I don't eat bread because of gluten issues, and Nutiva recommends spreading this on toast as a replacement for butter or cream cheese, so this wouldn't work for me, but I'm sure it would taste wonderful.  I do like smoothies and oatmeal,  and I also saw the recipe for manna icing on the Nutiva website so wanted to try that.  I love coconut oil and use it in many things...However, the Manna smells heavenly and acts just like coconut oil as it solidifies at certain temps. It came in the mail solidified.  I live at the southern edge of Indiana so it's cool here now.  I noticed on the label it says the oil rises to the top...well when I tried to measure out a 1/2 cup, I was having to take it out in chunks but then  I noticed that parts of it was a darker color, so I figured I was getting all oil so I let the whole jar sit in hot water so that I could blend it before removing the amount I needed.  Nutiva says to let it sit in hot tap water 5 to 10 mins.  I had it immersed in water for 20 mins and it's still hard as a rock.  Already,  this is a pain.  So unless you live in a house that is above 73 degrees, you will have same problem..I can't just take out a scoop and add to my oatmeal or smoothie if the oil rises to the top and separates when it hardens so this is a seasonal product for me because my house temps are on the cool side.

I have been making coconut oil smoothies using canned coconut milk and fruit and then adding a tablespoon of pure coconut oil.  I thought it would be better to use the Coconut Manna since the oil is already in it.  First I tried tasting it from a spoon (after mixing it thoroughly).  It was very gritty, very oily, and didn't have a fresh coconut taste.  It was like eating really oily, gritty peanut butter, but didn't taste as good as peanut butter.  Then I mixed it in a smoothie and it was still very gritty and so thick and "oily" tasting I threw out the smoothie without finishing it.  One of these days I will try coconut cream from another company -- maybe it will taste better and won't be so gritty.

This stuff really tastes great. It made of coconut oil mixed with liquified coconut "meat". In warm weather you just shake it to mix it up and pour it on. But in cold weather the heavier whitish-colored meat will harden underneath  with the clear coconut oil on top of it.I scoop a couple of spoonfuls onto my Ezekiel sprouted-grain pasta with fresh-pressed garlic and also use it on top of my salads.If you love the unique flavor of coconut then you should give this product a try.

I really wish there were more recipes as to what to do with this product. The coconut tastes like what happens when you open a fresh coconut and eat out the meat. Only it's put in a jar. It's not the milk so you can't really cook food in it or drink it. It's not the processed candy version so beloved of ice cream and sprinkles. Instead its fairly raw and tasteless. The jar seems to indicate that its a spread so am I supposed to put this on toast?I'm sure that there will be a use for this food stuff somehow but as it stands, I'm not sure of the point.

Both me and my husband love the manna as a spread on a homemade bread, it is delicious. It smells very much of coconut, and at first you expect it to be sweet, but it is not, well, almost. There is some sweetness to it. It does not leave that greasy feeling in your mouth as if you ate some lard, although it surely does look like it.It was not too easy to spread on soft bread at room temperature (we keep rooms about 72F) and keeping it in hot water didn't work, since the outside melted, but the core was still hard. I simply cut thin slices of it and put on my bread.Kids were brave enough to try it, but didn't really like manna. Probably because it smells so deceiving of being sweet. Only our two-year old asked for the second bite.I didn't try to cook with it yet.I think it is great nutritious alternative to regular butter, though an acquired taste.

To me this tastes really, really good.  It was sort of a pain to blend the oil with the solids though..  I tried twice placing the plastic jar in hot water as per the directions but it didn't help.  I ended up transferring the contents to a larger glass container and breaking up the solids and blending by hand.  Once mixed it remained mixed but I assume it would separate again eventually if left undisturbed for a long time, something that will not be happening in my case. If refrigerated it turns rock hard and stays that way for many hours.  I've had mine in the 'fridge the past few days to make it less accessible because it's very tempting and I find myself sampling it with alarming frequency.  The taste is so fresh it took me back to growing up in south Florida in the fifties and having all the coconut we cared to pry out of their thick hulls.  I've used this coconut manna (a very fitting name) spread on cornbread and also on warm roasted vegetables - both extremely tasty.  I also made a small batch of pie crust dough using this product instead of butter, pressed it flat and baked it and that was good too.  I plan to make a Thanksgiving pumpkin pie in a coconut manna crust this year.  That is if I can keep from eating it all up in the next few weeks.  Update - coupla' uses found since I wrote this:  added in when making a batch of nut butter and also went very well in a mug of hot coffee with soy milk added (a splash of brandy makes it eve better).
The product is every bit as good as the vendor claims. Moreover, the health benefits of coconut (though not widely known) are legion, and easily researched via GOOGLE.

column9: My new most favorite coconut oil
column10: Wow, when Amazon offered this to me to review in their Vine review program I jumped at the chance since I love coconut oil, and so does my dog.I just received this in the mail and I opened it immediately.  This is now my new favorite, not only is this organic but it is non GMO with zero trans fats. The company donates 1% of its sales to sustainable agriculture, hooray for them.It has a web site that you can go to for recipes and ideas on how to use this product.If you are not familiar with coconut oil here is the scoop basically.  In the cool whether it remains hard, it melts very quickly to a smooth liquid when heated.  In the summer is is always liquid, but if you keep it in the fridge it will solidify.  Just scoop some out for smoothies and sauces and to add a bit of flavor to cookies etc. The best way to use this you must make it liquid so you have to sit it in a bowl of hot water, be sure not to get water into the jar.  Stir it up somewhat to distribute the solids and oil and spoon out an enjoy.This Nutiva product is very smooth and melts in your mouth as it states on the label.  It has a very distinct flavor of coconut, not always present in all oils of this kind.  This is very refreshing to me.Coconut oil is excellent for your pooch but must be introduced very slowly by spoon over a long period as not to upset their stomach.  It helps with allergies and yeast infections. Start with 1/4 tsp. and work up to about 2 tsp. in a few weeks.  I just gave my dog a taste and he went nuts, he was jumping up on me for more, just amazing, this is a huge reaction that I do not get from the other brands.This oil can be blended in smoothies and cereals for added flavor.You get 2 15 oz. jars so the price is right, you get free shipping for over $25.00 which makes this an even better deal with just a small added purchase.I give this a thumbs up.

I just discovered Coconut Oil this year.  Coconut Manna is another form of my new favorite discovery.  I really like Nutiva because it's Organic.I just had a sinfully delicious breakfast sandwich.  Natural Peanut Butter (just crushed peanuts)sprinkled with cinnamon on Whole Wheat bread - grilled in Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna.  How can healthy food be SO DELICIOUS???  The Manna adds so much flavor and nothing artificial.I've used it in oatmeal- YUM! and coated my crock pot liner - so food doesn't stick.If you like the flavor of Coconut but don't like the texture - THIS is for you.Right now, I'm imagining Manna and Cocoa - my mouth is watering!!Melted and poured over Air Popped Popcorn....Only your imagination will stop you.  It's delicious and can soothe a scratchy throat.I highly recommend Nutiva Coconut Manna

column9: gritty and easy to choke on raw but great for baking, 2nd jar better
column10: I am a HUGE fan of Nutiva coconut oil, I use it in and on everything from Sambal Shrimp to smoothies, it's amazing. I was very excited to try this spreadable product. When it arrives it is like natural peanut butter only harder to mix. It was like hardening cement in oil. I had to pry it lose with a fork and it was difficult to blend even after soaking the jar in hot water. Finally I used my hand blender stick right in the jar and it whipped up creamy but struggled binding the motor a bit. I first tasted it on a spoon and it plastered itself to the inside of my mouth and tongue to where it was difficult to even swallow, a very disconcerting experience I wasn't expecting. While it blended creamy it is very gritty and choky and really doesn't taste all that great actually the oil tastes much better. If you have any choking issues which I usually don't, this is not for you. OK, so it's not good straight out of the jar, lets try a smoothie. I added this to my usual smoothie using frozen banana and plain whey protein powder and water with a touch of honey. It tasted good that way and blended well but I still found myself really choking on the grit. I like the oil much better even in my smoothie this product just sticks in your throat really bad. I would not buy this but I would highly recommend the oil by this company, it is very fine natural Coconut oil.I later upped my review from 2 stars to 3 stars. I have kept on trying to find a good use for this product and found it is much better when added to something baked. I made my usual sweet cornbread and added a heaping tablespoon of this manna as well as substituting the butter for their coconut oil and the results were truly divine! I still don't like the way you have to constantly keep remixing it and I still don't like this stuff straight out of the jar or in a smoothie but it is wonderful for baking.12/27/11 Update:This product came as two jars packaged together. This week I opened the second jar and was surprised to find it was much different then the first jar. This jar mixed much easier and was much creamier. The first jar was so hardened I had to pry on it with a steak knife. I live in south Florida, cold temperatures are never an issue, my coconut oil is always liquid. I again tried it straight and this time it did not plaster itself to my mouth and was not gritty like the first jar. It tasted better too. Not sure why this jar was such a different experience from the first jar, especially since they were packaged together. Based on the second jar experience I would try this again, I've been finding more and more uses for it. If I had only received the first jar I would not consider trying it again. Strange there are such inconsistencies with this product.2/3/12 Update:I ordered this again because the second jar was really good unlike the first jar. I am happy to report back that jar 3 and 4 were perfect. They were very easy to mix, very smooth and creamy and not easy to choke on like the first jar. In fact it was great right out of the jar this time. So, I'm not sure what was wrong with the first jar, maybe just old but since then every jar has been just fine and really good quality. Based on the last three jars I changed my review from 3 stars to 4. I hope there are no more inconsistency issues in the future because I really like this product. Three out of four jars were great anyway.

So muttered my sister as I was telling a friend I had two jars of Nutiva's Coconut Manna. Absurdly delicious, this wonderful food is distinctly different from other coconut products and a delightful substitute for butter and/or cream.Made from the entire edible portion of the coconut and not just the oil, coconut manna naturally contains beneficial fiber, minerals, and essential fatty acids. Creamy in texture with just a touch of natural sweetness, it works as a spread on toast and is heavenly mixed with oatmeal. As noted in other reviews, the manna solidifies at room temperature and needs to be softened and mixed before using. If you skip this step, you will end up with the oil separating to the top of the jar and the more fibrous part collecting in the middle. Not exactly a bad thing per se, but it is better completely mixed.The only downside to coconut manna is the high amount of saturated fat. The saturated fat in coconut has a strange structure: the fatty acids are medium chain, instead of long or short chain. What this means in practical terms is that your body has to heat up to burn off the medium chain triglycerides (or MCTs), leading some to claim weight loss benefits. The science on this so far is mixed, but too much saturated fat is never a great thing for anybody. So, everything in moderation, and no eating the whole jar in one sitting. Unless you have to.GRADE: A

I love coconut and I love this product. I have had it with Nutella on whole wheat bread for breakfast and it was delicious. I used some in some chicken curry and it worked great. I could eat a whole jar.I am so glad I discovered this on Amazon, I have never seen it in the super market. I am hoping to find more recipes for using it.

This seems to be about the same as the Tropical Traditions Coconut Cream Concentrate, which I also love.  I think they are equally good.  In the past I've had to wait a long time for TT to have a sale then buy 4 2lb. jars because of the high shipping, so I'm very happy to see this available for less than TT regular price in smaller quantities with no shipping cost if Prime or over $25 order.TT has plenty of recipes on their website. Actually I often just eat it with a spoon!The oil and solids tend to separate so I had to warm the jar and stir it up, then cool it and  it stayed mixed.  FYI the melting point of coconut oil is 76 degrees, the solids seem to need a little warmer than that to mix up.And don't worry, natural saturated fats are actually *good* for you.

I had used product by this manufacturer before.  I used their coconut oil for frying and seasoning foods that I wanted to have a tropical, underlying coconut, island flavor.  It had worked well for me and the numerous benefits of using coconut products are far too extensive to list in this review.  The overlying theme that I found when doing my research was to go "organic" so that no chemicals were used to strip the coconut oil from the inedible shell.  I was so thrilled with the coconut oil that I just had to try the new "manna" product and I am so glad that I did.This is a thick, flavorful spread at room temperature and I found it easy to put on fresh baked bread, corn on the cob, steamed broccoli, chicken breasts.... you name it, the list is endless.  It is wonderful and I do not think that I will be able to be without it in my kitchen.  The flavor is subtle, the texture is easily spreadable and the taste is going to transport your everyday foods to a new level.  I have really enjoyed Coconut Manna.

I love this product! It tasts delicious spread on toast instead of butter. Coconut's health benifits are many, fiber, potassium, and tastes great! I have used the coconut oil in the past but like this product better for using as a spread. Truly Mana from Heaven!

I used this coconut oil on my hair and as a skin moisturizer. Coconut oil provides nourishment to the hair and skin, and also softens it. When using this product on my hair, I melted it and turned it into an oil. It reduces dandruff and helps retain the moisture in my hair. In addition, it helps diminish hair shedding. I also mixed it into some of my hair products for a deep conditioning effect. I love the fragrance; it makes my hair smell heavenly. I wish I could give this product a 10!

Wow, I'm a HUGE fan of Nutiva. I buy their Hemp Seeds (best non-animal protein there is).I was excited to get this as I use coconut oil in cooking, coconut milk for protein & fruit shakes and everyone here is a big macaroon fan.This showed up as a solid mass. I couldn't even push a butter knife into it. I could only scrape some off the top, to taste it. So I did what I was told in the directions: "Place jar in hot tap water for 5-10 minutes & thoroughly stir."30 MINUTES LATER there was little liquid sitting on one side. That's 30 minutes with boiling tap water running into a small bowl where the Coconut Manna was immersed.I'm not sure what use we'll find for this, but I don't see the sense of liquefying it every time I want to spread a little on toast.MASSIVE DISAPPOINTMENT. There's no way a company could have tested this and not experienced what we did.

I purchased this nutiva manna because of the special price. It is incredibly difficult to mix. I left it in hot water a long time it did no good and even a microwave was not useful. Worked to mix it a long time. Then worse yet I ate it out of the jar this has very little coconut flavor and is waxy oily terrible. It even messed my stomache up later. Coconut is one of my fav flavors but not this manna. I thought maybe I use the jars for my face or feet so it is not a total waste. Would not even give this one star so gross.

column9: Read how to use this product. Let me share this valuable info on this product!
column10: I have been using Tropical Tradition Coconut Oil for years, primarily for sautéing and home-made granola. I had never heard of Coconut Manna and was not quite sure what it was, but it sounded interesting to try it out. MY EXPERIENCE: When I received it I wasn't quite sure what to think. It was very solid and obviously had melted, then re-solidified on its side. In addition, I could see there were 2 layers of different colors that had separated. The dark layer tasted pretty darn good and the lighter layer was oily. I was able to get on Nutiva's web site and get their 800-993-4367 x2 number and they had a very helpful guy on the phone that helped me understand the product. Let me share this with you:ABOUT THE PRODUCT: It is a whole-food product, meaning it is 100% coconut with very little processing. The difference between this and coconut oil is that coconut oil is put through a cold expresser process to get the oil out. Both are fresh-harvest coconuts that are dried, but the Manna is ground into a very fine powder right after drying. Then, they add some of their coconut oil (that's the light colored separate layer I saw when I opened my jar of Manna). In addition, Manna is lower in calories than coconut oil.PLEASE READ FOR CORRECT USE OF THE PRODUCT: According to the Nutiva guy on the phone, you really need to soften the product and mix thoroughly to truly appreciate the full spectrum of this amazing product. When I followed his instructions, I can assure you that this is an absolutely WONDERFUL coconut product!!!! It must be softened by achieving a temperature above 76 degrees and then mixed thoroughly. If you live in a warm climate, you won't have to worry about softening, but for my cool Oregon climate I need to soften before use. There were a couple suggestions the Nutiva guy had to soften the product, plus I've added my own recommendation listed on item #3:1. Run tap water to the very hottest setting, then fill a bowl and put the Manna container in the bowl for 10-15 minutes. After that time mix well before serving. (From my experiment, you need to refill with hot water several times and it takes more like 30-60 minutes to achieve softness.)2. Better way is if you have a gas oven. Place the Manna container in the oven without turning it on. With just the gas pilot, it will warm enough to soften the Manna, and then mix well before serving. You can actually store it in your gas oven, just remember to remove before turning the oven on or you'll have a disaster on your hands.3. If you have a food dehydrator, open the lid of the Manna container and put it in the dehydrator on a very low setting higher than 76 and below 100. After 15 minutes, stir the Manna, and then put back in for another 15 minutes, then mix well before serving.I absolutely love the taste and texture of this product and could eat it right out of the container. It's wonderful on crackers, sweets, or bread and adds a lovely taste to my green smoothies. This will not replace my regular coconut oil for sautéing, but is a nice "special treat" that is both healthy and delicious.  I tried sautéing in Manna, with mixed results: it tends to turn brown and add a burned flavor.MOST IMPORTANTLY: I would really like it if the product was distributed in glass rather than plastic. In my opinion, heating and eating products in plastic containers is questionable and I believe detrimental to this planet and our health. PLEASE Nutiva, switch over to glass containers!!! I will reuse the glass containers and it is the `right' thing to do for your customers. I have purchased coconut oil for years from Tropical Traditions web site and their pricing is comparable to yours, except they distribute in glass containers.HERE'S MY EVALUTATION ON NUTIVA'S PRICES VS. TROPICAL TRADITION:Tropical Tradition:"Gold Label Virgin Coconut Oil" IN GLASS CONTAINER 16 oz. buy one and get one free on their web site: $19.95 for two. Approx. $10 for shipping = $15 ($1 less than Nutiva's)Uses glass jars!!!Nutiva Extra-Virgin Coconut Oil:15 oz. $16 with free shipping on orders over $30 on Nutiva's web site15 oz. $10 Coconut MannaOn Amazon:  $18.80 (retail $22) for 2 with free shipping over $25.

I absolutely love Nutiva's coconut oil and so I thought I would love their Coconut Manna as well. Unfortunately that is not the case.I followed the directions on the container to soften the product so that I could mix the oil back into the coconut. I ended up using an immersion blender to thoroughly mix it which worked very well.I find it almost inedible. The texture is gritty and very thick. It sticks to the inside of my mouth and leaves an unpleasant dry sensation. It doesn't "melt" in my mouth as described on the container. I don't enjoy the taste either. The pure taste of coconut oil is there, but with another taste mixed in that ruins it and leaves an aftertaste.I'm really disappointed. I'm planning on trying another brand of coconut butter and see if it's a problem with the Nutiva brand or just my own taste/texture preferences. It's not anywhere near the expiration date, it doesn't taste rancid and the container was properly sealed, so I assume that the product is fresh.Update: 2-13-2012 - I purchased some Artisana organic raw coconut butter and compared the two. I have to say that I like the Artisana brand better. It's smoother and the color is lighter. It's also packaged in a glass jar which I prefer. The taste is also somewhat better. I now know that I don't really like coconut butter, it's just not for me. I would recommend that if you buy coconut butter buy the Artisana brand.

I enjoy Coconut Manna very much.  I  add it to my oatmeal instead of sugar or maple syrup or have a teaspoon of it plain and it satisfies my sweet tooth without any sugar.  And its not really very sweet, but it is very rich with a natural coconut flavor.  The only thing that I dislike about it is the need to soften it by sitting it in hot water (you are not supposed to microwave it - and I don't do that anyway since microwaves are not terribly healthy).  It is also a little bit grainy, instead of being creamy, but that is something that I was easily able to adjust to.  All-in-all, a product that I will try to keep on hand in my kitchen.

column9: The manna is quite good, but what a royal pain to use - if you live in cold weather areas, order this in summer
column10: Does it taste good? Yes. If you like the taste and texture of coconut butter, you will most certainly like this product.Does it spread nicely? Well, that depends on where you live and how patient you are. In cold weather this is a royal pain to use because the oil separates and hardens at temperatures below 76 F. The instructions on the label say to place the container in hot water for 5 to 10 minutes to soften the manna. Well, in my kitchen (room temperature  about 70 F) it took almost a half hour for this thing to melt.I placed the jar inside a stainless steel saucepan filled with hot water that must have been at least 180 F. After 5 minutes the water had cooled quite a bit and yet the oil had not even started to melt. I used a blunt knife to try and break the manna into pieces. Did the same thing two more times.
