Finally, the fourth water change did the trick and the manna now had acquired a nice consistency, perfect for spreading, but at that point I was not a very happy camper.I wanted to use this as a breakfast spread and that's not going to happen, at least not during the week. I just don't have the time nor the patience. It just takes too long.I buy natural organic peanut butter, which also must be mixed well for the oil to combine, but I only have to do that  once so I don't mind at all. With this manna it's an everyday event.I ordered two jars, one of them will live in my pantry until next summer, and we'll treat coconut manna as a warm weather food, I guess.This is a very nice tasting coconut product, which I would have rated 5 stars otherwise. Certainly worth a try, if you happen to keep your house above 75 F year round.

column9: Sinfully rich but oh so delicious!
column10: Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna is certainly one of the most sinful of foods but, oh my gosh, is it delicious! It is a very rich but very flavorful coconut cream made from certified organic dried coconut meat from the Philippines. (I live in southwest Florida and room temperature here is just perfect for ensuring a very spreadable coconut cream).When I first opened the jar the fresh fragrance of coconut made my mouth water! Just like a kid, I could not resist sticking my finger into the jar and taking a big, generous taste. My taste buds simply exploded when the unique flavor of this decadent coconut cream melted on my tongue like sweet butter! And just like a kid, I know I will be tempted to take those sinful dips into the luscious coconut manna jar.I have noticed other reviewers' comments about the "grittiness" of this product and I just want to point out that coconut meat is a high fiber food and coconut manna is 100% whole coconut, so the texture is much like one should expect in a high fiber spread. Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna contains 12% fiber and 9% protein, whereas coconut oil contains none.Coconut in general is such a versatile food with an extraordinary taste and all manner of health benefits. In Sanskrit, the coconut palm is called "kalpa vriska" meaning "the tree that supplies all that is needed to live." But I must be frank...I do not think Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna or any coconut product should be used as a food therapy for any health purpose. Coconut meat is nearly all fat, 80% of which is saturated. With that said, as difficult as it will probably be, I will be using Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna only sparingly (but with utter enjoyment!)Being a raw vegan foodie and with the holidays quickly approaching, I do look forward to getting creative with Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna and devising culinary applications with it, such as in my raw, vegan spreads, soups, smoothies, sauces, cheeses, and especially in desserts. Of course I will have to consider it a celebration food because of the high saturated fat content. This luscious treat is not the best choice for health or waistline but it is so good to the palate! I will definitely be using Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna for special occasions, for entertaining and for those times of private indulgence when I need to treat myself... and I will do so with wild abandon!

Like another reviewer, I too use this to make paleo/primal chocolate bark (coconut oil, coconut manna, unsweetened cocoa, vanilla liquid stevia, crushed macadamias).  Before I found this product I was making my chocolate bark in a base of only coconut oil, but the addition of coconut manna completely transformed the recipe.  For me, the chocolate coconut bark went from being merely a tolerable way to ingest massive amounts of coconut oil to a confection that I dream about eating at all hours of the day.  I'm addicted.  And consequently, I'm pretty sure I've discovered the only way to get fat on the paleo diet.  But who cares? It's worth it.

There was no expiration date on the two jars I received. I called Nutiva and asked if this product was to have an expiration date on it and they said that there should be two dates on the jar. A packed on date and an expiration date should be present.  I then went a local store who I thought might carry this product and yes there is a packed on date and an expiration date which is one year from the packed on date. Amazon did make good and refund my purchase price.

I really like this stuff, I just wish it weren't so pricey.I added a little non-caloric sweetener to mine and a bit of sea salt (after melting it) and then poured it into little candy molds and let it harden in the fridge. Instant candy!

This is essentially creamy "coconut butter." Following the directions on coconut manna's bottle will serve you well. I stir the contents right away and they usually do not separate out for about a month afterwards. Enjoy!

column9: Analog to Coconut Cream or Coconut Butter, Wonderful Product
column10: ****This Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna is actually a type of coconut cream or coconut butter NOT coconut oil. The difference is that the cream or butter is much thicker, has whole coconut in it, and a very strong coconut flavor. You would not use the coconut manna for cooking. It is used more as a spread (which you wouldn't usually do with coconut oil) or can even be eaten by itself or made into a candy (because it is slightly sweet). It can be added to smoothies or used in many other creative ways. Think of it like whole coconut meat in a creamy form.The reason I did not give this coconut manna five stars is because it is packaged in a difficult way. First of all, the container is plastic. In order to use the coconut manna, the container must be heated gradually to a very warm room temperature (say 80 degrees, I'd think) or else put in hot water for 30 minutes, stirred, and left in hot water for 30 more minutes. This is very inconvenient, plus the plastic container is not good for all of the repeated heatings.Other than that, it's a great product. It is very slightly sweet and tastes strongly like coconut. The consistency is a bit gritty or grainy due to part of the coconut flesh that is powder and has been reconstituted, but I found that fine, not off-putting at all. It's great all by itself, added to smoothies, or put into the freezer in molds for a whole foods raw candy.Recommended.****

column9: I like it, but you do have to put some work into it.
column10: I love coconut.  I buy shredded coconut from Nuts Online all the time (they also stock mediterranean pine nuts (pignolias) if like me you don't want the ones coming from China).  I use finer shredded coconut in omelettes and cakes.  I use larger coconut chips to just eat!  When I need to use oil to cook, I nine out of ten times it will be pure, raw pressed coconut oil.  I drink coconut water every single day with dinner!  (I like Vita Coco and Zico).  Coconut is a super-food!  It had been handed a bad rap over the years due to poor, agenda driven research and even poorer government recommendations, but in recent years coconut has been found to be one of the healthiest foods available.So what is Coconut Manna?  It's the name Nutiva calls this super coconut butter.  As a coconut lover, I never had coconut butter before.  So I still had no idea what to expect until I tried it.Apparently, it's pulverized pure coconut flesh, made into a creamy, buttery coconut spread that smells great and tastes even better!  Like pure coconut oil, Coconut Manna hardens at temperatures below 76 degrees fahrenheit and solidifies below 73 degrees.  However, unlike coconut oil, when the Manna solidifies, it separates into various layers of coconut oil and coconut flesh.  When I first opened it, it was a solid mass which had formed when the jar was on it's side.  In order to eat this properly, you need to heat it to liquify it and then stir it thoroughly to recombine it (kind of like natural peanut butter).  It takes some work, but it's worth it.  Basically you submerge the closed jar into a bowl of super hot tap water for 15 to 20 minutes and that should melt it enough to allow you to stir it.  It will take some work to stir it, but once stirred, spread it on bread or drizzle it on ice cream or just eat it right out of the jar!  If you are a coconut lover, you will almost definitely enjoy Coconut Manna!I like making coconut/cheese omelettes by beating shredded coconut into the eggs (about one tablespoon shredded coconut per egg).  Try it!  Using the Coconut Manna, I made a new dish where I substituted Coconut Manna for the cheese making a sweet/savory all coconut omelette!This is my own recipe - the coconut omelette:3 large eggs3 heaping tablespoons of unsweetened, shredded coconut2-3 tablespoons of Coconut Manna (pre-heated and mixed)some coconut palm sugar (about a teaspoon)some coconut oil (about a tablespoon)Beat the eggs, add the shredded coconut, then beat the mixture a little more until combined.  I use stainless steel to cook with over gas, so heat about a tablespoon of coconut oil in a 10" stainless steel fry pan (sized for 3 eggs).  Be sure to coat the pan well.  Get the pan hot, but not hot enough to smoke the oil - better to let it heat slowly over low to medium heat then to kill it on high heat.  Add the eggs/shredded coconut mixture.  Let the eggs slowly cook until the egg "pancake" breaks loose in the pan (don't try to force it).  Let the eggs slowly cook a little more until they start to "gel" a little towards the center.  Don't rush this because you do not want to burn the eggs but don't wait for them to fully cook either!  Now the tricky part, using a very large spatula, flip the egg "pancake" over.  Make sure the heat is on low at this point.  Spoon the Coconut Manna onto one half of the eggs.  Then sprinkle the coconut palm sugar onto the Manna.  Fold up the plain half of the eggs to create the classic omelette fold.  Plate it, maybe sprinkle a little sea salt on it, maybe sprinkle just a little more coconut palm sugar on top (for visual effect) and enjoy!  I usually have mine with some Trader Joe's Greek Style Honey Yogurt on the side.

column9: Yummy, but not sure what to do with it
column10: Honestly, I haven't searched the Nutiva site for recipes, so I'm not sure what all the possible uses are for Coconut Manna. I will say that all by itself it tastes pretty yummy. I keep finding my 9-yr-ld daughter sneaking spoonfuls of it! So far we've spread it on toast and tried making smoothies with it. The smoothies didn't work too well because it solidified into little chunks that wouldn't blend and then got stuck in the straws. I can imagine it would be good to bake with, though.It's essentially pureed coconut. The consistency is dependent on the room temp, as coconut oil has a rather low melting point. When I first bought this, the weather--and hence our house--was pretty warm, and the consistency was that of oobleck. :D  But as the temp dropped, it became more solid.All in all, it's been good, but not sure I'd buy more only because I don't cook a lot. I thought this would be more something that could replace cream cheese and such for me as I'm allergic to milk, but it's not quite right for that. Still, it does taste good and I'm sure it's loaded with nutrients!

If you have never tried coconut manna, you may be a little shocked. Texture is a bit like 'dry' peanut butter or almond butter. I thought that since coconut oil is very 'wet' (even though it is solid at room temperature) that it would give this that quality but I didn't find that to be the case. I purchased a two pack (very good deal, in my humble opinion) and it will last for quite a while.The flavor of this is good. It smells like coconut but the taste is not sweet per se and reminds me more of a nut butter (but without the 'sweetness'). It is unsweetened and consists only of organic whole coconut. You can find some recipes at nutiva.com but I didn't find them very helpful (unless you also are accustomed to purchasing hempseed and/or other ingredients). I have tried this with oatmeal a few times. Normally I eat oatmeal with only butter. On the jar it has a recipe for "Manna Oatmeal" but again, it includes hempseed -which I excluded. It made the oatmeal very very dry but it did add a pleasant taste to it.As with coconut oil, this is solid at room temperature. The container says it liquefies at above 73*. In our house it is generally in the 60s. I actually put it in the microwave for 30 second intervals until it was soft enough to stir together. Otherwise I use a spoon and scrape out what I need. When using it in my oatmeal, which is already hot, that works fine as it melts into the oatmeal but I wonder how well it'd work to spread it on toast when I wanted.I am interested to see how it can be used for other things (it says it can replace butter, cream cheese and cream in recipes). I wasn't sure to give this a 3 or 4 star rating because I've never tried it before by any other brand. I like it enough to possibly buy more in the future.

Maybe it's just the fact that i've seriously limited my sugar intake recently, but at only 1g of sugar per serving, this stuff is surprisingly sweet. If you like any kind of nut butters, you'll love this stuff. I leave mine out in the sun for an afternoon to soften it up initially, then it's all good after that. Amazing product.

When it came it was liquified and I just put in cupboard and then aa few days later when I took it out..Hard as a Rock..but DELICIOUS..my daughter and I have been eating it right out of jar...but plan on trying some of the receipes from the company's website.

I've tried all the different extra virgin coconut products at Whole Foods and have finally decided on Nutiva's products.  The Manna is the BEST tasting and I use that as a spread on bagels, eat it direct by the spoonful.  I choose the service of having it delivered every 2 months, in order to save substantially on s/h.  It's great value and best tasting.  I received it much earlier than expected.

column9: use ice tray and microwave to melt for smoothie
column10: First off I love this product!  It tastes great.  My only complaint is that the oil and coconut meat seperate and it needs to be melted together.  This can take a long time using the method on the jar (putting the jar in hot water) so what I do is melt the jar once, then pour it into an ice cube tray and cover with tin foil.  When I make a smoothie I scoop out one cube worth, put in a small bowl/ramekin and microwave till it melts, then stir and add to my smoothie.  Hope this helps someone!

I read reviews about how smooth and creamy this product was, and didn't understand why there was a hard, dry shell when I opened the canister. I thought I was mistaken, so I "dug in" with a spoon, to find that there WAS a hard crust (about 1 inch) or dried product and underneath was the "creamy product."I am not sure what happened in transit...I would have thought warmer temperatures would liquify the product vs have the hard crust. Perhaps a manufacturing defect?I want to like this product,  but I don't I'll order it online and/or from Amazon again.
I have truly enjoyed using this product. It has been a very good addition to my diet regimen. Will reorder soon.

column9: A strange, but rewarding experience in the end.
column10: I've had Artisana coconut butter before and it was solid from start to finish. To be fair I had it in the winter so it didn't get a chance to liquefy. It was bright white, had the somewhat gritty consistency of having ground up coconut flesh but as it warmed in my mouth it went smooth. So I ordered Nutiva because it was a better value for the price. It's August. It arrived warm in a tan liquid form with a hard to stir solid on the bottom. It was disgusting. After a little work stirring it all up it started to solidify to a syrup -- it would pour out if I tipped it. It was getting better at that point, though. A night in a cool cabinet and now it has reformed into a single layer light colored solid. It has grittiness to it but that's what the coconut's like. The flavor is good. I think Artisana had a marginally better flavor.

column9: Too much work for too little flavor
column10: As you will see from the extensive reviews, you need to soften this product before you can even use it. It's currently 70 degrees in my kitchen and it's solid as a rock. Then you need to blend it back together.It's bland. The container suggests that you can use it as a substitute for cream cheese, but I'm not sure why you'd want to bother. I can't see putting this on a bagel---too bland---and it's just sweet enough that you wouldn't use it in savory dishes.Let's say you *did* want to put it on a bagel. You'd need to factor in the softening time. Maybe this product is good for folks with time on their hands, but it's just not working for me.

column9: It is OK, but very bland, I expected more
column10: This is an OK product, but I expected more of a sweet "fresh" coconut flavor. This product is good, but not great.I liked it, but I did not LOVE it. It just was not yummy.It was kind of bland. Fresh coconut has a naturally sweet taste, this does not. I am not sure if it is lost in the processing. From now on, my coconut will come from the produce stand, so I can continue to enjoy the coconut water, fresh coconut, and toasted coconut in the oven. I guess once you are used to fresh, nothing can compare.I also love coconut oil, and will continue to use coconut oil, but the coconut manna is just lacking something.

column9: Nice taste, satisfying but timely to use.
column10: While this is an unusual product, it's a healthy substitute for many snacks.  Great on toast or added to a smoothie or just eaten out of the jar.  I would use more of it if it didn't take so long to melt.  You need to sit the container in hot water for about 15 minutes before you can mix and use each time as at room temperature it hardens and separates.  Tastes sort of like a mild coconut, butter, nutty flavor.  Hard to describe, but pleasant and apparently very healthy.

column9: Bask in the power of the coconut
column10: Yeah, that sounds way out there to me too.  This is amazing stuff.  Its basically coconut thats been dried and ground, also known as coconut butter.  Its rich in fiber and protein, plus plenty of saturated coconut fat.  A number of studies suggest that coconut oils, rich in beneficial fatty acids, may actually be a heart healthy fat in low to moderate amounts.  People who eat coconut frequently around the world seem to have lower incidence of heart disease and certain cancers, and the main fats in coconut all have been demonstrated to have healthful effects, improving HDL and creating LDL thats smaller, harder, and less likely to plaque your arteries.  About 2 or 3 tablespoons of this per day and you've picked up a bit of those oils and some protein and fiber as well.  Plus it tastes really good and goes great in baked goods and candies.When you get it, put the jar in some warm water for a few minutes and the manna will liquify.  Stir thoroughly and it will become a solid again at room temperatures below 76 degrees.  When its a solid, you can scoop some out with a sharp spoon or a butter knife.  As a liquid, it pours.My wife found a recipe for a 'truffle' that incorporates this, cocoa powder, dates, chia seeds and hemp seeds, cinnamon and a few other ingredients.  Its like the best tasting energy bar you've ever had, and all of those ingredients are high in good plant fats, protein and fiber.If you haven't tried this stuff, do some research online and read everyones viewpoint.  I'm not sure about the science behind it but I'm sure that it tastes good and a little wont hurt you.  Coconut manna is the best tasting coconut butter I've tried, and the company has a good reputation for quality.  Try the coconut oil as well.  It works out really well in many dishes, having a sweet, slightly coconut aroma and taste.

column9: Less an oil than a "peanut butter" type of product -- delicious once softened & mixed!
column10: If you are looking for a coconut oil product, this is not an oil.  There are differences.  The first review I read did a great job describing them and that reviewer talked to a company rep and provided all the info.  This is similar to "Coconut Butter," which I've purchased before and is available on Amazon(Artisana, Organic Raw Coconut Butter).  In fact, it's exactly the same.  I needed to blend both and the taste and texture were the same.  On that note, I also discovered Artisana Coconut Butter-Cacao Bliss.  Natural raw chocolatey, delicious!  Great spread on bread or just on a spoon!Anyhooooo...back on topic...In a mild CA climate, I found I needed to soften the Manna.  Placing in a deep bowl of hot tap water worked.  I put it in.  About 5 minutes later, I removed it and stirred a bit.  Got new hot water and repeated the wait and mix.  This combined it well and I had no need to heat it up again, as when it cooled, it didn't separate again.  I have used it in raw "baking" and also spread on bread or a cracker.As someone who enjoys the occasional real junk food(had Twix yesterday and a brownie at the in-laws house today), I still found the taste and texture good, just on its own.  It isn't sugary sweet, but as sweet as natural coconut, because that is what it is.It works great in thickening/helping hold together raw desserts.  I've used it in my cashew cream deserts as the creamy filling and also a combination of Manna and coconut oil with ground nuts and dates, for a crust.  As a raw foodie, I only dabble, but, once softened, it's easy to use.

I've been looking everywhere for organic coconut products with no preservatives.  This one is great.  It's not only rich and delicious, it's concentrated and needs no refrigeration.  It can be easily diluted to any consistency, and unlike many canned coconut milks and products, is organic with NOTHING added!  Very fast shipping and a good price.  Perfect!

The Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna is stiff so it's sometimes challenging to spread. However, it's so delicious that it's worth the effort. It's good enough to eat from the container, which occasionally happens in our house. It is a nice replacement for butter; I use this on sandwiches and toast.

column9: yummy addition to plain greek yogurt
column10: I "melted" mine by putting the jar in a pan of hot water. When it was pourable, I dumped it in a bowl and used a potato masher to get it mixed really well.  I then put it in three widemouth glass jars.  Two jars went into the fridge, one jar is in the cupboard. Since it is winter here, the jar in the cupboard has not yet separated. When I prepare yogurt, I scrape bits of the hardened manna (from the refrigerated jar) into the yogurt, along with other goodies like pecans, lemon zest, honey and ground flax - yum!Next time I am going to try to pour the manna into a lined dish so after it's hardened I can pop it out and use a grater, instead of scoring it with a paring knife and scraping it out of the jar with a spoon.Great way to get flavor, good fat, etc. into plain Greek yogurt!

I have never used something like the Coconut Manna - 15 oz - Container before, so it's all new to me. I didn't try it on toast or bread or make a smoothie with it. Here's how I used it - I used some of this to replace the face in a  vanilla cake and brownies.It worked well for the cake, gave it a slightly coconut flavor, but not very distinctive. The vanilla cake tasted very rich with the substitution. The brownies, I substituted 1/3 of the fat in the brownie recipe for the equal amount of coconut manna. Again, it worked very well, producing a rich flavored brownie with a slightly different flavor, but it was not a distinctive coconut flavor. I would say I'd probably have to substitute 1/2 the amount of fat with the coconut manna to get a coconut flavor. But that experiment will wait for a little longer.You can also use this product on your skin, if you choose to - it makes skin incredibly smooth. You can use it on your hair. It's not an overwhelming coconut smell, just a good clean smell.I only gave this 4 stars simply because there are no sort of instructions with the package. There's no info on making a smoothie or anything like that. There are no directions on how to use this product in baking or cooking. I did search on the interweb, but really did not find out much information.But, if you are the sort of person who is using this type of product, you definitely should buy it - you probably have dozens of recipes for coconut manna.As for me, I intend to keep experimenting by baking with it. I'm thinking maybe chocolate chop cookies, with the coconut manna taking the place of the fat. Or maybe use it to make a coconut cake or icing. I do enjoy this but unfortunately I don't get a lot of time to experiment with baking, just on the weekend. But the holidays are coming up and I plan to add a little bit of coconut manna goodness to my holiday baking. It should be fun.
Wow.. the answer here. For Thai cooking this product is perfect for many many recipes. Suddenly you have convience in a jar of a pure natural flavor you need in thai cooking.

I wasn't sure what Coconut Mana was good for, but I like coconut, so I thought it would be fun to try. Once I got it I... still had no idea what to do with it. The jar has a website on it that supposedly has recipes, but good luck finding the ones that specifically use Coconut Mana. I tried searching the web for uses and most people just said they ate it plain. Not for me. Finally I found a person who recommended melting it and adding sugar and cocoa to make a chocolate sauce to eat over ice cream. YES! That is the way to use this stuff! I mixed together Coconut Mana, sweetened condensed milk, and cocoa powder, to make one of the best fudge sauces I had ever tasted.So the only really complaint I have about this stuff is the melting time. The directions say to hold it under hot running water for 5-10 minutes. I stuck it in a bowl with hot water and let it sit. I had to replace the water twice and to took nearly a half hour. If it hadn't tasted so good, I probably would have just tossed it after that. But it ended up being worth the wait :) The slow defrost time just gets it knocked down a star.

As compared to other whole coconut items -- I find this one to be very smooth. It still has a bit of nutty body to it -- being whole coconut -- but is much closer to coconut milk than one may expect. It must be due to the processing process being very complete -- as "Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna" IS WHOLE COCONUT. I am surprised at just how creamy this is -- instead of being more meaty [nutty]. One does have to heat it up [as recommended] to get to the full liquid creamy zone. I put mine -- still in its jar -- into some hot water in a small sink and added some hot [nearly boiling] water from an electric hot water kettle about five minutes later -- and got mostly liquid coconut after about ten minutes. Later, I tried adding boiling water to inside the jar directly -- to quickly heat it up -- to add to some oatmeal -- which worked well. This stuff does taste rich -- for a whole coconut cream +++

column9: Coconut Oil is amazing...Manna, a bit disappointing.
column10: My family and I are slowly making changes to eat a bit healthier and naturally.We love Nutiva's Coconut Oil and use it almost exclusively in our cooking and baking, so we were excited to try Nutiva's Coconut Manna.Initially, after opening the jar, I saw that the Manna had separated and resolidified in an odd shape, as if the jars had been tipped during shipping. This didn't bother me much, as I know coconut oil easily liquifies at 76 degrees.The Manna doesn't seem to liquefy quite so easily (although the jar says 'spreads easily at temperatures above 73*'). You can place it in hot tap water for 5-10 minutes, as the directions suggest, but be prepared for the jar to sit a LOT longer before the manna can be easily stirred. A. LOT. LONGER. I even tried placing the jar on our warm, sunny windowsill (with baseboard heat below) for several hours...that didn't work well either.It's all well and good to finally get the Coconut Manna to a softer state, but, it quickly hardens before the next use. Perhaps the product will stay at a spreadable temperature during the warmer months. During fall and winter, everything needs to be warmed up in upstate NY.The smell and taste of the manna is wonderful. However, as much as I love cooking (and really wanted and expected to love the manna), the hassle of getting the product to a useable point is disappointing and too time consuming for using in a quick recipe or spreading on morning toast. :-(

NOTE: If you like this product and plan to use it, the quickest way to heat (and then properly store in a glass jar) is to put in the trunk of your car on a warm/hot day for a couple of hours...learned this as a soapmaker who uses lots of coconut oil! I then mixed well and poured it into a sterilized mason jar.I LOVE the smell of the Coconut manna, but then I love the smell of all coconut.  I normally use coconut oil in quite a few recipes and this is a slightly different experience as it includes the actual coconut.  The problem for me is that the ground whole coconut tastes and has the texture of....ground whole coconut.  Adding the coconut oil for creaminess isn't changing the gritty to smooth.  It changes the velvety texture of the oil to gritty, pasty (think really really thick peanut butter).The only way I use it is making fresh peanut butter or almond butter in the VitaMix using just the nuts and a spoonful of Manna.  Said peanut butter on sandwich with banana or used in peanut butter cookies is borderline sinful.  This is the only thing I've found tastes good with this product.  I use coconut oil for everything else.I was adding it to various recipes but have found that the earthy/dirty (hard to describe) taste of the ground coconut just doesn't work with much.  In addition, it doesn't work well in smoothies in the vitamix as the manna never fully dissolves or incorporates in the drink.

column9: I Prefer Other Forms of Coconut Over This
column10: The closest description I can think of for this product is any organic nut butter.  The oil separates & sits on top of the flesh.  Two difference are this needs to be rather warm in order to mix the oil back into the flesh.  Once you accomplish this task, it will re-separate in 24 hours.After leaving this to warm overnight on my electric space heater, I opened it up & prepared to stir it.  This was a messy affair & I tired of it quickly.  I scooped everything out of those horrible plastic containers & plopped it all into a glass mason jar.  I then got out my hand held immersion blender & proceeded to blend.  This took some time & initially the end result was worth it.  It was smooth & creamy dreamy!  I added a bit to my morning oatmeal & the flavor was amazing.  Surprisingly it did not add a coconut flavor, it created a buttery flavor.  I was impressed.I patted myself on the back too soon when by the next (keeping it warm on my space heater so I could use it as it is like a rock cool) the oil already separated from the flesh. I am accustomed to dealing with real food.  You know food - stuff that doesn't have a bunch of crap added to it.  I grow, raise & grind my own.  I buy organic & only organic.  My point?  This stuff was even more work than I wanted to deal with!My next attempt was to make an icing replacing butter with the coconut.  Oh my! Delicious!  All I did was combine organic confectioners sugar with the coconut & mix it with my hand mixer.  It turned out creamy with a light coconut flavor.  I loved it!  I put it in the refrigerator & then worried that it would turn hard as a rock.  Not so, it was simply perfect!My last attempt, I tried to recreate my icing.  I guess my house was too cold.  What a mess.  Eventually the bulb went off in my head to put the mixing bowl on the stove to warm it while using the hand mixer.  This did the job.  The next day I decided to enjoy some more coco-nutty icing & I just hated it.  Not sure why exactly.  It didn't turn out exactly the same as the first amazing batch.  I can't put my finger on what turned me off so badly but that is it for me.I am sticking with coconut butter & coconut oil.  This stuff is simply too much work & I can get the results I desire using either of the just mentioned forms of coconut with a heck of a lot less work.I removed a star for the plastic packaging.  What makes it worse is the need to keep this warm for use.  At the very least, get this stuff out of the plastic & into glass pronto for your healths sake!  If you love this type of whole coconut puree, try Wilderness Family Naturals.  They sell the exact same stuff in glass!  You can find them on Amazon & they have their own website.I removed a second star for the difficulty to use & my sudden dislike.  Excluding the chemicals that leach into the coconut, the only ingredient is whole coconut & it is Organic.  Vegans, this is a great alternative to butter on your toast, veggies & more!  It is way better than the fake stuff marketed as food to Vegans.

column9: Not sure....but I kind of like it!
column10: I'm just not sold on this product yet. It's interesting. I haven't yet figured out what all to do with it. It tastes good to just scrape some off with a spoon. I did what it said and melted the product (which wasn't easy - had to set it in a warm oven turned off for ages, stirring every hour or so) which just mixed the dark, grainier parts in. I've tried it on toast, which was strange but not bad. I've put it in my coffee, which tastes pretty good, but for the oil slick on the surface and the dregs at the bottom of the cup. I haven't tried it in a smoothie... not sure how much to add or in what form (melted? solid?) So, while this is a cool product - I mean, this much straight coconut in this form would be impossible to make yourself - I just haven't found the right use for it.

column9: Not sold on it, but not giving up on it either
column10: I have been trying to reduce fat, specifically the bad fats, in my diet lately, and try to find ways to increase fiber without eating things that taste like cardboard, so when I had a chance to try coconut manna, I jumped at it.  The packaging says it is a healthy substitute for butter, and can be used as a spread.  My mouth watered at the idea of a bit of this, some nutella, and a banana wrapped up in a whole grain wrap.  The potential here was exciting for someone who loves coconut like I do.The packaging indicated that the oil separates from the coconut, and you must put the container in hot water for five to ten minutes for everything to soften, so that you can stir it all up to a nice smooth consistency.  Sound pretty easy right?  Wrong.  I found after leaving the container in a bowl of hot water for 10 minutes, it was still too hard to stir.  It took three rounds of hot water bath-vigorous stir cycle to get this to wear I could use it.  I tasted it, and was sad that it did not taste nearly as good as I anticipated.  It also had a weird gritty texture, and overall I was not crazy about it.Since clearly this was not going to work as a spread for me, I instead used while cooking mulligatawny soup.  I had created a low fat version of the soup without butter, cream, or milk, so the coconut manna helped add a bit of richness to it.  However, it is still a bit high in calories to be something I would use daily.  I will probably continue using olive oil for much of my cooking, but I do plan on experimenting with the coconut manna when making smoothies, sauces, desserts, and ethnic dishes.  It did nicely in my soup.I am not completely sold on coconut manna, but I am not ready to give up on it either.

column4: J. W. Kennedy "in statu uiae et meriti"
column10: Just one ingredient:  super-fine pureed Coconut.I like the idea, but the physical properties of coconut create a severe disadvantage.  It "freezes" at too high a temperature (73 degrees Fahrenheit) and has to be warmed up each time you want to use it.  When the can arrived it had separated, with the coconut fat on top and the solids at the bottom.  I immersed it in hot water for 5 minutes and then spent another ten minutes stabbing, chopping and stirring it with a butterknife to get all the lumps out.  Once liquefied, it behaves quite a bit like sesame tahini.  It's very runny in the jar & on the knife, but on my tongue it felt sticky like peanut butter.  It tastes like coconut and is actually quite pleasant.  It might be really good mixed with honey.The next day when I wanted to have some more, I opened the jar to find it had solidified again like a chunk of candle wax.  So I re-melted it.  After another 10 minutes of chopping and stirring I have to conclude that this snack is not worth the hassle.  I might like it better in the summer when temperatures are high enough for it to stay liquid ... but in cool weather this item is a fail.  Too much work and not enough reward for me.

This delicious Coconut Manna spread can be used in smoothies, sauces, dressings, desserts, brownies, icing and baked goods. It contains 12% fiber and 9% protein and is a great nutritious  replacement for butter and creams. One tablespoon has 100 calories. A teaspoon full gave my oats a tasty coconut flavor. I also liked combining the Coconut Manna with honey for a snack.This whole food Coconut Manna (a product from the Phillippines) is made of pure, dried coconut flesh. The 15oz jar is certified organic by Ecocert & QUI and is distributed by Nutiva in Oxnard, CA.My only reservation about the product is that it needs to be softened before using. The instructions recommend the jar be placed in hot tap water for 5-10 minutes. For me it took over 20 minutes for the Coconut Manna to soften around the jar's edges. (It never did liquefy.) Some Coconut Manna chunks also took awhile to melt in boiling hot oats.

column9: A lot of work for a slight treat
column10: First of all, this is not easy to use.  My manna shifted during packaging or shipping, so it was a solid chunk on the side of the jar.  I put it in a hot water bath and stirred and chipped away, but it took about 15 minutes of my husband stirring frantically to get the top liquefied to a spreadable state.  The bottom would not soften for the longest time for some reason.  After that bit of chaos, I was hoping for something really special.I was disappointed.  We tried our manna on pancakes (which is a great fiber filled option for a sweetener, instead of syrup).  The gritty texture and not quite sweet flavor was off-putting to me.  My husband loved it, but agreed it was gritty.I also dipped some chunky granola in it.  I found the texture and flavor easier to eat on the granola.We will continue to use it, but we know to prepare a bit of time to get this ready.

I love this organic coconut manna. I eat it by the spoonful and I use it for cooking. It has a light, pleasant coconut flavor. The packaging is convenient and keeps the product fresh. The benefits of coconut are wonderful. Give it a try!

I am familiar with coconut oil as I use it for cooking and baking; however, I was a bit mystified by this product. It has a very hard texture, which is why they suggest letting the container sit in a hot water bath for a few minutes to liquify its contents.Coconut Manna is made from dried coconut meat. The company recommends using it as a spread, adding it to smoothies, dressings, sauces, and ice cream.I tried softening it in hot water, but the consistency never changed.It seems as if it could be a good addition to smoothies and cookie batter,  but getting it out of the jar is a bit of an impediment.

Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna, 15-Ounce (Pack of 2)  My kids and I were divided on taste. In my opinion, the taste is on the flat or bland side with a gritty texture. I expected a burst of coconut flavor and I didn't get that at all.The directions are to melt in hot water to ensure spread-ability. This was a pain in that you can't just open the jar and use the product.My kids spread it on brownies and Oreo's and they loved it. I added some in a batch of pancakes which I thought was tasty and quite different.Overall, I would try something else for more flavor but I think this is a quality product nonetheless and my kids really like it.

I don't eat bread or toast, so I can't speak to using it in that fashion, but I know that it's healthy and delicious. I've eaten it out of the jar thus far. You do have to warm it up and then stir it up, before eating it. Because there is dried coconut in the mix it's not completely smooth...but that just adds to the flavor and texture. I also use Nutiva's coconut oil for lots of things, including body oil, but I also mix it with peanut butter as a topping for low carb ice cream because it solidifies when it hits the ice cream forming a peanut buttery shell. I bet this would be excellent in place of the oil and add fiber, as well. I think I'll give it a try.This manna is fragrant, luxurious and delicious. I highly recommend it. As I type this it's on sale til the end of November '11 - so pick some up, you won't be sorry.

column9: Tasty, but too hard to just scoop out and use
column10: I received my jars of Nutiva Coconut Manna free from the Vine program, in exchange for reviewing the product.I've used regular Nutiva coconut oil for several years and love it - I use it in cooking and also as a body oil and hair conditioner.  I also occasionally add some to the dog's food to make his coat shiny. I love that coconut oil is ready to use right out of the jar, and it's shelf stable for years without refrigeration. I thought I'd try this "manna" and see if we liked it as much as regular coconut oil.Like regular coconut oil, the manna has a very nice coconut fragrance.  Like some of the other reviewers, I was a little surprised to see that it's very hard and solid in the jar.  It reminded me of wax or soap, the way I could scratch off little ribbons with a spoon.  I ate some that way and liked it despite the slight grittiness. I tried some on an english muffin in place of butter - I had to leave scraped chunks on top and melt it in the microwave to get it to spread.  I know the directions say to heat it in a pan of hot water before using it, but who has time to do that every day?The bottom line is that I'll stick with Nutiva coconut oil for daily use.  Even the added fiber and protein in this product doesn't outweigh the fact that this product isn't "ready to use" when you take off the lid.

column9: Not exactly a miracle food, but pretty darn nice.
column10: I've recently started using coconut oil in cooking mostly because I love its flavor and aroma.  I love Nutiva coconut oil, so I thought Nutiva's Manna would be worth a try, and I was correct.  It's something quite different from coconut oil.  I presume that since the only ingredient is "organic whole coconut" that Manna is basically finely ground coconut.  Powdered, actually.  And therein lies my only real objection to this product as a spread that "replaces cream cheese and butter"  It can have a gritty mouth feel.  Oddly, not every taste felt gritty to me, but the grittiness was more marked the warmer the Manna became.And yet, I ate it out of the jar in solid form (The temperature in here hovers around 65 degrees most of the year; much too cool for the Manna to liquefy on its own.) quite happily, so chalk one up for Manna as one of those things you dip into occasionally, like peanut butter or Nutella.  But Manna satisfies more quickly than the other two; a little goes a long way, which is good, I expect.  However I did put some on a piece of bread, and in small amounts, on something that has a lot of texture of its own, what you notice is the flavor, not the texture. Would I eat it with bagels and lox instead of cream cheese?  No.  Would I use it on a sandwich instead of butter?  Well it depends on what the sandwich filling was.  Something that would be complimented by a mild, sweet, coconut flavor would work, I think, maybe a slap-up variation on banh mi.I'm guessing it would be terrific in a smoothie, though unless you're using it for the alleged health benefits, I don't see much point since it would take some time to blend into a cold liquid, and at 100 calories a Tbsp, you'd be consuming a lot of it to get the flavor benefit.No, I'm going to think of it the way I think of peanut butter, a tasty snack for just the right time and place.  I'll use the oil for cooking as I always have.  If I end up lowering my cholesterol or getting any other benefit from Manna other than a lovely flavor, then lucky me.

Coconut manna is definitely an acquired taste.  In my previous review I mentioned that I hate the texture etc.  Since I have gone paleo and am cutting out all sugars etc I still crave and desire something sweet.  So I gave the manna another try.  I am glad I did.  It does have the right amount of sweetness to prevent me from eating something unhealthy and I can add cocoa powder to make something chocolately and somewhat sweet.  I am glad I stuck it out and got used to this.  Now I can't imagine living without it as it saves me from binging on some crap with sugar or corn fructose syrup.

column9: Way tastier than just coconut oil for a nutritional supplement
column10: I've been living the paleo/primal lifestyle for quite sometime now, and coconut oil has become a big part of my calorie intake.  I usually keep a jar with a spoon close by, but after months and months of downing spoonfuls at a time it has started to lose it's appeal.Enter "Nutiva Coconut Manna Good Stuff 16 oz jar."  It's actually a whole food with a whole food flavor.  It tastes like a bite of a fresh coconut - (a little richer due to the fat content) and I love it.  It doesn't have that sickening and dull taste that wore on me like regular cold pressed coconut oil did.If you want something to curb your hunger, make your skin softer (by eating, not topical - you would probably turn into a coconut if you rubbed this stuff on you) and you dig the full coconut flavor, then I highly recommend Coconut Jar Manna Yummy Paste.Heads up -- it's generally separated when you open a new jar. Melt it by holding the closed jar under hot water and stir well.Try this. Your taste buds will thank you.

Coconut oil is a saturated fat. At first glance that alone might make dieters and the health conscious recoil in fear.  Haven't we been told that all saturated fats are artery clogging sludge?  As it turns out, coconut oil is emerging as a near miracle food. Pacific Island populations who get 30-60 percent of their total caloric intake from fully saturated coconut oil have all shown nearly non-existent rates of cardiovascular disease.  The multitude of benefits, including strengthening the immune system and regulating metabolism, make fascinating reading readily available in technical journals and web resources.  Unlike many foods considered healthy, coconut flesh is incredibly delicious.  Since most of us, though, don't relish the idea of hacking the nut to pieces with machetes in the kitchen, coconut is being made conveniently available as in this product, Coconut Manna; a combination of ground coconut flesh and associated oil.  I've been incorporating coconut oil into health shakes so was anxious to try this product which incorporated the flesh as well.  Anyone who has used coconut oil knows that it likes to congeal and form a solid at normal room temperatures and inevitably so in cool locations.  Opening this coconut manna container revealed what resembled a wad of lumpfish stuck to the walls packed in oil.  Not very appetizing.  A metal spoon employed to break it up encountered stubborn resistance.  Submerging the plastic container in warm water would have returned it to an easily workable state, but not something you typically want to do if making a quick health shake or spread.  For that it lost one or maybe one and a half points.  But that's just the natural state of the food and Nutra can't be faulted for that.  The product itself once more malleable is absolutely delicious.  It's tempting to just eat it off the spoon before it makes it to whatever vehicle you planned to park it on.  For smoothy/shake makers, the pure oil form is probably easier to use, though it can congeal also, though probably not as readily or as stubbornly as this manna. It is delicious, but only if you want to take the time to render it at a temperature to make it more easily spread and applied.

Being a big organic coconut oil fan for several years now, I've been really curious about these coconut 'mana' products since I first heard of them so I was delighted to give this one a try.The coconut mana in my container was quite solid when I received it (being cold and in the middle of November in the Pacific Northwest) and the oil had separated from the creme (the former being pure white and the latter being a creamy color) so I let the container sit in hot water for about 30 minutes to soften so I could blend them together. (Nutiva's instructions recommend 5-10 minutes but that may only work if you're in a very warm climate). Afterwards I was able to combine the 2 together pretty easily.It has a pleasant and mildly sweet coconut flavour; but I would hesitate to say it 'melts in your mouth' like Nutiva claims.  It has the consistency of a natural nut butter that has had much of the oil drained out so it's quite dry and stiff and a little 'granular' which may be a problem if you want to spread it on something delicate. Me? I like to eat it straight right out of the container. But I think it would be awesome in recipes, say mixed with dried coconut, almonds or mixed nuts, rolled into balls and dipped in dark chocolate! Yummm!

column9: Still Experimenting-- So Far So Good
column10: "Organic Whole Coconut" sounds simple enough, but I think I have a lot to learn about Coconut Manna.  We've used coconut oil in cooking for years, and shredded coconut in cookies and desserts, and once in awhile we'll bring home a whole coconut to drink the milk and scrape out the meat-- but this is something different.  As other reviewers note, it needs preparation before use: warm the jar in hot water for awhile, otherwise it's solid and chunky.  This may take some time-- really the only drawback to this product.  Once it's achieved a soft consistency, it was good on toast for breakfast, tho I added some powdered sugar to taste. My wife and daughter enjoyed it on their morning oatmeal.  Next experiment: Thai food.  I'm thinking it may work well in the rice cooker as well-- we'll see.First impression: positive.  I look forward to trying it in other permutations.

column9: Tasty, healthy whole coconut - pure organic food
column10: Nutiva adds to its range of organic whole food products with coconut manna, a whole coconut meat product that is organic and nutritious. This is not the same as their coconut oil - this is the full coconut flesh - which does have a high "healthy" fat content. Having been satisfied with other Nutiva products I've used (such as hemp & chia seeds, coconut oil, hemp protein powder mixes, etc.), I expected high quality and wasn't disappointed. This coconut manna tastes great and is easy to use and store. You can put some in any recipe that calls for coconut and this sure beats having to crack open a fresh cocunut and cut out the coconut meat. For quality, organic coconut that doesn't require coconut cracking labor, Nutiva offers an excellent option.

I didn't really know what to expect from this product because I have never tried anything like it before.  The first thing I found is that it takes a lot longer to warm it up and get it to a point where it is spreadable, so if you're in a hurry for it, you may be frustrated.  The taste was pretty good.  I like the flavor of coconut, but I'm just not sure if this is worth the high fat and calorie content.  In small amounts it's quite tasty, but too much is just not good.  So overall, it is okay.  It tastes pretty good, but I wouldn't want to eat it everyday.

Manna is an appropriate way to describe this beautiful, pure and divine concoction, made purely and simply from coconut "meat." It literally melts in your mouth. It comes as a solid in the container. You just have to place it in hot water for ten minutes, then stir it. This can be used as a spread or for anything, really.

column9: Nice flavor, but not entirely user friendly
column10: Assuming you like the taste of coconut (and I do), Nutiva's organic coconut manna has a lot of potential in the kitchen. Just a spoonful of this coconut butter -- nothing but finely ground up coconut meat including the coconut oil -- will give everything you add it to a creamy coconut richness. I liked the short ingredient list (organic whole coconut) and loved the way it smelled when I opened the jar. It has a much more nutty, creamy fragrance than plain coconut oil.Getting the coconut manna to the point where I could use it was a bit tricky. As per the directions on the package, I put the jar in hot water for 15 minutes and attempted to stir. The top, mostly coconut oil, melted just fine. The bottom did not. Even after putting it back in the hot water for a while, I didn't so much stir as chisel away with the heaviest butter knife I could find.30 minutes later, I finally got it to the texture of creamed honey and tried a little. It definitely does coat your tongue with a sticky, slightly gritty feel (I would not recommend eating it straight out of the jar, on its own), but the taste -- coconut-y, rich, and not too sweet -- was pleasant. I spread it on toast with matamis na bao (coconut caramel) drizzled on top for a little more sweetness and enjoyed it. Due to the high fat content, it is very, very filling.My favorite application so far has been oatmeal. A spoonful stirred in made my regular oatmeal taste like Thai sticky rice! Just a little goes a long way to adding flavor, creaminess, and some stick-to-your-ribs fiber and fat. I haven't been able to find ratios for substituting it in baked goods, but I am more likely to try adding a teaspoon or two for flavor than swapping out all the oil of a recipe. I think the coconut manna will make some amazing tropical flavored smoothies once the weather starts warming up again.I feel a little daunted by the thought of having to stir the jar every time I use it, even though it shouldn't be as bad as the first time. Even in California, it's not exactly spreadable at room temperature. Although I doubt coconut butter will become a pantry staple for me, I find that I am looking forward to incorporating a spoonful here and there in my cooking and baking.

I routinely use some coconut oil in cooking since it is a very healthy fat with zero trans fat. Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna is different than coconut oil in that it is more of a solid, but I absolutely love it! It's almost like spread butter, in fact it would be good to use as a replacement for butter. The flavor is great and would be super to use it in cooking as well. I put a spoonful in green beans and I think it adds a wonderful flavor to them.Nutiva's website has some great recipes for smoothies, brownies, etc. I also got Nutiva's Chia Seeds and it has a recipe for cereal using both products. The product label states that it contains 12% fiber which is great and 9% protein...that is awesome!It's also really convenient to have the pack of 2. I absolutely HATE running out of something I use often and I like having the second one on hand. When I open it...it's time to get more! You don't have to refrigerate it either so that is a plus. Great product!Added review: Nov. 1, 2011My husband took one of the containers to work and said it is great when you use it off the top, but if you heat it up like it recommends the taste and texture changes. He hates both! He tried it as butter on wafers and he said it was not great either. However, he did use it as butter on popcorn and it was delicious. Based on his review, I changed it to a four star.

I love coconut oil, and Nutiva is one of my favorite brands, so of course I had to try coconut butter/manna. At least as far as I can tell, this coconut "manna" is what you also find referred to as coconut "butter". My boyfriend thought it would be a good substitute for coconut oil in baking - he uses the oil in a lot of things including flour tortillas and deep dish pizza crust (our "secret" ingredient) - but it really is better to use the oil. The tortillas are a little stiffer with the manna and pizza dough a little harder to work with and the end texture not quite as good. Still, the manna/butter does have some great uses - what I mostly use it for is my vegan cheese recipe. Once you refrigerate the nut cheese, the coconut butter is what makes it take on a more solid texture.The reason I didn't give it five stars is just because I think the Nutiva coconut oil is so great with great coconut smell and flavor and the manna is somewhat limited in comparison. If you already have the oil and are coo coo for coconut and looking for more, then maybe you want to try this. Or if you have a recipe that calls for it, it's probably worth it, but anything *I* have used the manna for I could have used the oil for with the same or better results.

The reviews that say it is hard to use because at room temperature it is hard as a rock are correct, Unless you have a way to heat the container up in hot water for several minutes I would suggest something else.  Once warm it is delicious, but it is kind of a nuisance.

I purchased this item from the local health food store - and it was in a glass jar.Fell in love with the flavor.  But when I placed my Amazon order, I didn't bother to lookas to whether or not it was the same glass jar (my fault).  My order came today, andyou guessed it, the manna was in plastic jars.It is the same product, but in my opinion it doesn't taste asgood as the coconut manna from the glass jar.  I'm willing to go back to the health foodstore and pay a little bit more, so I won't have the plastic interfering with solovely a product.

column9: Just what I had been looking for.
column10: I've been trying to shift my diet to paleo slowly.  I made coconut/almond bread and  using this spread along with either raw honey or almond butter was really a treat.  Also good in smoothies!!

column9: A new kitchen staple for us
column10: Just got this and my wife and I fell in love.  Took a bit of work to get it mixed up.  I tried what the label said and submerge the can in hot water for 5-10 minutes, but I was still unable to mix it with a spoon.  Ended up putting it in the blender and that did the trick.  It made it into a nice cream.  It's delicious plain - it's a bit dry, but that doesn't bother me.  We also put it in a mango strawberry smoothie, and it was excellent.  I highly recommend this.  I'm going to need to bump up the subscribe & save shipment time for this, 2 jars won't be lasting us two months.

I tried the artisana brand first, which i was head over heels in love with.. usually after trying one brand, ill keep switching around just to see whats great, whats not. I found nutiva to be pretty comparable for less. Yes artisana is ahhh-maazzinng, but this is just as sensational. I dont mind the gritty taste, to me its not even gritty. I dont melt it or anything. I eat it on a spoon right out of the jar, topped with some fresh coconut oil, smothered right on to a banana for breakfast, with a side of almonds and green tea. Its my new favorite breakfast, and actually keeps me full a lot longer. I'll continue to purchase, while i may explore other brands, i do like there coconut manna. As for coconut oil, jarrows by far has the best oil i've ever tasted. It is very rich.Cheers!

1. One tablespoon satisfies hunger pangs for 2-3 hours.2. The oil part is predominately MCTs, which are used directly for energy.3. Great for travel - no refridgeration neededI tried several other brands and this is the best tasting.

column9: Love the flavor! better than a spoonful of plain coconut oil
column10: I have been using the Nutiva extra-virgin coconut oil to super-charge my smoothies as I'm trying to gain weight. Although I love everything coconut, I was having a hard time liking the oil. I found out about this product, decided to give it try, and I'm so glad I did. I have no problems mixing it since it's 95 degrees outside at this moment. I was able to take a spoonful right out of jar and eat it. I think it will be super easy to reach my daily healthy fat intake with coconut manna.
It is good for everything like smoothies to using it like Peamut butter on toast. I sometimes mix the two.Besides, it is really good  for  you!!!!

I take a spoonful of Coconut Manna every day. This is a blend of coconut oil and the coconut meat and it tastes sweet and yummy. Very good antifungal and a healthy oil for heart, brain, hair, joints. I use regular coconut oil for cooking. Some people complain about it separating, which is true, but I use a fork and rake it from the glass to the middle. Then it is easy to take a spoonful. You could gently heat it (in a pot of hot water) and then mix it up but I never heat it. I prefer the glass jar to the newer plastic they are using, but I am happy it is Organic.
For some reason I expected this product to be sweet - it's not! It does taste great though when added to smoothies and yogurt. Yum!

This stuff is really good, little expensive. While the one amazon ships comes in plastic jars, you can still buy them in glass jars elsewhere. If your a coconut oil lover, you're gonna have a new love!
I use this in making Primal/paleo Chocolate Almond Coconut bark. It adds a nice texture and a boost of fiber. Shipped very quickly from Amazon.

THIS STUFF AMAZING! For coconut lovers it"s a must. And I'm not even a coconut flavor lover. Coconuts unless they're right off the tree can be really bad. This stuff is really good! It tastes just like "unfooled with" coconut. And there is solid (actually no pun intended) research on the benefits of coconut as a fat. YUM I'm happy.

column9: Love the flavor, dislike the packaging
column10: Trying to eat more unprocessed and natural foods, I had been interested in coconut manna although I wasn't quite sure what to expect. It's basically a coconut cream made from organic dried coconut meat that is spreadable like butter (a little more gritty than butter, though).When I received it, I opened the container - the wonderful smell of coconut wafted up, but it had clearly melted and resolidified. I was quite hesitant at that point. Reading some reviews and suggestions on how to eat it, I warmed it in a bowl of warm water, then dipped my finger in for a taste.Wow. It is delish.It is also high in fat, so I will be using it sparingly, but it teaspoon goes well with my chia seeds for a breakfast, and I've used it to saute meat for some Thai dishes. I also added it to a strawberry smoothie - YUM!My biggest complaint is that it's in a plastic tub, especially because it has to be heated to be used. I removed mine from the packaging it came in and placed it in a glass jar (which actually seems to reduce the warm water heat time).

I love coconut, but when I bought this product, I still wasn't entirely sure what I planned to do with it.  Living in cold, northern climes, smoothies aren't that appealing for many months a year.  Now, I know.  I'm going to eat it out of the jar on a spoon.Like I said, I live in the cold north, and this product was indeed rock solid when I first opened the jar.  I boiled some water for tea, then after the leftover water had cooled down for a few minutes, I pour it into a bowl and set the jar of Coconut Manna in it.  I confess I forgot about it for a little while and it probably sat in the hot water for 10-15 minutes.  After that, it was no harder to stir than a new jar of natural peanut butter.  When I licked the stirring spoon, it was so delicious my head nearly fell off.  I ate a couple spoonfuls and then put the jar away.A few hours later, I opened the jar again out of curiosity.  Though starting to solidify around the edges, it was still mostly soft.  Good to know that after you go through the trouble to process it, it stays usable (eatable) for quite a while.

I have to admit when I read 'made from dried coconuts...melts in your mouth", I thought this would be freeze-dried coconut bits for snacking. I did not expect the jar of heaven instead........I reviewed Artisana 100% Organic Raw Coconut Butter -- 16 oz, I've used it as my go-to spread for flax seed microwave muffins, and especially love it in yellow curry (or any curry for that matter!). I had not found another brand that I liked better for taste. Until now.I've been a faithful user of Nutiva coconut oil for a long time, buying it by the 5 gallon pail. If you love Nutiva coconut oil, imagine that wonderful coconut smell amplified a thousandfold. Imagine now, the coconut manna, which TASTES like that smell. It's so good, you can actually eat it on a spoon straight out of the jar. It does not have the high particulate content like the Artisana, instead this is very smooth and creamy yet it's substantial in your mouth. It also made my curry recipe FINALLY taste like the one from the Thai restaurant that we gave up for budgetary reasons.If you are searching for THE perfect coconut butter, THIS is your stuff! Don't even bother wasting a cent on any other brand, get this! There are instructions on the jar for tempering in case your product separates, but mine arrived perfectly blended even though the outside temperature was way above its melting point. It was easy to scoop out (and eat right out of the jar). I even put some of this on top of my sunny-side-up eggs right before removing from the skillet, and it made them taste even better!Love this and it will forever be on my reorder list! THANKS NUTIVA for yet another great product!

column9: Nice idea, but full of fat.
column10: If you're sick of using butter and need an alternative, by all means try this product. Unless you're frying eggs and do not wish for them to taste of coconut, this product was designed to replace the fat in your diet with something more healthy. There are recipes too - it's quite nice in oatmeal and enhances smoothies quite well - something I've been trying to find for quite some time. The most aggravating thing, however, is that the product solidifies and you have to let it soak in how water for 5-10 minutes before you can use it EACH time. That can be annoying if you're in a hurry as I usually am most mornings. It isn't sweet so you won't be adding additional sugar to your recipes - just the flavor. A very neat product, but something that you should use very sparingly because of the fat content. Recommend but with the above caution.

column9: Depends what you want to use it for
column10: OK, I am used to using coconut oil bought at grocery store and some stuff I ordered in bulk. The Nutiva is richer. you can feel the richness when you touch it and when you look at it. But for the things I want coconut oil for it doesn't work as good as the cheaper stuff....It isn't good to fry with. It turns quite dark when cooked with. If you just melted it over a double boiler it probably do a lot better.And I use coconut oil in soap making and skin cream making. Because it turns so dark when cooked it doesn't do well for either of these. Plus, it leaves a smell in the skin cream I made -- when the cheaper kinds don't have any odor. It isn't a bad smell but it isn't one you want on skin probably.So, I think it depends what you want to use it for. Melting it slowly and adding it to a spread is an ideal way to use this product. If that is what you use it for then it is probably quite good, better than the cheap stuff.

column4: Marshall Carter "Ornery Gamer, Fiend Club Member"
column9: Ok for cooking, but a hassle for "quick" use.
column10: Following the instructions provided with the Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna, you unfortunately still do not get a smooth, usable product. When I first opened it, I was surprised to see a hard, white surface right beneath the lid, where the product had obviously melted and then resolidified during shipment. I shaved a bit off with a knife to taste, and sure enough, it tasted like natural coconut. That's a good sign. I went ahead and followed the instructions to basically melt/mix the product, placing it under hot running tap water for 5-10 minutes (the directions say two), and that really didn't make much of a dent. After letting it sit for another 10 minutes, it was finally mixable.So mix it I did, only to be greeted with a very unpleasant, gritty texture. That might not be that big a deal if you're cooking with it (using it to replace butter for instance), but it's not exactly a good characteristic for something that Nutiva mentions spreading on bread or crackers. The smoothie recommendation is also suspect because of the grit, especially since it would start to harden again the minute it gets remotely close to a frosty beverage. For this kind of usage, the Coconut Manna is more hassle than it's worth.I'll figure out a way to use this (planning on using it in a Thai-style coconut curry), but this is not the convenient product it's marketed to be. As an ingredient for cooking, I say it works and would be easy enough to use, but as a quick, spreadable addition to your  foods, it's disappointing to me.

I'm totally hooked on this!  I have been eating it straight from the container and it's delicious.  When I first got this, I tried warming it up and eating it that way, but it was a little thick for me to swallow that way.  Now I just cut it up in the container and scoop up the pieces with a spoon.  It's really a wonderful product and I'm so glad I decided to give it a try.  I have it on my Subscribe and Save now as I don't want to run out.

Wow! We already have enjoyed using coconut oil in our house and at first glance, this looks very much like it is just coconut oil. But...the taste is heavenly, more coconutty than the oil. We'll be buying this again. Be sure to warm the product to mix and spread, if your kitchen is less on 76 degrees, and it will work just fine.

column9: Not as good as regular coconut oil
column10: I've been using coconut oil for some years and I selected this in the Vine program because everything else I clicked on was not available.It has an odd flavor, not like regular coconut oil and a gritty texture that I don't like, even when gently softened in warm water.It did not blend smoothly into the cream soups that I have been preparing (with coconut oil) for some years.I can't explain all the details of just why I don't like this product but it certainly does not live up to the hype.I will stick with the regular organic, extra virgin coconut oil from the same producer.  It is a superior product and much more versatile than this "Manna"

Let me begin by saying that I am not a super health nut. I don't shop at Trader Joe's regularly, partially because there isn't one near me and partially because I'm fine with eating regular/typical food from a regular/typical grocery store. I like coconut and I like to try new things, so I requested this from the Amazon Vine program.Nutiva brags that there are recipes to try on their website nutiva.com. However, all the recipes I saw required not only coconut manna, but also hemp oil or hemp seed, or other *natural/organic* whatever ingredients that I do not have nor do I want to buy. Anyway, so those recipes were a bust for me.The coconut manna, like it says on the container, needs to be heated by placing the jar in a bowl of hot tap water, and then stirring before it is the *melt in your mouth* consistency. Let me tell you, the first time I tried it, this required a lot of stirring. However, once heated and stirred, it has a runny peanut butter consistency. But, when tasted, there is a gritty kind of after taste.It is simply organic coconut, nothing else. This is not the "sweetened" coconut you get flakes of on cookies. That is fine, but consider yourself warned. I have tried it spread on toast (with butter and a little cinnamon sugar) and that was alright. It made a nice flavor on toast, but I could definitely feel/taste the grittiness of the coconut. I've also put it in plain oatmeal, with a little brown sugar, raisins, and cinnamon. This was better than the toast. I haven't tried baking with it nor with smoothies yet but will soon.I would not call this the "ideal everything spread" as the jar claims, nor would I replace cream, cream cheese or butter with coconut manna. However, I like it and will continue to experiment with different ways of incorporating it into snacks and meals.

I don't quite understand this product.The product at my kitchen temperature consists of a large and pretty sincerely solid solid on the bottom of the jar and an oil on top.  You may use either substance by itself, but if you want to use the product as designed you should mix the solid and the liquid together so that any cc is the same viscosity and has the same ratio of ingredients and as any other cc.The solid really is, and until it's liquefied you can't use the product.According to the Amazon description page, which is no doubt what many people will rely on in deciding whether to buy this product, "To liquify [sic], place jar in hot water for 2 minutes and stir."  I don't know exactly what the term "hot water" means, but unless it means more than boiling (which is impossible except in a sealed vessel such as a pressure cooker), this won't work.  Not after two minutes and not after twice that again.  Unless they're talking about two minutes on Pluto, whose day is 6 Earth days plus 9 hours, which is 6.375 times longer, which when multiplied by 2 minutes is 12 Earth minutes plus 45 seconds, which would make more sense (except for the Pluto part).The Nutiva Web site says you can melt it by placing it in a hot but not boiling water bath for -- and you'll see I'm quoting here -- "a few moments."  I don't know about you, but to me "a few moments" is significantly less than the two minutes we already know is more than a little bit too little.  And don't forget that to those few moments you have to add the time it takes to gather a heat-proof vessel and water and turn on the stove and then wait for the water to heat up.  Not to mention the expense, however little, of producing that heat and buying that water.  Not to mention having to remember to turn off that heat source.  Not to mention washing however sincerely you want to that heating vessel, after you've waited for it cool down sufficiently, and then drying it and returning it whence it came.Sheeesh.The texture of the properly mixed substance -- a colloid suspension that must eventually separate, if I'm not mistaken -- when eaten plain from a spoon or the superior end of someone's superior natal cleft is not what I expected, being more gritty like wasabi than velvety like the inside part of good caviar.  Still, like wasabi it's not designed to be licked from a spoon like ice cream, so I subtract no stars for this.Nutiva Organic Coconut Manna, 15-Ounce (Pack of 2) seems to me like quite a specialty product, almost a novelty, which is why I said I don't quite understand it.  In order to add it to "smoothies, sauces, and dressings" or to use it in any other way, according to the manufacturer you start by liquefying it in a hot water bath and then mixing it.  This makes it quite different from, say, apple butter, which you just open the jar of and out of from which you dip or pour some.So many other similar foods require less effort and certainly less time, such as margarine and honey.And this product, when used as recommended by the manufacturer, requires at least that you have a heating vessel and water and a source of heat, so you probably won't want to take it on a picnic or to the local swimming hole.  So many other similar foods require no additional parts except maybe a spoon, such as ranch dressing and yogurt and orange marmalade.  And they don't require mixing.For the inconvenience, which makes it less likely I will use the product even if I knew the best way to use it, I subtract two stars.The Amazon description page says, "Coconut Manna will delight people looking for coconut butter, coconut cream, coconut oil butter and coconut body butter."  If by coconut body butter is meant a substance you would slather all over your body for some reason, I will not be reporting on that particular use for this review.  Ever.Those of you who've read a few of my recent reviews will not be surprised to learn that I did experiment with some more off-label uses, and here are the results.-- You should not expect this food to be a good substitute for the butter in Alfredo sauce or for the egg whites in a meringue.-- You should not paint your house with this food unless you really, really like lots more local wildlife than you ever knew existed.  You should use real paint.-- This product is an utter failure as a substitute for parakeet shampoo.  You should use real parakeet shampoo.-- As a shaving cream it sucks hard unless you like many small lacerations on your face.  You should use real shaving cream.-- It makes for a terrible antibiotic ointment for many small lacerations on your face unless you like many pusillanimous and mephitic infections on your face.  Speaking strictly for myself here, as it turns out I do not.In case you're wondering, despite all the failures in the bulleted list just above I subtract no further stars.

This does have a true coconut flavor.  However, when I got it, the manna had obviously melted and then solidified again (it had obviously been on its side when it melted, because that's how it was when it came to my doorstep).  I had to soften it.  The directions said to set in hot water for 10 minutes to soften, so I did.  Still hard as a rock.  Tried setting the jar in hot water for another 20 minutes, but it still didn't soften.  So I put it on my kitchen heater vent for an hour.  That did the trick; it was mostly softened, so after stirring the hard part into the soft part, the jar went back on my heater vent for another hour.  The finished doing the job.  So, now, with a very soft product, I got a spoon and tasted it.  It was *so* gritty!  And it stuck to the roof of my mouth worse than peanut butter.I prefer Artisana 100% Organic Raw Coconut Butter -- 16 oz, which is slightly softer and has absolutely no gritty feel -- and the Artisana doesn't stick to the roof of my mouth either.

I tried  this several times and  have not been able to convince myself it is a great product.  Once softened it is spreadable.The consistenacy is fine once you get it softened and  mixed well. Very bland tasting. To me it feels like I was eating a spoonful of coconut flavored  crisco with a slightly different texture. I  cannot think of anything I would use it for except maybe some baking.As for giving it  to your pets becareful,  it can have a laxative effect and your pet may have an allergic reaction. I would consult my pets veterinarian before  giving it to my pet.

I can't say this "melts in the mouth" but it's good stuff.  As the package says, it tends to separate.  I received two jars through the Vine program.  The first I heated, stirred up and tried to use as directed - as a sort of peanut butter substitute.  It was ok but not something I'd do again.  Then I tried adding it to a lackluster jarred curry sauce and it was fabulous!  It added depth and a nutty warmth.
