If you really want something special fresh grade parmesan cheese on your corn, I guarantee you will love it.

column9: Best Popcorn Salt - Morton Popcorn Salt
column10: I had been looking for popcorn salt for awhile and this is the best popcorn salt I have found. Popcorn doesn't taste right without the fine granulated texture of this salt. Luckily I found this on Amazon and I can look forward to having my popcorn with the best taste for a long time.

My husband still makes popcorn the old fashion way. He likes to use the popcorn salt with olive oil. I use to be able to find it at the grocery stores but lately no one was carrying it. I thought of Amazon immediately because if you need an item and you can't find it you will on Amazon.

And I'm a huge fan of Diamond Crystal products, but this salt is far superiorIMO. Its smaller granules, much flakier, and adheres better to the popcornkernels.Its practically perfect, just has a good quality salt flavor with no fillersor anti-caking agents, and also works well on corn-on-the-cob, in salads, onbaked potatoes... just about everything!

column9: Perfect for popcorn, but take care when ordering
column10: The fine grind of the salt is perfect for popcorn however, BUYER BEWARE, when this is packed it is with anything else you just bought...and bouncing around in the box tends to pop the tops off of one or more of these little canisters making everything salt-covered (like my entire shipment was).  Not sure how to get around this, but you should be warned that this will likely happen.

I admit to being a saltaholic and this is my favorite of all time.  It actually allows me to use less, since it is so fine that a little goes a long way.  I use it on everything.  I would give it 5 stars, but it is not iodized (are you listening, Morton?).  I buy it in the 12-pack from Amazon for the best price around.  Also, it can sometimes be hard to find.

column9: A must for really great popcorn
column10: I originally found this in my local supermarket, and then for some reason they stopped carrying it. Your home popped popcorn will taste so much better with real popcorn salt instead of regular granulated salt. Normally I wouldn't want to buy a pack of 12 (after all, each one lasts quite a while) but I have taken to giving them to friends who can't believe how much better popcorn is this way. (Also, I *highly* recommend Trader Joe's organic popcorn to put this on - if you have a Trader Joe's near you, it's way less expensive than Redenbacher and even better.)

We love making popcorn on Friday evenings...after adding melted margarine/butter, the final ingredient to make the popcorn "just right" is this Morton's Popcorn Salt. It is the caviar of hand popped popcorn.
Good, fine salt works well. Multipack is nice to keep handy at multiple locations. Wish it was not so expensive.

When I opened the box, there was salt all over.  The tops were off 2 of the shakers.  Since there was no damage to the outside packaging, and there were air pillows all around the plastic shrink wrapped set of shakers, it looks like Amazon sent these out with the tops all ready off of the shakers.  This is not the first time something like this has happened.  Amazon, stop sending out products that are damaged!  I order a ton of stuff, because the prices are so good, and the free shipping.  But I am getting a little tired of the small things here and there that are damaged.

THese are delicious.  I use them as a breakfast subsitute sometimes, but mostly as an energy boost during or before long bicycle rides; the protein is a bonus.  They are also good to take on the boat or kayak during a photo trip or to fill in when you are not in a position to have a meal.

column9: They are good, but peanut allergy beware!
column10: I bought these for my wife actually because she can eat Almonds but not Peanuts. THESE HAVE PEANUTS IN THEM!Fortunately I was able to eat them. But my wife was out of luck. If you suffer from peanut allergy beware, the name of the product is deceiving.

These are unbelieveably good!  I've been indulging in them for 6 months now.  I'm glad Amazon is carrying them now b/c I previously had to have my sister buy me a ton (she lives in Portland OR where its trendy and I live in middle of nowhere MN where we have nothing good! LOL) and mail them to me.  Just now I was bummed to see that I am down to my last pack of them, but I'm happy that I can order them from Amazon now.  Amazing product - give em a try, you won't be disappointed!

Dark chocolate and almond butter--two of my favorite foods.  When I found out that Sunspire makes these dark chocolate almond butter cups, I was so very tempted to buy the 24-pack.  I refrained, though, because I wasn't sure it was worth paying $40 for a large package of edible items I had never even tried.  Instead, I happened to come across individual packages at the local food co-op, and was extremely jazzed to give them a try.  Unfortunately, they left me a little disappointed.  Don't get me wrong, the dark chocolate was really delicious, but that was about all I could taste.  There was hardly any almond butter within the cup itself, and that was what I was really excited about.  I would estimate that by volume, the cup is 80% chocolate and 20% almond butter.  So, in the end, it's not your Reese's-caliber cup, with a light covering of chocolate on the outside and a generous helping of nut butter on the inside, but it will definitely satisfy a sweet-tooth in a pinch, and the product appears less processed and even a bit healthier than the more popular alternatives.  My suggestion: don't blindly buy the 24-pack: see if you can find an individual pack to try first.

I love Sesmark Rice Thins!  I have intolerances to wheat, dairy, soy and eggs.  So, finding a cracker that does not contain either of these are hard.  So, I found out about Sesmark about 5 months ago and every since then, I have been hooked.  So, if you have intolerances but still crave something crunchy, slightly salty, then the Sesmark Rice Thins are for you.

These crackers are great, especially for people who cannot tolerate wheat, but they good for everyone.  My friends like them a lot, too!  They stay crunchy.  AND buying in quantity saves money over buying individual packages in the stores.  I cannot always find them in stores, so I am really happy to have them on hand!
Great crackers with no artificial ingredients. All they are is brown rice and salt. Very crisp and good taste!

column9: white rice IS brown rice...just naked...
column10: To the two-star review that has decided to eschew this product because the ingredients are "white rice with rice bran" instead of brown rice, that's a difference without distinction. Brown rice is unpolished white rice. For manufacturing/cooking or some other reason, the manufacturer decided to use polished brown rice, i.e. white rice and then add back the bran. I see no downside.To go further, they're crackers, not your main source for anything. If you eat rice as a staple or because you can't have wheat, then by all means serve brown rice, but like I said, they are a snack. Ok, beat that to death... now on to the review.I didn't realize that Amazon sold these, so I've been buying them in the supermarket. Just ordered a 12-pack. I like that they have no after-taste, have lots of crunch, will stand up to dip (or salsa, although they are a little small for that) and that they are relatively low in calories compared to other crackers like Ritz, Triscuits, etc.There is only one negative. I have a very difficult time eating just a couple. I have to put the package back in the fridge, less they all disappear while I am doing the bills, watching tv, etc....and my dogs love them, too...

I love the taste of these rice thins alone or with taboule. I have one issue with these "natural" crackers that I just realized, though. It does not say if they use sea salt or processed salt. Most products that use sea salt will say so. I would like to know if it's natural salt or not. If it isn't and I find out about it, I will not eat these again. If I am not able to find out, again I probably will not eat them anymore. I can find no info on their website about it. Not even under FAQ. Processed salt is a chemical poison and should not be considered natural. If it is sea salt, they should say so on the package. My lower rating is for the fact that they may not be using natural salt and/or they don't clarify if they do. Natural salt=healthy  Commercially processed salt=very unhealthyI am concerned about it because I know how dangerous Morton salt and crap like that is for you. When Morton first developed their "no clumping" chemical salt, they gave it to the farmer's cows in place of the natural salt they were normally given. In a very short time the cows developed health issues. As soon as they got them off the Morton "crap" the cows health were restored. Leave it to man to screw things up that God made perfectly.  This can't be a natural product without natural salt.

"May contain trace amounts of tree nuts, dairy and wheat." I was ready to order until I saw this info. Not good for a Celiac/Gluten-intolerant person with additional dairy allergy! How can products get away with saying they are gluten-free & then post a little warning that the food may contain wheat???!!! :(

Just an FYI, as of 3/2012, these crackers now contain SOY. they didn't used to, but they do now. We ordered a 12-pack only to find the change. This web site doesn't list soy as an ingredient, but Sesmark's web site shows the new ingredient list: brown rice, expeller pressed safflower oil, salt and soybean tocopherols.[...]

We have been eating these crackers for 6 years.  Recently my son started having allergic symptoms and we discovered these crackers now contain soy!  If you have allergies be aware the ingredients have changed in the last few months!

column4: Lover of Books, Food & Good Deals
column10: Besides the fact that Amazon Subscribe and Save lets me get these for a reasonable price whenever I want, they taste great, fill the yen for something crunchy and are stronger than other brands of rice crackers so they can be used as dippers. Now if only they were organic.

We ordered the Sesmark brown rice crackers because they do not contain wheat and go well with so many types of cheeses, dips, and spreads.  They arrived well packed so that only rarely is there even a crack in a cracker.
Best gluten-free cracker by far!  No strange after taste.  Crispy salty, but not too salty.  Low fat and delicious.  5 stars out of 5.

These are good crackers and very reasonably priced for those with wheat allergies. My youngest loves them.  Just wish they came with less salt and weren't packed in No. 6 plastic, but you can't have everything!  They're delicious!
Tastes good with any cracker pairing. Nicely flavored, not too salty and  made with brown rice. Is a great gluten free cracker.

I decided to try these because the other brand was no longer available in some of the flavors we like. The reviews were excellent and I totally agree that these are delicious and crunchy. I would definitely buy these again. My husband gobbled up the first box with different cheeses so I guess it's a winner with him too!

When I found out I was gluten-intolerant I had a lot of functional foods to replace. As I began to search out and try what the health stores and groceries had to offer I ran into a lot of truly unappetizing products - and no really great ones.When it came to crackers, breads, or other easy-to-use holders of spreads and dips and sandwich makings, I quickly learned that the bread choices were worse than eating cardboard. So I began to explore the various crackers.Most were rice based. Some were spiced up with flavorings that tasted like chemicals. Others were limp or crumbly. Some were terribly bland.Then I discovered Sesmark Rice Thins.They are quite crunchy, with a satisfying snap to them, and while the Brown Rice flavor is not an exciting taste, it serves very well with all sorts of other foods: sesame tahini or nut butters; babaganous, hummus, olive tepenade, caponata, etc; also with butter or cream cheese. They are not too salty, but do have a some sea salt that is just right for me in these settings.I also like them by themselves. A snack of 5 of these (about 40 calories, half a gram of fat) is satisfying for the odd moment of feeling like eating carbs.In fact, their blandness keeps me from wanting more than I 'need'. Limiting myself to 5 works very well.I really love the taste of the Sesame flavor of these Rice Thins, and could eat a full package at one sitting. They don't need any toppings, though they take them well. Their crunch is slightly less snappy, still great. If you like sesame, these are a great choice, gluten-free or not.
These are the best rice crackers I have been able to find, online or in a store.
Being on a special diet, this Rice thins are perfect. They digest easily and to me they are very tasty.  Everyone that has tried them thinks they are great.

At first I was happy to find this product in the store, since I am on a gluten free and no white rice diet.  The lable on the package says brown rice.  Thank you Amazon for noting the "brown rice" is actually a combination of white rice and rice bran.  It is amazing the amount of flexibility in labeling standards.

These rice crackers were pretty bland. Even for a rice cracker. If you're looking for something with a more pleasing flavor - try the brand sold at Target. (Archer Farms)  I will say these did arrive in good condition. Hardly a broken cracker in the lot. The packaging prevented them from arriving as a carton of rice crumbs. Alas, great packaging still didn't make a bland cracker taste better :-(
I love this crackers!! Very crunchy, not too much salt, just delicious. The price is right. No delays, and they come very fresh.

Crackers looked fine but I didn't try them because the ingredient list on the package listed soy, which I can't have.  I went back and checked the Amazon description and the ingredient list did NOT list soy.  Makes me hesitate to order grocery items if I can not trust the information on the description.
As with their others of their thin rice crackers, these contain so much salt they are not edible. BE CAREFUL before ordering these since there is NO RETURN and you might find yourself with landfill.

These are a bit salty but are very tasty. They are the perfect match to humus. They don't have a lot of flavor on their own but work well as a foil for other foods. The flavor is mild and delicate, even though they are made with brown rice they are not too dense or gritty.They are relatively low in calories so you can eat a lot and not feel too guilty. Beware, you can go through a package fast.

I am very restricted in what I can eat, and I eat a lot of rice products including ricecakes.  I get teased alot about eating "cardboard" until I let people taste these little crackers.  They are always shocked at how good they are and quit teasing me.  Thanks for making a product that I can eat....and enjoy!!!
These rice crackers are a perfect snack any time.  They are flavorful and have simple list of ingredients.
Love these crackers and love Sabra brand hummus (pine nut and jalapeno are my favs) and they are excellent together for a quick snack!
This is a nice simple cracker that does not trigger my food intolerances.  Good with tuna or some other topping.  Flavor is nice and not so overpowering.  I will buy these again.

I purchased these crackers because I have a wheat allergy and they are delicious.  They are not like other rice crackers I had tried.  Now everyone in my family prefers them over regular saltines, and I even have to order them for my mother in law!!!  They are crispy, tasty with just the right amount of salt, and very satisfying.  I highly recommend them.  Amazon is the best place to buy them for price and availability.
This is another gluten-free product that my daughter can enjoy.  I have bought these by the package, and it is less expensive to buy them by the case.

This is not real kombucha.  It may have a little bit of kombucha in it, but it is mostly carbonated water and juice. It comes in a plastic container, which real kombucha never should be in contact with plastic.  It tastes good, but I don't think there's much benefit in drinking it.
Good price and good product, have trouble finding the bites in my supermarket. Have subscribed to receive at my door every few months.

There's a sucker born every minute.. and I am one.  lol  I had no idea how much Red Hot candies weigh, but evidently it's more than my original estimate.  Although the bag is only 7 oz, the image of the item appeared to be a larger, so I ordered and paid $7 (or $1/ounce.  When the bag came I was shocked at the size.  This is similar to the boxes of candy you can buy at the movie theater (those are 6 oz, this is 7oz.  Since Amazon doesn't allow returns on grocery items, I'm stuck with a small and expensive bag of candy.  Buyer Beware.

I bought these red hots as a stocking stuffer. I looked at the price of $6 bucks for red hots and thought it would be a HUGE bag. The bag was tiny! I feel ripped off. why would such a small bag of commonplace candy be so expensive. I should have looked but in future I really need to stick to products that amazon sells.

column9: These arrived quickly, but I was really burned on the price...
column10: I needed these Red Hots for a recipe for my grandchildren at Christmas. The seven ounce bag sounded like it was very large, but when it arrived it it was very small.  The price was exhorbitant, so much so that I learned to go to a convenience store for the small boxes next time.  I did this to save money, but instead I got stuck.

I needed redhots to make Christmas cookies. They are getting increasingly difficult to find in stores so I turned to the net. I searched and compared and this is the best deal I found. It's a tradition in my family to decorate sugar cookies with red hots. They're also good to eat plain. Just don't eat too many!
This item is highly overpriced!  After purchasing, I found this in the store for $3.98.  I won't be ordering from here again.

This jumbo-sized canister of cilantro is perfect for our end-of-summer tomato canning. Definitely cost effective when you're processing nearly 100 quarts! We transferred the remainder into smaller glass jars and have enough for all our winter Mexican, Italian and Asian meals.

I sent the candies as a gift to Friends in Florida..... the comments were as follows  Delicious!!! Yumm,  Soft and Chewy  and very Addictive!!!my suggestion,  remember to ask for a gift card to be included in the box, or the folks won't know who sent them.
THIS IS SUCH A RIP-OFF.I FAILED TO NOTICE THAT THIS WAS FOR ONE, LITERALLY, ONE BOX OF POPCORN SALT. OF COURSE I AM RETURNING IT, BUT AMAZON SHOULD BE ASHAMED TO EVEN REPRESENT SUCH A RIP-OFF

I got to Amazon's page through a link from a Google Shopping page for a case of 12 containers of salt.  I failed to notice that the 12 containers that Google Shopping had promised had dropped to 1 container on Amazon's page, and the $9.99 price didn't do anything to stop me believing that it was a whole case that I was buying.  To add insult to injury, the shipping on 1 single 3.75 oz container was another whopping $8.99, for a grand total of $18.98, which works out to over $5 per ounce of salt.Again, it was my mistake, but you can easily find a whole case of salt on the web for what I paid for 1 container.
It's not the best quince brand but it's fine.The product arrived in perfect conditions and it worked to bake a "Pastafrola"

If you haven't ever tasted a Bergamot bonbon before do it! For me, this taste reminds me of my childhood, because part of my mother's family is still in France. She moved here with her sister, when she was 23, met my father,fell in love, and two weeks later they were married. They had my brother and I, and were happily married for almost nineteen years before we devastatingly lost him to melanoma when I was only ten, my brother twelve. My mother and father were 42. Our lives, changed, but were always wonderful because my mother is so loving, nurturing, and attentive. I have wonderful memories of the 4 of us opening a package from my Mem'ere, (my grandmother), and my uncle, who is my mom's brother. The chocolate was always delicious of coarse, (they don't add wax to their chocolate like we do in the states), but I was always quick to find the Bergamot candy! When I was little the candy came in tins, and there are some sites that sell them in the tins still which are almost identical to the old ones. They used to break the pieces, so they were all different shapes and sizes, but all of them delicious! The sweet, light floral flavor and easily dissolving pieces just seem to melt away. They now come cut, and individually wrapped, so if you want to take a few in your purse you can! :)We also visited France the year my father passed; my mother needed to be with her family for help and support. We stayed for a month, and got to visit Nancy, as well as many other amazing places. We even got to see the home my mother grew up in. My Mem'ere passed away a few years ago at 88 years of age, but my uncle and his 4-year-old son still live there, and we miss them so much. My uncle still sends us packages when he can, and we still open it together as a family. It's still as exciting to me as it was when I was 8. :)I hope everyone enjoys these as much as I do! Best wishes!

Sugar for the office!  Great tasting product, made in the USA!  Not the best price I've found on the internet, but still less than ordering directly from the manufacturer.  This is a semi-soft candy that has a great flavor (lemon) and everyone seems to like it very well.  It is not chewy, just melts slowly in your mouth.

column9: Not a good flavor. Tasted like chemicals.
column10: I was poorly surprised at how bad these taste. The after taste was horrible. This is just my opinion.Gave them to workers and they ate them up. To each his own, I guess.

column9: My favorite company for bully sticks hands down
column10: I have seven dogs ranging from 40 to 120 lbs and they LOVE bully sticks.  I am always looking for the best deals and the best quality - particularly ones that are long lasting.  I love this company, Best Bully Sticks.  I think they produce a high quality product with a fair price.  This is obviously not a cheap chew toy, but their price is one of the best around and definitely the best for the high quality of the item.  I buy them because my dogs love them, they are safe (unlike Greenies or rawhide which can cause blockages), and the smell on this is very mild.  Size is as stated.  Buy with confidence!

These were absouluty delicious.  American chocolates have alot more parrafin or other substance that is just not chocolate leaving the mushy or waxy tasting and these are from Japan and have great texture and taste far superior than anything here in the states.  Try at least one box of these before you kick the bucket and you wont be disatisfied.

This baby corn is delicious, crisp and ridiculusly affordable with the subscribe and save option. My husband and I use this primarily for salads and stir-fry.The cans arrived safely with no dents or other damages. We are very pleased and will buy again.

column9: Beautiful Baby Corn, Very Shoddy Packaging~
column10: I have always loved Baby Corn, and Roland Brand Baby Corn seemed like a very good bargain until the box arrived today.  Every single one of the cans was dented/mashed.  If Amazon had properly boxed the interior carton, then I feel that the package would have arrived in a much better condition than it did.  "An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure."  Although Amazon did make it right by giving me a full credit for this purchase, I still believe that the better choice is to make it right the first time, thereby keeping overall costs down for all of us.

This was the smallest quantity of Kombu I could find on Amazon. It's the perfect size (for me, at least). There are 10 strips in the bag.  I use half a strip for making beans. I break it off and add to the beans at the start of cooking (after the water has come to a boil) and leave it in for about 15 minutes. Then I remove and discard. It helps tenderize the beans, adds just the right flavor without having to use salt (which I avoid) and has the added benefit of iodine. I'm very pleased with the purchase and happy to be able to find the single bag quantity on Amazon.
Perfect and yummy... I used it for sushi rice and it gave it a good taste. Boil it with the water and rice and do not remove it until the rice is done.
Having purchased a number of Spicy World herbs and spices I found, after about three months and unopened, most of them to be contaminated and had to discard unused.  I cannot recommend this product.

column9: Lots of flavor, just enough heat
column10: These sauces do a great job of capturing the flavor of the habanero peppers without the overwhelming heat.  Great on just about anything.

column9: Melinda's - my absolute favorite hot sauce brand
column10: I have tried a lot of different hot sauces.  From Daves gourmet sauces to the cheapo "ass in the tub" sauces.  Melinda's is my absolute favorite.  Other sauces tend to either taste horrible, not have enough heat, or a little of both.  Melinda's has never let me down.  I've tried almost every flavor available from this line and every single one tastes absolutly awesome.  If you like your sauce hot, try the Melinda's naga jolokia sauce.  If you prefer something with some heat but not too hot, try the Melinda's red savina or the Habenero XXX.  If you like a mild hot sauce, get the jalepeno or the regular habenero with no X's.  They all taste great and there is something for everyone!  I highly recommend the scotch bonnet sauce from this line.  It tastes soooo good!  Give Melinda's a try, you will not be disappointed!

The color was off white and the contents cloyingly sweet--it looked spoiled.  It was not at all what I expected and given the opportunity I would return it. It  is a food so I am stuck with it but would never order it again and will likely have difficulty ever using it ---thank goodness it's shelf like is a few years

column9: This is "Cream of Coconut" not coconut water or milk...
column10: I thought I would add a review, as the one star review doesn't seem fair to the product. I have used this brand of cream of coconut for many years (used to own a restaurant and bar) and it is excellent. It can be used in a number of things, but is probably best known for it's use as the coconut element in pina coladas. (I personally like to double up on if I am making them for myself. :) )It is *supposed* to be slightly off white, and it is sweet. It is a condensed, sweetened coconut cream; it is NOT a coconut water or milk. It is not intended as a stand alone food or beverage (though I like to enjoy a bit of it right out of the can-- think coconut candy). I have seen it settle in the can a bit, if it has been stored for a while, but a quick stir will remix it, and it's good to go.I don't know what the previous reviewer had in mind when ordering this product, but the description given describes the product relatively well (cloyingly seems a little over the top)-- however, that is exactly what it is *supposed* to be. I think perhaps the previous reviewer was expecting an altogether different coconut product. If you're looking for a sweetened coconut cream, I would highly recommend this product.

This is an unusual and amazing tasting jam.  I love the pear with vanilla overtones.  Great on toast and my wife loves it for an unusual PB and J.  The only issue is that the supplier doesn't have anymore and doesn't know when they will get more.  If they had a case of it, I would buy it all- it's that great.

My almost 2 year old daughter LOVED this meal!  We give her regular food and sometimes supplement with these meals to make sure she's getting all her veggies.  She usually eats with her mouth practically closed, but she kept asking for more and gulped down the entire tray!  Will definitely be ordering more as it is all organic and chock full of veggies and protein.  Winner!

These mints are the best for all the reasons the other guy listed.  And they ARE really hard to find! And I just ate my last one! PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE if anyone finds anywhere I can buy these, either online, or at a California store, let us know!

The best mints out there.  Small.  Powerful.  A good value (50 per packet).  AND it's in a nice small plastic container - unlike altoids or tic-tacs, it's not going to rattle around in your pocket.  And unlike other no-cal mints, this doesn't taste like artificial sweetner.  You can't beat it.  Now why has it become so hard to find?!?!?!

I started buying Can Do Kid bars a few years ago for the purpose of having a ready protein source for my kids when we are on the go.  These vanilla bars are not quite as tasty as the chocolate, but they are a nice treat nonetheless.  I have been eating gluten free for half a year now, and have found that most of the protein bars I used to favor for myself are now out of bounds.  It was a pleasant surprise to find that the Can Do vanilla are GF.  They are a simple cookie bar with vanilla coating.  Each individually packed bar has two small portions inside, so you can share with a friend or save one piece for later!

I have used this product for several years and do not tire of the flavors and ease of preparation.  I personally chop fresh parsley, mint, tomato and sweet onion, add a few fresh squeezed limes from my backyard tree, stir and refridgerate overnight.  For the next few days, I feast on a beautiful, fluffy, "clean" tasting food that makes me happy and keeps me healthy.Thank you, Fantastic, for putting together this wonderful mix.  I hope Amazon restocks it again.  I have had to purchase it elsewhere because they didn't have it on several occasions.  Perhaps it is just too popular.  MMMMMMMMMM....

column9: Fantastic World Foods Tabouli Salad Mix, 6-Ounce Boxes
column10: This is one of the better Tabouli mixes. The taste is perfect. I do end up using more lemon juice than it calls for because I prefer a tangier taste. If you buy this mix you will love it.

I eat this at least once a week. I add diced tomatoes and parsley and a little lemon juice and it is just perfect! To reduce the calories, I sometimes leave out the olive oil...even then it's still super tasty!!!

I prepare this on a regular basis (along with Fantastic World Foods Falafel mix) for several reasons.  It's one of my family's favorites.  Allow me to enumerate the reasons why:1) It's easy.  Add the package to boiling water and olive oil.  Allow the tabouli mix to soak up the liquid.  Once soaked, mix with a diced cucumber and a chopped tomato.  Refrigerate in a resealable container.  Even a non-cook can master this!2) It makes A TON of food.  I don't consume more than 1/2 cup at a time, and the other two members of my family do the same.  We're able to eat on this three times before it's gone.  That's usually two dinners and a lunch.3) It's easy to make a meal with this.  Buy hummus (or get the fabulous mix from Fantastic Foods!), the aforementioned Fantastic Foods Falafel mix, pita bread, and olives, and prepare to please a crowd.4) It's TASTY.  I avoid wasting money on eating out by buying Fantastic Foods products because they taste much the same as the fare offered at my local Greek restaurant.  I think this tabouli tastes better than the one at my local Greek place.5) Again, it's cheap.  I can make three meals for my family for less than $12 total using the Fantastic Foods hummus, falafel, and tabouli.  That price includes pita bread, olives, and vegetables.  That's a pretty good deal, if you ask me!If you like Greek/Middle Eastern food, pick this up.  Your tastebuds and your wallet will thank you.
Great product. You can mix it with any food or salad. Don't need to cook it. I will recommand it to all.

This was my first fruity matcha from Red Leaf and I had really been looking forward to trying it because of the great reviews. The delicious aroma of this selection made my mouth water as soon as I opened the packet. I have enjoyed boysenberry syrup on many occasions in the past, back in the days when I used to eat waffles and pancakes. This definitely captures the essence of boysenberry nicely with a great balance between sweet and tart. I did what others have suggested, and mixed it up with 2 oz of hot water , then added  some almond milk, a splash of cream, a small amount of sweetener, and some ice cubes and shook it up to make a chilled latte. I will eventually try it hot, but I have really been in the mood for the chilled lattes lately! So this was the third flavor I've had from Red Leaf, and all have been outstanding. I'm afraid they could be somewhat addictive. If you haven't tried boysenberry, you should! I don't think you'll be disappointed.

When I saw this boysenberry flavor, I knew I had to grab it. I'm not sure if I've ever had boysenberry on its own, but I definitely know I've had it in yogurt form. There are several companies that make boysenberry yogurt, and it's delicious.For all my previous matchas, since they were desert matchas, I had been making them hot the traditional matcha way. Usually, after my first sip, it was a little too intense for me, so I added some milk to help bring out the flavor. But for boysenberry, hot and milk added just didn't sound appealing to me, so I thought I would try something new.I took my water bottle and measured 1/4 teaspoon for matcha. I then filled my bottle with 16oz of water. You can also use a water bottle, but since I want to be environmentally friendly (and I like my filtered water), I decided to just use a regular bottle. I debated whether or not to sift the matcha, but decided I wouldn't the first time around. I shook my bottle vigorously, and then sipped the results...WOW!!! I was really impressed. With all the other matchas, I had a hard time tasting the flavor just straight, but here I can definitely taste both the matcha and the boysenberry. The matcha is not overpowering and overly grassy, and  there are definitely berry undertones. I didn't need to add any sweetener, although I bet if I did it would bring out the flavor even more.I can't believe how easy this is to make. It sure beats using a whisk (no pun intended) and making water on the kettle. Those are good too, but this is better. I'm thinking I need to order some more fruity matchas in the future, since I liked boysenberry so much. I'm not sure how this would taste hot, but it's definitely delicious cold.

This matcha is my first experience with something boysenberry flavoured. I love blackberries, and boysenberries look similar, so I figured I'd give it a go.I'm so glad I took a chance on this flavour! It is really fresh and juicy tasting, with a light berry flavour that is both sweet and tart. It is almost candy-like in both scent and flavour, without being artificial tasting in the slightest.I would urge anyone who enjoys flavoured matcha to branch out a little and try a flavour you wouldn't normally try - I'm betting you'll be pleasantly surprised! All of the varieties that I've tried from Red Leaf so far have been really well done, and pretty much universally enjoyable.

As a kid, I practically grew up at Knott's Berry Farm.  I loved everything about that place, and boysenberries hold a very special place in my heart because of the theme park.  So when I saw that Red Leaf Tea carried boysenberry Matcha, I had to try it!And this does the berry - as well as Mrs. Knott - proud!  It tastes very authentically boysenberry... as if I might have plucked a few berries off a vine and pureed them and then stirred the puree into the Matcha - except that this is so much smoother.  The Matcha tastes rich and vegetative, with notes of butter in the background.  Deliciously creamy... this would make a great dessert substitute!Another exceptional Matcha from Red Leaf Tea.

So when I first smelled the dry powder I thought, oh tart, crisp, light, berry!My daughter's first impression was "Mom this smells like Red Bull energy drink."I was like OMG you are SO right!It does! I have to admit. I do love Red Bull. Actually I had a bit of a Red Bull problem not too long ago, before tea! Thank you tea!Nonetheless it has that exact same tart smell to it!Don't worry though this is totally healthy!Plus after preparing my matcha, adding some ice and milk, it tastes NOTHING like a red bull!Okay maybe a little something like it in the sense that it is light, crisp, refreshing, not too tart but just a slight berry tartness but nothing that is going to make you pucker!I love this!I feel bad and I owe an apology to summer. Here I was craving autumn and forgot all about berries, fruits, juicy ripe tasting delights and had went totally for heavier, richer, creamier, flavors. But you know what ... it is still summer and I am going to totally enjoy drinking this and many other light matchas to come!As I am sitting here in delight sipping away I am noticing this almost earthy flavor to it - no not the normal earthy grassy flavor of a matcha or green tea, but something else. The prominent flavors are still the same, tart, juicy, etc, not to be redundant, but there is something more, its one of those flavors you swish around in your mouth, tap tap tap your tongue around, make those smacking sounds trying so hard to pin point it but it is eluding me! I want someone else to get some of this so they can help me figure it out.Yes this one is a delight and to think I almost passed it up I mean I was not too sure what to expect and didn't want something too overly tart but thank goodness I went for it!

I didn't notice them when I gave it to her because the smoky color of the salt that muted the color. But after examining them under the microscope (we're in that industry), we found the coloration of the dots to be distinct from the colors found in the normal salt content (they had a tint of dark green and were adamantly stuck to the wall even after heavy shaking!). We didn't know what it was but considering that it grew despite the strong alkaline environment inside the salt bottle, we didn't want to risk using them any further. Furthermore, there is no return policy for this product so I just wasted almost $20 on something that I cannot even use.

Sleepytime is a popular tea that has been around a long time due to its high quality. The natural flavors and ingredients have made it a required tea for the cupboard of persons interested in healthy eating for the last 30 years! The predominant flavors are of chamomile and spearmint--but the additional ingredients--including rose buds--create a satisfying, complex blend that is very tasty and soothing. Not only is Sleepytime caffeine-free but it contains herbs that are mildly relaxing and healing for the stomach. Drink this lovely tea before bed either with or without honey.Sleepytime contains chamomile, spearmint, lemongrass, tilia flowers, blackberry leaves, orange blossoms, hawthorne berries and rosebuds. The healing qualities of some the herbs in Sleepytime are listed below, however please note that there is insufficient quantities of each herb to have anything more than a very mild effect. Blackberry leaves, which are soothing to the stomach, contain tannins which provides a tea-like base for the flowery flavors of chamomile and rosebuds. Spearmint is one of the milder mints and is also useful to soothe tummy ache. Chamomile is a wonderful herb that has a relaxing effect; it also can be used to soothe tummy aches, headache, menstrual cramps and is a mild anti-fungal.Celestial Seasonings gets extra points for their packaging: they utilize 100% natural recycled paperboard in their boxes and they don't package each tea bag individually. Instead they use a system of a waxed paper bag inside the box that stays shut when you fold it. It keeps the bags fresh and utilizes less packaging than individually wrapping each bag. The art they use on each box is beautiful as are the quotes and information they put on every surface.Quote from the box:"Ultimately, the bond of all companionship, whether in marriage or friendship, is conversation." Oscar Wilde.

My 4 cats and I are in Total Agreement on at least one Subject. We are all very pleased with this Fancy Feast Dry Food in 16 ounce packages. Two kitties are juveniles, seven months, and no one is over weight, so ad lib feeding of dry food is the rule of the house.At 5 PM, everyone gets one three ounce can of wet food, plus I feed the feral cat at that time. He has been my companion for about 8 years. He is now brave enough to sidle up to the back door and meow to make his wants known. He eats once a day. He is a Trap, Neuter, and Return Kitty and quite polite. He gets wet and dry food and eats the wet in the evening and the dry in the morning. But I have had 4 knee replacements and lugging heavy bags of food became a chore. Also, with kittens ripping and running around, those bags seemed to have a mind of their own and would turn over in my closet; thus, dispensing Dry food on the carpet instead of the cat food bowl. Now I take the lazy lady's way out.I order these 16 ounce bags in three flavors: the green bag which is Ocean Fish with Salmon;the Purple bag which is ChickenPurina Pet Care Fancy Feast Gourmet Gold, 16-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 12)and The Pink bag which is Filet Mignon with Seafood and Shrimp Purina Pet Care Fancy Feast Gourmet Gold, 16-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 12).I know this is a little pricier than buying it in the big, economy size bags, but since I have problems with lifting and carrying thanks to my knees, it is worth it for me!! Then as an added benefit, I use the left over bags when I clean the litter boxes. Scoop up the mess, put in bag, seal, and throw in trash. These work MUCH better than grocery store bags which always seem to have a hole in them! So, now, I just put these in my closet and rotate the flavor and the kitties are all happy.My two older cats, ages 4 and 3 have eaten Fancy Feast all their lives. The vet always gives them a clean bill of health and is pleased that there are no over weight issues. The kittens just saw the vet. They started Fancy Feast as soon as their Kitten Kibble was gone. Their coats shine and the vet is pleased with their progress also. So, we are a Fancy Feast Family and Proud of it. We Recommend this brand to you and suggest the 16 ounce pouches to anyone who has problems with the larger bags of dry food!Now, I have finally found my Kitty Litter in smaller bags, so I am a happy camper. Swheat Scoop Natural Cat Litter, 10 Pound Bag. Getting ones knees trashed is no fun, but Amazon surely helps by carrying all sizes and deliverying to my door!!! So, keep shopping Amazon!

column9: be careful, moldy product, USDA now involved
column10: My baby enjoyed this flavor when I purchased it at a store.  I ordered a case of it from Amazon.  the whole case arrived moldy.  Each jar popped when I opened it too, showing that it was properly sealed.  I contacted Earth's Best.  They said they would look into it but would not follow up with me.  Given what is going on in our food industry, I will not purchase any more products from this company.  It is to scary when feeding a baby.  Amazon refunded me but did not take it any further.  Be very careful and inform other families too.  UPDATE: I was so disappointed with the lack of concern from Earth's Best and Amazon.  I contacted the FDA, they referred me to the USDA because the product contained meat.  They took it very serious and had also received several complaints.  They have come to my house and written a report.  If anyone else noticed this problem please contact the USDA (1-888-674-6854).to report your claim/problem.  They will investigate the problem and the Earth's Best Plant to make sure they are following regulations.

column9: Small Jars and a Little Runny - like most commercial baby foods

Rare in the baby food industry.I am following a weaning guide that I used for my daughter, and it makes you pretty wary of commercial baby foods as babies easily get used to the bland, watery taste and sometimes take a lot of coaxing to go back to home made, healthy meals, resulting in picky toddlers and children. My daughter is now 3 and has never refused a home cooked meal yet, and I attribute that to the hard work I put in in the first year. Another problem with commercial baby foods is that they are usually so padded out with water that nutritional needs aren't fully met during the day and babies can start waking in the night due to genuine hunger.I'd love to ask, who came up with the magical 4oz measurement for all stage 2 baby food jars and packets, though? My son takes more like 6oz of my home prepared meals which are much "fuller", so I've had to add a little sweet potato to this to increase the volume. And it does seem really quite runny and padded out with water, so I add a teaspoon or 2 of rice cereal to thicken it up a little. Before long, I'm sure he'll just be on 2 full 4oz jars when I give him this.All that said, I'll reiterate, it is really quite tasty for a commercial baby food, and I have no problem giving it to my son once in a while. column9: Savory and salty spread; great for cooking and stirring in soups and gravies, too. 4 stars rating on price and delivery
column10: Guys:Marmite is what it is.  This is a difficult product to rate on its own merits because this is something that you'll either love or hate and if you're looking at this, you probably have already tasted this.  If you never had this before, the best description I can give this is that it tastes like a beef bouillon cube dissolved in a thick, paste-y gelatin like paste......almost like a thick. clear model-airplane glue that comes in the tube, like Duco cement (sounds yummy, right)?  I actually love this on toast, plain or with butter. I've also stirred it into gravy, soups and even coated a Thanksgiving turkey with it before roasting in the oven (just lift up the skin and smear this all over the meat, then place the skin back on and smear a little bit more on the skin; then roast regularly).The price for one of these tiny jars in NYC is close to $6, so at $4 a pop delivered to your door using subscribe and save, this is a decent bargain.Regarding some of the comments about expiration dates...honestly, I don't think this stuff EVER expires. It has way too much salt in it to go bad (in my opinion).  As an aside, I had an open jar in my cabinet that I noticed had an "expiration date" of 2002 (it's now 2012) and it still tastes GREAT....in fact, I think it even tastes better than when I first opened it in 2000 (lol)

column9: MSG nightmare, be warned, concentrated free glutamates
column10: I bought this item and last weekend ate quite a lot of it.The savory taste is appealing, yet I have had to educate myself on safe ways to enjoy that taste.Little did I know that my food sensitivity issues would peak shortly after.It began with searing pains in my shoulder, arm and neck. Then a supercell migraine and seizure.It was the most painfully harrowing ordeal of my entire 65 year life.For the first time in my life I was wailing and whimpering uncontrollably, as if tortured.My wife got me to the ER where they gave me IV morphine, then benedryl, then more morphine, then more benedryl.After an hour of blow torch pain, with emergency medical intervention,  it started to pass.I am deeply humbled to more careful choices in the future.This product has a cute bottle, quaint ad campaign, and interesting history.However the slogan: "love it or hate it" is not just about taste.If you have an MSG (monosodium glutamate), or any free glutamate sensitivity, stay far away from this stuff.All processed yeast products and many fermented food items, extracts, additives, concentrate free glutamate.Free glutamates function as a neurotoxin and we each have a different threshold of sensitivity.Phantom neck, shoulder or arm pains are the beginning of noticing where your threshold is.Long time, or early life overdose is linked to symptoms of asthma, migraine, autism, ADHD, ALS, MS, fibromyalgia, Alzheimer's, to name few.Please save your self if you are sensitive to these chemicals.Educate your self through the web info resources on what to watch for (so much it is in), learn to read and decode food labels, etc.This may not ever surface as an issue for you.All others, please enjoy.Word to the wise.Best Wishes,WV

column10: This is Green Mountain's response to the Coffee People's Donut Shop coffee.  Many people actually confuse the two which isn't difficult to do: donut house and donut shop -- both are extra bold in flavor, and both are excellent.  Since Donut Shop is my favorite, I decided to conduct a taste test between these two rivals.  Side to side they are very similar, very little acid taste, no bitterness which is what I look for in an extra bold roast.  Head to head Donut Shop edged this coffee, Donut House, out by the slightest of margin.  Donut Shop had slightly more body to it but frankly, it took me drinking a half cup of each before I could declare a winner.  This is why I also think this is a 5 star coffee -- excellent choice if you want a simple, great tasting cup of coffee that you will not get sick of.

column9: Not like drinking a donut, but great coffee!!!
column10: I was skeptical of this blend. I like my coffee dark and bold. But this one is really REALLY smooth, dark and rich tasting. My other fav is Caribou and this one is similar to that. Not bitter, not biting, just smooth and rich and consistant. A great daily brew for my Keurig. Try it. I bet you will like it.

I decided to try a box because Costco carries this and they haven't had my favorite Tully's Kona for a while. It lives up to the "light roast" description and brews one of the lightest (you might also say 'weakest') cups of coffee I've had in any K-cup. Even using two k-cups didn't help much. It's way too light for my tastes; glad I didn't buy the box of 88 at Costco.So, if you like a lightly roasted and somewhat weak cup of coffee, you'd like this. The flavor is good. But, k-cups run a little on the weak side in general and this one is simply too light for me.Amazon did ship fast and had a good price.UPDATE: Some reviews here don't seem to understand the terms being used."Light Roast" is a description of how long the coffee beans are roasted. Light roaster beans do not have the strong and sometimes bitter flavor of beans that are roasted for longer times, but they retain more of the subtleties of their flavor.  It does produce a `lighter' cup of coffee."Extra Bold" is a term Keurig/Green Mountain uses to describe a K-cup that has more coffee grounds in it than normal K-cups.  More coffee grounds makes for a stronger cup of coffee. The strength of the coffee also depends on how large a cup you brew.You can have a "light roast" coffee in an "Extra Bold" K-cup, but the result will still be a coffee with a lighter flavor.Personally, I like a medium roast; a nice balance between good coffee flavor and that strong coffee bite.

column9: Drinkable, but rather bland, not full-bodied, will not buy again
column10: I have been a Keurig user for several years, have one at home and one in my office. For at least 4 years I have been using the Green Mountain Columbian Fair Trade K-cups, been very happy with them. Recently I saw the Donut House flavor offered at my local warehouse club and it piqued my interest, problem is that the warehouse box contains 80 K-cups, didn't want to buy 80 of something I may not like. So, I picked up an 18-count box at my local Walmart, I'm so glad that I did!First, let me say that I'm not a fan of Starbucks coffee's, I think they are too strong, too bold, too bitter. I like a flavorful, medium roast but full-bodied cup of coffee. The Green Mountain Columbian Fair Trade K-cups fit this bill, whenever I would make a cup at my office, everyone would comment, "Wow, that smells so good!", it tasted just as good.I tried the Donut House coffee this morning, no inviting aroma when brewing, very bland in taste, I don't know how they get away with calling this "Bold". It says right on the box, "light roast", I don't know how a "light roast" can be called "Bold"? I was expecting a very full-bodied flavor, but without a bitter after-taste. Well, there was no after-taste, no taste period, just very bland!FYI, I usually use 16 oz. "to go" cups when brewing K-cups, I use 2 K-cups per 16 oz. cup, I brew the first K-cup on the middle button (8 oz. setting), the the second K-cup on the lowest setting (I think it is 6.5 oz. setting), this allows room for a teaspoon of sugar and some half and half to a golden color. I have been doing this for years with my Columbian K-cups and always get a great cup of coffee, did the same with the Donut House blend, drinkable, but not remarkable in any way. I will be sticking with my Columbian Fair Trade blend that never fails me.I will use the remainder of my Donut House K-cups, but I will not buy them again.

I bought this cat food because of the wonderful low price and I enjoy the adorable cat on the commercials. My cats did eat this food, in fact they really enjoyed it. However, after reading the ingredients and doing some research, I completely regret purchasing it and feel just awful for feeding it to my cats. The first few ingredients are (which indicates the most prevalent ingredients) are for one of the flavors: turkey, poultry by-products, water sufficient for processing, and meat by-products. Another flavor was: water sufficient for processing, chicken, and liver. At least there is turkey and/or chicken in it, but other than that its mostly nasty stuff. By-products aren't even a real meat! By-products are the stuff leftover once all the actual meat is harvested. We're talking beaks, chicken feet, eyeballs, even chicken poop! I would not recommend this product. It is just not a good quality cat food. I suppose you get what you pay for. I think the only reason why it was cat-approved may be because it contains artificial flavors that taste good to cats, and because I usually feed them dry food for dental reasons and wet food puts off much more of a scent for them to enjoy. I recommend to stay far away from Friskies, as it is simply a very low quality filler food. Some Friskies flavors are even worse than the ones I listed and contain no real meat. Even though the price is quite inexpensive, your cat will actually eat more than if you paid for a better quality food, because they will never feel full. Cats need to eat real, identifiable, pure, meat, and there just isn't enough real meat in this food. When purchasing a cat (or dog) food, the most important thing to consider is the first 3 ingredients; just make sure those first three are decent ingredients that you can identify and would eat yourself- provided that you eat a typical (not vegetarian or other restricted) diet. Now that I know what to look for, I usually buy my pets all natural foods such as Natural Balance, Blue Buffalo, Halo, or Wellness. All of those brands contain real, whole meats that I myself would eat, with no added fillers or low quality foods.

I'm not sure why some cat food gets a bad review because a cat doesn't eat it. We have 7 here in our rural home, plus some strays that stop by for a meal, and though they can be finicky they all eat pretty much what we put in front of them when they're hungry. They get fed 3 times a day and canned food is the morning meal so perhaps having nothing out from about 6 PM to 6 AM makes this pretty inviting. We have one cat that's about 17 years old and all she can eat is canned food. I can't say how good it is but at less than 45 cents a can (including shipping) it's less than at the local food store that happens to be about 45 miles away... as is the Vet. We feed them dry food (the grain free expensive kind) for the other 2 meals a day so the canned food is also a bargain.We had a cat develop a kidney stone, with urinary problems, and the Vet claims it was from the poor ingredients in some dry cat food. He wanted to put her on a special diet with a Science Diet special blend for Urinary Tract and then onto one of their regular formula kibble for life. That seemed a little useless because we were feeding the cats some decent kibble to begin with like Purina One. We did a search and found that it was true that a lot of filler in most dry cat food was grain and that is hard for cats to process. The diet we found involved a home made cat food of grinding up some rabbit or chicken and adding some vitamins. Tried it and it worked but it was a mess to make, rabbit is not cheap or easy to find and it takes up a lot of freezer space. Back to another search and a viable alternative seemed to be canned cat food, with some limitations, and a grain free kibble. The canned food doesn't have as much fillers and the main ones for us are poultry, fish & meats varieties in pâté or gravy form. That's what the cats are on now and the kidney/urinary problem is gone, their coats are nicer, their urine is less now because they don't have to consume so much water to process the grain feed and they really seem to like what they're eating. We feed them Friskies & 9-lives in the cans and Blue Buffalo Wilderness, Merrick Before Grain, Felidae or Taste of the Wild in dry food. The dry food is getting pricier, the bags are getting smaller and the free shipping deals are disappearing so it's more of a challenge now to get a deal but when we do we buy extra. No surprises here... as advertised cat food.  Variety pack is being enjoyed by my 2 yr old Russian Blue.  She loves it!No freight charges make it taste even better.
Awesome, my cat loves that! It is all with chunks of poultry and yummy sauce. Just what the doctor ordered! ;)

My cats love Friskies and with Subscribe and Save I can get a month's supply in at once cheaper than I can buy at my local store. I have had no problems (fingers crossed) with any damaged boxes or cans.

column9: Making all of my cats sick
column10: Due to the good price I started doing subscribe and save for my 3 cats. I just got my second shipment and am planning on throwing all of them away because I have realized it is making all 3 of my cats sick. All 3 have dry noses and warm ears. Ruffus Teague's Bar-B-Q Sauce is by far, theeee BEST sauce I have ever tasted.I like "touch o heat" and "honey sweet"  equally as well.I will not settle for any other sauce now that I have had a taste of Ruffus's.

column9: New Ovaltine - Please give me the original formula!
column10: What a disappointment it was to try the new Nestletized "Malt Classic Ovaltine." Gone are the granules - instead, it's now a fine powder. The taste has changed too. It's not really awful - still drinkable, but it's definitely not in the same league as the original that I grew up on. I'm not sure why they changed something that didn't need changing.  I am no longer a loyal Ovaltine customer -- it doesn't seem much better than Nesquik anymore.

column9: Original recipe was great - new one is awful

column9: Pleaes bring back the old formula
column10: I have purchased Rich, chocolate Ovaltine since my now 15 year old was old enough to drink milk, but wouldn't because of the taste. Doctor said to add chocolate. Since Ovaltine has more vitamins than the others, we started using it. Now I have 4 children all considered under weight and loved that Ovaltine made their milk palatable. My youngest and most underweight refuses to drink milk without it. Bought the new recipe a few weeks ago. Kids opened it up and the smell was horrendous! I thought it went bad. The taste was not the same either (sort of like egg nog that's gone bad). Then I noticed the "New Improved recipe". Who's the marketing genius behind this one. Yes I see less calories, sugar and sodium in the new recipe, but if I was worried about that I wouldn't be adding chocolate to my milk in the first place! PLEASE BRING BACK THE OLD RECIPE. My underweight children need it!!

column9: less nutrients, more sugar, higher price, ZERO STARS!!!!!!!
column10: My kids are very disappointed that I no longer buy Ovaltine. It costs more, there is less product, more sugar and less nutrients. I have 3 boys and I started my oldest, who is now 8, on Ovaltine ever since he started on milk. It was great to have something for him that I could count on for nutrients when he was a pickyeater. Now we are no longer an Ovaltine family unless they go back to the old formula.

This highly reminds me of "THE NEW COKE" debacle. Until recently, Ovaltine was perfect in my opinion. It dissolved perfectly and uniformly. Tasted great, and was better than most other chocolate drinks in a nutritional sense. Now the formula has changed and I can't stand it. It looks, tastes and mixes like Nesquik. I won't drink Ovaltine again until the recipe changes back. They should probably call it "Ovaltine Classic" or something to signify it's return.

column9: OVALTINE = ALTERTINE - Yet another tampered with product so the manufacturer can cut corners and save a buck
column10: I too have noticed the horrible difference in Ovaltine.  Open up the container and you get an instant whiff of the ocean.  It stinks like fish. column9: I grew up with the glass bottles....and some weirdo has changed it!!!
column10: Let's call the company and let them know that they need to change it back!!!!800-442-0099 - call them and let them know!!! CHANGE IT BACK!!!This product has gone from good to horrid. column9: The Change was not for the Better
column10: Ovaltine has changed its formula, and the change is definitely NOT for the better! I will be writing the company about this, too. They obviously think we're all stupid, and I boycott any company that acts like it thinks I'm stupid!
this stuff sux!!! i used to love ovaltine,  and now tht they have changed it, its totally descusting!!! i cant fathom why they would even want to change it!! eeeew. :(((((

When will they learn - if it's a long standing product with a loyal fan base - changing the recipe is NOT a great idea?!If you want a NEW product - create one.  But they have removed a great deal of the vitamins and nutrition - which was what had me drinking it.  Now I might as well just add hershey's syrup.  Not what I'm after!They have lost a loyal customer here.

They did it again! I can't see why the suits running this company feel they need to "improve" the recipe. I have been drinking Ovaltine for the past 45 years. This latest change might be enough to get me off this stuff.
I cannot buy anymore Ovaltine until the great tasting OLD formula comes back.  The new ovaltine smells and taste just AWFUL. Somebody knew exactly how to ruin a great product.

column9: Wish I could give it negative stars.

I am so disappointed in the new improved flavors of Ovaltine.  Why would they change a good thing?  I won't drink it anymore.  The LEAST Nestle could have done was offered the traditional flavors ALONGSIDE the new improved flavors so consumers could pick.  I don't like Nestle for doing this.

Wow, I haven't had Ovaltine in quite some time.  I decided to buy some the other day and what an absolutely disappointing glass of milk that was.  It doesn't even taste anything like it used to.  Too bad they changed their formula from the original.  I don't know why people want to change a classic.  I guess it is ultimately their loss.

column9: vs. Carnation Instant Breakfast (focus: artificial ingredients)
column10: I have been consuming Carnation Instant Breakfast Essentials (Rich Milk Chocoloate) daily for about a year now.  I decided to try Ovaltine for a change, as its price tag in the grocery store reflected slightly better value.  For some reason, I did not fully read the ingredients and instead focused only on the nutrition information, which compared decently.  Tried it for the first time this morning, and my observations follow: stirred into a glass of almond milk (which is slightly less viscous than regular milk) and it dissolved better than Carnation, less grainy.  Drank glass, noticed sediment at the bottom, even after a good stir, but much less  of it and a smoother consistency than what I regularly get with Carnation.  Flavor was fine, although it tasted a little more artificial tasting than Carnation, though I expect this from any "instant chocolatey drink."At this point it was 50/50, and I leaned toward switching to Ovaltine only because there are more servings per the 1.1 lb. package.  My true disappointment came when I read the ingredients and noticed "mono- and diglycerides, artificial vanilla flavor, yellow 6, red 40, blue 1."  These are just not necessary.  Value or no, I'm not switching. Carnation does not have food coloring added to it, and while there are still big chemical words on the list, they mostly seem to be the vitamin and mineral additives.Nestle, one of the world's largest food producers, has three major "instant chocolately drinks" on grocery shelves around the world. (Ovaltine, Carnation, Nesquik).  I can't imagine a good reason why one should contain such artificiality. Once I find a better way to get these same calories regularly throughout the day in a quickly digestible and palatable manner, I will stop buying these altogether...

I don't understand why they would do this. They have had a tried and true product since 1906 and the corner on the rich malty flavored beverage market. If they wanted to compete with other sickeningly sweet chocolate beverages, just slap a new name on it and keep the market they already have. If I'm going to be kicked to the curb, it sure would be nice to have my old ovaltine back. Creeps!

If you are sick of that malt flavour, as my kids and I are; then this Ovaltine is for you.  Where I live the only Ovaltine I can get is that old-fashioned, non-disolvable malty one - yuck - this new Ovaltine is great in cold milk or hot milk.  Simply delicious.

The previous reviewers are not happy with Ovaltine because of the change of flavor and texture.  I noticed a small change of flavor.  The texture of the dry powder is about the same not too grainy but not too thin.  I have to agree that it really doesn't dissolve in cold milk completely, like they mentioned.  Despite all that nobody could get me to actually enjoy a glass of Nesquik.  If I had to choose; I'd choose Ovaltine because it still tastes better by a long shot.Have you tasted Nesquik hot?  Eww!  o_0To give it a last chance, try the Ovaltine hot, if you really think the slight change of flavor makes such a big difference that you'd rather not have any chocolate milk at all, then I'd say you're out of luck.  I can't think of any chocolate powder better than Ovaltine.  Hershey's chocolate powder used to beat all the others in the 80's, but those days are over; it's just average now.  The Carnation Instant (breakfast) drink is disgusting. :(

Delicious.  Unlike the other reviewer, I had no problems with it's dissolving capabilities.  It's now unavailble. I sure hope Amazon gets it back in stock soon.  I only have 2 cans left.  I wanted to get the subscription to it.You can't go wrong.  The powder was fresher, noticeable by the fact that the texture was finer and less clumpy than what I've bought locally.Bring it back, Amazon, Please!!

I cannot imagine why Ovaltine changed a perfectly good thing!  It is disappointing, I have to agree.  The powder does not dissolve completely, even after stirring for a L-O-N-G time.  There is also a weird, heavy aftertaste, or almost a film, after drinking-I do not like it.

column9: This review is for the ORIGINAL recipe shown in the pic!

column9: One of my top 5 candies of all time

column9: Dear ReeseSticks Crispy Wafers... why are you so yummy?
column10: This is the diet killer. The King Size version of this candy packs a whopping 440 calories and 10 grams of saturated fat. You heard right, half your suggested daily serving of saturated fat in four little wafer bars. But oh, are they so good. These are my guilty obsession.If you've never had them, the ReeseSticks have very little in the way of chocolate - just a thin coating over the wafers. Multiple layers of wafers are sandwiched together by the Reeses peanut butter'esque filling, so the first taste impression you get is peanuts, then an overtone of general "sweet". Personally I like this bar because it's not overly sweet like a Snickers or Mars, but don't kid yourself into thinking that the peanut butter aspect somehow makes this bar healthier than its super-sugary compatriots... it doesn't....so good.

These are like Kit Kat (but not as crunchy) with the bonus of Reese's peanut butter. Not surprising since they are both made by Hershey (although outside the U.S. Kit Kat is made by Nestle).But the main reason I am writing this review is to praise the seller (Free Shipping Tigers). I had reservations about ordering the product because of the summer heat & the horror stories you hear about online candy being stale. I was going to buy a nice 24 pack and calculated amazon's price ($35.82 / 24) to be $1.50 per pack.  I took a quick trip to Walmart brick-and-mortar and they sell these for $1 per pack. column9: Take your dog out to dinner. Its cheaper and lasts longer.

column9: Gone in two days, but a hit
column10: My puppy loved the toy, but he ate it in two days.  Within a few hours a large part of the bone was gone.  I thought the toy was more sturdy.  But...a deer antler is more expensive and my dog didn't lose interest in this so I'll be buying it again.  My cane corso is also a pup so older dogs may not be excited about sitting down and eating the entire thing.  On the flip side, my corso isn't hyper but likes to have fun.  We are working on him entertaining himself and this definitely kept him entertained without making a mess.  My corso did have fun flipping it around and tossing and watching it settle after a few rolls.  Good toy all in all.  It may last longer for different breeds or dogs of a different age.

column9: Does not last more than a few hours
column10: I have a Great Pyrenees who ate half of this in an hour. Do not buy this for chewers, it will not last.

column9: Dog LOVES it, but not long-lasting
column10: My akita puppy LOVES these bones!  But he's only four months old, and he can chew half of it in one sitting, and the other half in another sitting....probably a total of two hours for the whole bone.  And he's still only a baby!!!!  So....unfortunately....I probably won't buy too many more of these, maybe for a special treat sometimes...although the older he gets, the faster he will eat it.Cool bone though.  Wish they'd compress it a bit more to make it longer lasting, and make a larger size.
Our sheltie went to town on the quado ginormous and had 90% of it gone in a hour. Good concept and dogs love it but for the price I wish it would last a bit longer.

column9: Great for chewers without a big mess
column10: I get these for my dog.  He is a big chewer, and he loves to get to work on the quado bone.  I get the ginormous.  It lasts him about 35-45 minutes (which is good for him).  I like these because they chew completely away without leaving a big mess like the busy bones.  Also, with rawhide, he has a tendency to chew for a little while and then swallow a big section without having chewed it. Not good upon exit.  =0)

My dog loved this but it was gone quickly as others have reported. My dog is a 75 lb Rhodesian Ridgeback mix. I usually don't give her anything like this because she's diabetic. I got it for $8 at Home Goods.
This had to literally be pried away from the dog because she liked it so much.  The package says not to let them eat it all in one day.

Gave this to our Bulldog for Christmas and made sure it was the first thing opened in hopes that he would let us leisurely unwrap our gifts in relative peace.  Worked like a charm!  He LOVED it!  Will definately buy Ginormous Quado Interactive Dog Bone again.

While my dog enjoyed this chew very much, he devoured the whole thing in under ten minutes. 40 pound Australian Shepherd that I would not describe as a particularly aggressive chewer, finished the 'average' says much faster than I expected. I thought the material would be harder and more difficult for them to break off pieces. It's probably great for small dogs, but too much money for something I wanted to last for much longer.

This may be an expensive chew (as other reviewers have mentioned), but it is still cheaper than furniture or shoes. When my lab puppy has this Quado available, he goes for THIS, instead of forbidden chews. In fact he goes for this over any other chew I have offered him.
I have a Giant Schnauzer and in less than 15 minutes it was gone.  In my opinion it was a bit to expensive for such a short amount of time.

I have a 9 month old cairn terrier that absolutely LOVES it. We usually give it to him when we will be away for a while and he spends the whole afternoon chewing on it. I've given it four stars just because it leaves a beige stain on the carpets (which I clean using the PETCO stain and odor removal and works like a charm). Other than that, it's a wonderful chewing toy and lasts a long time (at least for my 11 lbs dog).
they are a great chew for my very active Schnauzer puppy i buy a few at a time a better price then at my vets office

column9: So much money, so little time ...
column10: I gave these bones five stars, because our dog absolutely loves them. But, therein lies the problem. On the package it states your dog should not consume these in one sitting (look at the small print), but your dog will not agree with the package instructions. While "Bella" is quite fond of these and so I might purchase them again, it only takes her about 20-25 minutes to polish one off. They are not like rawhide, where they can last for quite some time because your dog will chew, then take a rest, then chew, etc. These are like dog "drug" bones. Like catnip for a cat. And we have not been following the "instructions" on the package. To take this away from our dog after 5 minutes so the bone will last over several days, is counter-productive and when you see how much tail-waggin' your dog does over them, even cruel.

We brought Belle, our golden retriever puppy, home two weeks ago from the breeders. She's already gone through two of the Quados and she's just about destroyed the third. Out of all the toys she has, the Quado is by far her favorite.
My lab puppy loves these! Giving it to him allows us to have a leisurely dinner with other couples in our dining room. He is occupied the entire time we are eating and chatting.

Our two pugs loved the Quados that Santa left for them under the tree!  The Quado kept them busy and gave them an outlet for their chewing needs.  Not much mess was left over, either.  I will definitely buy these again.

My pup is now 6 months old.  He is a lab.  Began giving him these bones at 4 months and they would last for almost a month.  Now at 6 months old he goes thru one in less than a week but he sure does love them.  Received my order quickly and in great shape.
This gum is very good, long lasting flavor for a bubble gum, and good bubbles!

My cat was having a lot of constipation, so I switched her to this food after speaking with a local premium pet store owner who gave me some samples.  She has been "going" very well for a couple of years now.  It is a bit pricey, but so much cheaper than the vet bills!  I order online to save money.

I use wellness dry cat food on my 5 year old cat and she loves it. Most people don't know good cat food from bad, there is so much hype about cat chow and food like that because there are so many advertisements about these foods. If only people knew how bad they were. Wellness cat food is very healthy and the cats love it! Yes it is a little more expensive than others but you will be happy when your cat lives a healthy life and you dont have so many vet bills to pay off. Our kitties have been eating wellness crunchies exclusively for over three years now. Kitties seem to really enjoy their dry cereal. I just wish amazon had a subscribe and save option for this kitty food. Still cheaper than petco though...

But what really mattered was the safety of my cats and this brand had been the subject of any recalls that I was aware of.  Luckily, my cats love it.It is more expensive than grocery store brands or even the premium versions of the name brands, but it is worth it to me.I also think that a diet of Wellness all-natural ingredients has made and ocntinues to make my cats feel, look, and act younger than their ages.  Your mileage may vary, but I gladly pay for Wellness quality.

column9: The Kitty Miss likes to crunch em.
column10: No complaints from The Kitty Miss when it comes to her Wellness crunchies.  They go in -- they come out -- we're happy.  We mix the yellow-bag kind with the red-bag kind 50/50 for a full-spectrum nutrition blast.

column9: Good cat food, a little pricey
column10: Our cat likes this food. I don't say "love" because he doesn't inhale it.  But that's a good thing.  He's trim and very healthy. Our cat can have a "sensitive" stomach at times, but he does well on this food.

I drink tea all the time. I used to brew it but found tea concentrates much easier and just as good. It can be made by the gallon or by the glass. Plus, you can change the strength to suit your mood, strong or weak.Sweet tea concentrate is relatively easy to find in most grocery stores but is often too sweet for my tastes. Unsweetened is not so easy to find. When my local tea concentrate supplier discontinued my unsweetened tea concentrate, I started searching for an alternative online.I found Island Rose Southern Style Tea Concentrate here at Amazon. I was a little concerned, as I'd never heard of the brand. I've tried off brands before and usually found them tasteless or too bitter. Island Rose turned out to be great! It has a very mild, smooth fresh brewed tea flavor with no bitter after taste. I really enjoy it.But be careful. I neglected to read the description carefully. The tea concentrate I used to buy came in gallon bottles and cost around $12 (plus tax). With the 11:1 mixture ratio that came to around $1.18 per gallon.Island Rose Southern Style costs $18 plus shipping, an extra expense I was willing to pay for gallon bottles, but this is actually HALF gallon size. For the price, this tea comes to around $4.00 a gallon mixed.So, its really great tea, excellent flavor, very smooth, but just a little too pricey for me.

In the product description it says you will receive 24/5.5 ounce cans of cat food. When received in the mail I received ONE can of cat food. It also says shipping weight is 10 pounds and turned out to be under one pound. They have false advertising! No wonder this turns out to be so cheap.
