We have a jura capressa S9 and wanted to find a bean that was smooth. We tried this coffee and it is fantastic. We are going to switch to use this coffee for every day. It is great both for regular coffee and espresso.
I have a Gaggia super-automatic espresso machine, and these beans are great for it. Nice, full flavor, no bitterness, and lots of crema. Great product for a great price.

This is superior coffee at a bargain price.  It is good for both espresso shots and for milk drinks.  Not for those who want a really dark and oily bean.  It is balanced and does make a nice crema.  Not as good as Illy, but at less than half the price, who's complaining?

I have been using these beans for about 6 months with my superautomatic Capresso machine.  I primarily drink cappuccinos and lattes.  The taste is great, and reminds me of the coffee in Italy.  Another nice aspect of these beans is that they are not oily, which is especially important if using a superautomatic machine.  I "subscribe" to the product, which comes in a one kg bag.  The price, including shipping, comes to less than $7.40 a pound, which is an incredible bargain.

column9: Lavazza Super Crema Espresso Whole Bean
column10: Awesome, probably THE best coffee in the world, no exaggeration!  Very smooth, not bitter, can make it strong and it doesn't taste too "Starbucky".  Can you tell I don't prefer Starbuck's?With the auto ship purchase, the price of this bag is literally half of what it is in the stores.
Very nice mild taste, doesn't have any burned or bitter taste like most of dark roasts

column9: The best for Espresso and Capucino
column10: I have tried other brand beans and roasts and Lavazza by far is my favorite. The price here is hard to beat and it is sent every month as we desire. This is very good. A+++

I really like Lavazza coffees in general.  Recently I tried the Super Crema since the reviews were really strong.The taste of this espresso is very much as described.  It is robust in flavor with a bit of a sweet taste and is very smooth, not bitter at all.  It works especially well with Lattes.  Can't say that I notice an extraordinary crema, but does make a notable amount of crema.Overall, again, Lavazza Super Crema demonstrated to me that it is worthy of my previous assessment of the Lavazza brand in general that it represents the best in class of espressos.  Super Crema is distinctly different from Oro and Blue, and like the others is smooth.
We are espresso addicts 365 days a year Caps and Lattes. This has become our favorite. It's rich, the crema  really is super, and through Amazon subscription program, it's very affordable
This is an exceptional coffee.  Absolutely love it and would recommend it to anyone.
Our Saeco super automatic has been getting fed this coffee for the past 8 months,it loves it,we love it..great results everytime.....highly recommend.

I noticed some reviewers calling this weak - but they are just used to strong coffee meaning bitter coffee.  This is not the case in quality coffee.  If you want a smooth espresso, even a bit sweet, you will enjoy this.  A+++++

column9: Very good expresso but not very strong
column10: I just got the package.  First of all, the price is excellent comparing with local food stores.  I would say an easy 20-30% saving and you don't have to drive to a store. I quickly made two shots with my Delonghi full automatic.  Everything is great.  The only thing is that I can use a bit stronger taste - just a little bit more.  I will try another type next after I finish this package. I won't buy from local store anymore.

I use these coffee beans in a Saeco Vienna Automatic Espresso machine.  They produce a cup of espresso or as it is known in Italy "cafe americano" that has a cream on top, full flavored but never bitter. The Amazon price is unbeatable if you sign up for regular delivery

column9: Lavazza Super Crema is everything you hope for in Italian espresso
column10: Smooth, creamy, nutty and a slight hint of chocolate.  Makes a great crema and beautiful shot of espresso!
Lavazza Super Crema has a great balaced flavor that we love for straight espresso and cappuccino's as well.

column9: nothing but lavazza at my house
column10: been drinking Lavazza for over 20 years and travelled to many other cities in the world and had their coffee....nothing compares.  It's not widely available in American supermarkets though...so I was very happy when Amazon started carrying it, for a good price too.Smooth tasting coffee, not bitter or overly roasted like some other big branded coffee here in the US. Get some today...

I have been using Lavazza Super Crema for lattes I make every morning with my Gaggia Classic for over a year now. In my humble opinion, this is the smoothest and best tasting espresso I have come across. There is no bitterness or bad after taste, just smooth and creamy and I make really good crema with it as well. Top notch coffee!!
This is pretty good coffee. Not bad at all.  Worth the price I paid.  I'll order it again.
Excellent coffee at reasonable price. You do need a good coffee grinder though for best result. For expresso, grind it on the finer side.

This is my favorite coffee in the whole world!  I have had a Starbucks Barista Espresso Machine for almost five years (a gift from my husband which I thought a foolish extravagance at the time).  To do it justice, I tried many different coffees, read a book about coffee beans and coffee types, experimented with specialty coffees and coffee drinks.  And finally discovered - this Lavazza coffee is the best!  It smells wonderful, develops an excellent crema, has no bitter after taste, is a lovely rich coffee all by itself, just bare and black - no sugar, no milk, no extra fluff - just superb coffee.  To make drinks with lots of milk (lattes for example), you need a stronger bite to your coffee (like Starbucks or Petes), but if you just want the coffee, black, then there is no better espresso than this one.
We have a Saeco espresso machine that we use daily and go through a lot of coffee.  This 2 pound bag is an economical size, and the flavor is delicious with good crema.

column9: Best crema and a forgiving espresso shot
column10: I am a newbie at the espresso scene. And my Rancillo grinder and espresso machine were a bit intimidating until i found this product. the beans are so forgiving to a newbie. The crema is wonderful. Now i have 4 shots everymorning before work - better than Starbucks can produce. Also makes an awesome cappacino.

Awesome Espresso Beans, and Awesome Value!  2.2 pounds sells for $41.99 at my local coffee shop!!!!!  Compare that to here!  With Subscribe and Save, it's even delivered to my door for free, and I get 15% off the already low selling price!  I am way under 1/2 price, approaching very close to 1/3 of the local price - which means almost 2/3 off!!!!  Amazing!  The flavor is GREAT whether it's espresso shots or whether it's made into a coffee or long coffee..... beats all the local coffee shops in flavor too.  This is the REAL stuff from Italy!

The Lavazza Super Crema Espresso is a good choice for relatively low cost coffee with nice aroma. The coffee has almost no after taste and is quite gentle, still enjoyable.The coffee arrives quite fresh and a pack of 1 Kg (2.2 lb) doesn't even last one month (although I try to limit my coffee consumption). I drink it all day long, even at night.I brew it with a super automatic (Capresso Jura F60), mostly as espresso, but it is well suited for cappuccino. Me and my friends enjoy it every time.

When I first purchased these beans, I had just gotten a Saeco Automatic Espresso Machine...I love the idea of the manual machines, I'm just not prepared to mess with tamping and grinding while I'm trying to get out the door in the morning. I have recently been to Italy and very much enjoyed the Lavazza beans I had there. These are nothing in comparison. The other reviews that said they looked and tasted stale- I have to agree. These beans look extremely dry and the flavor is just not there. Trying to order the Gran Filtro Dark Beans to see if they taste any different. When comparing these "Premium" beans to a local roaster...it is night and day. Not what I expected and shame on you Amazon for selling stale beans.

We own a Saeco Primea coffee machine and were having some issues with it while using Starbucks whole beans.  The place that fixed it told us that the Starbucks beans were too oily and causing the problems.  He recommended Lavazza and we liked the flavor and texture of the coffee.  Luckily we found it on Amazon's Subscribe and Save and we couldn't be happier with our regular shipments of coffee beans.  The price is reasonable and the free shipping is very fast.

We have a very good espresso machine and have tried many beans. After much trial & error, we just love the Lavazza Super Crema. It is very smooth, no aftertaste, and not bitter. People may want a deeper stronger bean, but for those of us wanting a moderate espresso taste, this one is simply perfect and certainly worth a try.
We now enjoy better espresso at home than at the best Italian restaurants.  Great value.

This coffee wasn't bad, it just wasn't as good as I had hoped it would be.  Just didn't have the flavor or aroma I was expecting.  I use a french press, my preferred method of brewing and that usually brings out the best a coffee has to offer.
I purchased this blend for few times already and every time I liked it !
I love this coffee!  It is great in my Jura Capresso burr grinder drip machine.  Makes a great cup of coffee!
Great Italian espresso flavor...it is so real LAVAZZA. I will definitely recommend this to all espresso lovers.

The Lavazza Supercrema, Whole Bean is one of the best if not the best espresso beans around.  A  little pricey but worth every penny.  The crema from this roast is fantastic!  I use a Saeco Odea Giro machine and they seem made for each other!  Try one bag, judge for yourself.
This is the best coffee ever.  So glad I could get it so reasonably and with no shipping.  Thank you Amazon.com.

column9: You'll get what you paid for....1 time more in my life
column10: I tasted Lavazza many times being in Italy as well in France and excellent quality (taste, smell) of it can't be confused with anything else. Have to regret - I'm EXTREMELY disappointed with this "Lavazza Super Crema" beans from Amazon - it's under-roasted, bitter and acid taste, weak (yes, there was a typo) and unpleasant smell and crema....well, even relatively old coffee beans from TJ Maxx produce better crema with proper grind&tamping or even just with the pressurized portafilter.I'm using semi-automatic espresso machine (DeLongi BAR32 before and now Saeco Aroma, Breville BCG450XL Conical Burr Grinder) about 5 years (I mean I'm not a novice for espresso), and have tried this beans immediately after the bag was opened (1st "news" - very weak smell), used fresh grind, careful and dense tamping, machine is properly heated and primed.The consumption date on the package marked as October of 2011 and I know that Lavazza's shelf life is 14 months - therefore, received in March 2010, it's 6 months old roast, not too fresh but I had used much older roasts without any problems. Not sure how it works for latte but as espresso coffee it's wasted money and lost expectation. Don't be fooled by positive reviews - some people never tried the real espresso and some even don't like it but coffee-infused milk drink. Also note that Amazon sells some Lavazza coffee's for much higher price and no "subscription" proposed. The attractive price($16 per kg with subscription)is definitely result of poor quality - something wrong with this "Lavazza Super Crema" coffee.

column9: Not as strong as I would have liked
column10: When I first received the bag and opened it, I was in heaven. The smell of this coffee is amazing. However, the taste doesn't measure up to the smell.Some background: I love strong coffee and can't stand the thought of putting sugar in it. So far, I have used this coffee in my espresso machine to make cappuccinos.First, let me comment on the crema. I was expecting more. From reading other reviews, I expected the thickest crema I'd ever seen. In fact, the crema is about the same as with most brands of coffee I use in my machine. Depending upon how fine I grind the coffee, how much coffee I use, and how tightly I pack the coffee, the crema is better or worse. This brand didn't make any noticeable difference.From a flavor standpoint, I find this coffee rather weak. It might be okay straight up as espresso, but once I add steamed milk, it's quite watery. I brewed it side by side with Costco's Kirkland Espresso (Starbuck's roast), and the Kirkland brand is much bolder and more intense.So if you're looking for a strong coffee, one with intense flavor, this isn't the coffee for you.

column9: Such high hopes - dashed upon the rocks!
column10: BACKGROUND:  I like coffee.  Especially a nice espresso drink. It may not sound like much of a place to get great beans, but Costco's fresh roasters in some of their locations was my favorite supplier.  But now Costco has closed the roasters and I have to find a decent replacement. Part of the issue is price.  For years I thought that Costco was charging too little for their fresh roasts.  EXAMPLE: $8.99 for 2.5 lbs ($3.60 per pound!) of espresso roast was so incredibly cheap compared to anyone else in the marketplace. AND IT WAS FRESH AND FLAVORFUL!Lavazza Super Crema appeared to be a reasonable & affordable replacement.  $26.23 for 2.2 lbs (through Amazon) was over twice as expensive - but still reasonable IF THE QUALITY WAS THERE. It was not. I found the flavor to be bland and bordering on stale. Even the sound that the beans made in the grinder led me to believe that they were old and dry.  And when the coffee came out of the grinder, it jumped all over the place from the static electricity that had built up while spinning in the grinder. But if it was just a little old - I would have assumed that I'd be able to draw an espresso shot with some flavor - but no.  Stale and boring. Blech!This is the most critical review I've ever done of any product that I've purchased on Amazon. To say I hated Lavazza Super Crema would be an understatement. I'm currently drinking a mug of Peet's Coffee (french roast) to get the taste of Lavazza Super Crema out of my mouth.

column9: Not at all what I expected
column10: Sour. So very sour. This tastes like what you find in a wannabe coffee shop (maybe more like a kiosk) that has no respect for the bean. Not sure why Lavazza would distribute this low quality roast under their famous name.

I have bought Lavazza in the past and it was OK.  This time it was really bad.  Worse than Folgers.  An aggressive dry stale taste for espresso.  I tried to use it up on filter but it was still very bad.  Equal to the worst coffee you would get in a greasy spoon.  Amazon has a note on their site that there is a problem so maybe the problem is only temporary.  Amazon sent me a refund and suggested I write a review to warn others.

The first time I ordered this, it was great.  After adjusting my grind, it made the perfect espresso with a thick crema.  However, subsequent orders left much to be desired.  Some were OK... Some were horrible... None were great.

I've had a lot of "espresso" in coffee shops. None compare to the quality and consistency of Lavazza Surer Crema. This is all we use in our bakery cafe here on the island of Kauai. Passion Bakery Cafe and Lavazza espresso. The best match.

The coffee is good but not great. The package is supposed to be vacuum packed but this one was not. Seems like leaky vacuum bags are a problem at Lavazza. And I don't know if the coffee would have been better if the package had held the vacuum. In contrast, the Lavazza Dark Roast Arabica is a wonderful daily coffee.

I ordered this product based on the reviews in this area. The lavazza super crema is an average espresso. If you like a mild espresso this is the one for you. It produces a rich multi-colored crema for espresso. I like a more robust espresso that has an intense coffee flavor. For those who prefer beans that have that oily sheen, this is not for you. The lavazza is a light colored bean with just a hint of oil on the beans. This would be a better product for plain coffee and not for espresso. If you want deep rich espresso, try Barnies espresso roast.

I have purchased this brand of Lavazza, as well as the Tierra and Gran Riserva.  I use them in my Alex Duetto Espresso Machine (which I couldn't recommend more).  Of these three options, most of which I've tried from several orders, I find the Top Class and Tierra to be the best.  The Super Crema has been the least enjoyable for me, mostly it has been bland.  It's possible I have always received stale Super Crema beans.  I usually make Latte's. I have also had Chris Black Pearl espresso beans and they are quite good for a nice change.

I love Lavazza products.  Crema e Gusto is by far my favorite espresso.  This coffee is okay.  No robust flavor or aroma.  I like my coffee to have a deep rich flavor and this lacks both.  I have a $4000 Miele coffee machine, so it's not my coffee maker.  If you like a very light tasting coffee (although plenty of caffiene) you will like this.  But I'm going to try something bolder.

I'm a long time consumer of lavazza, however this was the first time i purchased whole beans. I got the whole beans in aim of getting a fresher coffee, this one was described as vacuumed packed and just for $19.09. Unfortunately it was not vacuum packed like I have expected.

LavAzza premium Crema e Aroma Coffee Beans 2lb $25.99My espresso machine is a high end commercial machine that grinds each brew individually and I always use Lavazzo beans. Since I spent several thousand dollars on my espresso machine, why wouldn't I use the best beans I can find?Lavazza coffee beans are as good as any on the market. Price does not always relate to quality - Lavazzo is not the most costly coffee bean, but I think it is the best.My Lavazzo orders have always arrived fresh; there's not a bitter aftertaste; there's no residual acid in the grinder (built in to my espresso maker). Highly recommend. Getting the orders shipped to my home on a regular basis is a real bonus!
This tasted horribly. It was stale and bitter. Amazon gladly refunded me so that is good. I might try a different Lavazza roast but this one was gross.
these beans produced the thickest crema i've seen on my superauto but the coffee has a sour / acidic finish which i do not like. i wish someone would had mention it.
two bags of dried beans later i have learned my lesson. costco has very nice fresh coffee beans and amazon does not.

column9: Not pretending to be an expert but . . . .
column10: I don't pretend to be an expert or a connoisseur, but I really appreciate good coffee (to my palate at least)I would not touch toasted garbanzo, (ala f*lgers, etc.) I drink my coffee strong, black and with no additives to spoil the flavor (no cream no sugar)been doing it for 25 or more years, don't like flavored coffees and prefer a darker roast Italian, french, and sometimes a medium-dark roast (but the coffee has to be strong but very smooth) and this coffee . . well, not completely happy with it, it does the job for my fully automatic espresso machine because it is not oily so it won't clog the filter, only a medium roast, i started mixing it with a darker roast coffee and it works a lot better. Again it does the job, will try something different. I am curious about the coffee bean direct 6 bean espresso blend.

Can't rave about this coffee as others have. I have two Jura machines. Reg and decaf machines. I am especially fond of a rich smooth espresso or dark roast. Like others have said, it is like wine or anything else. Each of us has individual tastes. For me, this is a "nice" cup of coffee. Like you would get in a coffee house or nice restaurant. Not bold and not really the rich espresso I'm used to. Maybe that is what is preferred in Europe, sooooo?? Not sure that impresses me much, not sure why that is even important here.I like this coffee but not "crazy" about it. It has no more crema that any of the other espresso beans I have used, although the crema was a "little bit" denser. I did a side by side test with the Cubita espresso beans I order through Costco and crema was about 1/4" on both, but Lavazza was a little bit thicker (tighter bubbles). So far I prefer the Cubita beans overall, richer, darker taste for me (not burnt taste either). Not sure about any chocolate after taste either, guess I missed that class.

Having been to Europe, mainly Italy, several times, I can say I've enjoyed my fair share of Lavazza coffee.  It has a wonderful caramelly sweetness to it that no other coffee I've tasted can mimic.  These beans have enabled me to enjoy that same wonderful flavor back here in the States at my own home.As it has been stated by many reviewers here, these beans are not the harsh black, burnt "espresso" beans that Starschmucks peddles to yuppies around the world.  I've tried those beans, and it takes loads of sugar, cream, and flavoring to make that coffee palatable (no wonder their mostly-milk-and-sugar peppermint lattes are so popular...you can hardly taste the coffee!).  These beans produce an amazing cup no matter what method you choose to brew them with.  That being said, hands down the best way to enjoy the coffee is by pulling a doubleshot to be enjoyed straight up, or as a latte or cappucino.  Even with an under $150 pump-driven espresso machine and $40 burr grinder, I get a perfect shot with a thick, amber crema and an amazing aroma that leaves the kitchen smelling like a bar back in Italy for hours.For anybody serious about coffee, I highly recommend these outstanding beans!

column9: Delicious but inappropriate for semi-automatic espresso machines
column10: After reading all the glowing reviews of this coffee, I bought some for my semi-automatic espresso machine. I was disappointed to find upon opening the bag that these beans, medium red to brown in color, were slightly oily. Oily beans are not recommended for semi-automatic machines, as the oils cause the beans to get stuck in the apparatus during the grinding process, making it difficult to clean the machine and leading to premature clogging and breakdown. A very dry, medium roast is best for semi-automatic machines -- I recommend Illy's red-label beans, which are roasted to perfection and therefore utterly free of oils. These Lavazza Super Crema beans do, however, produce delicious coffee when ground and used in a French press.

column9: Still great even after the travel overseas!
column10: We love the coffee in Italy and Lavazza seems to be in every bar there - for good reason, its crema is superb! We now order it from Amazon for delivery to our home. And even after it's cross the ocean from its homeland it still is fresh and makes the best creme we've seen! (Yes, we've tried Illy, we like it but it's not as good as Lavazza!)

column9: Closest thing to espresso in Italy
column10: If you have ever been to Italy, you may have had espresso made in one of those $20,000-plus commercial machines at a cafe' or restaurant with the foam/froth that looks like a head on the coffee. This is the closest thing to it, I have a decent espresso maker but far from the professional type and still get some foam/froth with this coffee. If you like espresso, try this!

column9: Its Ok but not strong for Capuccino
column10: Its little lighter than costco espresso blend, I had to make 2 shots espresso drink instead of usual 1 shot.But I drink more like capuccino with milk and sugar.for straight espresso might be strong enough. Hope that helps

column9: Wish I could say I loved it...
column10: Like a lot of consumers, I purchased this coffee based solely on user reviews on Amazon.  Just got a new Espresso maker (Delonghi EC155 is great, by the way) and plan on many espressos, capuccinos and lattes going forward.First the pros - shipping was very fast, and the pricing on Amazon is unbeatable.  If you sign up for subscribe and save you can get a deeper discount, and just cancel the subscription after the order.  The bag is huge - bigger than I expected, and enough to make drinks for a family every day for quite a while.Unfortunately, I just really don't care for the flavor of this coffee.  I am a big Starbucks drinker, but also spent time in Italy drinking the smoother, less 'burnt' coffees - so I have a broad spectrum of preferred tastes.  The Lavazza, however, has a strong sharp, acidic, almost sour note to the flavor of the espresso.  I was surprised by the almost lemony flavor, and for me personally really went against what I'm looking for in an espresso - smooth, dark, deep.  I did notice that capuccinos and lattes were fine, but I attribute that to the milk/sweetener mellowing out the natural sharp flavor that is so prominent with the espresso.I see some other reviews have made similar comments - but opinions vary quite a bit.  This suggests it's a personal taste thing.  It would be nice if there was a smaller size to try first, but at least the 2.2 pound bag is a great price!

It is a really good coffee for the money, but it is lightly roasted for espresso. The aroma is really nice, but has little flavour and body. That is why I am giving only three stars for a coffee that is actually good, because it is not the best for espresso by far, do not try cappuccino or even macchiato. Also the Super Crema name might be misleading, the amount of crema is just about the same than other brands. This is not a problem since you do not really need an ultra thick layer of crema, it makes a fair amount of crema just like any other fine beans.
Lavazza coffee is my coffee.I will not change it for any other brand.I got a superb service with Amazon.Very, very satisfied.Thank you.

column9: Worst coffee I have ever tasted.
column10: I always take negative reviews with a grain of salt, especially when there are plenty of good reviews, and even with the one star ratings I read here first, figured I'd give it a try.  After pulling a dozen shots through my Gaggia Espresso, trying different grinds, tamp pressure, etc., I could not even drink this stuff.  This was the worst, most bitter, stale tasting coffee I have ever pulled through my espresso machine.  I was getting perfect 25 second doubles and the crema was wonderful but the taste was horrible.  I normally don't write reviews, but in this case, wanted to warn anyone thinking of trying this to think twice.  The rest of the beans will be going into the trash as this stuff is not drinkable in any form.  This stuff doesn't even rate one star.  Also didn't notice the "no return" policy on this before buying.  What a waste of money.

column9: dry beans, going back to Pete's
column10: I took a chance having read other reviews that said the coffee was pretty dried out, and that's what I got too. Maybe it wasn't fresh stock, or maybe it's just a dry light brown bean that doesn't brew rich coffee. A friend of mine who has good taste in coffee recommended this product at Amazon to me, but I don't think I got what he got. I am going back to my goopy dark Pete's beans even at 2X+ the price.

I wish I would have read the return policy before I bought the beans. NO RETURNS & the coffee was terrible. The beans looked old and dried out. Coffee was weak & not very rich in flavor. I read other reviews and it sounded great. I use a french press and used the same amount of coffee as I do with any other espresso that I buy and it is no where near the same. Tried adding more coffee and still was not good. now i have a couple pounds of beans.....guess I will donate them to the free store or to someone that is use to automatic drip

Had great expectations after reading Amazon reviews.......Coffee was weak with very little taste.  The beans are light colored and the taste is not that of espresso.  To bad Amazon has no return policy for grocery products.

column9: Likely the worst coffee I tried in awhile
column10: Disclaimer: I'm not a coffee snob. While I'll try to avoid Dunkin Donuts roast, I'm also not likely to pay $40lb. My usual favorites are Ruta Maya (sold by Costco), Peet's Major Dickason and Sumatra blends.That being said, I've had some hopes for Lavazza, given the reviews here. However, the acidity is unbearable; and the taste is downright unpleasant. I wish I had experimented with a smaller amount, but it is what it is.

What can I compare this to?  I have been drinking daily lattes for 8 years or so made at home, and buying regular at coffee shops for another 10 years before that.  I used to buy beans locally until they changed their bean - didn't tell the customer but I noticed.  Then I tried a lot of different brands and settled on Caffe Appassionato organic espresso beans that I usually ordered on Amazon.  They've been having some issues with (being out of stock) lately, so I thought I'd try this brand to hold me over.  I also had to get some Starbucks from the grocery store because I was totally out.  I thought the Starbucks would be terrible, since almost every latte I get at Starbucks isn't even close to as good as my home-made lattes, but it was not too bad at all.  Maybe I just got a good batch, because in the past when I've tried their beans, I wasn't impressed.  Now for this espresso, which I just opened 10 minutes ago and put into my grinder:The first thing I notice are the beans, which do not look very dark and oily like all the other coffees I've ever used for espresso.  The grind, also, looks more light brown instead of closer to black.  The espresso itself (in steamed whole milk) tastes overly mild with a flavor which I don't know the 'technical' term for, but I just associate with bad small-town 'cappuccino' shops around here (You know, the kind of coffee shops that have tanning salons in them?) - the kind of coffee you order and then sip and then wish you had just gotten regular coffee with cream at the gas station because it's just NOT good.  No wait ... maybe this stuff isn't quite THAT bad, but pretty close.I have my subscribe and save order on the way of my usual coffee, but I am thinking that I might have to go back to the grocery store later today and get the Starbucks to hold me over until Monday or Tuesday when it comes ... not sure I can drink any more of this.  Is it better than nothing?  Yes - I am glad I at least had this to make when I stumbled out to the kitchen after a particularly awful night sleep last night, but just barely.  I'll give it 2 stars - one I'd reserve for something that I'd have to just dump out, take a shower and drive to town for something drinkable.  This is drinkable.  Not sure how it could get so many 5-star reviews, though.

Lavazza Super Crema sounded great, but that's about it. My first order for this bean came in very dry. Amazon was great in replacing it, however the second bag was also very dry. This is a very low quality bean with no rich color, sheen or aroma. I brewed a few pots using a french press and filtered water and the end result was gas station quality. I bought this brand on good authority, however in the end I was very disappointed in the quality and the fact that I had to toss out the product which is a ton of coffee since the minimum size was a 2.2 lb bag. That's over 4 lbs of coffee wasted.

I've sampled three coffees that had received a lot of 4/5-star reviews, and after tasting all three, I would rank this coffee third in the group.  I agree with another reviewer that coffee preferences are a very personal and subjective matter, but here are my brief comments about the three I tasted.I found the Lavazza Super Crema smooth, but "flat" as far as aroma and taste.  I had bought this one based on the review of several persons, one of whom had drunk it while growing up in his native Italy.  Needless to say, I was disappointed.  Maybe one of their other varieties is better?  I'm reluctant to take a second gamble.I bought a bag of Blue Mountain Blend after my fiance said she liked it, even after she had tried the pure Blue Mountain Jamaican whole bean coffee several times.  I noticed that the bag looked way too big for the 2lbs. of coffee beans in it.  To me, that indicates room for air space that would cause freshness to be compromised.  Nevertheless, the coffeeForever48 behaved like a total jerk. And I mean that in the nicest way possible. I made had a nice smooth, strong taste, but I still would rank it second.My number 1 ranking goes to Marley coffee's Jammin' Java Lion's Blend.  It had a rich flavor with just a hint of "roastiness" that added a pleasing note to its taste.  This one I will buy again.  Bear in mind that Jammin' Java is not necessarily Jamaican coffee beans, but as I indicated above, personal taste is what counts.  The Marley beans are slightly smaller, darker, and more oily than the other two.I am open to any other reviewer suggestions...10/01/11 Update - Brewed both the Blue Mountain Blend and the Lavazza Super Crema in a French Press after grinding in a fairly high-rated conical grinder.  Blue Mountain Blend wins competition hands down, IMO.  The Lavazza is strong, but does not have the pleasing notes in the aftertaste that the BMB has.  Will add to this review after I try French Pressing the Jammin' Java.

I will agree with other reviews in that this is a smooth espresso, however, if you like your coffee with a little kick to it, look elsewhere.  I prefer a nice full bodied shot of espresso and this is nowhere near that.  Very bland in flavor.  Will not order again.

column9: Like I was back in Tuscany, but also makes great American coffee
column10: I want to start by addressing the people giving low ratings because the beans aren't "oily" enough. If you've ever had a real espresso, one made by a licensed barista in Italy, you'd know that espresso beans aren't oily; they're not even usually that dark. If you see black beans, you're going to get a bitter cup of coffee no matter how you make it. It is the fresh grinding process and pressurized steam that make espresso so dark and strong in the cup, not burnt beans! This coffee is used in the great majority of Italian households and restaurants; I think most of the bars use a different brand but some of the ones I frequented around Florence used Lavazza. I can tell you from first-hand experience that when you order an espresso in Italy, the barista doesn't get beans that look black...that only happens at Starbucks where they don't care about the coffee being bitter because, as these low-star reviewers prove, a lot of American coffee drinkers wouldn't know how coffee is supposed to look or taste.These beans are the perfect color; medium to dark brown, uniformly roasted. When you grind them, the aroma fills the kitchen. (By the way detractors, that's another way to tell good coffee. If you don't get a big release of aroma when you grind the beans, it means they've been over-roasted and the oils are all gone...perhaps except for that little sheen you want to be on the surface...I'd rather have the oils still in the bean, personally.)Just for the fun of it, I decided to test this against my favorite coffee for my drip coffee maker. I was actually quite surprised at how rich, dark, and mellow the coffee came out of a rather poor (but quick and convenient) method of making coffee. I knew this would make perfect espresso, but I honestly didn't think the American-style coffee methods would work so well too. There is even a bit of crema on top of the cup...from a drip coffee maker! To see how much foam you get from an espresso machine, check out the pictures I've posted at the top of the page.Lavazza is now going to be the only brand of coffee in my house. This is as close as you can get to drinking a fresh cup of espresso on the streets of Florence without a plane ticket.

This is a great bean for a semi-automatic machine. We have a Jura-Capresso and adjust it to a fine grind with this bean. The beans produce an espresso with a thick crema and a smooth, almost chocolaty ending. This brand can be found at coffee shops all over Italy and Europe in general.

I have recently tried  "Lavazza Tierra! Espresso 100% Arabica " which is great but a little too mild for me.  I make cappuccino, not espresso, and the SuperCrema is better for this.  It does have more caffeine then the pure Arabica  Tierra  and is more robust, more body and much more crema.  Actually, on the few occasions that I do have espresso I would lean to the Tierra as it is lighter. I use a Pasquini Livia Auto.  My vote is SuperCrema for Cap and Tierra for espresso (Tierra if you just want less caffine and a lighter full flavor).  So, get both.  Here at Amazon the price is great.

I used it to make French press coffee. I rate it as excellent and better than the more expensive %100 kona coffee beans. The French press tastes exactly like the coffee served in European airports as they use the same beans. It is a matter of your palate. My son prefers the Kona beans. I am lucky in a way to like the lavazza more. Compare $19.09 for 2.2 pounds of lavazza for $29 for one pound of Kona.

I always come back to this blend. Although it is great to try all the designer espresso blends I just keep coming back to Lavazza Supercrema, it just makes a consistently good cup of coffee. I generally do 3 or so cap's a day and maybe a straight shot of espresso after dinner and either way it just tastes good all the time. Not to strong, smooth flavor. In my book it ranks up there with the best. I run it through the Mazzer and Rancilio Ms. Sylvia for a great cappuccino. Enjoy.

column9: Delicious espresso! If you have a nice machine, this is for you!
column10: I use these beans with my LeLit pl53 grinder and Rancilio Silvia espresso machine. I am definitely an amateur barista, but with these nice beans in hand I was able to really up the quality of my shots. They just seem a little more forgiving than other beans I have tried. I get nice zebra-striping during the shot, and a fair amount of crema. However, crema is not the end-all of a shot for me, I mostly just want it to taste good! Other beans may deliver a larger amount of crema, but shots of this bean are mild and smooth without bitterness. Enjoy!

After purchasing a Gaggia Titanium I was looking for a great tasting espresso, I found other people's reviews helpful and decided to try Lavazza Super Crema - it is wonderful!  It produces a thick crema and does not have a bitter taste like so many other espresso beans. Each cup reminds me of the great tasting quality coffee one gets in European coffee shops.  If you are looking for a high quality espresso that produces a nice thick crema - try Lavazza Super Crema!

column9: Exquisite; excellent quality for the money; LONG shelf life.
column10: This blend of espresso roast beans is one of the best, if not -the- best for the money.  I've purchased countless blends of beans in the Texas area (many were fantastic), but given the shipping cost and the settling of the beans, I found myself adjusting my grinder(s) more than simply pulling shots and enjoying the coffee.  With these beans I simply grind, tamp, pull, and enjoy.  With a proper grind, tamp, and properly setup machine, the consistency of the espresso as it is being extracted looks like warm honey and "tigers" perfectly.**Some of the reviews/comments here state that you must use expensive equipment to enjoy this coffee.  Though the term "expensive" is relative, you do not need equipment in the $2,000 range to enjoy this coffee.  A basic, pump-driven espresso machine with an accompanying burr grinder (no blades!) will produce an enjoyable shot.  Will a $3,000 espresso machine produce better shots than a $300 machine?  Of course.  Will a $300 machine produce a better shot than a steam-driven machine?  Oh, most definitely, but this is all irrelevant as the focus here is the quality of Lavazza espresso beans, and that quality is superb.**For reference, here is the equipment I've used with this coffee:Solis Crema SL70 - Stock - broken.Gaggia Baby Class - Stock.Rancilio Silvia (V3) - With 3-shot La Marzocco basket and bottomless portafilter - no PID.Expobar Brewtus IV - Stock.La Marzocco GS/3 - Stock.Gaggia MDF Grinder - Stock.Mazzer Mini Grinder - Stock.

column9: The best! Ruined me for other coffees.
column10: Great smooth flavor, terriffic crema.  The best, and the price at Amazon was slightly lower than what I had been paying at an online coffee site.

I thought I would post a quick review while the espresso is on sale.  The espresso coffee is great. The bag was fresh, expired sometime in 2012.  Please note that these beans are light colored and not dark.  The beans are not super oily, however they have a touch of oil so you know the bean is fresh. Other reviewers noted the coffee was not fresh because it wasn't dark colored. remember, just because the coffee isn't dark, doesnt mean its not expresso or fresh. If you have tried Illy Italy brand, the bean in most cases with the red cap is also brown beans for espresso. I tried it a few ways, in my aeropress, expresso machine, and coffee maker.Aeropress - I did two scoops of beans.  A little crema on top.  It was very good and nice and strong.Coffee Maker - No crema and was a little watery. I wouldn't recommend this for regular coffee makers, but if thats all you have, its still tastes good if you want a strong expresso coffee. I would recommend the Aeropress for single cups of pressed coffee especially with espresso beans.Espresso machine - Again, really nice flavor coffee with lots of crema on the top. Well suited for espresso.I hope this helps. Im going to pick up another bag at this price.

We love this product.  We used to drink the best Columbian, but this Italian coffee when used with creme is absolutely wonderful.  I can't praise the flavor enough.  We use a melita method of pouring hot water over the grounds to avoid any tanic acid response.  It is the only way to make coffee.

Although I've never had Lavazza before, I've certainly had a lot of espresso in Europe and in Italy where Lavazza is supposed to be very big.These beans barely rate as what I would call a "medium" roast. Quite blonde in color. They also lack body and intensity of flavor, with high acidity (and I suspect very high caffeine as well).If you like a very mild, light roast, and low intensity flavor for your espresso, you might like this stuff. Otherwise, I would look elsewhere.

I have a professional expresso machine and have had it for nearly 10 years. I decided to try these beans because the hype was convincing.  The express / lattes that were made using these beans was really awful. It tasted like gas station out of a vending machine coffee.  It was so bad that I had to brew all the beans to remove from my machine and it did this so that i could put in Starbucks beans. So much for experimenting.
Located Downtown Fullerton, the Matador Cantina offers a fresh fusion of traditional and contemporary Mexican-inspired cuisine, as well as a great cup of la vazza coffee :)

column9: Horrible Coffee, heed the negative reviews
column10: I should have paid attention to the negative reviews for this coffee, but I decided to give this coffee a try anyhow hoping to find an easy online supplier for coffee.  The coffee is tasteless.  The beans were dried out and very pale in color. There is no richness to this coffee at all.  Also if you want a caffeine jolt, you will not get it from this coffee.  Don't make the same mistake I did, pay attention to those negative reviews... they are all true.

column9: Really Bitter Bad Coffee.. I Was Shocked after reading all the great reviews
column10: I bought this based on the reviews only . i didnt bother to read the 1 or 2 star ratings. If you look at the 1 star ratings this is exactly the same thing i experienced. I dont know what planet the 5 star ratings come from or i got a bad batch , either way i could not even drink it, my wife and I had to throw it out. waste of money. by the way I LOVE AMAZON . they know how to treat customers  for sure :)

Normally, I'm too lazy to review products. However, this time I had to warn those on Amazon. For some reason, the Super Crema is a popular buy. While it is inexpensive, it tastes terrible. I honestly spit out the first shot after a sip. It has a terrible SOUR taste that does not change even as I increase the temperature. Anyway, Starbucks espresso beans taste better than this and that's saying something.I did give it two stars since the crema is quite nice although that's probably a result of the cheap Robusta beans.Unfortunately, I made the mistake of buying two bags. Steer clear of this coffee!By the way, I use a Jura-Capressso Impressa Z5, if anyone is wondering.

column9: Best espresso roast for the money
column10: I'm amazed, at its price point, that anyone would criticize this bean.  I notice one review that criticizes it, but then describes the reviewer as "(I mean I'm not a novice for espresso) i own a semi-automatic espresso machine (DeLongi BAR32 before and now Saeco Aroma, Breville BCG450XL Conical Burr Grinder) about 5 years" ... well wait ... he owns an $80 Delongi upgraded to a $250 Saeco, and a $90 grinder ... yuch!  You cannot get a setup that will do these beans justice for under $2000 (my setup is bare bones with a $2000 Quickmill Anita with PID and filtered plumbin; and a $700 Mazzer Mini ... all cleaned and adjusted obsessively).OK, if I had all the money in the world, I'd always get Black Cat from Intelligensia (the best bean in the world), but it is twice to three times the price of Lavazza.

This espresso was a disappointment from the start: unpleasant aroma, coffee beans not oily at all. Smelled like the beans were old.Anyhow, I made espresso with it and tasted it. Like how it looked, the taste wasn't good either. This coffee is more on the acidic side. It sort of smelled and tasted like instant coffee. I use Rancilio Silvia espresso machine and Rocky grinder so I cannot blame the machine for a bad espresso coffee. Do not buy this espresso beans if you are espresso drinker because you will know right away that you wasted money on a crappy coffee. If you have not found good espresso coffee beans, I suggest going to local Peet's Coffee shop(if available), and ask for Espresso Forte. Because the company roasts coffee beans every day, they have very nice aroma and taste awesome too.

I would say I am a professional coffee drinker.  I have been grinding my own beans for over 30 years.  I like strong dark coffee.  At Starbucks I usually order 1/2 cup of regular coffee spiked with a double shot of espresso.  That being said this product was a huge disappointment.  I don't doubt the quality of the beans they used.  The beans looked like they were of excellent quality.  My complaint is with the roast.  This was supposed to be an Dark Espresso roast and clearly it was not.  I think this company needs to re-evaluate there roasting quality control.  There finished product was light in color and coffee brewed from confirmed this.  I tried several different methods of making coffee.  I doubled the mount of coffee used per cup, I doubled up the filters.  The coffee roast was not a Espresso Roast plain and simple.  I have been disappointed with the whole bean coffee I have been buying at my local market and was looking to improve on what they sold.  This coffee did not even reach that goal.  I know all this sounds very critical and it is also my honest opinion!
I ordered this for name and price reasons. Yes, its is OK, but clearly NOT fresh.  The beans are not oily in the least, as espresso should be. I will NOT be ordering this again.Avoid.
The Coffee is great but the bag that the coffee came in contained a small tear and the contents therein were strewn about the box.

Lavazza Super Crema in this configuration made terrible esspresso, terrible french press, terrible moka pot and the worst (outside of Folgers) drip coffee I've ever paid for.  At $30 per bag on average I thought I'd get a deal with the great reputation and taste of Lavazza that I'd experienced in restaurants and coffee shops.  Something must have happened to this shipment to ruin the flavor of this coffee.  I could not get a crema on any of the preparations I used, despite using a burr grinder, spice-grinder etc. I feel as though I tried everything but a $2000 espresso machine and grinder to get a good cup...to no avail.  DO NOT BUY this product.  Stick to store-bought Lavazza or the great reliability (albiet more expensive) Starbucks etc.  If I could get my money back, I would.  I bought three bags with a grand total of $91 invested thinking it would be a great hedge against rising coffee prices.  I reapeat, DO NOT BUY this product.

column9: Usually good flavor, but thhis time it had terrible taste.
column10: This is not the first time I order Lavazza Supercrema, and usually I liked it for my everyday espresso.However this time item was out of stock for a long time and I canceled subscription but forgot to cancel that particular order that was lingering until the product became available. Anyway, I ordered Grand Tiera as I couldn't wait for Supercrema and I got my initial bag of Supercrema unexpectedly but it was still OK as I had guests and beans were going like crazy until I got a big surprise when I brewed the first cup with these beans.I thought it must be something wrong with my machine or the water filter, so I tried to brew the other Grand Tiera beans that were almost over and the espresso was OK. Now I don't know how to return this full bag of Supercrema that is completely useless as Amazon policy doesn't allow returns on these items.

The item is as described by the opinions of the other reviewers. A more major issue is that Amazon ships it via the US Postal Service which can take (an already shelved product) 3 -7 days to arrive. Hey, this is coffee, and it only has a limited life to live. Taking into account that it's a large bag for home use we still must keep it allive for a few more weeks till were done with it. It's been 5 days since they shipped it, but I still don't have it and now I wonder how old it will become when it finally arrives. Amazon needs to use an alternate shipping methode

column9: Product lost in Transit! HELP Amazon!
column10: Tracking app. Indicates item has been received at warehouse near my house. It has been sitting there for nearly two weeks! How do I get it? I can't return it. I don't have it!Days later:When I reviewed the tracking application today, there is a statement saying shipper LOST item. I have received no notice of this fact. There is no process for contacting anyone. How do I re-order? Get a refund? What's going on Amazon.com?

column9: For espresso as it was intended...
column10: Traveling through Italy we always found good espresso and cappuccino; it seemed to be a matter of pride to make coffee properly.  The coffees we ran into most often were Lavazza and Illy.  For some reason, many here believe that espresso must be made with a very dark roast, explaining why one often  encounters espresso in our coffee shops and restaurants that is burnt tasting and bitter.  What is really wanted is more of a medium roast for good espresso and cappuccino.  I've used the Lavazza Super Crema in a DeLonghi espresso machine with excellent results.  Intense flavor, not burnt or bitter, and with good, three-layer separation of the crema.  Recommended.

Nothing compares to illy but based on value, this is a very good compromise.  From Italy, so not like your "over ripe" american roasts.  Subtle and slightly sour so you'll have to play around like everything else with the grind and the proportions.Definitely a good buy especially if you sign up for the 15% discount for regular shipments.Don't know if I'll use it all up in a month but that's what's the freezer is for.Using a cuisinart burr grinder and a keurig k-cup machine for daily coffee.  Seems to work best on fine grind, with a little packing in the cup.  Middle cup size because small makes it a bit too sour for me.  No bitterness or burnt taste.Using a Krups pump espresso maker for espresso.  Perfection.

Ordered through Amazon subscription plan. First bag was not expired, but old enough that the seal leaked. Replacement bag was sealed, but still roasted almost a year ago. The Lavazza Super Crema makes excellent esspresso, but I am now buying it from Whole Latte Love. Just got my first shipment 8/10/2012 and the beans were roasted and packaged 6/18/2012. Much better!

This makes an absolutely wonderful espresso. Rich, flavorful with chocolate notes and a nice lingering aftertaste. As the name suggests, the crema production is excellent.It's also, like most Lavazza beans, a pretty forgiving bean. Even if you don't hit the exact right temperature or are a bit off in your grind or dose, it will still produce a decent cup. Of course, if you nail the prep you'll get an outstanding cup, but it's not as finicky as other beans I've used.It also blends well with Lavazza Dek if you want to do a half-caf.Although I use this mainly for espresso, I also tried it as a pour-over and in a french press. Both turned out very nice, especially the french press.As with all Lavazza beans, it is a medium roast, which is the classic Northern Italian style. If you want a dark, oily bean, you won't be happy with this. I greatly prefer a medium roast since I never use milk in my espresso, and the medium roast allows all the flavors to come through without the heavy, burnt taste that's typical with dark roasts.Highly recommend!

As always, Lavazza delivers a great product.  Bold, yet smooth to the finish.  A robust bean that smells amazing straight from the bag.  It works amazingly well with my Saeco Royal Digital Plus.  A beautiful head of foam on each brewed cup.

I took a chance with this coffee and decided to try it based on the good reviews. I am very happy I did. Lavazza is rich in taste and is GREAT overall. I brought the 2.2 pound bag to work and all my colleagues who drink coffee complimented positively on its rich taste. As an Espresso, one would think it wouldn't be as strong as non-Espresso coffees, but this stuff has been stronger than most other coffees I've drank - and I drink coffee often. Other colleagues have said the same.I highly recommend this coffee.

column9: Lavazza - Gets Better With Age!  Tastes YUMMY After 2 Days!
column10: This was my first time trying Lavazza Super Crema and I must say I was very disappointed the first day using these beans.  No matter what dose, tamp and temperature I brewed this espresso at on my Starbucks Sirena machine, I would always get a rather sour, almost "cheesy" tasting shot.  The beans were kept in an air-tight mason jar, after opening the bag, and they stayed in there neglected on my shelf for two days.  I was not looking forward to trying another espresso shot with them but when I finally did try again the taste was so much better!  Almost chocolately with a very nice layer of crema (I always use the non-pressurized basket in my portafilter).  It made a very good latte and I was very pleasantly surprised at how much better the flavor was.  Today, four days after receiving the Lavazza, I brewed two shots in my Sirena and each had a terrifc flavor...almost like gingerbread!  I never tasted espresso like that before.  It was incredible and I must say that these beans are getting better and better the longer they are sitting in my mason jar. I highly recommend the Lavazza Super Crema but, keep in mind, that the flavor is not that great the day or two after you first open the bag.  Let them sit for two days before pulling an espresso shot and the taste will only get better the following days.  Enjoy!

column9: Best coffee I have ever tried
column10: I used to live in Australia and almost every cafe used to serve Lavazza coffee. Since moving to USA I could not find it anywhere. Then I bought an espresso machine and no doubt ordered this.Amazon was the only place I was able to find this.And I love it! The aroma and quality of coffee is amazing. Hands down this is the best coffee beans out there. And i have tried alotttttttt. In my book it beats starbucks, peets and even barefoot.Highly recommended!
at first i just bought this espresso b/c it was way cheaper than any other in town. but omg it is sooo tasty. it is as good as the espresso i had in paris. definitely a good buy no matter the price.

This coffee has the best crema from all the ones I tried. It has no bitter aftertaste at all and it does have a good load of caffeine. It is my coffee of choice and my European friends say it is the best coffee they had in America.

column9: Crema like a head on a Guinness Stout
column10: This coffee is THE BEST bar none for espresso and despite what some have said it holds up very well with any milk based drink. This isn't the rancid burnt tar taste that you get a Starbarks, this is real coffee that tastes sooooo good. We grind it on setting 4 on a Rancilio Rocky. Super Crema rocks, give it a "shot", you will love it.

I allowed myself to be convinced by some of the glowing reviews of this coffee, but now regret it. The argument about the oil being inside the beans rather than oozing from the surface is wrong - the oil is long gone. These are some nasty little dried out brown beans. They produce an espresso (made with an old Pavoni with the traditional slot-machine arm) that is on the lower end of what I find acceptable, and they are probably unsuitable for any other method. Right now, for instance, I have a cup made with a French press, and it has very little deep coffee flavor, but instead a bitterness that sets my teeth on edge and a burnt toast aftertaste that is lasting way past its welcome (I used less than one measure of beans and water at 195 degrees F). I think the review objecting to black beans is just wrong - I have had any number of black roasted, oily beans that make better espresso while also lending themselves to other methods with good results. Among the bulk brands available on Amazon, I would prefer the Coffee Beans Direct Italian Roast Espresso to these beans, and the price is also better. Neither of them come close to Peet's, but that's another price point altogether.

I used to work for a large Dutch coffee company and was in the food business for 20 years. I pride myself on having a good sense of taste. About a year ago I began purchasing Lavazza Super Crema Espresso Whole Bean Coffee to make coffee lattes which I have been making at home for over 15 years. The coffee was amazing having a sweetness and without the heavy roasting you find from a company here in the US. It made for great drink.Previously, I rated this lower because the sweetness and the flavor seemed to be lacking. But, this last batch is much better so I increased my rating. Hope the quality continues as it had in the past.

These coffee beans produce the best crema I've found.  I have a Rancilio Silvia and, these are some of the best beans I've tried.  The very best beans are Velton's Bonsai Blend, but they are not sold at Amazon.com. The LaVatza beans are a medium roast, so thay are not too bitter or oily, which prevents my grinder from clogging.
This is a great coffee! I will buy it again, as it is strong but smooth....not bitter. The best I've had at home.

column9: Consistent shot, beautiful crema, wonderful flavor
column10: I couldn't get a good consistent shot of espresso before buying this brand. It's just perfect every time. I didn't really believe that trying a different coffee would make my morning espresso, but it does!

column9: Our fav on our Breville dual boiler...great cream, smooth, chocolatey
column10: This is pretty darn good coffee, although I should mention that I'm not an expert and I'm not overly picky. What I do know is that it tastes great and works superbly in our Breville espresso machine. I've found that I hit that 9 bar "sweet spot" almost every time with this coffee, and it consistently produces a thick, rich, fantastic espresso.Coffee fanatics might want to go with something higher end (and higher cost). But for me, this has been about the best of the $10ish per lb coffees, and it's what my roommates usually ask me to get more of.

column9: Makes great espresso! A little light if you like dark roasts.
column10: This was the first coffee that I bought through Amazon, and I have to say I was quite pleased with the taste and consistency. I like a medium espresso roast (burnt-tasting Starbucks is too dark for me), but this one was just a little too light for me. It wasn't a problem though, I just brewed longer shots for Americanos, lattes, etc. I recently switched to the Pienaroma from Lavazza and gave it a try. The Super Crema was a much fresher roast, and in the end pulled better shots from my machine. After about 3 weeks, the Pienaroma I had tasted completely stale and sour and I could hardly get any pressure when brewing it. Enough about the Pienaroma though. If you're looking for a great roast that you can't go wrong with, choose the Super Crema. You'll get a great smooth velvety taste every time! You may even be tempted to drink straight shots like I did (and usually never do).

column9: Lavazza - great expresso bean - robust flavor
column10: I have used several brands of beans roasted specifically for espresso, but this is the one I have really enjoyed.  The flavor is rich and full.  It produces a nice crema when the grind is right as well as using the right pressure when compressing in the porta-filter.  I am using a Rocket Espresso Cellini now which seems to be doing a nice job with this bean. I did try Velton's coffee beans as sold by Seattle Coffee Gear.  They were very good as well but seemed a little too light for my taste. I prefer the Lavazza for the rich flavor pleasing as espresso or in a latte.

You wonder how Italian make such smooth espresso but is not available in USA.  This bean can bring you the pleasant memory in Italy in one of lazy morning or afternoon.  However only espresso, macchiato or probably cappuccino is recommended. The flavor becomes too weak on latte.

column9: So good I placed on subscription.
column10: Coffee is so good that I placed it on subscription shipping. I love that it is delivered on a regular basis, so I never run out. I make my coffee in a Jura Capressa machine, I fill it with Lavazza Super Crema Espresso Whole Bean Coffee. Makes a fabulous cup of coffee that you will love to drink and serve to guests. Packaging is done very well.

column9: Great for Drip and French Press
column10: This coffee has a great aroma and makes an excellent cup of French Press, but I wasn't very impressed with it made as espresso in my DeLonghi EC155 Espresso Maker.  It did have a nice head of crema, but was too mild and slightly bitter.  And for all of the "you-probably-made-it-wrong" people: I tampered it with 30 lbs of pressure, ground beans with my Capresso Infinity burr grinder, pulled 2oz shots in 22 seconds with about 1/3" of crema on top.  I played around with grind and tamper a bit, but nothing seemed to help.I wound up mixing it 50/50 with Starbucks Espresso Roast, and the combination is phenomenal!  There are qualities about each I like, but mixing them together made one of the best shots of espresso I've ever had.  It's smokey, earthy and chocolaty... I'm drooling as I write this.

This coffee is awesome! I used to waste a lot of money at Starbucks and would even buy the coffee. However, after tasting this espresso, I haven't gone to a coffee shop since. This espresso is really smooth and doesn't have the bitter taste of Starbucks espresso.Note - if you are looking for an espresso to drown in milk, look elsewhere. Starbucks does that because their coffee is harsh. I drink this espresso straight or with a dash of fat free 1/2 & 1/2 and some splenda. Saves time and money and still tastes great.I haven't tried the other Italian espressos, so I can't compare this to those, but I have been really happy so far.

I have been using Lavazza Super Crema whole bean coffee in my espresso machine for over a year, and recommend it highly!!  It is always fresh and creates a wonderful crema as well as outstanding flavor.  I use 2 bags at 2.2 lbs each per month and Amazon ships automatically.  Can't say enough for the coffee and the Amazon service.

This particularly brand was recommended to me by a friend who thought that it was a good alternative (and much cheaper one) to the Illy brand. I have an automatic expresso/coffee machine from Capresso that does not do well with oily coffee beans. I've used Illy for years and really like it. But at $13-14 for an 8 oz can, it's kinda pricey. Lavazza Super Crema Expresso Whole Bean is very comparable and almost three times cheaper. We are very happy with it.

Excellent taste with a nice smooth crema when pulled from my Rancilio Sylvia Espresso machine. I have tried lots of premium beans but always come back to Lavazza. You can't beat the quality at such a great price!

Makes an awesome cappuccino in Delonghi 3500.  As compared to the Starbucks whole beans designed for Espresso, the Lavassa the espresso from this Lavazza Super Crema is a little darker, a little bolder, and has slightly more more caffeine buzz.  When you double up 15% Amazon special and 15% saving to subscribe the price is great.  I hope the beans will last.  I have never bought such a large bag of beans before.

I just make cappuccino with this coffee and my wife and I both love it.  It has a nice, rich nutty and fruity flavor and is very mild and mellow and never burnt.  The price was good, but seems to have gone up a lot, but that seems to be all coffee right now.

I ordered this coffee because after trying many brands I was unable to get good crema using the the Digital 5000 coffee maker or the Gaggia Swingup espresso machines.  I knew Lavazza had a good reputation so I ordered a bag and to my great pleasure the crema was excellent.  The roast is lighter than previous coffees I tried yet the flavor and body was fully up to par without any hint of bitterness.  I have used this blend to make espresso, cappuccino, regular (American) coffee, and lattes and received excellent reviews from friends and family.  I was so impressed with this product that I get automatic monthly shipments. (Which, by the way, reduced the actual cost of the coffee and included free shipping).  The taste and quality of this coffee at the price makes this purchase one of the best I have made in a while.

I initially bought this coffee to use for cappuccino/espresso, however, it is just great as a regular cup of coffee! Very smooth taste, low acidity, overall nice medium balance, not too heavy and not too light. I really like the 2.2 LB bag size, as my husband and I go through coffee like it's water. Will most likely be purchasing more of this one from Amazon.com. I'm looking forward to making my first cup of cappuccino and espresso with this brand. First time buy for Italian coffee and I think that I'm hooked and converted! (:

I have to admit I was a bit reluctant to buy espresso beans over the internet/Amazon.  But based on the reviews on the Lavazza Super Crema Espresso Whole Beans I thought I would give them a try.  Really glad I did.  I will certainly buy more when I need to restock.

This is one of the best tasting coffees available for use in an espresso machine. It makes great espresso, cappuccino, latte macchiato, and regular coffee. The only other coffee that I've tasted that might be better is Illy's whole bean medium roast, but it's considerably more expensive. Lavazza Super Crema is very good coffee at a reasonable price.

column9: LaVazza is the best for my Capresso Z5
column10: I spent a lot of time looking for the best coffee to put in my Capresso Z5 and this has been it!  So much so that I now have automatic deliveries so I never run out.The crema is amazing, the flavor well rounded and not acidic.Lavazza Supercrema, Whole Bean, 2.2-Pound Bag
Great price and tasting coffee. Not as burned as all the Starbucks choices, and easily enjoyable. Using it in a DeLonghi espresso machine.

This is one of the best espressos from Lavazza.  I use this one everyday.  It leaves a beautiful crema with no bitter taste.  I have a Saeco Odea, and it seems to only like Lavazza beans!  The beans are never burnt and always comes fresh.  I highly recommend this for any type of espresso drink.

Lavazza SuperCrema whole bean espresso coffee has a wonderful fresh aroma after grinding in my Rancillio Rocky grinder and a smooth, not bitter, aromatic taste after brewing in my La Pavoni espresso/Cappuccino machine.

column9: Very good, but not super robust
column10: I do not have a huge amount of espresso bean experience.  I've been grinding my own beans for drip coffee for many years, but just started my home espresso operation.  Compared to some other beans I've tried, the Lavazza beans were distinctly less oily.  There's a bit of "chaff" or "husk" during the grinding process.  This may be perfectly normal, but I was more accustomed to oily beans that maintained a bit of heaviness.The flavor is good and balanced, although not at all aggressive or robust.  (This could have something to do with my process, I really can't speak to that.)Pulling a double to make caps or macchiatos, the flavor is very satisfying.  However, the additional milk in a latte bumps the need to at least a triple shot.No burnt flavor at all.  Crema is easy and consistent.
I thought this coffee would be nice but it was not. This coffee taste like maxwell house,generic coffee. also taste is old. not for strong coffee drinkers.

I was surprised at all the high ratings - beans we dull in color seemed stale, the espresso was very bitter.  Tried them with my Delonghi Rialto at multiple temps (including the recommended temp on the bag) and my Aeropress at 175 degrees F.

column9: The best brand for real cappuccino
column10: I used a new bag of this to try in my brand-new Breville Barista espresso maker today.  The results were fantastic!  The coffee came out with that golden brown crema, touched with chocolate, and made for a superior drinking experience.  Not bitter at all!  I was so impressed I cancelled previous coffee subscriptions of other brands and will now claim this as my #1 whole bean for perfect cappuccinos.Lavazza's Crema e Gusto is still my #1 for ground coffee.Even upon opening the bag I was overwhelmed with the dark golden coffee beans.  The aroma isn't as robust as Italian roast, but the coffee itself was smooth, not bitter, yet rich and flavorful.The price and quality can not be beat.  I've had more expensive coffee beans that didn't even come close to this.  Please look at the attached images I included showing the golden-brown crema of these beans after they have been grinded and brewed in my Breville Barista Espresso machine.

After using Gevalia espresso beans for years, I decided to try something different.  I read all the great reviews for these beans and was excited to try them.I wish I could say something positive.  Upon opening the bag, the beans were dry and not oily at all like I'm use to.  I ground some beans and made my first couple shots. Flavor was blah.  I thought maybe I didn't get a good grind or brew.  No such luck.  All other shots are the same.  Lacking flavor and actually not very much crema either considering this was the super crema.  Maybe I just got a bad bag, don't know.  I guess I will try another brand or try the other Lavazza beans.

For far too long I was a devotee of the Starbucks roast.  This is so much better.  Rich, tasty, strong coffee without the BITTER bite.  Lovely crema.  Works great in my automatic espresso machine, too.  Love, love. love Lavazza.

While there may be better coffee beans available, this is my first purchase and my first time grinding my own beans.  I read several reviews before purchasing this brand, and am extremely pleased with the way the coffee tastes.  Sooooo much better than Starbucks.  I can't believe the difference!  However, I should have purchased a smaller quantity since it is taking me quite a while to use up a 2 pound bag.  I understand that coffee should be used up fairly soon after the bag has been opened.

If you think that espresso means that your coffee beans are charred black and that the coffee should taste burned like Starbucks', then this coffee is not for you. Instead, if you are looking for a rich taste, aroma, and crema, I can recommend this coffee very highly. If brewed right, this coffee will have very rich undertones, without bitterness, and with a hint of chocolate. I have tried Illy as well, and while do I like the Illy, I prefer this Lavazza variety (the Illy is also more expensive). For those who haven't tried the Lavazza yet, I suspect that quite a few among you might like it, especially if Starbucks' taste is too harsh for you.

For a latte person like myself, this Lavazza coffee is pretty good. I've made it my morning coffee.  I have found other coffees that I liked better, but they're usually pricier. For example, illy coffee is good and all but I think the price is a bit too high, and there are other good coffees that are even more pricey. This Lavazza bag is a good size bag of coffee at a reasonable price, and the coffee tastes pretty good (if you like a less bitter coffee). The shipping is quick too, overall a good purchasing experience.

For those looking for a mild, mellow espresso, this is a good one. No after taste so not much sweetener needed. My wife - not a coffee drinker - is now drinking it and has not tasted another one that she liked.
When it comes to coffee beans, one can't simply go past Lavazza.But I love my mid strength smooth.This is ideal.

Lavazza Super Crema has lots of robust flavor.  I use the whole bean version on my Jura Capresso expresso machine and the coffee comes out perfect all the time with a beautiful layer of crema on top. The beans are not oily which is a must for expresso machines.  Absolutely love Lavazza Super Crema Espresso whole bean coffee!

I had read lots of reviews on the BEST coffee for my superautomatic espresso machine and this blend kept popping everywhere.  I have tried many other espresso beans, and this was the best.  Great smooth flavor and the best crema. And the beans aren't too oily, so they don't clog the grinder.  I go through the beans so quickly that I'm glad it's available in this larger bag.  Thanks Lavazza, I'll be buying this blend for life.

column9: They aren't kidding when they call it "super crema"
column10: This roast of Lavazza beans is a wonderful tasting medium, which appeals to a wide variety of people. Bold flavor, but not bitter or burnt tasting. For those who like their beans especially oily, these are not, so you may not enjoy this as much as others that are. Lavazza isn't kidding with they call this their Super Crema espresso. There is a good amount on top of every shot pulled using these beans. The bag I received was very fresh, so I had no problem with a earlier expiration date, that a few others had mentioned. These are a great choice if you're going to be serving several people, and are interested in something that would appeal to everyone.

column9: Lavazza Super Crema Espresso Whole Bean Coffee
column10: Lavazza Super Crema Espresso Whole Bean Coffee is my favorite morning beverage!  I have been drinking this coffee since becoming hooked in it during a trip to Europe several years ago.  It produces a rich and flavorful cup of coffee every time.  I use it in my Miele built-in coffee maker with great reults!
I recently stopped buying beans from a specialty roaster and purchased Lavazza Super Crema and am, to my surprise, very satisfied.

I have been ordering this coffee using subscribe & save for over a year now. This coffee is simply great, full of flavor, low on the bitterness and has no bitter aftertaste. When I travel, I always curse the local coffee places because their coffee is no match to this one, but oh does it feel so good to get back home and have an excellent cappuccino again.Last week I ran out before a shipment arrived (I drank too much coffee I guess) so I had to get a replacement until my extra shipment arrived. I got a Starbucks Espresso Roast and realized how bad it is. I just got my extra shipment and had the first cup - life is good again. :-)

column9: Cup of Coffee gets such Complements
column10: We have been using this coffee for 3 years and get rave reviews from everyone. Friends come over for coffee and I'm not sure it's for us or the coffee. It tastes and smells so good

The Lavazza Super Crema does make nice crema and is a nice tasting lighter coffee. You need to go to finest grind on my Krups Espresseria to make espresso with a stronger flavor, which then has a slight harshness in the taste. Overall, not as rich or as mellow as the Peet's Mocha Java we regularly use. All in all, the Super Crema a very good, but not great cup of coffee.

I have tried other brands and also other Lavazza coffees and this is the BEST BY FAR! The Crema from these beans is amazing! My machine makes both espresso and coffee and the crema is the same on both. I have to agree with the other review that said this is the same espresso that you get in Italy, after visiting Rome last fall I was craving an espresso like I had there and this coffee DID NOT disappoint!
This is a great tasting coffee. It is medium roast which makes it a fairly mild and gives it a nice round taste.

I've really liked this coffee so far, much better than starbucks. I've used it in my french press also, and tastes fine also. The beans smell good, and look good. Look forward to when I can use them in my espresso machine again. Gonna go make some in the french press soon, since I'm not at home. ^^
We have a professional espresso machine and would never use another type of coffee. Try this and you will not be sorry.
I really enjoy my Lavazza Super Crema Espresso Caffee in the morning.This caffee is very good quality.Excellent product !!! Fast shipping

I love this Lavazza because it is consistently fantastic. It fits all the coffee drinkers in my house making everything from an espresso to an americano equally well. I use it in my Jura fully automatic, it's not too oily as some beans can be. I first started using it in Europe 5 years ago and was thrilled to learn Amazon carried it, after I returned to the States.
These beans work great in our Jura ENA 4 machine, they have a nice aroma, color and dry to the touch.  (They wont gunk up your super-auto)  I prefer these vs Illy medium beans.

This is good solid espresso.  This has become our daily default coffee.  I wouldn't say it's the best coffee i have ever had in my entire life, but it's the best one i have found so far for the home (like not counting cuban coffee shops who can't really tell me how to chase down their beans).

This coffee is very smooth, bold and the same coffee served by Magiano's Little Italy. I asked the server the name of the their coffee and he is the reason I bought Lavazza. Will I buy again, you betcha, plus my wife loves it also.
Whether brewed as a shot of espresso or a tall coffee, LavAzza has become our #1 choice in coffee.  We were introduced to LavAzza at the best Italian restaurants in Boston's North End.
