Boxer has been on Blue Buffalo for 6 months; decided to order food due to convenience and price. Not a good idea must have gotten an old bag because the food made my dog's stomach upset. Would not order dog food again from Amazon. Not sure if they sell much of this product or it just sits in a warehouse for a long time before it goes out.

column9: Great Price -- Free Shipping with Amazon Prime
column10: Our "puppy" (90lb Rhodesian Ridgeback) has been on Blue Buffalo since she came home with us from the breeder almost a year ago.  The Blue Buffalo brand is synonymous for quality in my opinion.  We will continue her on Blue Buffalo for her adult and senior years.  I have price compared buying from Amazon and the "big-name" pet store and more times than not Amazon has been less expensive.  I do have a young child so getting the 30lb bags delivered to my door (FREE with Amazon Prime) has been a real blessing.  I highly recommend this product.

column9: If You Like to Cook Healthy for Your Family.....
column10: If you want to cook healthily for your family, you'll love this KING ARTHUR ORGANIC WHITE WHOLE WHEAT FLOUR. If you're looking for a healthy, light whole wheat flour, a nutritionist recommended KING ARTHUR'S WHITE WHOLE WHEAT FLOUR. It has the nutrition of whole wheat with the consistency of white flour--so it's not too heavy and gritty. I make gravies, soups, muffins, pancakes, cookies etc.--everything with it. I'll never buy white non-nutritious flour again! It's a great way to sneak whole grains into desserts. I never feel guilty cooking with this as I know it's healthy for my family and provides necessary whole grains. It has the whole grain yellow stamp on it, which my son says means it's good for you. I love cooking with this flour and use it all the time.

I actually used this on one of my chocolate cakes and it was beautiful! It gave off a beautiful glitter shimmer. The only problem I had was that it was a little messy. It's kind of hard to get off surfaces if you get it on the table or something. It also sticks to your fingers when spreading it on your baking goods, but that's not much of a problem because you can easily wash that off. If you are afraid that it's too expensive for the small amount of glitter, I can tell you that a little glitter can go along way. :)  I will be buying more different colored glitter from this brand.

This edible glitter is BEAUTIFUL! I used this on 8 dozen cupcakes I made for my friend's Mardi Gras themed wedding reception. They sparked and glittered like you wouldn't believe! There is no shaker on this glitter, so I used a small clean paint brush to dip in and grab some, and tap my finger on the brush to sprinkle it on the frosted cupcakes. The container looks deceivingly small, mind you I said I made 8 dozen cupcakes, and did not make a dent in the glitter! You will not be dissapointed, I'll be purchasing other colors of disco dust asap.

OMG, you have to try this tea.  I bought it because I read on a website that hibiscus tea would reduce your blood pressure (whether that is true or not, I don't know, I haven't used it long enough to tell).  But whether it works for the blood pressure or not, this is a wonderful tea.  It has a beautiful color and great aroma and it is very flavorful even with out adding a sweetner.  I would recommend it highly.  The fact that it is organic and fairtrade just adds value to me.

I am not a tea drinker but when it came to providing for a little 'healthy beverage' in my life, I was steeped in decision making as to what tea.  Amazon is my favorite place to shop these days and why not. The Hampstead Hibiscus caught my eye.  For a first time user, I can pat myself on the back for choosing a winner!  Good flavor for it's easy and mild to my taste without adding sugar, the color is a rich red, the quality seems supurb. The sachets of tea brew up nicely. Very satiifying - will look to other varieties from Hampstead.

I too read about hibiscus tea and blood pressure and wanted to see if it works.  Well, two weeks later I can attest that it does work as my blood pressure dropped seven points!Also, I'm not sure if all hibiscus tea is similar in flavor but, WOW, this tea is delicious!  No honey needed!  Just brew and enjoy!  Best tea I've ever tasted!  It has a fruit-like flavor that somehow tastes semi-sweet.Finally, I really like the fact that this product is Fairtrade certified and organic.  It's nice to know when you purchase this product you are supporting the best farmers at fair wages.

Dr. Oz says if you drink 2-3 cups of hibicus tea a day the upper number of one's blood pressure will go down 7 points in a few weeks.  I don't have high blood pressure but the tea sounded good and beneficial.So I bought this tea and Ambassabor tea, both hibicus, from Amazon because they had high ratings.  I have to say they are both excellent in their own way.  This tea with the rose hips in it is more mild but still has a great flavor.  It has a little tag on each bag that says made in London.After a few weeks I checked my blood pressure and it did indeed go down, the top number.  So I guess it works.

column9: Sorry, I can't agree with these 5 Star reviews...
column10: I can't imagine my taste buds being that different than all the other reviewers here but the tea I received tasted terrible.  Maybe I got a bad batch, I don't know... what I DO know is that I could have spent $30 on something far more palatable.
The rose hips combine with the hibiscus to create one of the best-tasting teas out there. I could drink this tea every day. Highly recommended.
This is a great product! Came with a wonderful booklet also. I am very delightedwith this purchase and plan to buy thistea again.

I had already read about the benefits of Hibiscus tea, and this tea does not disappoint! It's delicious iced or hot and I like that the bags are all individually wrapped so they'll stay fresh for a long time.

column9: Marzetti Fat Free Raspberry Vinaigrette Dressing
column10: BEST FAT FREE DRESSING EVER!!!! Discovered it when I ordered the Almond Berry Chicken Salad at Wendy's!  I, too, was instantly hooked.  Love it!  Haven't been able to find the dressing in my local grocery stores. Just did an online search and found you can purchase the packets online at Amazon and at mybrands.com.  It's more expensive on Amazon. Also, you have to buy a case of 60 packets. Haven't found it bottled anywhere so far, but will continue to look cause I have to have this stuff in my fridge!!!

column9: Really Close to the Wendy's Dressing
column10: Like Kate (the other reviewer), I fell for the Wendy's chicken and berry salad and its terrific dressing.  A week or so ago I found a couple of leftover dressing envelopes in my fridge, so I used them and wanted more.I ordered some from the Amish Foods Company, through Amazon, last week,  and received my order very promptly--within a couple of days.The envelope looked different from the Wendy's package.  It's not see-through, contains 1.5 oz instead of 1.1, is not labeled "Exclusively for Wendy's" and, most unfortunately, is also not labeled "All Natural No Preservatives" which probaly accounts for the difference in taste.  The dressing looks different too (not as purple, more red).Here's a breakdown comparison of the ingredients and pertinent nutritional info (the other numbers were 0)--Wendy's stuff:  sugar, water, red raspberries (including dehydrated), corn syrup, red wine vinegar, acai juice, balsamic vinegar, shallots, salt, xanthan gum, spice, natural flavors.  KEEP REFRIGERATEDCal 50, fat 0, sodium 160mg, carb 12g, sugars 11g, protein 0The stuff you'll get:  water, high fructose corn syrup, sugar, distilled vinegar, cucmber juice, raspberries, salt, xanthan gum, onion*, bell peppers*, natural and artificial flavors, citric acid, sodium benzoate added as preservative, garlic*, spice, red #40, calcium disodium EDTA added to protect flavor, titanium dioxide, blue #1.  *dehydratedCal 50, fat 0, sodium 320mg, carb 13g, sugars 12g, protein 0Of course I prefer the Wendy's stuff because it's all natural, but I'm not part of the franchise, and neither is Amazon, apparently . . . yet.  Still, this stuff tastes pretty good--for those who like their dressing quite sweet.  I find that one envelope will cover two cereal-bowl-sized salads.

I discovered this marvelous dressing by ordering a Wendy's salad earlier this year, and since then I have had two of these salads a day - only because of the Raspberry Vinaigrette. To my surprise not only was it delicious, but I could invite my diabetic friend along for lunch and she became hooked on this dressing. Then one family member after the other tried it and fell in love with it. When we ate our lunch you could hear: "oh, yum, umm, umm, umm." We would giggle at the fact that we were in ecstasy over a salad dressing. Our hearts were nearly broken when one Wendy's after the other began to say it was the end of the season for the berry salad which had the Raspberry Vinaigrette on it, so we loaded up on extra packets where ever we could hoping we could eventually discover where to order the dressing. This is my attempt.

column9: I am in LOVE with this dressing!
column10: I had ordered a Very Berry Chicken Salad at Wendy's last year. OMG! I fell in love with it! The dressing really makes the salad! I can not get enough of them! It is more like a dessert than a salad to me. I have had a hard time trying to find the Marzetti Raspberry Vinaigrette dressing at the grocery stores. Thank you for providing the option for Half Caff.  The larger size box is perfect for home and office, I can grab as many whenever I want.  Perfect.
Heally, bovine disease free product, just the right size not to get all skanky.  Great outlet for your pet.

These treats arrived quickly, well packaged and substantially lower priced than the retail stores.  We have a rescue cat that was seriously underweight.  We had a difficult time finding any food that would appeal to her until we found these protein treats. It's important to feed a balanced diet; however, these treats added to our Rescue Cat's diet, have done wonders to improve her overall condition.

This item is wonderful... My cats LOVE IT. This product is the best quality freeze dried cat treat on the market.  Another brand, also high in quality, "we pity the kitties" is harder to find and more expensive.  Our 2 cats are on a raw food diet and this treat is in keeping with that.  These are pure meat, freeze dried, with NO additives.  We buy them by the 12 pack.  They can also be used, crumbled, as food toppers if your cat is finicky or ill and having a hard time maintaining a healthy appetite.

My cat loves these. I break off many pieces for him every night and he thinks it's the greatest thing ever. I personally like how it is a great way to give him a good amount of protein in his diet.I've bought maybe 15 2.2 oz containers of these and I plan to keep buying more.
My cats go crazy for these treats. The quality of the chicken is far superior over other freezed dried chicken treats I have tried.

My two domestic Bengals love this treat.  They scarf them right up, even when they're not hungry.  I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 only because the price is sky high for what you get.  I understand why I guess.  My son told me that I could can up real chicken and give those as treats.  I haven't canned chicken because the flavor suffers a bit, so I microwave chicken breasts after cutting them into bite-size pieces, refrigerate them and it serves the exact same purpose and is more affordable. column9: The best sauce for BBQ steaks!
column10: I love this sauce and we have it here in California, highly recommended, the best BBQ steak sauce and I also like to mix it with my Italian dressing for salads, which is good too.
I have been using it on Chicken, Pork Chops & Lamb for years.  I have moved from CA to TX so now I have to order it online...

Shipping was fast. It arrived fresh. It stood up to being placed in the slow cooker. The smokey flavor was delicate but just strong enough to convey an earthiness. I highly recommend this product for gifts for your pork eating friends.

This coffee was actually better than I expected.  Although visually it looks like some robusta has been blended with arabica, the brewed product is rather pleasant with an actual coffee taste.  No, this is not as good as one that has been decaffeinated by the Swiss water process, but I would rate this is smoother and more flavorful than the typical store bought brand in the red plastic container. In short, a serviceable product for those of us who for one reason or another are restricted in the amount of caffeine we are allowed to ingest, particularly is you catch it on sale

These come 20 to a pack, but the individual twist is about as wide as a regular drinking straw, and 2/3 as long.  If you have a very small (as in toy breed) dog, they are probably great. This is some of the best canned tuna I have ever tasted.  To me it is tasty enough without adding salt, especially if made into a tuna salad with a mayonaise dressing.  Because it is somewhat pricey, I will probably not buy it as often as I would like.

The sauce seasoned the chicken just right and gave it extra moisture just like brining. I used to brine my chicken all the time in the past but now will switch to marinating in this sauce instead.

column10: This stuff adds so much good flavor to anything you barbecue or roast without adding too many calories.I LOVE it on Chicken, vegetables, pork, and beef.

column10: We have given our cat tinkerbelle all the fancy feast appetizers. The chicken variety is his favorite and his second favorite is the sea bass and shrimp. He actually likes them all but the sea bass and shrimp is cool because it has a whole shrimp right on top. so cool. It is just a treat not a meal, at only about 35 calories each. Even though this is 2 oz it is at least half water so not enough for a full meal.

These appetizers are the bright spot in my cat's day! I don't feed them to her every day. About twice, sometimes three times a week I give her a soft form of food like these or the Wellness packets or Whiskas Purrfectly Fish. She prefers the moist foods over the dry, but it would get extremely expensive to feed these preservative free, all natural forms of food to her all the time! I agree with the reviewer who recommended reading the labels; I am a 'label reader' and I too noticed the "Supplemental Feeding" on the appetizers. These, as well as the other wet foods, are either mixed in to a dry (also all natural preservative free) cat food, or given as a treat between meals.My spoiled rotten Princess of a  cat loves these. It's as the heading states; I almost feel guilty that I cannot feed her one of the three aforementioned forms of moist food all the time!

Great supplemental food, BUT...READ THE LABEL: "Fancy Feast Appetizers are intended for SUPPLEMENTAL FEEDING ONLY. This product may be fed daily along with a complete and balanced cat food diet."DO NOT FEED this as only food source for your cat. These DO NOT contain a very necessary ingredient, TAURINE. Feeding processed/canned or even home-cooked meats and fish to cats requires Taurine as the cooking process destroys Taurine. Lack of Taurine is known to cause eye and heart problems in cats. . Do some research on Taurine! It's in all cat food, by law. I don't know how Fancy Feast got away with omitting it. They assume all cat owners read labels....so not true. . column9: Salsa of the Month was Great!
column10: I just received The Salsa of the Month Club package and everything was great!  I was excited to try two new salsas from different specialty companies that I would've never been able to try.  They arrived in a sturdy box with foam packing peanuts.  I admit that I was a little nervous that they wouldn't arrive safely, but the glass jars were completely fine.  They were even accompanied by a newsletter giving some background about the salsas and the companies who made them.  They both looked so good, it was hard to decide which one to open first!  My wife and I decided to open the Pink's Mild Salsa from Pennsylvania to accompany our fajitas that we were making for dinner.  It was bold, fresh and made with minimal ingredients and also contained no allergens.  Medically, my wife has to follow a Gluten Free diet, so we are always concerned with allergens and trying to eat foods closer to nature.  A few days later we opened the second salsa (after scraping the first jar dry) and were equally impressed!  The second jar was a Picante Salsa from Hillside Orchard farms in Georgia and was very flavorful and had some visibly large cilantro pieces (my favorite), but was not as chunky as the other one.  This one was great to pour over tacos, as it had more of a sauce consistency, but it was a little harder to pick up with a chip.  Overall, I was very satisfied and I'm looking forward to next month's salsas!  This was the perfect gift for us and would highly recommend the Salsa of the Month Club!

the other reviewer is 100% on the nose. From the second I opened the box. The smell was awful. It didn't even get to the bowl. I grabbed some and ate it....bad idea. Quickly opened a box of cocoa pebbles.

i love this butter. it's better than regular butter and makes eggs or anything else taste great. Plus it's organic with higher levels of Conjugated Linoleic Acid (CLA). A must in every home, i think

Got about 5 boxes of this stuff: 2 from Amazon, and the rest from the local Home Depot as they are cheaper. (sometimes it pays to check local store before, not after Amazon...)Got them in the ground close to the roots of my 60 Green Giant Arborvitae this spring. They grew very well the whole summer (and we had a drought and we didn't really water them). Also, the grass around the spikes got so denser and greener, I am thinking about grinding this stuff and spread it in my whole yard :)Ah, don't follow the instructions to get it in the ground: the spike will crack or brake if you hammer it directly (they include a plastic thingamagic but it is pretty useless). Instead use a 1x2 wooden spike, or a pry bar, hammer one of these and then insert the fertilizer spike in the hole. I drew a line on the 1x2 to give me the proper depth, and hammered it in. 60 of these puppies went in without a hitch (other than having to change the wooden spike a couple of times - hey there is so much beating one can take).The problem is having to buy 5 more boxes in the fall and start it all over again... It never ends...

column9: No need for a professional when you have these spikes.
column10: Easy to install and results seen in 2-3 weeks (with rain). No need for a professional when you have these spikes.
This product is great on ALL EVERGREENS, in my opinion, the best by far !!!

I hammered a bunch of these spikes, about a yard apart (follow directions) around a magnolia I've got going, in poor, rocky washed out dirt.  Won't know till next year how well they work, but I have been using MG products for over 40yrs, potting soil, everything, and found it to be better than Scott's or anything else I've tried, and I've tried a bunch.  You can't go wrong with Miracle Gro.

Just put in to try to give a fall boost for SPRING GROWTH. Some crappy soil needs a boost, so trying to help out a little now, in the MN Fall...***Still not sure - the grass is very happy where the spike went in the ground - lots of new growth on the pines - and others, but is that becuase of the extremely wet spring thus far in MN??  Didn't hurt - I know that for sure!fyi, I used a 2x2 stake and pounded it into the ground to create a hole first, then dropped the spike into that. Otherwise, the spike gets pulverized trying to drive it in by itself, with that silly little plastic cap on it.

My dog is a finicky eater and in the stores when I bought the packets that come 4 flavors to a box, my dog loved the chicken and the turkey but none of the other flavors so buying just one box full of the flavor he liked seemed perfect. However, I had not fully read the ingredients before making the purchase. The good part is that it is all meat with no grains and my dog seems to have an allergy to many things which makes him finicky. BUT it has onion powder and garlic powder. Now these may make it taste better and the dog seems to enjoy but it also causes damage to his already weakened liver. Had I read the ingredients fully before even as finicky eater I would not have purchased because I know onion in any form is very dangerous to little dogs. column9: my dogs like it, high quality dog food

I give them high quality canned food for dinner & breakfast; EVO Dog 95% Meat Venison Canned Dog Food or the fish one, and this is their lunch. column9: A saving grace for Green Mountain Coffee...
column10: When we received our Keurig Elite for Christmas, we were so excited to break open the sample pack of pods to try out different blends and flavors.  Of the 12 pods we had in the box, four were Green Mountain Coffee brand.  I'd never tried anything from this company before, but from what I had researched online, they have the largest range of Keurig pods and have even bought out competitors to produce coffee under their brand names as well.Unfortunately, I was immediately disappointed by the quality of the coffee.  We tried their Dark Magic, Decaf and Breakfast Blend and all were underwhelming, to say the least.  I was almost completely set on writing off Green Mountain altogther.We had one GM pod left and being of the mindset of waste-not-want-not, I figured I'd give it one last go around before forgetting about them completely.  And I'm glad I did.The Nantucket Blend is a perfectly pleasing cup of coffee.  It is nice and flavorful without being thick and pungent (unlike some of the other GM blends we tried).  I added some flavored creamer to it and it almost measures up to our go-to Caribou Blend pods.  Almost.  All in all, this is a very standard cup of coffee which, while it isn't anything new or exciting, is very pleasing and definitely one of the better Keurig options we've been able to test out.  When we run out of all the pods we've accumulated, I'll probably pick up a box of these as well.Now that I know Green Mountain isn't completely disappointing I'll definitely be open to trying a few more of their coffees (with our promotion for getting the bewer we ordered Green Mountain Coffee Golden French Toast,  K-Cup Portion Pack for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, 24-Count to try as well) and see how it goes from there.If you're looking for a go-to choice, this is your cup!

column9: Delicious medium-roast blend with complex tones
column10: Length:: 1:30 MinsThe name belies an intoxicating medium-roast blend that fuses flavors from Central America, Indonesia and East Africa. The blend proved a winner, and the name stuck."I drink Nantucket Blend black, using Keurig's small mug (7.25 oz) setting. My wife, who will often add creamer to darker roasts, also enjoys this blend black.In summary, this medium-roast blend is a new favorite in our house. column9: My favorite coffee K-cup so far
column10: I first tried this brand and blend as part of a k-cup sampler pack. I was immediately in love with this k-cup! It's my very favorite so far. My personal preference for coffee is a nice bodied medium roast, and this more than fits the bill. It has the smoothest taste of the 6 or 7 medium roasts/breakfast blends that I have tried so far. If you like high octane, this is not going to be your favorite k-cup, but you would certainly enjoy it as a nice change of pace every now and then. My benchmark for a good k-cup is that I can use the large (9oz) setting on my Keurig and still get a cup of real coffee, not coffee flavored water. This passes the test with flying colors. If I need a kick in the pants to get out the door in the morning, I drop down to the 7oz setting for a slightly stronger brew. I like the fact that the taste remains smooth, even if I make it a little stronger. I give this k-cup an A+!

column9: Too Weak for Me; Turns White After Adding Cream
column10: I've had to hunt far and wide to find the right K-cups for me.  Generally, I like coffee people donut shop, and that had been my go to coffee for a while. If I use two pods, this is a decent, but weaker, coffee for me to use in my travel cup for the ride into work.  Otherwise, it is much too weak.  I was very surprised that the first time I brewed some and poured in half and half, the coffee turned very light brown.  It was almost white.  I will get through this package, but I will not buy again.  It's not cost effective for me to use two pods to be satisfied.  Any other suggestions?

column9: Delicious medium-roast blend with complex tones
column10: Length:: 1:30 MinsDelicious medium-roast blend with complex tones (5 stars)The name belies an intoxicating medium-roast blend that fuses flavors from Central America, Indonesia and East Africa. The Nantucket Blend is deliciously complex - a mélange of four coffees from three continents - opening with the aroma of berries, spice and wine and soft floral undertones and finishing smoky and sweet with a touch of French Roast.According to the Green Mountain Coffee website, the blend's origin dates back more than 20 years ago, "created at the request of a loyal customer who lived on Nantucket Island. The blend proved a winner, and the name stuck."I drink Nantucket Blend black, using Keurig's small mug (7.25 oz) setting. My wife, who will often add creamer to darker roasts, also enjoys this blend black.In summary, this medium-roast blend is a new favorite in our house. We first purchased Nantucket Blend during an Amazon sale for about 55 cents per Keurig cup. Regular price is about 66 cents, 15 cents higher per cup than other brands. Is it worth the additional price? Yes, but keep an eye out for sales.Added bonuses:Nantucket Blend is certified kosher by the Orthodox Union.Green Mountain Coffee is Fair Trade Certified.Green Mountain Coffee is organic.Rating: Five stars.BTW: Here's my recent K-cup coffee reviews for Amazon:5 stars: Green Mountain Coffee Nantucket Blend5 stars: Coffee People Donut Shop Medium Roast5 stars: Van Houtte Chocolate Raspberry Truffle4 stars: Green Mountain Coffee Lake & Lodge Blend4 stars: Green Mountain Coffee Vermont Country Blend4 stars: Green Mountain Coffee Wild Mountain Blueberry4 stars: Tully's Coffee Kona Blend4 stars: Green Mountain Coffee Dark Magic3 stars: Green Mountain Coffee Breakfast Blend3 stars: Green Mountain Coffee Fair Trade Gingerbread

column9: It's Hard to Do Better than Wellness
column10: Wellness is among the best cat foods out there.  It is grain-free and it has ingredients of high quality. There are no meat by-products.  My only caveat is that Wellness' products with fish are not so good.  Quite frankly, cats don't eat fish in the wild, so their digestive systems are not designed for consumption of fish.  That being said, this is a fantastic specific product.  The meat is fresh, and I know my cat loves it.  I adopted my cat (he is five), and within weeks his coat was softer, the colors more vivid and I began seeing markings and colors I never saw before.On another note, I can't help but take a dig at one of the worst, if not THE worst, foods out there...Science Diet.  Take a read on the ingredients.  In doing so, you will the natural, very high grade, pure ingredients of Wellness contrasted with the low grade, artificial, even mysterious ingredients of Science Diet food.  Hill's chooses the name "Science Diet" to lend it credibility that it just doesn't have.  Finally, cats can't digest grains and soy.  Hill's food is riddled with that stuff.  Bottom line:  stay WITH Wellness; stay AWAY from Science Diet.

realy good cand if you are a sour lover.tags are cool good soury bursting exiting likeing war heads mega mix

I am on a course of chemotherapy; and I am therefore not allowed to drink regular coffee because it has caffeine. I tried Nescafe Taster's Choice decaf coffee and I was very much in love!This coffee can be made in any coffee pot or coffee maker. The coffee is consistently tasteful.You probably should refrigerate the container after you open it; but I have left it outside on my kitchen countertop and the coffee I make with this still tastes fine. If you're lucky enough to catch a great sale on this terrific decaffeinated coffee I would suggest that you stock up. You can even put the unused containers in your freezer for up to several months, maybe even a year. It will stay fresh and taste every bit as good after you let it defrost.All in all, Nescafe Taster's Choice is an excellent decaffeinated coffee and it remains extremely popular. Buy some and try it today--you won't be disappointed!

I love Nescafe from Taster's choice, I buy it all the time, both regular and decaf. I love buying it from Amazon.com because I get it same as at the store but cheaper and delivered home with free shipping.

Hey, I don't buy instant coffee because I'm expecting a flavorful delight.  I buy it 'cause I want something hot and coffee-tasting that I can throw some splenda and milk into.  This does the trick. If I want coffee that tastes of cream and vanilla, I can pour in the right flavored mix and get a decent result.This stuff tastes fine, prepares easily, doesn't leave grounds, and stores compactly and forever.  Most days, that's all I want.

column9: New Decaf House Blend quite different from old Decaffeinated Blend
column10: In an earlier version of this review I gave this product only 1 star.  I have now changed my mind and I now give it 4 stars.  What I originally said was:"This is a warning to those who, in the past, greatly enjoyed the DECAFFINATED BLEND.  Taster's Choice switched to a new blend, called DECAF HOUSE BLEND.  Yesterday I finished the container containing my DECAFFINATED BLEND (whose aroma and taste I had greatly enjoyed) and opened the new container of DECAR HOUSE BLEND.  I noticed immediately that the smell was very poor.  It has an unpleasant, burnt smell.  It smells also a bit like chocolate mixed with earth.  Then I noticed that it has more of a chocolate taste than a coffee taste!  Gone the coffee flavor and smell I used to enjoy.  It was at that point that I pulled my old container out of the trash and then noticed that the BLEND has CHANGED from DECAFFINATED to DECAF HOUSE.  What a disappointment!"Why have I changed my mind and now give it 4 stars?  Well, I noticed that, over time, the smell and flavor was improving!  I figured that the surrounding moisture in the air must be altering the aroma and taste, so I poured the contents out, spread them and let them sit for an hour.  What an improvement!  Also, during the time of my disappointment, I tried Trader Joe's 100% Columbian Instant Decaf Coffee and it was terrible!  No taste or aroma at all!  So then I tried Sanka's Naturally Decaffeinated Instant Coffee and, while better than Trader Joe's, it is very inferior to Taster's Choice.  So I now recommend Taster's Choice but, in my opinion, you have to first let the granules "breathe" in order to eliminate that initial unpleasant, burnt, earth-like odor.

column9: Good enough to serve to company!
column10: If you look forward to kicking back and the end of the day with a soothing cup of hot coffee, but dread the jolt of another dose of caffeine to set your nerves on edge, Nescafe Taster's Choice Instant Decaf is for you!You've probably already tried other decaf coffees and gave them up in disgust because of the weak flavor and strange bitter aftertaste. Taster's Choice Decaffeinated Coffee is so good that you'll never even know that you're drinking decaf -- it's just that good!Once you try Taster's Choice, you'll never want to be without it!

column9: Great product at a great price
column10: I love Nescafe Taster's Choice coffee.  I had been using the Gourmet Roast, but when my blood pressure became slightly elevated, I switched to the Decaf.  It is delicious, and my blood pressure is now behaving.  I love being able to buy this product for such a fair price.
I tried every instant coffee on the market in the last thirty years and you cannot beat the smell, flavor and taste of Taster's Choice Instant Decaf Coffee.
This is a great tasting, smooth instant decaf coffee. You can decide how strong to make it by how much you add. Have a cup every night before bed!

I've been drinking coffee for a little over 50 years. I started too young with the strong, black kind. No cream or sugar, just super straight! Lots of it, every day, daylight to dark. I built up such an immunity to the caffeine no way it kept me awake. Didn't give me any extra energy either. What it did do was help raise my blood pressure! So, along comes Taster's Choice. It's instant, oh God, not brewed, not dripped, not steamed, it's instant. That can't be good now can it? On top of that it's {{{shudder}}} DECAF! I've had to give up so much. Smoking, refined sugar, white flour, salt! It isn't fair that I now have to settle for Instant Coffee and Decaf to boot. **sigh** I begrudgingly fixed a cup, followed the directions. I looked at it for a bit before that first sip. I finally put it to my lips and *slurp*. Hmmm, not too bad, but then it was still pretty hot so I waited again and then took a gulp. I waited for the gag reflex to set in. It didn't happen. Hmmm again. As it turns out, it was pretty darn good. I have to be fair, it's darn good and I can easily live with it. It's well worth the price (compare the same in the stores, weight etc. and all) I just may actually live longer as a result and as Martha says "That's a good thing".

I find that caffeine bothers me so I drink de-caffeinated coffee. I prefer Taster's Choice and have used theirproduct for many years. Coffee is expensive and the brand I use, Taster's Choice, I rarely see on sale. Amazon had athree-pack offered online and I found the price to be better than I see offered locally in stores. Plus having aback up supply, I don't have to worry about running out for quite awhile.
Can't get it in any grocery store nearby, so this is a lifesaver for me.

I bought this coffee online because I had no time for shopping around in different food stores supermarkets or stores like Costco, where I buy regular Taster's Choice Coffee but which does not have decaf coffee of that brand. Hopefully,  I didn't loose much on this purchase.

Taster's Choice regular is the best instant coffee and now the only one I buy.  Not surprisingly, the Decaf version is the best on the market too.  Actually, I could be fooled into thinking it is the regular version at times.  One possible reason is that although it is Decaf, it is not caffeine free.  If it is your first cup of the day or late at night, you can feel the buzz of the available caffeine.  So, one of the reasons for the good taste may be a lower level of processing. I'm not telling you that this is the equivalent of a cup of Decaf Starbuck's or Peet's but it is cheap and convenient - just what an only coffee drinker in the family needs.

Taster's Choice Decaf has ruined me for drinking coffee almost anywhere else...I do all sorts of things to it also; add cappachino, creamers, make all sorts of fun things.  Chill it, etc.  It is a great coffee.

I've been drinking this for YEARS, and it is the BEST I've ever found in decaf coffee. If you don't want the MESS of coffeemaker coffee and no caffeine, this is the one!! I highly recommend it!! Glad it is available online, as it is always sold out at the grocery store!

Taster s Choice decaf coffee is the best decaf coffee around. Unfortunately its not available in my area. when I found out that Amazon sells it I immediately got on line to buy it, and Im glad that I could find it here. Amazon sells everything why would I go anywhere else? thank you Amazon.

column9: Sure It's Not the Best, but I Still Love Decaf Nescafe
column10: Though Nescafe has been on the fringe of my coffee radar since youth, I never gave it much thought until my first trip to India several years back.  The average coffee drinker is crazy for instant Nescafe, and boy do they make it strong and milky.When I switched to decaf (like 99% of the time), I was saddened at the loss of one of my favorite coffees.  I'd never seen Nescafe in decaf, but admittedly I'd never looked.On a recent trip to London, I happened upon instant decaf Nescafe and felt like an explorer stumbling upon the fortune they unknowingly sought.  As soon as I returned State side I found my tasty treat on Amazon and placed the order.I won't convince coffee connoisseurs that this coffee is the best, but it is pleasing both to my palette and my sensibilities...I'll always dream of India when I sip my Nescafe.

i bought this becuase i liked the nescafé packets of instant coffee that i got in my hotel room the last time i was in the dominican republic and i'll admit, i don't like coffee. but when i tried this stuff from dominican i was like omg this is a party in my mouth and i'm drinking it black!!! so i bought this nescafé canister hoping it would be the same. well it wasn't. this stuff has nothing to recommend it. it's worse than most coffees i've tried.

column9: bad taste when used as an instant coffee
column10: I bought this coffee based on the superb reviews it received at amazon. I wanted instant decaf coffee. This one tastes very bad. This is because the roast intensity of the coffee is between light and medium, so the coffee looks brown (rather than dark). This information is on the canister itself but not in amazon's online description. It dissolves instantly but tastes like wood. This is some of the worst Coffee I've tasted.  It doesn't desolve well, and is just plain gross.  Maybe it tastes OK in a coffee maker, but definitely not a good instant coffee.I usually buy Maxwell house, and it is SO much better than this.

I don't believe I've ever used apple cider vinegar in food before, but it's great for hair! I mixed the vinegar with water and a bit of tea tree oil and spritz it on my hair as conditioner.  Works wonders for dry itchy scalp.  I definitely recommend using it this way.  Give it a try!
This product isn't just good in deviled eggs it's also good for you're health. It's great for head aces and high blood pressure.

column9: Guar gum for the gluten intolerant stomach

column9: Fabulous Slightly Spicy Flavor from 2 Natural Salts
column10: I fell in love with this Coarse grain salt after a trip to Hawaii this year. I switched to Sea Salt for everyday use a couple of years ago but continued to use Lawry's Seasoned Salt for a bit of punch. This is the only salt I use at the table now.Its a combination of Alae'a and Rock Salt with a soft peachy orange color to it. The coarse grain adds a bit of crunch.I was thrilled to find it listed with Amazon at an affordable combined price for 3.

The Jelly Belly people actually put real licorice in these jelly beans. There is usually only one of the licorice beans in a bag of assorted beans, so if you love licorice, you can buy them solo. These are authentic tasting and really good. You can't beat Jelly Belly for flavor.

column9: This is an amazing Jelly Bean
column10: I have met the creator/inventor of the Jelly Belly and I can report with full confidence, that this is one tasty Licorice Jelly Bean.  A Jelly Belly is smaller than Jelly Beans and that is why Ronald Reagan liked them so much.  My personal favorite flavor is Licorice.  5 STARS!

These jelly beans were very unusual when they showed up.  They came in a package without a jelly belly logo, the jelly beans themselves had no jelly belly logo, and I don't really know if they were actually jelly bellys.  I got them as a gift, so I didn't try any of them, but it was odd giving a gift where it didn't seem like they were anything special, like I'd bagged up some licorice jelly beans from the grocery store or something, big woop...so I was disappointed.  And because they were a gift I had no idea what they tasted like.  So were they really jelly bellys?  Who knows?  I felt silly giving them though.

Just because I sent an order of these jelly beansto my oldest son in Roswell, Georgia.  He travelsa lot and enjoys a snack while he is driving andhe loves licorice jelly beans.This would make a nice gift for any special personin your life.

My 12-month-old granddaughter absolutely loved this. All of Earth's Best foods are great. I would recommend this to all new moms and dads. I'm so glad my daughter-in-law discovered this brand and recommended we try it.
The taste was a little bland. I really like the concept of Goji and Edemame mixed, but found it a little uneventful.
great taste item i got better taste ill be back for these bcause these are the best in America!I just cant waits to nget more!

column9: Not too sweet, not too bitter
column10: Love this tea. Not like Bitter Betty Honest tea or Diabetes in a Bottle Snapple. The White Tea with Mango is my faves!

With full disclosure, I work for a non-profit partner of Tevolution. column9: A nice pick me up and throat soother!
column10: There are so many benefits to ginger that I don't know where to start!  I had a bit of a sore throat due to a lot of singing I've been doing with the band.  I opened this matcha and absorbed the spicy scent and put it into a tin to keep it fresh.  The small size fits perfect in the tin with a little wiggle room...enough to be able to get the measuring spoon in.  I had been saving this matcha for the perfect time and after a day of singing I needed to bring it out.  Not to mention the fact that I could use a bit of a pick me up.I decided to prepare this matcha hot first since I wanted to sooth my throat.  I added just a pinch of sugar and a generous helping of honey (I love my honey)!  I did take a sip before adding the honey just so I could get the original flavor.  This matcha is very smooth and spicy.  It is not in your face spicy, but just enough to give it a little flavor.This matcha was very soothing on my throat so I think I'm going to save this one for next week when I have to sing again.  Sorry friends, no sharing of this one!Red Leaf Tea mentions this for treating motion sickness when suffering from an unsettling stomach among other things so it's definitely useful for everyday use.  Think I might have to save a bit for my hubby to try. Here is how I ordered my Ginger Matcha from Red Leaf Tea:Size: SmallQuality: Classic Starter GradeFlavor: DelicateStorage: Air tight refill flat pouch - would definitely recommend purchasing a tin for your matcha to keep it fresh.  I did not order one this time since I already had a tin.To get your own tasty Ginger Matcha from Red Leaf Tea - GO HERE NOW!!!![...]A sore throat soother!

Seasons Tall Pink Salmon, 14.75-Ounces (Pack of 12)Flavorful but mild tasting firm chunks of salmon, no additives other than salt. Superior to national brands because of taste, texture, ratio of fish to broth (almost none) and cost per serving. Great price on Amazon with a clearance special but even retail would have been a good value.

The other reviewer didnt like the bones and skin.... well that's why you eat Salmon - calcium and fish oil.  If you skip the skin and bones you might just as well buy tuna.  Not the lowest price, but almost - with free shipping

I make salmon cakes for my family on a regular basis and thought I'd try a new salmon "brand".  The result was a very flavorful pattie with excellent light flavor-not overtly fishy or oily.  I am picky about canned fish, and, this being the first time I've tried this brand, was very pleased. Very little bone and skin, by the way...
The meat was tasty enough, but having to sift through it to remove skin and bones was obnoxious.  I won't be purchasing this again, simply because it's inconvenient.

I made the mistake of opening one of these right after they arrived following several hours inside a delivery van in 90º heat. It was a gooey mess, but tasted OK.One thing that puts me off bars of this type in the seeming inevitability of "stale peanut" taste. I got none of that  from Planters Big Nut Bars, Double Peanut even though the "Best when used by" date was less than a month away. I'm not a big fan of candy bars or granola bars in general; my snack food temptations are salty: almonds, spanish peanuts, and various chips. However, I would probably  choose Planters Big Nut Bars, Double Peanut if I found it in a vending machine filled with less-healthy alternatives.As peanuts are the first ingredient and peanut butter is the fourth, it's probably safe to assume that most of the 13 grams of fat is derived from nuts. Palm kernel oil and coconut are probably the source of the saturated fat. There are also 22 grams of carbs, 12 from sugars.Having one of these a day as a snack or even quick meal substitute would be OK, but the low melting point of the peanut butter makes it impractical to carry in your pocket, your car, and maybe even in a backpack.

First off, I'm not the biggest peanut fan in the world. I like peanut butter, but peanuts themselves don't do a lot for me.  I usually won't eat brownies or blondies if they have peanuts in them and although I can eat them by themselves, I generally don't.Now, having said that, I've done the 'bar' thing to death.  I did the weight watchers bars (which are good and three of them make one snack), done the south beach bars. Tried about a dozen different kinds, all in an effort to watch my calories, fulfill my hunger and do so with something that tastes good.These peanut bars were terrific.  The bar itself is well put together. I know some people found their bars sticky inside the wrapper, but I did not.  What I found was a delicious snack with 7g of protein (and yes, there's a fair amount of calories here too) that was plentiful. Essentially, one bar became breakfast and I enjoyed it thoroughly despite the peanuts.  Not only will I eat the rest of the box, I'm ready to order more.If you like peanuts, you'll love this bar. If you, like me, are only passable on peanuts, you'll probably like it too. If you hate peanuts, well, you're probably not reading this review.Let me know by comment your thoughts!

If you're a lover of things peanuty than this snack is perfect for you - it's almost entirely peanuts.  It says 'peanut granola bar' on the package but there really is minimal amounts of granola - after taking a bite I was like 'there's granola in here?'  You can't really taste it and can hardly see it.  I would say if you're looking for a healthy granola snack than you might want to look else-where, but for a great-tasting peanut snack this is perfect - just the right size to satisfy a peanut craving.

column9: a satisfying snack for peanut lovers!
column10: Alright, first, I saw it said BIG on the box, but I really didn't believe them, but yes, it is about 30% bigger than most granola bars, so that was a nice surprise.  Now if it tastes good we're all set I thought....well, not to worry, Planters knows peanuts and this bar is full of them in a nice chewy bar that is a perfect balance between sweet and salty.  On the bottom of the bar is a peanut butter coating.  Delicious!  These bars come in at 220 calories and pack in 7g of protein.  I would definitely buy them and would recommend them to people that love chewy granola-type bars.  I think these would be perfect for putting in your pack for biking, hiking or purse when you need a little something.  Excellent bar!

column9: Pretty Good Tasting But Too High in Calories, Fat and Carbs For Me To Buy!
column10: Let me start off by saying that I am not a big fan of granola bars but I enjoyed the big nut taste and peanut butter flavor in the Planters Big Nut Bar. On a taste basis alone, I'd give this product a 4-star rating. The only negative I had is that after eating it I was left with a quite dry taste in my mouth and had to drink a lot of water to get rid of it. If I wasn't a person who is trying to carefully watch my intake of calories, fat and carbs I'd be looking to eat Planters Big Nut Bar on a regular basis when I wanted a good tasting, high protein snack. However, given that each 1.62 oz. bar contains 220 calories (110 from fat), 13 grams total fat and 22 grams of carbs, I'd only give a 2-star rating to the nutritional qualities of this product; thus, resulting in my overall rating of 3 stars. While I liked the taste of the Big Nut Bar, the product's amount of calories, fat and carbs will prevent me from being a buyer on anything more than a very occasional basis. However, if you are not carefully watching these nutritional factors and you want a good tasting, high protein snack bar, than I think you will find that the Big Nut Bar will satisfy your needs.

column9: Very tasty!  Keep 'em in the fridge on hot days though!
column10: These are very yummy peanut bars.  Not the most nutritious thing I've ever eaten but I do love anything peanut.My only complaint is that the peanut "glaze" on the bottom of the bar melts all over your hands if it's warm....best to keep these in the refrigerator.

I'm a big fan of sweet nut bars like the Odwalla Sweet & Salty Almond Bars and the Nature Valley Sweet & Salty Nut Granola Bars.  On flavor and consistency, this bar falls somewhere in between those two-- it's not quite as sweet as the Nature Valley, but definitely sweeter than the somewhat bland Odwalla.  It has a perfect mixture of crunch and stickiness that comes from the caramel-like sugary glue that holds the peanuts and oats together.  If you're a fan of the Odwalla or the Nature Valley Sweet nut bars, give these Planters bars a try.  Bonus--the name is fun to say too.

I opened my Big Nut Bar to see what appeared to be a rice krispies treat coated at the bottom with peanut butter.After taking my first bite, I realized that the texture was far chewier then a rice krispies. This wasn't surprising, as dried peanuts are a bit tougher then rice krispies.All in all, I thought that the peanut bar was pretty tasty. However, it was a little to chewy for my taste. This should be avoided by all people who wear dentures, as one bite may take your teeth right off.

When I received these Planters Big Nut Bars, I had just brewed a strong pot of coffee and it happened to be the time that my four kids usually have their afternoon snack.  Overall, we thought this was a great snack.  My two daughters, who each love to eat peanut butter and jelly sandwiches, said:13-year-old daughter: "Ummm, this is good!"10-year-old daughter: "Really, really good!  Tastes just like peanut butter with a ton of nuts."My two sons, who don't usually opt for the PBJ sandwiches but do like to have granola bars for snacks said:14-year-old son:  "It's really peanut-buttery.  It's okay." Then he ate it all.8-year-old son:  "I kind of like it.  I don't love it, but it's pretty tasty."  He finished his, too.  The bars are blocks of peanuts with a soft layer of peanut butter on the bottom.  They taste great with a cup of coffee or a glass of milk. They have no trans fat, 7 grams of protein, 3 grams of fiber and 220 calories, so I felt like I was giving my kids (all of normal weight, active) a filling and healthy afternoon snack that would hold them over until dinner.

column9: Pretty tasty even if you're not a granola fan
column10: Because I'm always looking for ways to get my son to eat more protein, I thought I'd give the Planters Big Nutty Bars a try.  I'm not a fan of granola OR peanuts but I thought these were actually pretty tasty!  They're not dry like some granola bars are (this doesn't mean they won't make you thirsty).  They reminded me more of a candy bar, maybe because of the layer of peanut butter on the bottom.  I kept the wrapper on while eating it (rolling it down as needed), avoiding any sticky hands or mess.  I'd recommend this as a filling snack that's easy to keep in your purse or backpack.  It didn't earn 5 stars because though it's made of whole grain oats, it also has a bunch of  oils and fructose (which is probably why it actually tastes good).

If you like peanut butter, and chewy-yet-firm, sweet candy bars, you'll probably love these.  Although the taste and texture remind me of a candy bar, this is actually a much more healthy snack.  The first ingredient is peanuts, so you get 7 grams of protein and 3 grams of fiber.  The total sugar count is a reasonable 12 grams--less than half what you will find in the most popular peanut/chocolate candy bars.  To me, this means I'll get a longer lasting boost of energy and be able to satisfy my sweet tooth without having too much sugar.In summary, love the taste, and think these are a great balance of sweetness and nutrition.

The most important thing to know about these bars is that they are filling.  They could probably replace a meal for hungry eaters.  I should also add that they are delicious--a nice blend of sweet and salty.  Think a Pay Day dipped in peanut butter and you are on the right track. Make no mistake, these are pure junk food, but they do provide a nice boost of energy.  Another convenient surprise is that they do not melt in the summer heat.  These bars are the perfect in the car, on the go, or at the beach hunger catch-all.

These bars are actually pretty good. They have a layer of big peanut chunks and rice, and then a bottom layer of a peanut-butter-like substance.Not only are they fairly tasty, I grabbed one for a quick breakfast and it filled me up more than a bar usually would.My only complaint is that they are a bit sweeter than I would prefer. Otherwise, I was pleasantly surprised.

column9: Planters Big Nut Bar - Very good and filling
column10: 46 grams, 220 calories, and 110 fat calories. The bar is a mix of peanuts, rice, and granola on a layer of peanut butter. I kept the bar in my shirt pocket for about an hour before eating and it made the peanut butter melt a little and stick to the wrapper.Taste wise it was delicious. Saltier than I would have liked - 160 mg sodium. Wrapper claims it is 30% bigger, and I did feel that the bar lasted longer. It was filling and satisfying.I found it interesting that there are only 5 bars in each box. There is room for the sixth one, but why would you put only 5?Overall, I recommend the product. I feel it could have been made bit more healthful. I am sure I will enjoy the remaining bars.

I jumped at the chance to try these peanut bars because I'd tried and really liked the Planters Big Nut Triple Nut bars last month, and I was hoping I'd like these Double Peanut bars just as much.  Although they are good, they aren't as good as the Triple Nut bars.  They are not as soft, and it's much harder to chew these.  Also, there is a layer of peanut butter on the bottom of the bar, and I just found that to be a bit of overkill.They were good, better than other peanut snack bars, but my heart belongs to the Triple Nut bars.
This is a delicious and dare I say "reasonably healthy" snack containing lots of peanuts.  Highly recommended!

These bars start out sweet when you first bite into them - almost like you're having a peanut butter sandwich. But then they leave a bitter after taste. On the plus side, it's really very nutty! But that bitter after taste is the main the reason why I don't like this product. And if that matters to you, I wouldn't buy this.

Despite the fact that they are nutritionally not much better for you than some candy bars, I really enjoy the taste of the Planters Double Peanut Big Nut Bars.  A little bit salty and a little bit sweet, their flavor is similar to that of a Payday candy bar crossed with a spoonful of super-chunky (and I do mean SUPER chunky) peanut butter.My order arrived in the middle of a hot Texas afternoon, and the first bar I ate was a bit of a gooey mess.  But after a night in the pantry, the peanut butter on the bottom of the remaining bars had re-solidified, leaving them slightly sticky but firm enough to eat with my fingers.  I had my second one right before setting out on a 30 mile bike ride, and found it to be a good source of sustained energy.  I normally eat an energy bar in the middle of a ride to refuel my body, but the Planters Big Nut Bar stuck with me through my entire exercise.Comparing the Big Nut Bar to a regular sized Snickers, I noticed that the Planters product has less fat, a lot less sugar, and more protein than my favorite candy treat.  I can definitely state that I will purchase this product in the future and enjoy it whenever I feel deserving of a special guilty pleasure.

column9: Will beckon you with it's evil sweet, salty, creamy goodness. Dang it.
column10: So I got my pack of the big nut bars...I had, coincidentally, just eaten a Weight Watcher's "sweet and salty" snack bar. It was not yet dinner time. My craving had already been crunched...but there that box sat, on my car seat, taunting me......Mr Peanut smugly snickered there on that blue box amidst a background photo of a nutty bar. And as if that wasn't daunting enough, that photo depicted the bar being pulled apart to show a creamy smooth peanut butter topping...a real double-decker-o'-sin. right. there. in. my. car.Yet I countered my objections thinking how bad a sin could it be with only 12 grams of sugar? Not bad for a treat, per se. Couldn't I justify the indulgence by the fact that peanuts are a healthy, filling food, full of protein and actually the good monounsaturated fats... and there were hidden whole grains within it's creamy crunchy sweety salty nutty bits before me?I looked away."Come hither" it continued to beckon.Hating myself and my loss of self-control, I hung my head, shunned my values, tossed aside my diet, and told myself I'd allow myself just one small moment of sin...one tiny piece of rapture...a taste...but no more.I opened my lips...freshly painted with tulip shimmer lip gloss (as I had no intention of peanuts crossing them mere moments earlier.)And, alack and alas...Dang it.It was good. Soft yet with a mellow crispness from crisped rice and granola and that rich peanut heaven that so often goes hand-in-hand with sinful indulgences--just beaming it's taste throughout.I closed my eyes and shuttered in shame.I filled my mouth with all 220 calories.And I have no regrets.

These things are advertised as "chewy", but they are actually pretty stiff.They don't taste so great either.  The peanut butter on the bottom is not especially good, and the rest of it lacks flavor.The nutrition content is not much different from a Payday, which is a good combination of salty and sweet (and also softer).  Both have similar calorie totals, similar calories from fat, similar saturated fat, and similar sodium.  Both also have peanuts as the first ingredient, followed by 2 forms of sugar as the 2nd and 3rd.  The Planters bar has only a single extra gram of fiber to show for its meager dose of oats.I wonder if the only reason planters included an insignificant amount of oats is to qualify as a "granola bar" instead of "candy".  But if you check the nutrition label, there isn't much reason to choose this unsatisfying lump.

This is more like a large candy bar than a granola or health bar. It's a combination of peanuts and peanut butter and is very sweet. It tastes good and seems to be of good quality as you'd expect from Mr. Peanut. I was surprised at how messy the peanut butter bottom was--this is definitely not something you want to snack on in the car.

column4: Miz Ellen "all the letters of my real name"
column9: Not Nutty Enough For A Peanut Nut
column10: The binder ingredient in this large snack bar is crisped rice so it tastes like a "Rice Crispy Treat" with peanuts inside. The crispy rice forms the dominant texture of the bar.  An occasional peanut is not enough to give the rich meaty crunch of a handful of roast peanuts which I was expecting from the picture on the box.  The dominant flavor comes from the coating of sweet peanut butter on the bottom of the bar.  Because the sweetening is corn syrup, the bar is sweet but the flavor is not remarkable or distinctive.  Certainly the "Double Peanut" marketing implies one thing, but I find the bar disappointing and the peanut butter undercoat is messy in warm weather.However, there are worse snacks!  Each bar offers 100% of vitamin E, no cholesterol and no trans fats.  There's a reasonable amount of sodium and 7 grams of protein per bar.  A decent energy snack and a quick pick-me-up when the blood sugar is running low.

column9: Okay for a quick peanuty snack, but...
column10: If you're craving a handy peanuty snack, then this will likely suit your tastes.  However, I found it a bit too sweet for the 'salty' I was looking for.While the package highlights 7gms of protein, don't think this is 'lean' protein.  With 13gms of fat per bar, you're packing away 20% of your RDA.  I was surprised at other contents as well.Pleasantly:Sodium is 160gms (7%)Carbs 22gms (12%)Fiber 3g (12%)I expected all these numbers to be higher, so this swayed favor with me.Ultimately, I'm not keen on the inclusion of corn syrup (though not hydrogenated) as an ingredient, but was happy that most of the rest of the listed ingredients were 'natural' in that I recognized the names. However, I'd hardly call this a 'granola' bar, as is listed on the packaging.  The 'granola' element is barely noticeable between the nuts and the peanut butter.I wouldn't plan on one a day to supplement my diet, but as an occasional quick and peanuty treat, it's not bad.My 3 year-old 'picky eater' niece enjoyed it too :)

column9: If you are in the mood for peanuts...
column10: These are perfect for the peanut fan in your life - basically what you have is a ton of peanuts held together by peanut butter.  Now true they threw in a bit of granola and some fake honey like stuff to kick it up a notch - but 95% of what is in this bar is either peanuts or something made from peanuts.  Needless to say that the fat content is pretty high, but you DO get some protein in the mix.I don't know of many people who could eat more then one of these - maybe my youngest - but most people will need a full beverage because much like bar peanuts, these Big Nut bars are salty.  The good news is that they are filling.  So if you are stuck in a long meeting at work and your stomach rumbles while the lunch hour looks to be sneaking farther and farther away - one of these should do the trick.Though they probably won't be a regular buy in our household (I mean, where's the chocolate REALLY?) they are most likely something that we will pick up now and again for road trips or to keep an extra one in the desk drawer at work.***Adding to the review - apparently not ALL of the bars are salty - the first one I ate was.  A few days later on a road trip I had another one and it was far sweeter then the first.  Perhaps the batch my box came from wasn't fully mixed - either way they were good sweet or salty***

This is a very large, tasty and filling bar.  Normally, when I eat a granola bar, I eat TWO granola bars.  These are so much larger and more filling than normal granola bars that one is a complete snack by itself.  As to taste and texture, they remind me more of Rice Krispy snacks than peanut based snacks - the peanut taste is not overpowering.  They do make you thirsty though, so have something handy to drink.  Overall, a great snack - or even a small, quick meal.

Those nuts are really big, but as a trade-off, there is only 5 bars in each pack. They made out of thick layer of nuts with thin layer of peanut butter-like substance, but not as sticky as real peanut butter. The bars taste very good, but a little too sweet to my taste. My kids think they are perfect. They both beg me now to buy more of the bars.On the other hand, I am not thrilled with the list of ingredients for the bars. I think it is Ok to eat on occasion, but not as everyday snack.

column4: Megan Bostic "I am Creative Chaos. I may have...
column9: Good taste but lacks nutritional value
column10: Length:: 1:24 Mins

column9: Peanutty candy bar disguised as granola?
column10: Don't get me wrong- I like peanut butter. I like peanuts. I like granola too, but nowadays you have to read the labels to see if what you are getting is really healthy or not.  Many folks think that if the word "granola" is on something, it must be healthy for you.Out of curiosity, I compared the nutritional label on these Big Nut Bars, to that on a Reese's Peanut Butter cup:Big Nut Bars:Calories = 220Fat Calories = 110Carbs  = 22gSugars = 12gProtein = 7gPeanut Butter CupsCalories = 230fat calories = 120Carbs = 23gSugars = 20gProtein = 4gSo you will get more protein from a Big Nut Bar, and there is less sugar in it than a Reese's Peanut Butter cup, but I wouldn't go so far as to say either is healthy!Health issues aside, this bar is a conglomeration of peanut butter, peanuts granola, and what tastes like Rice Crispies. Not sure.It is messy to try and eat (you'll get peanut butter all over your fingers, etc.) but if you like those ingredients, you'll like the taste of this bar.  The picture on the front of the box matches the look of the actual bars really well.Pretty straight forward, but not going to win any health awards.

These nut bars are perfect if you want a big, filling snack. They are much more like candy than I was expecting (much like a Payday bar) but with more sweet stuff on the outside. Not the best for watching the waistline, but very yummy.

These are the second distinctly nut-flavored meal or snack bars I've ever tried, but I didn't enjoy them as much as I did the Planters Big Nut Bars, Roasted Triple Nut, 8.1-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 10) because it turned out that "Double Peanut" in this case meant peanuts and peanut butter, which I don't usually care for.  Anyway, I won't be ordering anymore because of a somewhat uncommon (and thus not specifically warning labeled about) food allergy.I'm extremely allergic to Canola Oil, also known as Rapeseed Oil, which in me produces severe hives and swellings in the throat.  Fortunately, my allergic threshold is relatively high so that small amounts usually produce no reaction.  However, caution induces me to check labels and avoid it whenever I can; labels reading "may contain one or more of the following vegetable oils:" are the bane of my existence, asking me the question, "Do I feel lucky?"Unfortunately, near the end of the ingredient list, near the end of the sub-list for granola is my old nemesis Canola Oil.  Consuming no more than a single bar per day and that not on consecutive days spared me any allergic reaction, but I will take no further chances when I am NOT obliged to write a review.

These Planters Big Nut Bars are just so-so.  They're not sweet enough to be super-yummy, and not boring enough to be just normal peanuts.  They're right in between.Personally, I prefer the sweeter taste of some of the other bars on the market such as the Nature Valley line.The size of these bars is pretty big, though, and certainly bigger than their competitors.  Too big?  I wouldn't say that.Size aside, they could have fit 5 extra bars in the packaging if they just turned them a different direction.  Odd.One complaint: the wrapping around the bars is difficult to open without: 1) tearing it into shreds, and 2) getting peanut butter all over your fingers.  I don't seem to have this problem with other bars of a similar nature.And as other reviewers have noted, these are far from being a "healthy snack"... unless your alternative is a Pop Tart.

column9: BIG On Peanuts! BIG On Taste!
column10: My family & I tried Planters Big Nut Bars for the first time.  My 15 year old daughter absolutely hates any type of granola bar and/or those so-called "health" bars - associating their products to an icky blend of what she'd imagine cat litter blended with sawdust would taste like...so I figured of any of us, she'd be the really picky one to judge Planters Big Nut Bars.  Watching her take the first bite, I literally held my breath, waiting for the inevitable "ewww" to follow.  Guess what?  Not only didn't she say "ewww", she ate a second bar immediately after the first!  She loves Planters Big Nut Bars & because of this, it's now a frequent staple on my weekly grocery list.  Personally, I love the mix of salty & sweet (one of the main reasons I still mix M & M's with popcorn at the movie theatre!).  Easily I could see parents offering this as an alternative to the less healthy candy bar as a treat or an energy boost.:)

column9: Big On Taste, Not So Much On Size
column10: I confess. Even though I've sworn off sweet treats, sometimes a craving gets the best of me.I could eat little snack cakes, cookies, some extreme-chocolate ice cream, but I choose for something a tad bit on the healthier side: Planters Big Nut Bars.Sure, they have 220 calories, 12 grams of fat, and high fructose corn syrup, but they also offer 7 grams of protein to help balance (out (somewhat) the "nasties."Something that snack cakes and other junk food I crave doesn't.And the Planters Big Nut Bars taste good - something you generally won't find is a treat that offers some nutritional value.So when the sweet tooth kicks in and I've got to satisfy it, I eat a Planters Big Nut Bar or a Planters Triple Nut Bar - so I don't have to feel as guilty when it's over.Only wish they were actually BIG as the name implies; yet only the size of your average candy bar.But they do satisfy a BIG craving so I'll deal with it.

Planter's Big Nut Bars are basically bars of peanuts, sugar, granola, and crispy rice with a layer of peanut butter on the bottom. They're very chewy and pretty good, but I can only handle half a bar at a time.These "healthy" snacks are pretty high in calories, and I sometimes found them to be too sweet. I have a serious sweet tooth, but for some reason I couldn't really take all the sugar in these bars. I don't know if it's because Planters wants me to think that this is a healthy alternative to granola bars, and so my mind was rejecting the sugary sweetness, but I definitely could not finish a full bar in one sitting.I'm kind of impartial to the Big Nut Bars; it's definitely something that I won't go out of my way to get at the grocery store, but if it's on sale I would probably pick up a box.

Taste wise, These are great. Nutrition wise, That's where this falls shorts. When I Think "Granola Bar" Which these are falsely labeled as, I think of something that isn't an almost exact equivalent of a 2 pack of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups, which nutrition wise, these are, give or take 10 calories.It's pretty much just a bar of peanuts with Corn Syrup and peanut butter. I'd say Stick with Planters Original Peanut Bar or Snickers Munch or just plain Peanut Brittle. Those pack more of a great Crunch.Tasty Treat, which is why it gets 3 stars But Labeling it as a Granola bar - False advertising.

This the best of the nut bars I've sampled.I'm a nut guy: make my own peanut butter, eat handfuls as a snack and always order Thai food with peanut sauce. I know nuts! So trust me on this. This one is gooood.While it's not rated as a nutrition bar its contents are as good as some bars that claim the title. There's a healthy dose of protein, the mono fat is higher than the other fats (which is a good thing) and the carbs are fairly high for that workout boost.Good stuff.

column9: Tasty, but high in fat and calories
column10: I really like the taste of these -- but that taste comes at the price of a bar that is very high in fat, sugar, and calories.  Each bar contains 220 calories, 110 of which come from fat, and each one also has 12 grams of sugar, which is very high for a bar this size.Also, when my husband tried these, he wasn't too keen on the taste.  When I asked for his opinion on them, he just said that they were "Meh."Bottom line?  These are tasty, but certainly should be eaten in moderation.  Since I'm a health nut, I won't be buying these again.

I like them, and so has anyone I have offered them to.I like planters, they have a good reputation. I also often eanjoy the "Nature Valley" nut bars. The Planter's bars taste very much like them, so I would buy whichever seems to be a better value at the time. I would not consider either to be a `healthy' snack, but somewhat better than most alternatives. I think they would be good to have in vending machines.They are very sweet and nutty. They also somewhat resemble Kashi `go lean' bars (that do have more protein), but somewhat easier on the teeth. But they are still pretty crunchy because of the excellent Planter's nuts. I would place them more in the realm of energy bars than in healthy snacks (i.e. low carb, low fat, organic ingredients etc.) as they do have a bit more salt, so if you are out on the trail but have plenty of water, they might be a good choice. I think they are nothing like a "Payday" bar. They are filling. They have a bit of frosting on the bottom that wa kind of melted, but still good!

column9: Very tasty, but not very healthy
column10: This is one of the better peanut bars I've tried.  The bars are quite large, filled with peanuts, and very tasty.  I tried one soon after getting the box out of the mailbox, and it was gooey since it had sat in the heat for a while.  Gooey from the heat, or eaten after storage at room temperature, they are a great snack.  One of my sons loves them and has since claimed them for himself.  The only drawback is that it's a little high in calories (220 per bar), so it's not for someone who is dieting or looking for a healthy snack.  If you're just looking for taste and love peanuts, this is a great choice.

column9: Perfect for those who go nuts over 'nuts.
column10: Planters Big Nut Bars, Double Peanut promises and delivers.  If you love peanuts and more peanuts then you'll want to pick up a box of Double Peanut bars.  A layer of peanuts sandwich with guess what????  Another layer of peanuts.  Every bite is filled with peanut goodness.  Those with allergies to legumes need not apply.  But if you're a peanut lover then by all means, go NUTS and buy some today!

I actually prefer the Triple Nut version of this bar better despite the fact that I really like peanuts.  I think it is just a little bit too much like a candy bar for me to actually want to eat it too often and when I had one in my pocket for a few hours it got really messy because the peanut butter melted and got all over the inside of the wrapper and made the bar sticky and not that attractive looking, in fact it was a hot day when these were delivered so they were already pretty messed up before I even got them.  They do taste pretty good, so if you like things sweet, like peanuts and peanut butter and don't mind that they can get kinda messy, you would like this bar.

column9: hunger satisfying sweet nut bar with big peanut taste
column10: Planters Double Peanut Chewy Granola Bar is delicious and filling.  The wrapper states that it is "30% bigger than the leading nut & granola bar" and it contains 7 grams of protein.  It also contains 220 calories, half of which are fat (6 grams), 3 grams of fiber and last, but not least, 12 grams of sugar. It is delicious in the way too sweet candy is delicious.  I eat one of these mid-mornings instead of breakfast and lunch.  It leaves a sweet pleasant aftertaste in my mouth. This is definitely not diet food, but a hunger satisfying nut bar with big peanut taste.  The bar is made in Canada, features Mr. Peanut on the wrapper and is a Kraft Foods Global, Inc.  product.

column4: Chris Swanson "I'm just this guy, you know?"
column10: If, like me, you enjoy little more than having a good set of nuts in your mouth, then you'll be quite happy with these nut bars!The bars themselves are basically peanuts stuck together with some sort of noughty binder with, and this is the fun part, a layer of peanut butter on the bottom."Death by peanuts" might be a good description.I have no complaints about these nut bars! They are very good, quite filling and reasonably priced. If you enjoy Payday candy, but always thought it needed peanut butter, you'll like these!

column9: A Salty, In-Between Meals Kinda Snack!...
column10: These bars are GREAT as a hefty snack. You want something more then a handful of chips, but it's not yet lunch or dinner time...grab a Big Nut Bar! There are TONS of peanuts in each bar, and I thought them to have a perfect amount of salt (some may think them too salty, but I love a lot of salt). I'd definitely recommend these for peanut fans, or people who eat a lot of 'snacks-on-the-go'. Planters certainly didn't skimp on the nuts...very tasty!

column4: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
column9: Nutrition & Ingredient info...Almost as tasty as Snickers!
column10: Basically a chewy granola bar, but not as sweet.  Lots of peanuts packed in and then a thin layer of peanut butter on the bottom.  Fairly healthy (for a granola bar, which I guess isn't saying that much)  High in fat due to the peanuts, but the fat from peanuts is monounsaturated.  Not a lot of ingredients I don't recognize.  I ding it for using corn syrup and "fractionated palm kernel oil."Very filling due to the peanuts.  Definitely healthier than a Snickers and almost as tasty.Amazon doesn't list nutrition info on their food items so here it is:220 calories each bar, 110 from fat, cholesterol 0, 160 mg sodiumTotal fat 13g, Sat. 3g, trans. 0, Polyunsat. 3.5, Monounsat. 6g22 g carb, 3 g fiber, 12g sugar, 7g protein100% Vitamin E, 4% iron, 2% calcium, other vitamins 0If you've found this review helpful, please let me know!
My 4 year old and I loved the nutty flavor and the peanut butter coating was yummy. This was a good size bar as well. Should be fairly satisfying as a snack.

I would never consider this a healthy option, but it tastes pretty good. I'm not a huge fan of peanuts and sugar since I prefer the peanuts and salty combination, so this snack is too sweet for me. And I should say that it's very dense and filling. I could barely finish my whole bar and finishing food is not normally a problem I have!

column9: So This is How They Killed Mr. Ed.
column10: Salty is the only word I can use to describe this bar. My husband found the taste of it to be cloyingly preserved due it tasting nothing like peanuts but for me the saltiness of it alone was enough that I had to drink 3 glasses of water to rid my mouth of a horrible dry feeling. I actually had to drink some water during eating, because I couldn't get the entire bar down.Planters' touts on the package that you're getting 7 grams of protein but the trade off is the high fat content. I wouldn't eat this more than once a week and I wouldn't give this to my kids as a healthy snack. But if they wanted to do a little brick and mortar work these'll do just fine.

FLAVORAs everyone else agrees, this is pretty tasty. It is full of delicious nutty flavor. But, it barely has a hint of granola (in my opinion). Also, it is very filling. I only ate half of the first bar I tried because I was full thanks to all the nuts. Nuts, in moderation, are a good source of good fats.NUTRITIONAL INFOThe bar is indeed big; about 30% bigger than regular granola bars. This 46 gram bar has 220 calories, no trans fats, 3 grams of saturated fats, 160 mg of sodium, 22 g of carbohydrates, 3 grams of fiber, 12 grams of sugar, 7 grams of protein, a negligible amounts of calcium and iron, 100% of you Vitamin E daily value and 10% of your daily value of Phosphorous. It has no other vitamins. It also has 3.5 grams of  polyunsaturated fats and 6 grams of monosaturated fats.All these fats are not unhealthy. As I mentioned before, nuts are a good source of healthy fats.
