But, this bar may just a be too big for a regular snack.COMPARISON WITH A SIMILAR BARA single Planters bar is 220 calories, almost as much as a Clif Bar (240 calories), but not as healthy. Why? The Planters bar has 110 calories from fat which equals to 13 grams of fat, 20% of your daily value. It also has 3 grams of saturated fats, which is not the best heart healthy choice. Whereas a Clif Bar has 7 grams of fat, 11 % of your daily value and 1.5 grams of saturated fats.Also, Clif bars are made with organic ingredients. Two of the first three ingredients of a Planters bar are: sugar and corn syrup. Doctors, nutritionists, exercise and health experts all tell you to avoid or reduce food items that have sugar and corn syrup in the first five listed ingredients.It also has artificial flavors AND more sugar (brown sugar, dextrin, fructose, evaporated cane juice, etc.). Yes, I know that Clif bars have 21 grams of sugar, but at least they are natural and organic based. Moreover, the Clif bar is full of vitamins and minerals.Further, the Clif bar is recommended for people doing high intensity sports or requiring sustained energy: hiking, rock climbing, or any other sports.  This Planters bar being advertised as a snack.BOTTOM LINEIs such a big bar truly necessary, especially for a snack? This bar makes me think of the McDonald's Super Size idea. But, bigger is not necessarily better. A snack should not be so substantial high in calorie and fat content, unless you are about to go on a 8 mile hike or you are replacing an entire meal with this bar. As a snack, it is too much. I do not recommend as a regular snack.Full nutritional info below:Nutrition Facts - 1 bar - 220 calories, 12 grams of fat, 1.5 grams of saturated fat, 0 grams of trans fat, 3.5 grams of polyunsaturated fat, 6 grams of monounsaturated fat, 0 milligrams of cholesterol, 230 milligrams of sodium, 23 grams of carbohydrates, 3 grams of fiber, 13 grams of sugar, 7 grams of protein, 2% calcium, 100% vitamin E and 10% phosphorus.)Ingredients: Peanuts, Corn Syrup, Sugar, Peanut Butter (Roasted Ground Peanuts), Crisped Rice (Rice Flour, Sugar, Malt Extract, Salt, Caramel Color, Mixed Tocopherols (to Help Protect Flavor)), Evaporated Cane Juice Invert Syrup, Whole Grain Rolled Oats, Fractionated Palm Kernel,  Oil, Granola (Whole Grain Rolled Oats, Brown Sugar, Whole Grain Rolled Wheat, Coconut, Canola Oil, Wheat Bran), Partially Defatted Peanut Flour, Salt, fructose, Contains less than 1.5% of Sodium Caseinate (From Milk) Soy Lecithin, Resistant Corn Dextrin, Natural Flavor, Mixed Tocopherols (to help protect flavor).
This granola bar is sweet and crunchy but doesn't leave me with a candy bar high and I love the peanut butter flavor.  VERY addictive!

I love peanuts, and I love peanut butter.  I was hoping these would be good, but they just weren't.  They were kind of bland and chewy.  The flavor isn't much different than eating peanuts, but the cost is a lot higher.  There is no sweetness and not much saltiness either.  If you like peanuts I recommend getting a jar of peanuts and skipping this product.

This is actually a chewy granola bar rather than the 'nut bar' (like Munch) that I thought it was.When I opened the wrapper and bit into the bar, it tasted slightly stale.  I checked the expiry date on the box - it's 16th August 2009 - less than four (4) weeks from now.There really is no good news for Planters for this one.  If the 'stale' taste is how it tastes, thumbs down.If it is stale four weeks before the expiry date, thumbs down.I don't like it.OTHER INFO:  Each bar is 220 calories (110 of those from fat), 7 grams of protein, 160 mg. sodium, 22g carbs.

The reviewer who said "It is probably a half way decent choice for an snack" is, respectfully, wrong. This stuff is FULL of junk! What's "decent" about it? That it doesn't have rat poison?Too many ingredients to list fully, but a quick review: A ton of corn syrup and other sugars, plus terrible oils. It could be a list of what to avoid from a health conscious book. Want to know what to avoid eating? Look at the ingredients on these things!That being said, if you are not health conscious and don't mind a snack once in a while that is full of unhealthy stuff, it taste pretty good. Although another downside is, like another reviewer said, it is messy. You can't just grab it and eat it on the go - you will need a cloth, if not water, to clean up the mess on your hands!

column9: nothing special, you are better off eating an apple
column10: Planters, the company, behind tin and glass boxes of peanuts, has decided to diversify their portfolio and to begin making snack bars that capitalize on their tasty nuts. Sounds ideal? Hardly.I found the taste of these nut bars awkward and preserved. One feels bloated and full (at 220 calories per bar, it's hardly surprising!) after eating one of these bars but not satisfied. The peanutbutter backing serves the purpose of underlining the flavor, but there is no flavor to speak of, and thus nothing to highlight.Planters, do everyone a favor and stick to producing peanuts. Leave the snack bars to Clif Energy Bars and other companies. And the consumer will be better off getting tastier morsels of nutrition elsewhere.

If you like peanuts, you'll absolutely love this bar!  It's full, I mean really full of peanuts.  Plus, they taste crisp and fresh, not at all soft or soggy the way they do in some peanut bars.  The taste of the bar is sweet, but not too sweet with a pleasing balance between the nut taste and the sweetener.  In addition, the bar is a generous size.  We'd buy them again!

Planters Big Double Peanut Nut Bar is a newer granola bar from a company that knows a few things about peanuts. I have been enjoying Planter's peanuts for as long as I can remember and when I heard about these granola bars, I was anxious to give them a try. With Planter's peanuts and granola, it sounded like a winning combination.Planters Big Double Peanut Nut Bar, like the name suggests, contain plenty of peanuts. Looking at these granola bars, one can clearly see the peanuts, along with added oats, brown sugar, and other ingredients. Other granola bars contain peanuts, so this is nothing new. But few come close to matching the amount of peanuts used in Planters Big Double Peanut Nut Bar. The peanut- enhanced flavor will bring joy to the taste buds of peanut lovers everywhere. This, balanced with the great taste of granola and other ingredients, make these nut bars better tasting than most competitors in the granola/breakfast bar market.These granola bars offer a nice balance of flavors. They do tend to make one thirsty, but one surprise is that each individual bar contains only a small amount of sodium. Based on the taste and the tendency to heighten thirst, I would have guessed the sodium content was much higher, but Planter's managed to keep this ingredient under control, and this is certainly good news for the health- conscious. However, some other facts about these granola bars could make them a questionable food option for certain diets and nutritional concerns. First, there are thirteen grams of fat in each bar. If you are the type who usually eats two or more bars at a time, these numbers can add up quickly. Second, there are a few less-than-desirable ingredients. The majority of the ingredients are natural, but there are some that could raise a few eyebrows. Nutritionally, however, these bars are better than most. Each serving provides seven grams of protein and one- hundred percent of your daily allowance for Vitamin E.I enjoy granola bars and I enjoy the taste of peanuts, so Planters Big Double Peanut Nut Bar is a product to which I have taken an instant liking. These bars are a little more costly than some and there are only five bars in a standard box, so they aren't likely to last very long. But they are still a product worth trying. The great taste of peanuts, peanut butter, and granola combine to make a very good- tasting snack for morning, noon, or night.

Both me and my son liked these bars very much. They have a burst of peanut flavor with every bite, because they are LOADED with peanuts. When I first received them, I thought they would be more like the peanut brittle, but I was pleasantly surprised. Now I do love the peanut brittle as well, but these were REALLY good. The crunch in this bar comes from the peanuts, not a hard candy, which makes it more like a granola bar, only very peanutty.Now I buy all kinds of breakfast and granola bars to keep as a run out the door snack, because my son is 16 yrs. old, and to try to keep him inside the house to sit down and eat something has been a job in itself. Well after he tried these, he didn't hesitate to load up his back pack with them, and run out the door. Not something he normally does with the other bars that I have bought. So now these are on my grocery list next time I go shopping. Thanks PLANTERS!

These bars were tasty, but extremely dense and heavy. I really had to chew! They are definitely filling, though, and taste pretty good. Probably a good breakfast for someone who needs fast protein and sugar.

column9: Something else to get hooked on
column10: Well, these are addictive.Darn!  I don't need to be hooked on another snack food.These are called granola bars on the box, but I wouldn't have noticed if it hadn't.  Peanuts are front and center here.  Peanuts and peanut butter.  These bars are slightly sweet, not candy bar sweet.  They're nice sized, chewy and crunchy, and delicious.They're not a health food.  There's plenty of calories packed in each one.  They're a treat.

I am not a breakfast person but this delicious peanutty bar fills the breakfast thing for me. It is delicious and also quite filling. A cup of coffee and a Planter Big Nut bar gets me off to a good start for the day. This bar also makes a nice snack for the afternoon when you crave something sweet but not too sweet.I have not tried the Triple Nut bar but that sounds even better.

column9: Double The Pleasure, Double The Fun
column10: When I received my box of PLANTERS DOUBLE PEANUT BIG NUT BARS, I immediately passed them around to my family.  Everyone, including the 4-year-old who can be picky and stubborn when she feels like it, declared these bars "super yummy!"  Made with peanuts, peanut butter, crispy rice, and rolled oats, PLANTERS DOUBLE PEANUT BIG NUT BARS contain 7 grams of protein, 3 grams of fiber, 100% of your daily allowance if vitamin E, and NO cholesterol or trans fats.PLANTERS DOUBLE PEANUT BIG NUT BARS are very tasty, with a big, slightly sweet peanuty taste.  Peanuts are the number one ingredient listed (good for you, Planters!), and these bars are chock full of peanuts.  The layer of peanut butter on the adds to the peanut punch and helps hold these soft, chewy bars together.At 220 calories per bar and full of protein, PLANTERS DOUBLE PEANUT BIG NUT BARS are a nice snack for my kids after a sporting event or a dance class.  They are individually wrapped, making them easy to throw in a purse or sport bag.  Add a bottle of water or a box of juice, and this snack makes a great energy booster and a satisfying snack after a good workout.The one drawback is that the PLANTERS DOUBLE PEANUT BIG NUT BARS box contains only FIVE bars, instead of the typical SIX found in most snack packs.  That makes the price per bar a bit more expensive than some of the other choices out there.  For that, I am deducting one star.  (Come on, Planters, you can make a six-pack, too.)  But overall, PLANTERS DOUBLE PEANUT BIG NUT BARS are HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

column4: Therabbitssing "on the rock that spews lava.."
column9: These nut bars are making me thirsty!
column10: These nutty bars are huge compared to the average granola bar.  They actually taste pretty good too. They are definitely not a healthy type bar, more like a candy alternative.  The thing is covered with a peanut butter like coating on the bottom of the length of the bar which tastes great.  There are only 5 bars in the box, so I guess the large size is supposed to offset that.  I am a little on the fence, as they do taste good, but they aren't something I would normally crave for.  I do think they should be eaten with a drink nearby as they are a little on the dry side.

column9: Not as great as they look
column10: Sure it sounds good and looks yummy on the box, but this is one mess of a "candy" bar. First of all, the peanut butter is all over the bottom (or is it the top?), so it forces you to use the wrapper or else. The flavor is a little more bland than I had expected as well. Overall, it wasn't bad, but I wouldn't rush out and buy any in the future.

column9: Don't Forget to fix the Jug of Water While You Are At It..
column10: If you choose to have this salty/sugary snack bar, which is basically a candy bar, fix yourself a jug of water, you will need it.  I love Planters peanuts, but I prefer the old fashioned peanut bar, the real old fashioned one.My question is this:  Is it a granola bar, a nut bar, a candy bar, and I'm inclined to believe with the ingredients of 13 gms of fat, which is certainly not as much as some candy bars.  Then, there is a layer of peanut butter spread on the bottom.So, I don't think I would buy these if I had a hankering to fix the sweet tooth.  For the healthy side, no;  it's too sweet, too salty.  ...Rizzo

Planters Big Nut Bars, Double Peanut, 8.1-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 10) there are a total of fifty 50 bars that is about  $.49 each 1.07 ounce bar.I liked these peanut bars, it is a salty and sweet combination that remind me of payday bar candy bars. They have a bit of nutritional value in them of protein 7 grams a bar.I give them 5 stars. I hope this helps.

When the box arrived today I had my dad try them and asked for his opinion. He LOVED them. Said they were crunchy and chewy at the same time which seemed to leave him awestruck. I ate one, too, and really enjoyed it but probably not as much as dear old dad. It was crunchy and chewy and I really loved the lower layer of peanut butter. They weren't too salty and they weren't too sweet. What they were was delicious tasting. I'm not certain how healthy these are, but if they bring such pleasure to an 88-year-old man who really gives a crap?! Maybe they should start giving these as the top BINGO prize at the Whispering Pines Old Folks Home. I highly recommend Planters Big Nut Bars and will purchase these as long as there is someone willing to eat them.

First up, no this is not a DIET bar and should not be judged as one. It is a great snack, especially if your next meal is going to be late. Everything in the bar is good; Peanuts, peanut butter and granola, a good balance. My one complaint is that it is a little messy & sticky since the peanut butter is on the bottom of the bar. Maybe if it was in the middle.But other than that, if you need a boost between meals (or if you have skipped a meal), this should keep you going till the next one.

column9: Peanut fans - this is the one to buy
column10: If you're a fan of peanut snacks and peanut bars, don't pass up the Planters Big Nut Bars. There are plenty of peanuts and peanut butter to keep you happy. I liked the triple nut variant of the Planters bars (tested in another review) but found the almonds and cashews to be overpowered by peanuts in a good way. These Double Peanut bars just capitalizes on the peanut taste and makes it even better! The bars are very large but they only come in a box of 5. I wish they'd squeeze in maybe 6-8 bars per box.Pros: Nutty taste, large servingsCons: Only 5 per box.

column9: Great tasting, but it's more of a meal than a snack...
column10: I recently got a chance to try the new(ish) Planters Big Nut Bars from Kraft Foods and I have to say that they're pretty darn good.  If you're into granola bars, these will be a little bit of a departure as you really don't get that kind of consistency.  These are also nuttier, and overall seem to be more akin to a nut-based candy bar like a Payday.As far as the pluses go, the bars have a nice balance of sweet and salty, and though the consistency doesn't scream granola bar, it's just chewy enough that it also doesn't scream peanut bar (like the various brands of peanut brittle-esqe bars you tend to find in vending machines.)  The peanut butter coating on the bottom also has a nice consistency and taste, not chalky or too sweet like peanut butter tends to get in products like this.  Also, at 46 grams, it's pretty satisfying, and I'd think it would certainly make for a decent small meal on the go if you're in a pinch.There are some drawbacks though.  Mainly the bars can get a little messy where the peanut butter is concerned, so I can imagine it would be a nightmare with kids.  The bars are also pretty high in fat, which isn't as much surprising (they are peanut based), as it is unfortunate.  At 13g of fat per bar (3g saturated), these really are in the category of meal replacement, and not snacks.  If you're looking for a healthy snack I'd stick with a more basic granola bar.

This is one big bar full of soft sweet granola and peanuts on a bed of peanut butter. My kids thought the bars were simply delectable. Not having a big sweet tooth myself, I would have preferred more salty nut and less sweet granola and peanut butter. That said, the bars were fresh tasting and everyone else seemed to think they contained plenty of nut.With 220 calories per bar and 13 grams of fat, this is obviously not a diet food. It is probably a half way decent choice for an snack; after all sometimes a celery stalk really won't do.

The package doesn't lie: these are BIG bars! They are also very dense, and as a result are very filling. They're very chewy, so if you've got jaw problems you might wanna skip these. That's the only thing I didn't like about them. That being said, they have a great peanut flavor and I enjoyed the layer of peanut butter on the bottom. I think the peanut butter makes the bar. Overall, a very tasty snack and a nice, large bar.

The taste of this product is very good.  It has that peanut buttery taste along with real peanuts for crunch.  The only thing is that it needs a bit more work.  1st of all, 220 calories!!!!  110 from fat!! Yikes.  For all you health nuts, this may not be the product for you.  2nd and most of all, you can't really eat this without getting your hands full of the peanut butter.  The bar is made up of nuts on the top with an underlayment of peanut butter on the bottom.  This means you can't eat the bar without the wrapper otherwise your fingers will melt the peanut butter and get all messy.  It would be better if the bar had the peanut butter "sandwiched" between two layers of peanuts.  Less mess and you won't need the wrapper.

column9: Very filling - must have water nearby!
column10: These bars are large - I would even use them as a meal-on-the-go type of deal because, well, they're so substantial. If you need to fill up on something and have no time for a meal, these are perfect. But HAVE WATER NEARBY. I ate mine while outside and had to run back inside to gulp down some water by the third bite. I don't know why but these really built up my thirst.

I really wanted to like these nut bars.  My mouth started watering as soon as I ordered them.  Unfortunately, the reality didn't live up to the anticipation.The first thing I wanted to know was the nutrition information, which I was unable to find anywhere online before ordering.  Each bar contains 220 calories, 13 grams of fat, and 3 grams of fiber.  For comparison, that's 5 Weight Watcher's Points(tm), where most granola bars I eat come in at 2 points.  This wasn't far out of line with my expectations, since this bar is primarily made of nuts, and a tasty snack is occasionally worth it, but it does keep it from being an every day snack for me.The taste of the bar was okay, but way too chewy, with a sliver of peanut butter spread across the bottom that adds mess without adding much to the taste.  It was less messy when eaten upside down, but my jaw still hurt by the end from working so hard to chew it.  I was also expecting the bar to be either sweet or roasted salty, but this was neither.  Unless you are a huge fan of practically raw peanuts, give this nut bar a pass.

Peanut lovers rejoice!  This is one chewy, nutty, delicious treat.  It's bigger than those granola/power/protein bars and loaded with peanuts on top of a peanut buttery/yogurty base that's sweet but not too sweet.  This yummy snack is a good source of protein - and fat.  At 220 calories, it's not for the dieter, but is tasty and satisfying.  Highly recommended.

For those that have a peanut addiction like I do - toffee covered, plain, cinnamon etc. This is the perfect snack. Twice as much as their ordinary peanut snack bars, they still could use more. The provide the right amount of runch, saltiness, and sweetness, making it one of the best treats around. If you are on a diet though you won't be happy. They simply don't make grade. High in fat and sodium they can easily send a diabetic or high blood pressure candidate over the edge. They pack a wallop though and the boys loved them in their lunch. Planters has done it again.

column9: Payday with a little something extra
column10: This product reminded me of nothing so much as a Payday bar--the candy bar that is essentially skinless peanuts embedded in a caramel core bar. The difference with this bar, and what makes it marginally a snack bar, is the addition of crisped rice to soften and texturize the chew just a bit. I found it to be tasty and satisfying, though the peanuts did not taste quite as fresh as I would have expected from a Planters-branded product. The "Big Nut Bars" name is obviously intended to appeal to young hungry men, and I'm sure it will satisfy.
If you like peanuts you will love these bars. They are thick and chunky with a touch of sweetness. My family (ranging from age 5 to 38 years old) loved these.

column9: Very tasty snack, from the peanut experts
column10: This is a very tasty snack from the peanut experts-- planters.  Only 220 calories per bar and loaded with protean.  They taste very good, I will buy again.

You'll love these.  Planters' quality that you'd expect, yet ordering them through the internet is a double-edged sword of a process; less expensive than what you'd probably pay for them in the store, BUT more than likely one or more will be (as was the case here) broken into pieces.  Not a big deal if you're going to share one, but not quite the aesthetic pleasure treat to hand out.  Still, they're sugary and peanuty and . . . well, Planters knows the nut biz!

The "big nut" bars from Planters peanuts are exactly as promised: extremely nutty. They remind me of Paydays, but without the chocolate covering and the intense sweetness.Even though I love peanuts and PB, I'd probably only buy it if it were smaller or if the nuts were honey roasted...or if they had more than one flavor. They are a little too big for a mid-morning snack, and I'd definitely alternate this product with something else on a frequent basis.

If you like salty peanuts with a hint of sweetness, you can't go wrong with this box of bars.  I quite enjoyed them and they made a wonderful treat.  I love peanuts and anything made from peanuts (peanut butter, YUM!) and these did not disappoint.Some people have commented that they aren't healthy.  Well, they don't purport to be healthy.  Nothing on the box seems to indicate that they want you to believe that.  If you are looking for health, this is not the way to go.  If you are looking for something to snack on then give these a try.I'm not sure what the price is so I can't comment on the value of these bars.  Anything less than $8 a box should make this a good deal.One last note: don't have these shipped to you in the middle of summer if you have an out-door mailbox.  They sat in mine in 110 degree weather for half a day before I got to them and they were quite toasty when I got to them. Either meet the mail carrier at the mail box or pick them up at the store instead.

column9: Yes it's messy..but like a good hamburger messy
column10: I am a nutrition nut and these won't be any different than basically any candy bar out there as far as health. However, for a good snack that needs to quench a sweet binge, these will do nicely albeit with some napkins of course. Yes they are messy and chewy and flimsy but how many times have we caught ourselves with a half melted candy bar as we handle it in disgust only after eating coyly thinking "Hey this wasn't bad at all!". Maybe even we secretly wish candy bars were a little bit more mushy, although we don't like to lick our fingers after eating one.They pack a lot of peanuts and they are filling, so that's a plus side. You don't have to keep eating these to get your sweet urge relinquished. It seems to me they are made simply so that you only have to buy one at a time instead of "2 Snickers and a butterfinger".This candy bar is like eating honey roasted peanuts stitched and held together (well until you get it wrapped up in your fingers) by soft honey. So get a paper towel ...or two and give these bars a try. Your peanut loving self will thank you.

column9: Not Bad, But Definitely Not the Best
column10: Planters, of course, is the granddaddy of all peanut purveyors. They have been around forever and still put out the finest plain peanuts around.  I would have thought that their forays into the niche market of nut bars would be more successful.  Not so.  These Big Nut Bars are tasty, quite good, but honestly cannot compare with such products as Nature Valley Sweet & Salty Nut Granola Bars, Peanut, 6-Count Boxes (Pack of 12), to name one. As I try to put my finger on the difference, I think it is this--the Planters product is just too big. If you want a lot of peanuts, this is for you. If, however, you want something a little smaller but with a more nuanced taste and palette, go with Nature Valley or one of the other competitors.  Good luck next time, Planters.

While hardly health food, the Planters Big Nut Bar is tasty (in a candyish sort of way) and a good source of protein when you can't take a break for a real meal. The bars are soft and chewy (and if shipped in the summer, maybe a bit melted) and have plenty of peanuts, packed into a fudgy base. While  a bit sweet for my personal tastes, I found that it balances nicely with a cup of coffee for a quick sugar, protein, caffeine fix in the morning. One caveat: the bars are gooey so if you're eating in the car, you may want to have some wet wipes handy to unstick your fingers!

I was quite impressed with this product.  Yes, it's a little high in calories...but less than most candy bars.  For some reason, I did a comparison of a Planters Nut Bar with a Snickers.  Planters had less calories, way less carbs, and more fiber.  And I'm serious when I refer to it as "candy bar good".  I'm a sucker for nuts and peanut butter anyhow so I gave one of the bars to a friend of mine.  All I told him was that it was a new granola bar I was trying and what did he think.  He loved them also--but almost didn't believe it was intended as anything other than candy.  Will I buy any at the store?  The only reason I wouldn't is because they're addictive.  Yummy!

column9: Just the right balance of all the good stuff
column10: Before the details:  The Planters big nut bars are a great tasting, quick energy and nutritious snacks.  Lots of peanuts and almonds make it really good on taste and nutrition.Taste:======Does not taste like a Granola bar, tastes more like a peanut bar with some almonds and oats in between.  Infact, you can hardly taste the Oats.  The Peanuts looks like they have been dry roasted in salt, so with every bite - you experience a slightly salted peanut + roasted almonds + caramely sugar tasteNutrition:=========220 calories in one bar.  Whats not good is that 50% of the calories come from sugar.This is not for those who are on a low calorie diet.If there was one thing which Planter could have done, they could have probably decrease the amount of sugars in it and instead added more peanuts/almonds and made it more protein rich

A delicious and satisfying snack, if you like peanuts and peanut butter.  A bit crunchy, not too chewy, just right in the middle.  The nutrition info, which is apparently not on either Amazon or the Planter's website is:220 calories, 110 fat calories.  13g fat, 3g sat. fat, 0g trans. fat, 6g monosat. fat, 0g cholesterol, 160mg Sodium, 22g total carbs, 3g fiber, 12g sugar, 7g protein.

As far as convenience foods go, these nut bars are probably reasonably healthy.  Sure they contain sodium caseinate, a neurotoxin, but overall the list of ingredients doesn't look any worse than most nut / granola bars that are advertised as healthy.  And Planters doesn't even make any health claims.I enjoyed the flavor of these nut bars.  Beware of trying to consume them in hot weather, they easily turn into a gooey mess.If you like peanuts, you should like these bars.

For what is essentially a candy bar, the Planters Big Nut Bars are actually pretty healthy for a snack. Nuts have lots of valuable nutrients, so you could do worse. There is a lot of sugar here, and these are probably awful for cavities because they are so sticky. But for a filling snack, these bars deliver. They taste great, very peanutty and sweet. A real pick-me-up between meals.

column9: Good but too much like a candy bar
column10: The Big Nut Bars are named properly... they are indeed huge! Very filling, and tasty too. I was expecting something like a granola bar, but these are really more like candy bars. Very sweet, chewy, jam-packed with peanuts.

I really, really love peanut butter, and could just eat it by the spoonful.  Too many snack bars just mix peanut butter in with other things in order to hold the peanut butter together and keep it from gooping all over your hands.These bars were just what I needed.  Peanut butter on the bottom, with a bar of peanuts on the top.  It ends up tasting just like some extra super chunk peanut butter with the peanuts crunching in your mouth while the oozy goodness of peanut butter clings to your tongue.  I think Planters snuck some other grains and such in there, but you wouldn't know it from the flavor.I haven't checked out the fat content on these bars, and I can only assume they are bad for you, like most delicious things.  They might be a notch up from your average candy bar in terms of health, but I really don't know.  What I do know, is that they are delicious, and if you are a peanut butter fan you will find this a little bar of heaven.

column9: Good? Yes. Messy? Yes, in Hot Weather
column10: No doubt, this is a good tasting peanut and peanut butter bar. All the kids liked it. The only issue is in warm weather, like mid-80s up, the peanut butter coating on the bottom melts easily. It is messy when it does. Just be aware of that.

column9: An Example of Truth in Advertising
column10: These things are definitely big, definitely have peanuts and peanut butter, and they're chewy. But they're also rather boring. You REALLY have to like peanuts to be able to work your way through one. It feels like something's missing -- a little sweetness, a little salt -- not sure what it is, but something would help. I asked the techs on my production crew to test a couple. Bear in mind that they'll eat anything from a craft service table, but they also found them lacking in some essential ingredient.The bars also get a bit mushy to the point of being messy when warm.If you're a big fan of peanuts and peanut butter and that's all you want, then these bars are for you. If you need a little variety in your treats, then maybe go for something with a little chocolate or other added flavors.I'm sorry if I've hurt your feelings, Mr. Peanut. I've always been a big fan.

These are what we have all come to love about the Planters products.  Fresh peanuts with rich peanutbutter and other grains make this a delightful snack that actually leaves you feeling satisfied.  Each bar is a really good size and sooooooooo tasty.  I just love peanuts!!  We had a family cookout this weekend and I passed them around for each of us to try and the the overall vote was fantastic.  A great product from a great company.  I think the fact that the peanuts weren't ground up to small pieces added to the richess of the product.  The peanut size in the bars was half a peanut and there are loads of them.  Planters didn't use a pea shooter to put the best of their product together.  Some products will stress a certain item only to have very little in there.  Not so here.  This is a must have snack for anyone who loves or likes peanuts in its best forms.  YUMM!

These Double Peanut flavor of Planters Big Nut Bars make for a soft, chewy, and overall nice treat for any occassion.  A little too salty for my tastes, but overall the Big Nut Bars are a tasty treat that anyone who enjoys peanuts in general will more than likely enjoy regardless.

column9: A good combination of size, flavor, and energy
column10: Planter's "Big" double peanut bars are good.  They provide a great combination of energy (220 calories), protein (lots of peanuts), and flavor.  Each bar has a firm peanut butter-like base and lots of peanuts.The consistency of the bar is a cross between that of a nut-roll and a snicker's bar.  There is some substance there, but it's different than just a bunch of peanuts rolled around a nuget center...there is no nuget center in these bars.  The nuts (and there are plenty of them) are held together by a matrix of material that is tasty but not particularly sticky.This is a good snack to take along while hiking, fishing, etc., when products that contain chocolate would be likely to melt and make a mess.A solid four-star product!

column4: Tom D. "Opportunity is limited only by imagin...
column9: Chewy granola bar loaded with peanuts and a peanut butter coat on the bottom
column10: Length:: 0:42 MinsWatch my short video review to see for yourself! :-)

column9: Not for diets, good on taste
column10: After receiving my box of Big Nuts bars from Amazon Vine, I eagerly tore into the box to get my first taste of this treat.  Expecting something more along the lines of a candy bar, I was pleasantly surprised by the taste: peanuty, definitely, with a slight sense of the granola bar that it is meant to imitate. They are not overpoweringly sweet, but the second and third ingredients in the label are sugar and corn syrup. At 220 calories a pop, they could easily be diet killers, including the 22 g of carbs each medium sized bar provides. Would I purchase these in the store? Probably not. Granola bars aren't my favorite thing. It was worth a taste, however.

column4: Raquel S. "Avid Amazon Fan and Kindle User"
column9: A peanut lovers delight. They won't last long in your home.
column10: The quick and dirty of Planters Big Nut Double Peanut Bar: It's so good that it won't last long in your home if there is a peanut lover in your home.That's exactly what happened in my home. When I got a box of Planters Big Nut Double Peanut bars home, I took one for myself immediately, because I figured there wouldn't be any left if I waited. Sure enough, hubby polished off the rest of the box before the day was over. He loved them!As for me, the non-peanut lover, found these bars to be tasty and find myself going back for another bite - even though peanuts are not my favorite nuts. The bars are peanut packed sticky bars with the bottom being a thin layer of peanut butter. The bars are a sticky mess to eat because the peanut butter melts too quickly. Keep a napkin on hand if you plan to nibble on the bars for any length of time.Pro: These are not peanut candy bars. These are super peanutty snack bars.On the con side: Planters Double Peanut Big Nut bars are so good, you'll want eat more than you need to.

I enjoyed every bite of this tasty peanut bar.  I knew that it had to be good when I ordered it because who better to make a peanut treat than the market leader Planters.  I am a fan of savory-sweet treats and this bar did the trick.  Some of the other bars on the market are just too sweet for my liking.  I also am not a big fan of chocolate in the morning.  This bar has just the right balance of nuts - salt and sweetness brought out from the peanut butter layered bottom.  The peanuts were crunchy and large - they did not fill the bar with broken pieces.My only heads up on this product is the calorie count - 200 per bar.  I try to keep my energy treats around 120 so this was a higher than I would like - I have to make choices in the day to manage this higher level like more celery in the afternoon - it is worth it in the end.  Enjoy!

Peanut lovers will love this granola snack because the peanut flavor is overwhelming!  The bars are a nice size too.  I assumed that these bars would be fairly small when I ordered but was pleasantly surprised when I saw the pack.Not as crunchy as you might expect with so many peanuts and that may disappoint some.  I looked for a little more crunch based on the picture on the package but the flavor is smooth and strong and is enough to overcome the need for a crunchier snack.  Definitely would use these snacks again.

Granola bars tend to fall into two categories: dry and tasteless or overly sugary and sickly-sweet.  Luckily, this peanut granola bar doesn't fit into either of those categories.  It's overflowing with peanuts and peanut butter, so it definitely has a strong flavor, but it isn't too sweet.  It was chewy but not dry, and it didn't leave my fingers sticky or oily, like so many snack bars do.  My only complaint was that the crisped rice part of the bar seemed to taste a little funny, but I'm not a big fan of crisped rice at the best of times, so it's probably the normal taste.  With 220 calories, 110 fat calories, 7g of protein, and only 7 g of sugar, it's not a treat that will make you feel guilty or unhealthy for the rest of the day, but you probably wouldn't want to down 4 or 5 of them in one sitting either.

column9: Planters BIG  Double Peanut  chewy granola bar
column10: These Planters Double Peanut Bars are good...at least that's my family's consensus. Although I like them, I think they're a bit high in calories.  Each bar is BIG, 1.62 oz,  filled with peanuts & coated with a bottom layer of peanut butter. (The bottom layer is not pure peanut butter but a peanut butter mixture. The coating isn't sticky like peanut butter & not  overly sweet). The generous size accounts for the 220 total calories in this bar.  One-half of calories in this bar (110 fat calories) are fat calories. The fat calories are high because peanuts are high in fat. As a comparison, an ounce of Planters Redskin Spanish peanuts contains 170 total calories of which 130 are fat calories.This is a fairly healthy snack for the days mealtime is delayed or you could grab one for breakfast when you're running low on time.  Each bar contains the following percentages of your daily requirements: 12%  fiber, 7%  protein, 7% sodium, 4%  iron, 100%  vitamin E, 10% phosphorus, & 2% calcium.  Because it is mostly peanuts, it also contains 20% of you total fat limit for the day (saturated fat 3 gr, trans fat 0gr,  polyunsaturated 3.5 gr, monounsaturated 6 gr). For those of you that count carbs, each bar contains 22 gr of total carbohydrates. The 12 grams of sugar in this bar would equal about 3 teaspoons of sugar.Did you know?Peanuts are a rich source of protein &  significant source of resveratrol, a chemical studied for potential anti-aging effects and also associated with reduced cardiovascular disease and reduced cancer risk.Ounce for ounce, peanuts contain almost 30 times as much resveratrol as grapes.Roasted peanuts rival the antioxidant content of blackberries and strawberries and are richer in antioxidants than apples, carrots or beets.

Basing this review on what one might expect when buying a pack of these bars, I can say that they do not disappoint.  I think they even taste better than what I expected thanks to the bottom layer of peanut butter.These bars are essentially a cluster of peanuts bound together with some kind of glaze on top of what seems to be a delicious white "chocolatey" peanut butter substance.  Let's face it.  If you buy a product called "Planters Big Nut Bars", you're expecting something like what I just described.So, when it comes to that, these bars are excellent.  They have an airy crisp to them as if there are puffed balls of rice mixed in with the peanuts to give them a more pleasing texture.As far as nutritional content, they're actually pretty good.  220 calories.  7g protein. 3g fiber, only 12g of sugar, but 13g of fat.  Compare that to a Clif Bar at 240 calories, 10g protein, 5g fiber, 22g sugar and 5g fat, and it's probably a smarter move to go with the Clif Bar.  But the Big Nut bar is no slouch.  It's certainly a viable option when competing with other typical energy bars on the market.So, if you like peanuts, and you want to try a new energy bar, I would definitely recommend giving these a shot.

I think that 220 calories is a little higher than you really need. The bars have 230 mg of salt, also a little much. The sugar content is 13 grams out of 46 grams, about average for this kind of product, although unfortunately some of the sugar comes in the form of corn syrup.As to taste, you have to like peanuts. The bars taste a lot like Reese's Peanut Butter Cups, but without the chocolate. The texture is crunchy. The surface is sticky at room temperature, but ok if you keep them in the refrigerator or carry them in your pocket for cold-weather activites like winter hiking or skiing.Altogether, I think that these bars are ok in taste and texture, but high in calories and salt. However, they can be just right in calories if that is what you need at the moment for a strenuous activity.

column9: Good new nut bar in the Planters Bug Nut Bar Series
column10: Planters certainly wasn't lying when they have the word "chewy" on the label.  These are very chewy, which I prefer but others may not.  While these bars have been criticized for their high calories, they are bigger than other "granola" bars and can be a meal or snack and leave you feeling fairly filled.  You may save calories since one of these will do it while you may end up eating two normal granola bars.They have a good peanut taste combined with a nice chewy peanut butter layer on the bottom.  Pretty good combination, kind of like a peanut butter sandwich with a layer of whole peanuts on it.  Obviously salty but that's to be expected.These have been criticized for not being healthy for you, and they probably aren't, but again their fat content, salt, etc. is comparable to other bars that advertise themselves as healthy, organic, etc. and don't have any trans-fats.  So if you like them eat them, life is short, treat yourself.The Planters Triple nut bar has a more distinctive flavor which I prefer so you may want to try it.

column9: Tasty but I liked the Triple Nut bar better
column10: If you like peanuts, you'll love this bar as it's basically all peanuts (peanuts with a little granola in the bar, along with peanut butter on the bottom of the bar). I'm not sure why they call this a granola bar - it does contain granola but the peanuts hide any taste (or texture) of the granola. Taste-wise, it is good although if you're not use to sweets, this bar would probably seem too sweet to you. I wouldn't recommend keeping one of these anywhere where it could get hot and melt - I would think that the peanut butter bottom could cause a mess on a hot day.I also tasted the Triple Nut bar by Planters and of the 2 bars, I like the Triple Nut bar better - while I do like peanuts, I liked the addition of almonds and cashews better than this bar.All that's missing is a chocolate coating and this could be called a candy bar. Considering the nutritional value of these bars, eat one as often as you would a candy bar. This is not a healthy treat, but it is tasty.

First off, I absolutely love peanuts and these bars are chock full of them.  Further they taste crunchy and fresh, not at all softened as the nuts in some bars are.  If you like peanuts, this bar's for you!  There are 220 calories in a bar, and I wish there were less.  Nonetheless, they're great for a quick snack when you're on the run or traveling.  One caveat they do soften if exposed to high temperatures.  I carried one in my purse in hot Texas weather and it was a bit sticky to eat (but worth it).  The bars are a good size - 4 1/2" long and 1 1/2" wide.  The price is reasonable for a box of five, and I'd recommend them to all who like peanuts.

This is the first time that I've tried Planters Big Nut Bars but I found that I thought they were pretty good. They have good flavor, I especially like the peanut butter on the bottom of the bar. I also liked how chewy it was. I hate when granola bars, or bars like this one, just crumble when you eat it. One thing though was that I got thirsty after eating it. I owe it maybe to the peanuts and the salt that comes with it. The calories are a bit high at 220 but it's true that any granola bar like this is usually higher in calories.Planters Big Nut Bars are a perfect snack or addition to your lunch.

Planters Big Nut Bars, Double Peanut, are chewy, crunchy and delightfully delicious with lots and lots of peanuts.  I love to eat them as a snack while watching a movie.  In fact, I love to eat anything with peanut butter while watching a movie.  I grew up on peanut butter.  I spoon it right out of the jar and put it in my mouth.  When there was the recent recall on peanut butter because of salmonella poisoning, I continued to eat it.  "I don't care if I die," I joked to my parents, "at least I'll die happy with the taste of peanut butter on my lips."  Whenever I've gone to the theatre, I've always sneaked in single serving size bags of Planters nuts.  (I don't care if I get caught; it`s not like I stole them.)  Now, I'm going to have to sneak in these delicious Planters Big Nut Bars.  Only problem, you must keep them stored in a cool place because the extra layer of velvety smooth peanut butter will melt onto its wrapper.  These bars are highly addictive and highly recommended for anyone who loves eating peanut butter and isn't counting calories.Joseph B. Hoyos

column9: Do you Like Peanuts? Then here is a tasty snack
column10: My fingers stick slightly to the keys as I type this. I made the mistake of taking the Planters big nut bar out of the wrapper. The layer of peanut butter on the bottom makes it messy. That however is what wrappers and wet naps are made for. Next to me is a full cup of liquid with ice because this is a snack that requires a drink. Coffee tastes wonderful with it by the way. It is peanuts, with more peanuts and then peanut butter. It's no wonder that a drink is needed. So why am I willing to have sticky fingers and a slightly dry cotton mouth (sans drink), because they are sooooo good.  It is a pleasure to chew these tasty treats.  If fact the only think I would like to see is a layer of chocolate on the bottom, personal issue I know but the creamy peanut butter taste reminds me of that not to be named peanut butter cup.  Reading this you might think that all the ingredients are peanuts. That is because it's all you really taste. That and a little salt (tastes may vary). In these gooey bars are crisped rice, whole grain rolled oats and granola. Those ingredients along with a size larger than most snack bars would explain why the planter's nut bar is so filling.But are they healthy? That seems to be the question in some of the reviews.  First I see nothing from planters or amazon at the time of this review saying Healthy, low calorie or diet. That said. Yes these bars have 13g of fat. Most of that is healthy fat, the kind that has been found to reduce heart disease.  There is no Trans fat in these bars. Zero. That is because I have finally found a product that does not have Hydrogenated Oils in it. At the time of this review there is no hydrogenated or partially hydrogenated oil.  Yes it has 220 calories but they are filling calories with iron, Vit E, good fats, calcium, fiber, and protein. Sounds good? Now the not so good news, the ingredient also has 6 different kinds of sugars in the bars, a whopping 17g a serving.  40grams it the daily recommended intake.Pros - The chewy peanut butter taste. They are really filling; one is all you need at a sitting. They are not empty calories. No Hydrogenated oils.  Good at work or on the go.Cons- A lot of sugar, Need to have a drink with it, have to keep the wrapper on.In conclusion if you like peanuts, have a drink can don't feel compelled to rip the wrapper all the way off (or have wet wipes) then you should enjoy this tasty treat. While it's healthier than most processed foods, it's not replacement for fruit. It is a sometimes snack.  A delicious one.

While I love the Roasted Triple Nut (Planters Big Nut Bars, Roasted Triple Nut, 8.1-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 10)), this "Double Peanut" just left me unimpressed. There was just not any "chemistry" in the taste. It was worse than just eating peanuts alone, and that defeats the purpose of eating a value-added product.I won't even go into the nutritional information, which is, as you can expect, on the high-fat side since this is double-peanut.If you want to try the Planets Big Nut Bars, I highly recommend getting this one instead: Planters Big Nut Bars, Roasted Triple Nut, 8.1-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 10)

column9: Melt in heat, and not the healthiest
column10: Tasty, and healthier than candy bars, but a health bar it ain't (after peanuts, the next main ingredients are corn syrup and sugar).  The bars are currently a little over 50 cents a piece, which isn't bad for something to quench your hunger, which these little bars aren't too bad at.  That said, this deal is for about 5 lbs of peanut bars.  5 pounds of dry roasted, unsalted peanuts (which would be healthier than these bars) would only be a quarter of the price of these.  Maybe the convenience is worth it to you though.  Be aware that these bars do not do well in warm temperatures: the peanut butter they're smeared with gets melted very quickly.

Planters Big Nut Bars, Double Peanut, 8.1-Ounce Boxes:The first thing I noticed is the calorie count. 220 is a bit high for a snack/granola bar. At 13G fat, it's no lightweight there either. There's no sat-fat and salt is relatively normal at 160mg. OK, this is not a health bar so it better taste good. It definitely has a big peanut taste. The combination of peanuts and peanut butter layered on the bottom assure a big burst of peanut flavor. You better keep the Mylar wrapper on because it can get messy. The peanut butter on the bottom will stick to your fingers if left unwrapped.The overall taste is pleasant to me, I like it. The size is fairly large too, so you should get any hunger pangs satiated. The chewiness, to me is about right. You feel like you're eating something substantial, which it is. Overall, if you like peanuts, I think you'll be happy. Enjoy.

column9: Tastes decent, not very good for you
column10: These are good, but I will not order these again.  They taste like a payday granola bar, so good to substitute a candy bar, but not a good sub for a better snack or meal.  They are a bit messy and have some ingredients I normally avoid: corn syrup and more salt than I prefer.They are also very chewy; if you have complicated dental work, TMJ or issues with eating chewy foods -- you will want to steer clear of these.

column9: Tasty, Filling, Nutty, what more could you ask for?
column10: These bars have big time peanut flavor.  Incorporated into the mix is peanut butter, crisped rice, sugar and peanuts (plus a box side of other stuff).  By using the peanut butter and crisped rice, Planters has allowed the big taste to remain, while cutting back on the peanuts.  But even so, the total fat count is 13g per with 3g saturated.  Total calorie count is 220.However, I loved these things.  Bravo, Planters.  I would have given it a 5 star rating, but I had to subtract 1 star for not being as crispy, crunchy as I thought it should be.

column4: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
column10: The peanuts were fine, but bland. The peanut butter was also bland.  Personally I could take it or leave it.  However, my girlfriend really liked them. She thought the combination of peanuts and peanut butter was great.  Calorie wise, they are average with a candy bar, and to be honest, I'd prefer a nutty candy bar with caramel.

Planters Nut Bars are a good candy bar, not a healthy snack choice.  They are a chewy, peanuty, salty, sweet snack.  Just what you would expect out of the typical candy bar. The taste is sweet and chewy with a good peanut taste.

Don't let words like "chewy granola bar" or "7 grams of protein" fool you into thinking that Planters Big Nut bars are any healthier than a candy bar.Check out the ingredients:(in order)1)peanuts2)corn syrup(a sweetner)3)sugar4)peanut butter(roasted ground peanuts)5)crisped rice(rice flour, sugar, malt extract, salt, carmel color, mixed tocopherols)6)evaporated cane juice invert syrup(a sweetner)7)whole grain rolled oats8)fractionated palm kernal oil9)granola(whole grain rolled oats, brown sugar, whole grain rolled wheat,coconut, canolaoil, wheat bran)10)partially defatted peanut flour11)salt12)fructose (a sweetner)13)soy lecithin14)resistant corn dextrin15)natural flavor and mixed tocopherolsThats a lot of sugar when you add it all up with each 46gram bar (which really isn't that big) weighing in with 220 calories, 110 calories from fat, 13grams of fat, 22grams of carbohydrate, 3grams of fiber, 12 grams of sugar and 7 grams of protein.Inspite of all the sugar, I would have given a slightly better rating based on taste alone if I didn't get the impression Planters was trying to promote this product as something "healthy" instead of just another candy bar.  Consumers already have a difficult enough time wading through all the hype when trying to make healthy choices at the supermarket!

column9: Baraw Crow Bamas' Review: Planters Big Nut Bars
column10: Are there healthier choices for a snack bar? Yes. Are there better tasting choices for a snack bar? Yes. Is there a snack bar with more of a peanut taste? Eh, maybe. I wanted to suggest these for when you go hiking. However, with 220 calories, and 110 of those being fat calories, I'm not so sure I would suggest these for hiking. Factor in the 160mg of sodium, it seems counter productive. Health wise, I would suggest countless other bars. Taste wise, I don't see these bars replacing Blueberry Trio Bars in our snack drawer. As for peanuty taste, it's a toss up between these and a Payday bar. I would give the edge to the Planters Big Nut Bars just on the healthier factor.All in all, if you love peanuts, not worried about indulging, and don't mind a heavy feeling snack. Then by all means, this is a good choice for you.

These are a hit at our house !1. GREAT peanut flavour---exactly right amount of flavour..delicious2. Just the right amount of crunchiness not too soft nor too hard3. Reminiscent of the Payday bar4. Healthy5. Betcha cant eat just one of these =0)So all of the nut lovers in our family are wild over this snackOh, almost forgotPERFECT size !!! it can be a nice mid day snack or a quick "breakfast" with a piece of fruit and milk when you are rushing out the door
I'm not sure that these bars are really all that different from a candy bar -- they're pretty sweet and not exactly low-calorie. However, they are quite tasty.

Each bar is 1.62 ounces and absolutely packed with peanuts!  Contains corn syrup, sugar, milk, and soy, but no hydrogenated oils.  Very peanuty tasting and a hit with all ages. 7 grams of protein and 12 of sugar in every bar.

column9: Tasty but too high in calories
column10: To begin, I definitely think that the taste of Planters Big Nut Triple Nut Bars is very good.  I like roasted nuts and these are very nutty.  The dominant taste is that of peanuts, but as we know, Planters is known for their nuts.The label states that these "big bars" are 30% larger and therein lies the problem, from my perspective.  They are also 30% higher in calories.  Also, because of the larger size, there are only 5 bars per box versus the usual 5.I would much prefer that they reduce the size by 30% and give me 6 nut bars per box.  This would cut the caloric content from 220 down to about 150 calories per bar, lessening the guilt factor and giving one an extra bar to enjoy.So the product itself is pretty good, but I think that the portion is too large.

column9: If a Payday & a granola bar could have babies....
column10: These are GOOD!  If you like Payday candy bars and/or peanut butter granola bars, this is the snack for you.  It satisfies salty, sweet, and crunchy snack cravings, and is PACKED with peanuts (#1 ingredient).  With 220 calories, 3 grams of fiber, 7 grams of protein, and 12 grams of sugar, this snack bar eats like a meal.

These are nice large sized peanut nut bars, with an excellent flavor, both sweet and salty, neither overpowering the other. They have a well rounded flavor that is very satisfying. These are an excellent anytime snack bar, but my one complaint is the peanut butter goo on the bottom can be a bit sticky and messy. It tends to stick to the inside of the wrapper and to your fingers more than it does to the Planters Big Nut Bar. Overall an excellent snack, just be sure and have napkins at the ready if you plan to eat them on the go!

I liked the Planter's snack bars.  Basically it is a larger and higher calorie version of a regular granola bar with the added joy of having fat planter's peanuts on top.As other have said, it is not a diet bar and is probably a bit messier than your average granola bar which are always nice to have in the car.  However it is tasty and sweet and depending on what you are looking for in a granola bar (did I just type that) this should satisfy both your sweet and salty cravings.

column9: Really Good--now if only they had chocolate!
column10: I have to admit, when I want a snack bar, I usually choose chocolate.  But, I wanted to try these, because I like nuts, too.  These bars were surprisingly good!  And my kids liked them (huge surprise to me!)  They aren't big nut fans in general, but they ate these bars right up.The list of ingredients is pretty good.  They do have corn syrup as the second ingredient, but no high fructose corn syrup which is what I really try to stay away from for my family.The bars are a nut bar with a thin coating of sweet peanut butter on the bottom side.  If you took these to a warm outside event, that coating would definitely be melty and messy, but on a regular day, these would be great bars to take a long for a snack!Now, if they'll only make them with a chocolate coating... =)

I was expecting something a bit more on the salty side, but these bars are definitely sweet. The peanut butter layer was on the bottom and after spending the morning in my postlady's truck was very melted and very messy. I would not recommend storing these in a warm place or in a lunchbox unless they were near an ice pack as the melted peanut butter coated the inside of the wrapper and made my fingers very sticky.As a nutritional snack they don't make the cut with 220 calories and 13 grams of fat per bar. They were yummy and filling, but I'd prefer a bit more salt flavor to offset the sweetness. I might pick them up on sale, but I can't see this being added to my pantry as a 'must have' item.

If I could describe these bars in one word it would be: meaty. Yes, because they're big, thick and filling.  They have really big peanuty taste and the nuts on top are large and plentifulThey remind me of another granola bar, the Nature Valley Sweet and Salty Peanut bars. Those too are coated with peanut butter and have big peanuts on top. These bars are very similar to those and to be honest, I really couldn't find a difference between the two. One pro I did find was that the peanut butter coating did not start melting while eating. I did not find myself needing to get a napkin to wipe sticky fingers.While these bars are filling, it's also due to high calories and fat. This would scare someone from eating this as a snack everyday but they are good for a meal replacement if you're busy and can't take a break for lunch. In fact, one bar is much more filling than eating a Slim Fast meal replacement bar.Overall, I did enjoy these bars. They are tasty, filling and portable to carry around.  If possible share with a friend, for maximum enjoyment.

column9: Tasty but only 10 calories less than a Payday candy Bar & will melt in summer heat
column10: I really enjoyed the taste of these bars but it's probably because I love Payday candy bars.  I compared the caloric intake and was surprised to find that your normal 1.85 ounce Payday bar was only 10 calories more than this product which promotes itself as a "healthy" snack.  I'll grant them this - the Big Nut bar is better for my dental work since it doesn't have the chewy nougat filling that a Payday has but beyond that, there's not much of a nutritional difference.  I found that the Big Nut bar satisfied my need for a snack in the long stretch between lunch and dinner and since it din't make me worry about my bridgework, I'd probably keep some on hand for snacking.  The taste was very similar to a Payday bar and I liked that.  It was a little less salty and slightly less sweet.Here's the downside - like a lot of the tarted-up granola bars of today, The Big Nut Bar has a sweet coating on the bottom of the bar that melts easily.  The day ours were delivered it was only about 85 degrees out and that coating was liquified.  These bars would have to be kept in a cool place to be properly enjoyed because once that bottom layer melts, it's a big ole mess and no fun to eat.  Also, the wrapper was somewhat difficult to open.  I have to use scissors each time.  I didn't mind doing that but I'm a grown-up.  I can't imagine giving this snack to a kid and expecting them to deal with the wrapper without trying to tear it with their teeth!In summary - nice taste, virtually same calories as a Payday bar, melts easily and wrapper is hard to open.  I liked them and would buy them on sale because they taste like a Payday without having the Payday's problem of sticking to your dental work.

I am a HUGE fan of Payday candybars.  I also love granola bars. The Planters Big Nut chewy granola bar is the perfect combination of two of my favorites.It is the same size as the Payday but with less calories (WOOT!).  It is also more filling than a granola bar. I have to admit, I rarely eat one granola bar so the calories of the Planters bar are pretty close to two granola bars. The bonus is there are no granola crumbs from the Planters.With fiber and protein, this bar will be a new work snack staple for me! LOVE IT!!

When used as an occasional treat, or as a quick filler when a meal is delayed, I think this bar is a good choice.  It does have some protein, but the high caloric and fat contents mean you should not eat one every day.  The bar is a bit messy since the peanut butter is smeared along the bottom, so I do not think it is a good option to keep in your purse as a "quick-fix".  Living in San Antonio, I can only imagine the horrific goo that would greet me after a day inside my purse in 100+ degree weather!  Though it might make the bar more expensive, it might have been nice to put the peanut butter inside, layered between the peanuts, rather than on the outside to stick to the wrapper and to fingers.

For those who love peanuts this bar has a great nutty taste since it combines both peanuts and peanut butter.  It's 220 calories with 20% of calories from fat and has 7 grams of protein.The only disappointment I had was that my bars arrived with the peanut butter melted making it very messy to eat.  Therefore, if you decide to purchase these bars, keep them out of extremely high heat or just accept that the top peanut butter layer melts in hot weather as a chocolate bar would.Overall, it's a great bar for peanut lovers and a much better choice than candy for when you are craving a non-fruit snack.

You only get 5 bars in a box so the price comes out to almost .60 cents a bar, that's expensive.  Especially when it's just a glorified PayDay candy bar.  It does have 7g. of protein but also 22g. of carbs. so it's not a diet bar and it's not a low-carb bar.  It also doesn't compare to a nut and granola bar, the granola in this bar looked like oats covered in a sugar glaze.It tasted good on the start but by the finish it had a fake, burnt peanut taste, almost like rancid oil.  Apparently my box had gotten too hot because the coating of peanut butter that is on the bottom of the bar had melted and it was a mess inside the wrapper.  This would not be kid friendly in the car.  It would be a great big mess.I would pass on these for the cost and nutritional information alone.  But then combined with the peanut butter coating on the bottom (!) it's definitely a no-go.

The Double Peanut flavor of Planter's "Big Nut Bars" Is a large size bar that tastes good and is also quite filling. At 220-calories per bar it can't really be considered a lite snack. The bars have a layer of peanut butter on the bottom that coats the wrapper and eventually your fingers. If your are looking for a salty/sweet snack, like peanuts and don't mind the calorie count or mess, these might just be what you're looking for.

These bars taste great!  If anything, they may be a little on the salty side, but that's what you would expect if you've ever had salted Planters peanuts.Upon opening the wrapper for these bars, the first thing you notice is the peanut butter on the bottom.  So these bars are not for youngsters unless you don't mind a little cleanup.  They are also a very substantial size (1.62 oz each) and much larger than say a Quaker granola bar.  For those considering this product as part of a lunch for your kids, these bars are on the high side in calories and fat (220 & 13g) so this may not be a good idea to stick in a child's lunch every day.For anyone who is not too concerned about eating healthy and enjoys both salty and sweet snacks I say give this product a try.  You won't be disappointed.

I'm a fan of Planters Big Nut Bars, Roasted Triple Nut, 8.1-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 10), so I was thinking these would be similar, only with all peanuts.That wasn't the case...These are more difficult to chew and more chewy than I like.  They also have lots of sweetners included (in order): corn syrup, sugar, evaporated cane juice invert syrup, brown sugar (in granola), fructose to add up to 12g per bar.  This is actually 1g less than the triple nut, so I'm not sure why I notice it more with these...Overall, they are ok, but I wouldn't put them on my shopping list.

This was alot better then I expected. I liked that it was bigger, and more peanut butter. My only bad think I can say is when it arrived (I live in Florida) It was mushed I put in the fridge and it turned to brittle but it was still good. my gripe is that its a little salty I dont think its a great kids snack but it was good

My son and I really love these bars.  If we had it our way, we would have eaten the whole box in one sitting.  My wife on the other hand prevented us from doing just that. So we had to settle for 1.5 bars each.  The flavor is just the right amount of sweet and salty and gooey at the same time.  Would really recommend these if you like chunky peanut butter.

I really liked this snack bar combination of peanuts and peanut butter.  It is made up of a thin bottom layer of peanut butter topped with just peanuts that does not become too gooey or sweet. There are 5 bars to a box and it comes out to around $14/box which is a bit expensive (I deducted a star for value) but peanuts are the first ingredient.  I would rather pay more money for these then have my kids (and myself) eat a peanut bar where peanuts are listed as the third or fourth ingredient.I am not a fan of the health snack bars and this one is a good substitute for me.  It's not exactly a diet snack but it's better then the other options I usually go to when I am feeling peckish.  Here are some of the key nutrional facts:calories - 220daily value saturated fat - 20%daily value protein - 7%daily value fiber - 12%

I am not really a "peanut" fan. I prefer pistachios and other more expensive nuts in general. But these peanut bars are fantastic in flavor. The (I guess you'd call it) nougat around the peanuts is very tasty and creamy and the bar is pretty filling even if you only eat one.It's a higher calorie bar. It actually has 220 calories in only one bar and also has some saturated fat so it's not for people who are looking for a diet snack. Also, half its calories come from fat (110 out of 220). The second ingredient says corn syrup so that kind of gives you an idea of this bar's target audience.They come in a box so if Amazon is selling these as a set of 10 boxes. Doing the math, that's only about 56 cents per bar, which is definitely a good deal for a general snack. I highly recommend them even though I usually go for a lesser fat snack.

I love planters peanuts & I'd never had a nut bar before these but I can clearly see that I've been missing out.  These are quite yummy.  I wasn't expecting the peanut butter layer that's on the bottom.  Not sure why but I always assumed that it was just the nuts all stuck together & that was all.  I was really excited to see that peanut butter layer.  It was quite yummy.My kids really liked these as well.  My daughter said that they were a little tough which I may agree with but I think it's my problematic jaw saying that more than anything else.  My jaw wasn't happy with me eating this but it's too good to pass up so my jaw will have to deal.  :)If you like peanuts then I would highly recommend these Big Nut Bars.

My Vizsla is an EXTREMELY picky eater (won't even eat canned food by itself!) and I was hoping a "raw" food might please her picky palate.  She is on a grain-free diet and doesn't tolerate chicken, lamb or beef so this was perfect for her!  I also love that it is a nutritionally complete dog food.  It doesn't have a strong smell at all (unlike most canned foods) and I was worried she wouldn't like it but she scarfed it right down, even mixed with dry food.  I also like that you mix it with warm water, she seems to like warm food better.  Great dogfood, well worth the price!

column9: flavorful and healthy without being "nutty" or chewy
column10: This is the BEST whole wheat pasta we've had, and trust me- we've tried most of them. Not only does it taste really great, it stands up to just about anything you subject it to- overcooking, baking with sauces, being sauteed in oil, refrigeration, etc.The bionaturae pastas all cook up lovely. And unlike other whole wheat pastas, there's no weird aftertaste or bitterness no matter how long you cook it for. No matter how al dente (or how tender) you like your pasta cooked, this pasta holds up to whatever you subject it to. We tend to like pasta more on the tender side, and the pasta retains its shape, doesn't disintegrate or get glue-y even after 12 minutes in boiling water. Holds on to sauces very nicely. Also refrigerates well after being mixed with sauces.This particular pasta (the Chiocciole) is perfect for ziti and other baked pasta dishes (macaroni and cheese!)My daughter, who is four years old and a SUPER picky eater, prefer this over her regular semolina pasta.The best part about this? The Chiocciole boils up LARGE and fluffy and really fills your plate, so you can have a nice large bowl of pasta for not a lot of calories.Highly recommended.
Bionaturae is my favorite brand of whole-wheat pasta, and I've tried quite a few. It's smooth, as opposed to many brands whose pasta is gritty and rough. The flavor is excellent, as well.
This was quite disappointing.  After cooking for precisely the amount of time recommended, trying to eat the pasta was like trying to eat rubber.  Don't waste your time or money.

This is, by far, the favorite whole wheat pasta my family has tried. The quality of the wheat comes through in every bite--and the texture is perfect, not grainy or gritty. With Amazon's subscribe and save option, it is very reasonably priced, as well. Highly recommended!
Love love love this pasta, and it's whole wheat, so it's good for you. Haven't been so pleased since they found out chocolate was good for you...

column9: first really good whole wheat pasta
column10: I have tried all the store brands and they were not good enough to use. I had read a NYT review of this and tried it. It is quite good and I plan to buy other shapes as well.

column9: Only dry pasta I will eat.
column10: Although this pasta is super expensive it's totally worth it. This pasta comes out consistently al dente. Sometimes I'll end up buying other pasta at the store, but I always come back to this because the texture is always perfect. I'm very happy to find this on amazon because it's still much cheaper than at whole foods ($4 a bag). Both the wheat and the white versions of this pasta are delicious. The wheat isn't too wheaty, although you will notice the difference in taste.

I bought this product because of Cook's illustrated made this company the #1 Whole wheat product for pasta. I can't say much more than the review that "Chel Micheline's" review said. It is a great whole wheat product but I would still rather have a traditional dry pasta. I'm on the South Beach Diet and this is fine for the Italian craving. I've tried their other products but always gravitate to this shape. It's great for catching the vegetables in the pasta sauce I'm making.
Organic, nutritious, beautifully made Italian pasta. What's not to like? It has a satisfying bite, a delicious texture and most important for me - no aggressive whole-wheaty taste.

column9: Tasted Much Better Than I Thought It Would
column10: I was sort of dreading eating whole wheat pasta, but this was amazing! It didn't taste too heavy and it didn't resemble anything like cardboard like I thought it would. Very good! I will be buying more of this.

Upon recieving order, Boston Baked Beans were immediately thrown in the trash. It may be a personal preferrence but, they were hard as a rock and not soft at all where the coating is concerned.They were removed from my list. I ordered a good supply but, was really disapointed. Not so much in the seller but, in the product.

column9: Melina's Pomegranate Merlot Vinegar, 2-Ounce Glass Bottle
column10: The tag on the bottle reads. Ingredients: White Wine Vinegar, and Pomegranate Juice Concentrate.Nutritional Facts: Serving size 1 Tbsp. Calories 10, Acidity 6%, Total Fat 0, Sodium 0, Total Carbs 1%, Sugars 4g., Protien 0. Next time I'll make my own.
This vinegar is too sweet.It tastes and smells more like wine than vinegar.Maybe this is how all merlot vinegar is like, but personally I am disappointed.

column4: Joe Bruno Sr. "Fiction and Non Fiction author"
column9: Tasty balsamic vinegar at the right price
column10: I use balsamic vinegar both as something to add to my salads, and to include in a marinade. Melina's Pomegranate Merlot is delightful to use in both instances. And at under five bucks for two ounces, it's a bargain to boot.Highly recommended!
I was really pleased with the variety I received. It included most of the KCups I was really wanting to try from Brands I had heard great things about! Thanks!!

column9: bought these cookies to qualify for fee shipping!!
column10: I just bought these cookies so I'd get free shipping on a couple of other items I wanted. WHAT A FIND. They are fantastic. I didn't realize I was getting a box of six boxes of TOP QUALITY, DELICIOUS cookies. We polished them all off in short order with lots of company at the cottage this summer. My husband was thrilled that they were organic, my brother and his wife found them a chocolate lovers delight, the grandkids gobbled them up, and I was astounded that they were gluten free and wheat free so I could enjoy them as well. We will all be ordering lots more.

I have a sweet tooth or two and love chocolate....but despite that I found these cookies to be over-the-top sweet. (Sugar is the first ingredient on the package.) I will stick to a chocolate bar to satisfy my gluten-free chocolate cravings after these are gone.If you plan to buy these, you may want to know that there are 9 cookies in each box. All of mine arrived broken and crumbled (not sure why since no previous problems with having food shipped to me by Amazon) but still taste good.

my family loves these, they don't last very long in our house.  I send these to school so that when a mom brings in cupcakes, or cookies or something with gluten that my daughter cannot have, she has a nice treat that is really good, so she does not have to feel left out.
These taste so chocolatey and are delicious but they are a lot smaller than they seem when you see them online.

I've been eating cookies for over 60 years (among other things) and these are the best I've ever tasted!Edit: I have bought these several times since and have found they aren't always the best I've ever tasted.  Maybe the first time was a particularly fresh batch.  But even the worst of them were still near the top of my list right up there with the New York Times version of the Toll House chocolate chip recipe.
I really enjoy Pamela's products. This one is good because I can just pull out a package and have 2 cookies and leave the rest....I have no willpower over the regular bag once it is opened.

As a gluten-free chocoholic, I will say that these are the best mass-produced, gluten-free chocolate chocolate chip cookies I have found.  The quality of the chocolate is very good -- a nice, rich, bittersweet flavor.  The rest of the cookie, however, is disappointing.  The cookies are very thick (more than 1/4"), dry, and brittle.  That's rather surprising given their fat content:  a whopping 9g per serving.If you're a baker, you're better off making your own.  But if you're not a baker and you love dark chocolate, these might be right up your alley.

I used to have an allergy to wheat products.  I still try to eat a relatively gluten-free diet.  Therefore, I have been looking for a good cookie alternative.  These cookies are delicious.  They are slightly buttery-flavored and do not taste too grainy.  While they are slightly crumbly, they are better than any gluten-free cookie that I have come across.  Definitely a recommend buy for any gluten-intolerant person.  They have a great aftertaste too.One complaint: They are VERY addictive.  :D

column9: Taste Great, Sugar Content TOO HIGH, First ingredient
column10: Sugar is the FIRST ingredient on the package (Organic Natural Evaporated Cane Sugar), however, when Amazon lists the ingredients they do not list them in the order on the package. Shame on Amazon. I love Amazon and order from them frequently every month and love their service. But regarding this issue I think THEY ARE WRONG not to voluntarily do the same thing. The government requires manufacturers to list ingredients in the order of largest content first. I had ordered this as part of Amazon's Subscribe and Save program because it sounded like a great product after reading the ingredient list on the site. Wrong.
