column9: good coffee, right amount of pumpkin spice
column10: Good coffee for when you can't go to the local coffee shop, and want a pumpkin coffee at home.  I use this to make pumpkin lattes every morning.  Just the right amount of spice, not overpowering.  I wish they made this coffee available year round, but it is only available for a few months in the fall.
This coffee smells so autumn, makes a pleasant cup of seasonal coffee, a little on the weak side, but good.

I love the Pumpkin Spice K-Cups!! I have been using it for both hot and iced coffee and it tastes fabulous! I am also so pleased that the coffee is fair trade. The price is right and will definitely purchase again! (After I go through 80 cups of yummy coffee!).

I am obsessed with this coffee.  I know it is Spring and pumpkin spice coffee is VERY out of season.  I feel fortunate to be able to get a morning staple at any season.  Thank you. Transaction was flawless and very satisfied with delivery time.

It was 7 days from order date to arrival via FedEx. The big beautiful box held 80 loose k-cups packaged by the manufacture. This coffee is only available/produced from Green Mountain yearly between August to November, so after that the "Best before" date needs to be noted. (it doesn't mean the coffee will go stale though) Most are dated with Feb or April, but to my surprise, this box is dated for June 2, 2012 which made me even more happy because the listing description has no note on the date.Oh! lastly,..I LOVE GM Pumpkin Spice! It's my favorite flavored coffee!

column9: I think it is the best mustard.
column10: I go through mustard very quickly. Love sandwiches and use this on all but peanut butter. I switch between several brands. I think this is the best.

The pecans tasted great but you can buy pecans at your "club" store for an average of $7/lb - $8/lb.  This 5 lb bag is overpriced for what is available in our area of Texas.  I'd check local pricing before popping for this offer.

I was looking for a good deal on pecans when I found these. This 5lb bag was the best deal at the time (prices do change). These pecans came in a thick plastic bag, well sealed, and were fresh tasting and nice big pieces (no pecan-powder). I will definitely be buying these again!

They are very fresh.  Since it is such a large package, I am keeping them in the fridge to keep them that way.  The piece size is very nice for baking, etc.  No need to do any chopping, but the pieces are not to fine as to appear ground.

These cakes are really yummy!  They come packaged 2 together, so you really get 6 wrappings in a box with 2 cakes in each wrapping (total 12 cakes).  But let me tell you, these are overpriced online.  If you buy these in the grocery store in Pennsylvania, they cost $4 a box (that's not even a sale price).  I love these cakes, but it's just not worth it unless you're getting a bunch of stuff to make shipping them worth while.

column9: Tastes great, but not exactly a "health" bar.
column10: I bought these to try to supplement my fiber intake without having to deal with powders and pills. Over the last few years I've found that increasing my fiber intake is a great way of losing weight and maintaining it, so I try to get around 30g a day. Foods high in fiber fill you up more quickly and aid in digestion, The Daily Recommended Value of fiber for adults is 25g per day. Most people in America probably get much less than that, closer to 7-10g a day. At 9g of fiber per serving, just eating one of these bars a day will provide a lot of assistance in meeting the DRV.In addition to the fiber content, the bars really taste great. I've never been a fan of granola-type bars, and figured with a name like "Fiber One" these would taste like cardboard, but they are one of the best meal bars I've eaten. They are moist and have a good texture. All of the ingredients seem fresh.At 4g, these bars are very low in saturated fat (they contain poly and monounsaturated fats - the "good fats). Total net carbohydrates is 19G (28g-9g of fiber), so they do contain a little more sugar than I would like (it is the third largest ingredient). Here is the nutritional info:Calories - 140Total Fat - 4g (2g saturated)Carbohydrates - 29gFiber - 9gProtein - 2gMy only real problem with these bars are the ingredients.  They are fairly heavily processed.  The second main ingredient is "Semisweet chocolate chips."  Following that are whole grain oats, and then corn syrup. Although these are a fairly significant source of additional fiber, I would have preferred they not add all the extra sugar.

I have bought the Fiber One Bars in Oats & Chocolate, and Oats & Peanut Butter.  I love them both.  The Chocolate are my personal favorite.  It's nice to me to have them individually wrapped for a quick snack or meal to keep in my car while I'm driving to jobs or between jobs.  The taste is sweet and satisfies my sweet tooth without a lot of the guilt and it does fill you up and has 35% fiber.  It's especially nice to order groceries through Amazon when they are having sales and then get them delivered for free to your door.  My kind of grocery shopping!  You won't go wrong with these snacks or meals!

When I tasted my first Fiber One bar, the only thought running through my head was, "why on earth didn't I buy more of these?"  These bars taste better than any high fiber bar out there.  I had to read and re-read the nutritional information.  There are 9 grams of fiber in each bar.  Imagine eating something REALLY good and good for you.  I can't say that about too many food items.  But, I gladly recommend this product.  Every flavor has an outstanding taste.  Even my three year old loves them.  Need I say anything more?

column9: It would be great, if it wasn't for the poops
column10: I love the taste of these bars, but the poops always come within 30 minutes of eating just one.  It's not just poops, but crazy poops.  Still... I eat them, but I make sure I am alone at home and near a bathroom.  Those who aren't effected must have intestines of steel.  Co-workers and I were speaking about these bars this afternoon.  I'd asked if any of them had ever eaten them and, if so, what kind of side-effects resulted.  After all the embarrassed smiles and giggles, I didn't have to ask further.  Maybe they could reduce the fiber just a little?  Otherwise, the Chocolate Peanut Butter is the best.

Yes, indeed!  These are really yummy bars with a delightful chewy texture, but OH MY GOSH!  THE GAS!  I ate one this morning and am still suffering from gas and groaning bowels.  I don't give up easily, either.  I got a box of 30 of these things from Costco and have "tested" about half of them and the same thing has happened every time I've eaten one.  I am giving up and throwing the rest out.  Please note that the first listed ingredient is chicory root extract.  I looked that up online and found out that chicory root is a mild laxative!  Goodbye tasty little bars!

column9: Great for getting your fiber up...not for the weak stomach peeps
column10: I have been eating Fiber One bars for 2 years now, and I've lost 50lbs. I am a runner and I'm always thinking of ways to increase my fiber intake. Luckily Fiber One products have me covered. These bars are so easy to take with you; to the gym, work, lunch, as a snack! I buy them in bulk now and enjoy them in my lunches. The recommended amount of fiber a person should have a day is about 18-25 grams...and this one little bar can take care of 9 of those grams! How awesome is that?!  I love the chocolate ones the best, but they now have a new one call chocolate mocha! And the gas that people have talked about on these reviews goes away once your body is able to handle more fiber. I have none of those side effects now.  Enjoy!
The Good:  Fiber One Bars taste great, are high in Fiber, and are a filling snack between mealsThe Bad:  Causes extreme gas, like nothing I have eaten before, and some minor stomach cramps.

The reviews of this extraordinary product pretty much cover the bases.  Tasty?  Check.  Full of fiber?  Check.  Causes extreme gut pain?  Check.  Causes nonstop farting like you were born in New Jersey?  HELL YEAH.What can I add to this?Well, a few months back my coworkers and I drew up a contract for a spirited competition.  The contestants were to eat three bars back to back with plenty of fluid at breakfast.  The winner would be determined by the last person to use the bathroom.  Unfortunately during a test run where I consumed three bars in one sitting, I discovered that even tapping out and running at a full sprint to the bathroom was too much of a risk - especially at work!  Thank GOD I was wearing  my Ex Officio Give-N-Go Briefs!  That at least contained the rush that I experienced.We devised a different sport to compete in.  Eat one bar and then 30 minutes later go to the gym and use the elliptical machine.  You win in one of two ways:  1.  Hold out and do not pass gas at all during a 20 minute workout. However you can also win by passing enough gas to drive your competitors off of their machines.  So even if you tap out early you can still win.It is critical to use the elliptical during this challenge due to the rapid cheek movement it causes.I gotta stop eating these things.  No one wants to sit near me anymore.

I've built up a tolerance to the fiber one bars. Don't eat too many if you haven't had one in a while. It's best to slowly introduce them.I don't always eat them, maybe every 3-4 days. But when I do it's usually a binge of at least 5 or more at a time( I know, it sounds excessive but my stomach handles them no problem). To me, it's better than gorging on candy or other complete junk. After a binge I am so satisfied from the fiber, oats, and chocolate. They are always delicious every time, I never get sick of them. And after plowing through 5 or more, I know they are gonna go right through me and take other junk with them on the way out, what's better than that? enjoy!

Yes, these bars are SO tasty. They are chewy, chocolatey bars of delight.However, if you don't want to risk an embarrassing situation later, don't eat one for breakfast. It doesn't seem to happen with everyone, but I've eaten two of these in the past month, and both times they've given me horrible, annoying gas.

column9: Taste Great but hell on the stomach
column10: Wow, I had one yesterday and all afternoon and night I was filled with gas.  I couldn't figure out what I ate that caused this but I loved them so much that I was looking on line for a place to order a big box.  I'm so happy that I came across the reviews on Amazon, otherwise I would have ordered more boxes and had to get rid of them.One thing I do know is that if your body is not used to a lot of Fiber that it can upset your stomach.  What you may want to do it gradually introduce it into your diet i.e. start with a third of one and see if that bothers you.  If it does, then its not the fiber - its something else in the bar.  This is what I'm going to try because I really like them.  Thanks for all of the reviews because I'm not sure I would have figured it out.  There is a blog on the internet about these bars complaining about the same thing.  They actually wrote to the company and received a response back that they all had a good laugh for the day!!!!  The blogger said that there is chicory root in the bars and that can cause GI problems I will have to look at the ingredient list myself then look up the chicory root.  If its not that, then its the fiber which means you have to gradually get your body used to it.

column9: One of my favorite snacks! Filling and non-fattening and tasty.
column10: I started eating fibre one bars when I began Weight Watchers. I found it to be a tasty filling snack. Oats and chocolate is my favorite flavour. I don't really care for the caramel or the peanut butter ones. But the oats and chocolate ones are delicious.It's hard to find them in large packs where I am but whenever I do, I scoop them up. I find them filling either for breakfast or as a mid-day snack. I used to hide them from my kids, as I do with all my Weight Watchers stuff, but finally realized that I should be happy they were eating them too (albeit frustrated that I would be met with an empty box when I went to pack my lunch).These taste so good that it's hard to believe they are healthy.

column9: High fiber isn't necessarily a good thing!
column10: I recently cut fiber one bars out of my diet after I noticed that I get all the fiber I need in a day just by eating whole wheat bread, fruits, vegetables and nuts. If you don't have many of the aforementioned foods in your daily diet, then one or two of these a day may be a good fiber supplement. However, this comes at the cost of making you extremely gassy all through the day, which can be embarrassing and sometimes even annoying when it's more frequent than the occasional toot that slips out. IMHO, it's better to get the daily dietary fiber your body needs via the more natural means that I mentioned above.Another thing to keep in mind, especially when dieting, is that these bars are pretty high in sugar. (As much as 10g added sugar per bar!) Considering a "healthy" amount of added sugar per day maxes out at about 40-50g per day, eating a few of these bars will chew right through that cap in no time. There's also emerging research showing that eating high-sugar foods (like fiber one bars) will make you crave more sweets, leading you to eat or drink even more unhealthy things like candy bars and sodas. So if you're on a diet, eating these bars probably aren't as great for your diet as you think!I've been fiber one free for two weeks now and I'm happy for the decision. (And so are my friends!)

column9: Great Bars, with a good price
column10: These are really good chocolate oat bars, and although I know the price changes, the unit price I paid for them were pretty close to the unit price at Wal-Mart. You get 12 boxes of 5 for a total of 60 bar which is a lot. But I highly recommend them as daily snacks or even breakfast plus they're high in fiber with their being 9g per bar. There are different flavors, but Oats and Chocolate is usually the cheapest. Overall, the bars are tasty, healthy, and great for snacks. I highly recommend.

column9: Any real peanuts in the bar?
column10: I just had my first bar drawn from our kitchen cupboard. It was the Oats and Peanut Butter bar.  I was attracted by the full-sized peanuts on the package photo.  About halfway through I realized that I hadn't yet tasted a peanut.  Even the peanut butter flavor was pretty weak.  Looking back at the package I realized that the photographer had placed full sized peanuts in the photo to make it LOOK like they were part of the bar.  Old time deceptive advertising.  You wouldn't think they'd need to do that still.  But then, we are easily fooled... aren't we?

I state that you can compare, as I have, and for the money and taste and freshness, Fiber One bars are the best in quality.If it cost less, check the fiber content of how many grams of fiber, and thats the answer. You need to eat two bars, or close, to equal one Fiber One bars grams of fiber.I tried a less expensive bar at Amazon and the taste made me gag.I bought three cases and the product was very stale.All that waste of money for garbage.I am staying with my tried and true best value Fiber One.

column9: Best granola bars I've ever had!
column10: The Fiber One Oats & Chocolate granola bars are the best granola bars I've ever had -- I guess that's clear since I'm willing to buy a 12-pack.  In my opinion the Chocolate flavor is the best, and I've tried them all (the Peanut Butter is okay but not great, and the Caramel is waaay too sweet and tastes more like butterscotch).  The bars are chewy and not at all dry, and there's tons of chocolate!  Feels like an indulgent sweet treat, but you're getting 9 grams of fiber.  Yes, they are more calories than other granola bars like Quaker (140 cals vs. ~100 cals), but you get way more nutritious value, a better taste, and a more satisfying snack out of it.  What's not to love!

Most health bars taste awful. Fiber One Bars Oats & Chocolate is not bad at all. A little chewy, but it does not crumble when you bite it while other snack bars shatters to hundreds of pieces of crumbs. This one you can enjoy even if you are in front of your computer keyboard.I like the Fiber One  Granola Bars Oats & Caramel better as the chocolate tends to be a  little bit too sweet.  Also kinda small for my satisfaction.

I signed up for subscribe and save and my last delivery was June 12th! Today is September 17, 2008 and although it shows these now in stock, I still haven't been shipped mine. I've called Amazon about this a few times and cannot get anyone in the USA. The out of Country people just don't get the problem. If I suscribe to save, how can you be "out of stock?" Don't they pre-order for those that have the subscriptions? I just cancelled, they are cheaper at Sams & Costco anyway and ALWAYS in stock. Beware of this subscribe & save....you'll save all right since you won't get this. Down to a 1 star for customer service, 5 stars for taste.These bars are chewy, sweet, delicious and loaded with fiber too! If you love chocolate, you can't go wrong buying this flavor of Fiber One Bars. These make a quick meal, a snack after exercising, dessert or just ue as an addition to your fiber intake. Be careful, they become addictive and it's easy to eat another one...

I just bought these fiber one bars a couple hours ago and I'm completely satisfied with the taste, actually I was surprised it tasted so good. I will definitely purchase more in the future. The only down side is that it has to many carbs, but taking one a day for those times where you need something sweet is perfect.

I am laughing while writing this. You would NOT BELIEVE the sounds coming from my body today after eating one of these for breakfast! I feel I could float away, I have so much gas in me! They taste delicious! But this is one heck of a side effect! I've never tooted for 30 seconds straight before so it's quite amusing, but I won't be eating another one. I think I'll give the rest to people as gag gifts.

Opened a box of fiber bars from general mills took a bite to discover I bit on a crwaling worm. The color is the same as the oats, so do be careful. The product expires Feb 2013. I'm looking for the customer service dept at General Mills.

column9: Constant farting so not worth it
column10: Great flavor, but beware...it will make you have the WORST gas!  It's not worth eating. Something about all the fake "fiber".

column9: Great taste for diet and weight loss
column10: After reviewing some photos of me with my shirt off after a vacation I realized that I needed to loose some weight.  I heard fiber increases metabolism so I started buying these.  I've tried a few different brands, but these tasted the best to me.  I ended up loosing 30lbs in a month and a half by eating two of these a day, and taking soda out of my diet.  I went from 195lbs to 165lbs.  Fiber Works!  What better way to loose weight than to eat something that tastes like a treat in itself too!

Many people have been complaining about gas from these. I eat one for breakfast on workdays, and have been for awhile and never had an issue. Maybe people's bodies are used to the amount of fiber? Fiber does help "clean out" your system. Its the perfect breakfast food for me: tastes great, easy to grab n go, and pretty healthy. I also will eat one when I am craving some chocolate. So much better for you than a candy bar.

column9: Just don't eat more than one
column10: These are my favorite granola bar. I love that they have 35% of my daily fiber, but I learned the hard way to never eat more than one at a time (or a day for that matter). If you eat more than one you will have the worst gas of your life...as in you can't leave the house or be around other people.

column9: Fiber One Chewy Bars Very Satisfying
column10: The fiber bars were very satisfying when you have a craving for a snack especially, and do not want to eat something high in fat and calories.  Even children ages 7 and up will find this chewy fiber bar a healthy way of receiving a special treat!  I purchased this item from Amazon.com.  I was a little hesitant of purchasing in bulk, because I though it might possibly not be fresh.  It was very fresh.

These fiber one bars are just as tasty as a snickers but much better for your health and waistline. I would highly recommend this to anyone who has a sweet-tooth. I feel a lot less guilty chowing down on one of these instead of a twix or any other saturated fat calorie bomb gut buster.These are also great for the fact that General Mills has the box top for education on them as well. I collect these and donate them to my old school.Bottom line, these are by far the best snacking bars I have ever had in my life!

column9: Great TASTY source of soluble fiber
column10: I needed to find a source of soluble fiber that I didn't turn my nose up to.  I found it here.  LOTS of soluble fiber and a great taste.These make terrific breakfast bars (soluble fiber is easier on an empty stomach than insoluble fiber.)I gladly eat several bars a day for my fiber intake.  It's nice to have a tasty snack that really IS good for you!

I grew up eating pop tarts and cereal bars, nutri grain bars, nature valley bars, and all the other crap out there.  I promise you, nothing can compare to these fiber bars, they are so delicious I just crave them, and they have a ton of fiber in them (obviously) 9 grams I believe.  Compare that to the other bars I just mentioned, they usually have only 1, at most 2.  Fiber is very important, a fiber-rich diet can lead to a much longer life and prevent many forms of cancer.  Most health food I would agree lacks taste and substance for me, but not this.  I eat these everyday and I'm still not sick of them, and they keep me full until lunch(sometimes I may have a banana to go with it).  At first my girlfriend would not try these she said they were nasty (even though she hadn't tried them) and she continued to buy and eat Quaker Oats breakfast bars, which have the nutritional equivalent of chalk.  Finally I got her to try these and she has been hooked ever since.  They're covered in chocolate, and have a very sweet taste, but they are not high in sugar.So in conclusion.  I don't care if you're on a diet or not everyone should start eating these, now I'm just wondering when they are going to come out with Fiber One bread so I can make super healthy tasty sandwiches or Fiber One cookies so I don't have to feel bad about having dessert...who's with me?

column9: As much joy as possible for 140 calories
column10: Tasty little things. A very compelling chewiness. However, go slow at first until you know how many you can handle or you will be your family's flatulence champion (or villain, depending on your family).

Great way to combine snacking and adding additional fiber to your diet.140 caloriesTotal Far 4 grams (1.5 grams of Saturated Fat)Zero Trans FatDietary Fiber 9 gramsZero cholesterolCarbs 29 gramsSodium 95mgProtein 2 grams
I am happy to be able to buy these in case lots at a much reduced price. They arrived within a couple of days and are fresh and not damaged. I've put them on subscription.
These bars are great and help me keep my weight under control. I have one for breakfast and I am not hungry til lunch.

I hate energy bars and protein bars, but I buy them and I even try to eat them.  Most are grainy slabs and taste awful, but Fiber One Bars, especially the Chocolate variety are actually tasty.  They don't pack much other than fiber, but they still taste good and offer a nice alternative to straight candy bars that have no nutritional value.
The Fiber One Oat and Chocolate have a great taste, almost like a candy bar! Just wouldn't eat one everyday.

I've been looking for ways to get more Fiber in my diet.  I've tried the cereals.  Cereal has always been kind of a pain for me because I usually like to sleep in and it's not something I can take to work with me.  These have been great.  I can grab one on the way to work or throw one in my lunchbox.  They are a super convenient way to get my fiber.The added bonus is that they taste pretty good and satisfy my sweet tooth while being pretty low and fat and decent in calories.I'd recommend them to anyone that wants a better way to get more fiber.

My sister introduced me to these Fiber One bars, and they are just delicious!  I haven't tried the other flavors b/c I'm a chocolate lover, so...what would be the point!?!  But, these don't have any weird aftertaste or anything, and you get about 1/3 of your daily fiber in one bar for only like 130 calories!  I highly recommend these!

If you are on a diet or looking to cut calories and fat, Fiber One's line of snack bars will be a dream come true. The chocolate and caramel ones are on the sweet side, so go for Peanut Butter if you can't handle such a sweet taste. I don't care for the apple flavored ones because of their plastic, fake taste and haven't tried strawberry.These bars contain 35% of your RDA for fiber which is great! They should not give you digestion issues unless you get very little fiber normally or if you eat more than one a day. But do pay attention to the ingredient and nutrition lists. This is not health food! They are high in sugar, carbs, and have ingredients like shellac, ethanol, and hydrogenated oil. This is junk food that happens to have some redeeming qualities.5 stars for taste and 3 for health factors. Overall, I give it a 4.

I wouldn't call these health food, what with the hydrogenated oil and all, but if your goal is to increase your daily fiber intake than these bars are an easy and delicious way to accomplish your goal.

One of the better bars I've found in terms of price, taste, texture, and nutrition.  I've been eating them as "emergency snacks" as my pregancy progresses, and they do a good job.  I really like that I'm getting a good portion of my daily fiber requirement (extra important for expectant mothers) in one serving: this is hard to do with highly processed "bar" type foods.  And I like the fact it tastes like an oatmeal chocolate chip cookie rather than a sawdust or twig-textured health food.I noticed one customer said they made her sick: if you're not used to getting much fiber in your diet, jumping straight to your recommended daily allowance without a careful ramp up is quite likely to cause gastro-intestional distress.  Be careful!

These make a great mid-day snack when combined with a piece of fruit.  Not the best in terms of eliminating preservatives from your diet, but delicious.  The only thing I would change is that they come in two packs - which means a lot of extra cardboard.

column9: Great snack - 2 pts on weight watchers
column10: Great snack - only 2 pts on weight watchers. MUCH cheaper if purchased in 30/box at... er... big chain warehouse store. Too bad - I love subscribe and save for other things, but the other place is still like half of what it costs on Amazon, even with the 15% discount.Choc/peanut Curves bars (also on subscribe and save) are also a good WW snack - 1 pt. Similar taste to this, smaller slightly less dense bar.

column9: Better than a Granola Bar ... But Don't Go Overboard
column10: These things are awesome. If you weren't told they had fiber, you wouldn't know it. They taste just like junk food should - but they're good for you, and relatively healthy. Just don't eat the whole box in one sitting - they aren't kidding when they say each bar has 35% of your daily fiber allotment. If you eat two, you're at 70%, and since today's processed/fast-food culture makes us lucky to hit 50% RDA for fiber, you WILL experience gastro-intestinal upset. If you get the munchies, hit the chips, not the fiber bars.

They taste great, BUT one bar gave me VERY bad stomach pains and diarhrea for several days.  Unfortunately I didn't realize it was the bar for a week.  I just thought I was sick.  Do a google search and you'll find dozens of people with similar reactions.

column9: Great taste, very filling, and lots of fiber
column10: I love these Fiber One Bars Oats and Chocolate.  They're very tasty and satisfy my chocolate craving.  Granted, these aren't the most healthy thing in the world, but given that my other breakfast options are either a) no breakfast, b) the drive thru with the shortest line on my way to work, or c) Pop Tarts, they're far healthier than my own personal alternatives.  They're chewy, sweet and easily portable (a huge plus for a busy worker and student).I generally get far, far less of the daily recommended fiber, so this was a fantastic way for me to increase my fiber intake and actually eat breakfast most mornings.  I actually found that eating one of these in the morning along with a big bottle of water spiked with some sort of calorie free flavoring (like Crystal Light) kept me very full until lunch, and sometimes later.  So I wasn't contemplating eating my keyboard by lunchtime anymore.At 140 calories per bar, they aren't super low in calories.  But I've also tried a number of the 100-calorie bars with flavors like Oreo, Chips Ahoy, etc, and the Fiber One Oats & Chocolate are larger, more filling, way higher in fiber, and taste a lot better, all for only 40 more calories.  It does contain 4 g of fat, with 1.5 g of that as saturated (bad) fat.  On the plus side, it does have 1.5 g of monounsaturated (good) fat, no cholesterol and is low in sodium (only 90 mg or 4% RDA).The main pro for me has been the 40 pounds lost that a healthier diet and exercise helped me to achieve, and Fiber One has been a part of that healthier diet.  These are certainly healthier than my usual morning routine; I could only eat 3/4 of ONE Pop-Tart for the same number of calories (and be honest, who ever only eats even one of the Pop Tarts in the little foil pack?  Not me, I always eat both, so one of these bars is approximately 1/3 the number of calories as the two-pack of Pop Tarts, with 9 times more filling fiber).I never had the gas or upset stomach problem that others have mentioned on here, and I usually have a pretty sensitive digestive system.  If you don't usually eat much fiber, there is the off chance that you'll have a few less than pleasant reactions to increasing your fiber.  I had no such problems, and have learned that the increased fiber makes me fuller longer than pure carbs like Pop Tarts and that my digestive system seems to be working better now that I'm getting an extra boost of fiber.  Give them a try and see how they work for you!My diabetic dad and I both love these.  My dad has not noticed any significant impact on his blood sugar levels or how he feels after eating these, and they're so good that he sometimes eats two or three at a time.  He calls them his candy bars.In terms of flavor, the chocolate is my favorite.  I don't like peanut butter in anything, but I guess that flavor is okay if you like peanut butter.  I don't like the apple or the strawberry; they're too chewy and don't actually taste like fruit in any way.  The caramel was okay, but almost too sweet for me (and that's hard to accomplish!).  I haven't tried the mocha because I don't like coffee either.  The chocolate is great though, it does taste almost like a chocolate bar and is very yummy for chocoholics like me!So, overall, I highly recommend that you give these a try.  I've found these bars to be fabulous, and I stock up when they go on sale because I know that I will (eventually) eat them all.  I keep a couple in my purse, car, and desk drawer- you never known when you're going to get stuck working through lunch or sitting in traffic until Doomsday.

Every month, I send Fiber One bars to my cousin.  She has been bedridden in a nursing home for over 5 years.  AND SHE LOVES FIBER ONE!I was greatly disturbed when she called me and said she had not received her monthly shipment.  I checked with Amazon and discovered that the package had been delivered on May 4th.  Therefore, I can only speculate what happened.I don't know who is more distressed - my cousin or me.  She LOVES her Fiber One Oats and Chocolate!  It serves as a healthy evening snack or when she is watching television and gets "the hungries."I hope there will be no further experiences of this type and that I can continue to send her Fiber One every month.Thank you for the opportunity to relate this story to you and for the wonderful Fiber One products.
i love these bars! I was sad to find out that I spent almost 2x as much as I could have - the warehouse store had it for 9.99 for 30.
My favorite fiber bar. It is really in disguise as a health bar that tastes really good. That is always a plus for my taste buds!

column9: A daily source of GI distress (cramping & flatulence)
column10: I ate approximately 4 of these rather deceptively delicious bars through a one day period and had one of the worst episodes of cramping and gas in my life. And on top of that, I was at work, orchestrating a cacophony of trumpet piercing farts in the acoustically optimal office restroom. I had to sit on the toilet about 8 times that day and by the end of the night, the mucosa of my rectum was prolapsing out of my anus. It was burning down there as if I had an enema with a pint of Tabasco sauce. If you insist on eating these, be sure you are alone and at home.

column9: Trip #10 to the toilet after one bar, WATCH OUT!
column10: A co-worker left these in the breakroom. I ate one up, boy was it delicious. Within 90 minutes I had to go to the bathroom, it has continued all day. Gastric Distress to the max! I read the wrapper, it has 9 grams of fiber. If you are not a large consumer of fiber in your diet, I say eat 1/3 of a bar and stop. See what happens. Due to the unexpected results I had to give this a one star. No wonder the bars were up for grabs in the breakroom! I wonder who else in the office is suffering.

At roughly 55 cents (subscribed price) per unit, I unfortunately found out (too late) that this was at least 20 cents more than my local grocery store. I called Amazon and there was nothing they would do about it. I suggest checking out pricing at your local grocery store prior to purchasing this item. Don't make the same mistake I did. Its a good product, but sadly overpriced on Amazon.com

This bar is very very sweet and contains many ingredients that I have tried so hard to stay away from for the past few years.  Anyone interested in their health will find fibre in much more healthy foods. If the ingredient list had been provided, I probably would not have made the purchase in the first place.. duh

This product is known to give people gas.  I actually counted over a period of several days and each bar caused me to fart 18-22 times from four to six hours after I ate it.  If you live alone or are on cipro for athrax exposure and your intestines are sterile, maybe you can live with that side effect.  Otherwise, it's better to give to someone as a joke than to eat yourself.Other than that, it tastes pretty good if not too sweet.Additional comments 17 months after my above review:First, let me state on their box General Mills had plenty of room to educate about different fiber sources while promoting the variety of fiber products they produce.I had a chance to try Target's generic competitor to this food product and found the same stinkin' results.Using Wikipedia (yes a printed dictionary would be more reliable) I see that the main ingredient of these products, called "Chicory Root Extract", is full of an indigestible sugar called inulin that ferments into gas in your large intestine. Inulin is no doubt responsible for the too-sweet taste of the bars that I mentioned in my first review 17 months ago.Another vegetable containing inulin is the Jerusalem Artichoke for which Wikipedia has the following snippet:Gerard's Herbal, printed in 1621, quotes the English planter John Goodyer on Jerusalem artichokes:"which way soever they be dressed and eaten, they stir and cause a filthy loathsome stinkingwind within the body, thereby causing the belly to be pained and tormented, and are a meat morefit for swine than men."Ergo I conclude Fiber One bars are more fit for swine than men. If people knew that in year 1621, why is General Mills putting out an inulin-filled product now? And why in all their biased, pro-fiber packaging is there not a single mention of the gastrointestinal side effects known to effect a large swath of the population for almost 400 years?  Corporate food scientists don't just throw random boxes from the undesirable vegetable dispensary into a stew, and somehow get instant FDA approval and national distribution channels, folks.

column9: Fiber One Bars - Palm Kernel Oil!
column10: Are these tasty? Very! High in fiber? Of course. But come on General Mills! Palm Kernel Oil?For those who have to watch their saturated fat content BEWARE - one of these bars have 9% of the recommended daily allowance. Palm Kernel Oil? Shame on you General Mills!

I have tried and enjoyed the Fiber One 90 Calorie Chocolate bars, so I thought I would try these Oats and Chocolate bars since they were on sale.  After making my way through two boxes (I usually eat one a day as a snack).  At this point, I can't eat anymore.  The taste is just bad.  It's not disgusting or anything, but they do not taste good by any means.  I can only handle eating one a week now, or have one daily and always have something else better to eat right afterward.  Oats and Chocolate made me think I was going to get something that tasted like Quaker Granola Bars.  That is not the case, I don't even know that chocolate is an ingredient.  They just taste bad.  Try the Fiber One 90 Calorie Chocolate bars - somehow, the healthier bars taste better.

Per doctors orders, I am trying to add more fiber to my diet.  I purchased these with high hopes after reading all the positive reviews.  The texture is a lot like sawdust and cardboard mixed with chocolate chips.  I could not choke it down without a full 20 ounces of water.  I know you are supposed to increase your water intake with a high fiber diet, but I dont want to have to eat something where I feel like I am gagging on it.  These are going into the office slush bag of food no one would eat unless desperate.
Used to take to work for lunch. Tastes OK but is not real filling and a bit bland. Still a good idea for a quick meal.

i received this as a gift and i use it primarily in cocktails. in a standard cocktail of 1.5oz liquor, dash water, bitters, etc. i use 3 drops from a dropper. in fact, before i instituted the dropper, it was way too intense in mixed drinks. i'd like to see a conversion from boyajian as to uses in baking, drinks, etc. all in all, it's a great product, perfect taste when used in the correct amount, and keeps forever in the fridge.

I started using Boyajian citrus oils years ago upon the recommendation of a professional baker/chef when I was making my daughter's wedding cake.  Now I use them in almost anything I would normally grate zest into, or I just use a fraction of the zest for the visual appeal.  NOTE: THIS IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR LEMON JUICE.  Otherwise, a few drops of the oil is plenty to impart the tang of real lemon to most recipes.  It can last for years if kept refrigerated. Having the bottles of oil on-hand is a huge money, time and space saver;  I no longer have to buy and store the fruit, or as much of it, and I don't have to take the time to grate it.  Concentrated, intense, delicious!  Pure LEMON Oil (Boyajian) 148ml (5 oz)
Unable to find lemon oil locally, I ordered online to save time. The product was delivered within the week, was packaged well and was as described on the website. I could not be happier. Thank you!

I bought this to make some of the recipes out of "Luscious Lemon Desserts" by Lori Longbotham.  It was well wrapped, but there was just a small amount of leakage from the trip - which ended up making the kitchen smell wonderful for several days!  Added to cookies and cakes, it is just delicious.

column9: please read the item fully before buying! not blueberry!!!!
column10: please read the item fully before buying! not blueberry!!!! this is a mix thats mostly blueberry but ends up tasting like a concoction not blueberry.... I didnt read it well enough to understand this is not blueberry. tasty. works well stove top and oven. if you are like me looking to get blueberry itself and not a mix this will totally NOT work and you will be running to stores looking for a backup. if your looking for tasty you will be pleased. and this big bottle will go a Long way.

I love Carl's Gourmet spices and use the regular roast rub all the time.  I've added this one to my spice cabinet.  Tastes delicious on chicken and pork!  Even a little sprinkle on Tilapia tastes delicious.  A nice addition to a variety of spice rubs!

column9: one of the best I have tried
column10: I do LOTS of BBQ, and have tried hundreds of rubs. This one is sugar free, lower in salt, and tastes as good or better as any rub twice the price. It is good on chicken (I add some thyme as well) ribs, and pulled pork. Good enough that I have given it as a Christmas gift to BBQ savvy friends.

I buy this at my local supermarket and it find's its way into a lot of things I cook.  Most notable is the deeeelicious chicken this rub can make! My family & friends love my chicken salad and the key is this spice rub that goes on the chicken breasts before I bake them.

column9: nice for babyback ribs, dry rub!
column10: very good for dry rubbing baby back ribs, tastes great, gives ribs a beautiful color!
My husband and I love this seasoning it is soooo delicious!  We love to use it on Tritip and pork!
Joseph's Lite Cookies Sugar Free Chocolate Walnut Cookies, 11 oz bagsCARL'S GOURMET SPICES ARE THE BEST.I AM ADDICTED to the OL' Western Barbecue Spice.IT GETS 5 STARS!

i drink community coffee-i like expresso-i like a little sharp bite-but no after taste - this is a quality coffee- i like it a lot-and i have shared it with friends who have like tastes-it doesn't cloy in your mouth like some columbians- if you want a rich coffee in the morning-i think you will like this one-I DO

The Ginger People are on to something.  My husband use to pop Tums like crazy.  He now chews on a ginger chew.  Very effective and all natural.  Try the plain ginger chews too.  They have a variety of flavors.The Ginger People Ginger Candy Sampler Pack

I didn't think I would like these but I read the other 2 reviews and decided to try them.  They really are great!!  If you are thinking you like coffee and ginger but not together, just order them.  You will be pleasantly surprised.

column9: Oh yum yum yum yum yum!!
column10: These are fantastic. The coffee and ginger together are just the best blend ever. I was leery when I picked them up (somewhere else) but found I couldn't stop eating them. They are very addictive. If you love ginger and you love coffee - you will be in heaven. If you like either one - give it a shot, they are absolutely delicious. :D

These are probably my favorite of the ginger chews made by Ginger People. The coffee flavor is perfectly balanced with the ginger to provide warmth in the mouth without over-powering the coffee flavor.  They are sweet, but not overly sweet, so even though I like my coffee black, the flavor is very pleasing.  Try them, you won't be disappointed!
Description says 3.2 ounces. These were a small bag that sells everywhere else for $2 or less. These were $5. Ripoff!

My dogs refuse to eat the light green hard side of these treats. They do enjoy the soft dark green side, but they easily eat off that part and leave over the other side completely. The two sides aren't as 'together' as they look on the package, and it is super easy for my little dogs to pull off the soft side. I have never successfully been able to get either of my dogs to eat the whole thing, and I the other half is just completely wasted. These treats do smell really good, and might be good for a bigger dog that will just eat the whole thing instead of separating it. However, I would not recommend these treats as my dogs are NOT picky eaters and if they reject the light green hard side, I have a feeling most dogs won't like it. Considering the price, it just isn't worth it if the dogs will only eat half.

column9: Sprite-esque drink with no added sugar
column10: All of the Knudsen spritzers I've tried are good. This is not one of my favorites, though it's still pretty good. It's similar enough to Sprite, but could use a little more carbonation. There's NO added sugar or corn syrup -- just fruit juice and sparkling water. One 10.5 oz can contains 120 calories and 28g of sugars.

column9: goes with everything you regularly sweeten
column10: This stuff has really helped me kick the sugar habit. I use it in tea and coffee and smoothies with no difficulty. It is extremely portable and mixes easily (I almost turned away from stevia because I tried the powder form first). The taste is as subtle or strong as you like. Some people may take some time to adjust to the taste and find the right amount for their tastes but it is worth trying as it has no blood sugar effect and no side effects (ie aspartame). I get the subscription price at amazon and this is way below the lowest price I've found.

This flavor tastse vary good in coffee. It only takes literally 3 drops to flavor an 8 ounce cup of coffee, any more and it might be too strong. This bottle will last me a very long time. Love the taste

I have read some of the reviews indicating that it is too sweet and has an after taste.  I think it is fine.  You only need 2-3 drops. If you use a regular creamer, such as coffemate, the calories add up fast.
My favorite flavor for water! It makes me want to drink more water and curbs my sweet tooth! Highly recommend!

column9: Sweet Leaf Vanilla Creme Liquid Stevia
column10: Exactly as described at the best price !  I searched the entire Internet and by far this was the best deal on Amazon!
The vanilla is pleasant enough, but it still has that Stevia aftertaste.I'm going back to sugar (in moderation, of course).

I love Stevia because it's the only non-sugar sweetener that doesn't give me a stomachache (I am a reformed Diet Coke addict for this unfortunate reason).  This form of Stevia is super convenient (no more dealing with a zillion little packets), and I love the vanilla creme flavor!My favorite uses (besides the usual tea/coffee) are for plain yogurt and club soda (trust me, it makes it into a really tasty pseudo-cream soda!).

When I first tried Stevia, it was in one of those little packets, and it was in powdered form.  Yuck!  I was not a fan.Since I want to avoid both real sugar AND artificial sweeteners, I was disappointed....UNTIL I found out about this liquid stevia.It doesn't have the bitterness and strange flavor that the powdered form has.  And the slight vanilla flavor makes my coffee delicious.  In fact, when I go to my favorite coffee house, the coffee doesn't taste "right" to me until I add a dropper full of this Vanilla Creme stevia.I keep one bottle at home, one bottle at work, and one bottle in my purse...so anytime I want coffee, I am ready.  The price here on Amazon can't be beat, so I will be buying it here from now on.

Sweet Leaf Vanilla Creme Flavored Liquid Stevia, 2-Ounce Bottle is the perfect 0 calorie all natural sweetener. I really enjoy the extra flavor this particular liquid stevia adds to my coffee. I don't experience any after-taste with this one either. My favorite is the chocolate. But since I'm allergic to chocolate this is an excellent substitute!

It adds a nice sweet flavor to my coffee.  I combine it with a little spoonable Stevita.  Better than Starbucks.  Its sweeting strength is a little weaker than I anticipated, but it will still last maybe 3 months because I combine it with the spoonable Stevita.  I iniatially used it without the spoonable stevita, but didn't like the taste.  Combining it is perfect.  For a 12oz. cup of coffee I use about 1/4 tsp. of spoonable Stevita and 7 drops of this van.liquid Stevita and some almondmilk for the cream.

I bought it as a substitute for powder Stevia hoping for better after-taste.I am disappointed. The dropper design is faulty and I can't get drops in the coffee with out getting some on my fingers - an avoidable waste.I also found that one needs to use more than a few drops to get the sweet taste.The powder form is more economical if somebody makes half-packets of powder?

column9: Great flavor, concentrated Stevia is expensive though
column10: I like this flavor, the dry Stevia doesn't taste good as good as the concentrate. In stores the basic price is $14.99, so besides shipping this item is priced right, only place I found flavored Stevia was a local health food store, it wasnt easy to find, so this may be a good option.
It takes only a few drops to transfer a glass of milk into a sweet vanilla drink.  I love it.

column9: Sharper taste than expected, unless heated
column10: I prefer Splenda or xylitol for baking because neither adds the bitterness I find in stevia, but sometimes use liquid stevia for sweetening other things - especially my morning oatmeal, which is what I wanted the "vanilla creme" stevia for.  Since a dietician has persuaded me to add textured vegetable protein to my oatmeal to add some protein to my breakfast, I have to flavor it with something or it tastes like dog kibble.  This stuff plus some cinnamon really helps breakfast to taste pretty good again.I do find it's best when added to the water before the oatmeal is microwaved.  When used to sweeten oatmeal that's already cooked, it has that sharp stevia aftertaste and I was wondering where the "creme" in its "vanilla creme" name comes from.  But cooking makes a big difference - it's just fine after cooking along with the oatmeal.  I haven't tried using it with anything else.
This is a very yummy, sweet, healthy option for sugar. And I believe it is alchol free.Best liquid stevia I have had.

I have purchased this sweetener for the second time now, I do not use it all the time or on everything, but I use it often enough esp. when I am trying to cut back on agave or other high glycemic sweeteners. Its flavor does not always work with coffee, but it does if you also add a bit of the usual sweetener you use. It works well on: yogurt, hot cereal, cold cereal, hot chocolate milk (home made). It is concentrated ergo economical, but I find I use more of it after I get used to the taste again, on cereal I sometimes go up to almost a dropper full, esp. with cinnamon or pumpkin spices which blend well with this sweetener. I like the idea that I am cutting back on sugar and also the vanilla flavor improves the stevia taste for an unaccostumed palate. Saying one gets used to the stevia flavor is very subjective, as even for me there are days I just do not want this taste and others I am OK with it. Again, my method to use it except on hot cereal and yogurt where it works fine, is to add just a little of another sweetener, or conversely, support the overall sweetness of a liquid drink with about three drops of this stevia mix when I want to cut back on sugary type sweeteners. The tongue experiences different sweeteners in various ways, and I just like to have this on hand always, as inevitably, I use it either with another sweetener or straight with cinnamon type spices. Be careful to start with very little it gets very intense and off flavor fast, and if you just dose it right it will taste fine. Less is more -- you can always add a drop at a time as needed. Once you find your approximate "dose" -- mine is like three drops in liquids max or the flavors just go south for me... and a half dropper on solid foods - but I do like my things pretty sweet. With proper experimentation and without instant rejection of the flavors, mostly due to using too much product, this can become a staple in your home too.

It is difficult to review food items because everyone has taste preferences that vary.  I purchased this because I wanted some sort of sweetener for my coffee that would not affect my blood sugars. I found the flavoring to be a bit overpowering.  I ended up using less than the recommended amount.  I only use one drop in my coffee. I would suggest you start with one drop and then taste and adjust accordingly.To me the vanilla flavor tastes artificial but you can't find any information on the label other that it contains "natural" flavoring.But it does what it promises which is to sweeten and flavor. It will also last for a long time since only drops are used.
I put in more drops than the directions indicate are needed but the result is a scrumptious cup of coffee! I keep one in my purse and now that I've found this, I'll never be without it. GREAT!!
A little goes a long way, but enclosed dropper makes it really easy to control the amount used.  I've only used this in my coffee, but I'm looking forward to trying it in a few recipes.

column9: made great calorie free coffee flavoring
column10: Had to give up creamer in my coffee,this made my mornings do-able! Not bad on apples either,it had a little wang to it but about the same as other sweetners

All of these flavors of Stevia from Sweet Leaf are good, but Vanilla Creme is my very favorite! Use in coffee, tea, and sometimes a little in my bottle of water if I'm getting tired of drinking it plain
Sweet Leaf Vanilla Creme Flavored Liquid Stevia is a great addition to smoothies as well as hot and cold coffee drinks. My new favorite is espresso, coconut milk and 5 drops of vanilla stevia. Yum!

Extremely Fast delivery!! I can now follow my diet and enjoy my coffee, without adding sugar. The drops made my coffee taste very creamy and good. Thanks a lot!! Warning: Don't taste the liquid on it's own..very very sweet!!
Easy to use and great flavor. I like to use to sweeten plain yogurt.  Less expensive on amazon than in store.

Maybe my expectations were too high. Heeding the warnings about adding too much I started with 8 oz of bottled seltzer and added a few drops. The taste was more of a hint than a true flavoring so I added a little more, figuring if I got the taste I liked I'd start from scratch and get a better measurement. It never happened for me. When I added enough to create some flavor I also found an aftertaste that was somewhat alcohol-y. Not a problem for most people but I strongly dislike the taste of alcohol so it's not good for me. Played with it some more and never got a satisfactory result. Into the fridge, back of the shelf.A couple of weeks later I came home with some diet orange soda. Thought I'd try it again and see if I could make some orange cream soda and voila! Delicious. I say this having only tried one 8 oz serving and I made it a little too sweet but I have no doubt that once I get the ratio correct I'll add this to any orange soda I drink from now on. I'll probably try it with other flavors too altho orange seems to be the sure thing.
Sweetleaf vanilla stevia has very good flavor. No calories and good for you. The best choice in sweetners. I have ordered several bottles of this product, i use it everyday in water and in my tea.

I'm glad I read the reviews saying to only use a few drops in a beverage. Too many drops and it quickly goes from delicious to strange and bitter. The directions on the bottle say 5-8 drops, but I find 2 or 3 is perfect in a 12 oz drink or a cup of yogurt.

column4: H. R. Smith "Kickin'  it home school"
column10: Just a few drops of this Vanilla Creme flavored stevia turns a glass of ordinary water into a sweet-tasting treat. There's no bitterness, no aftertaste, and no licorice undertones that I have heard some stevia users complain about when trying other brands. This is just a pure, lovely vanilla sweetness. It's also great in smoothies, baked goods, and oatmeal!
The bottle recommends 5-8 drops, but honestly just 2 drops in my coffee or tea is perfect. No calories, sweet, natural & great vanilla taste!
This works wonders in coffee, tea or baking. I didn't give it a full 5 stars because the stevia aftertaste is  still quite strong compared with other sugar alternatives.

Sugar is toxic, it kills, it feeds illness, switch and do what's best for your body.

I hate Stevia in the powder form, but, the liquid is great and so convenient.  I particularly like the Vanilla flavor the best because it is fabulous in so many things such as coffee, pancakes, sparkling water (makes it like creme soda) and so much more.  I highly recommend it.  I'm not crazy about Chocolate Rasberry and the Lemon Drop is ok.  The Valencia Orange is great in water.

I like the Sweet Leaf Vanilla Creme Flavored Liquid Stevia. I use it to sweeten my coffee and various other things. It tastes good when I want something other than plain stevia.

No complains on the delivery time or a package, everything was fine. It's just the taste - it is horrible - so bitter and artificial! I can't imagine how people can like it and use it all the time, it changes the taste completely, like a drop of kerosine in coffee! Total waste of money.

column9: This does not work. All this did was make me go to the bathroom every day, other then that i gained weight.
column10: this left a bad taste in my month at all times, i tried to use it in every thing but just couldn't stand the taste of it .It was like drinks equal times 5 omg this was really bad.

I have tried the vanilla on cereal, in a smoothie and I don't really like the flavor.  It seems too bland to me.  I don't know that I would purchase it again.  I think it is a matter of what a person likes.  I have never liked Vanilla  ice cream either so that is probably just me.
I ordered a few items and completely forgot that I ordered it, till I needed it in my cooking, unfortunately I have never received it, but its been more than 30 days.

column9: Tastes Delicous but made my belly hurt
column10: I discovered Stevia about a year ago (around the same time I found out I had to give up sugar!) and really I like the taste of stevia so much I don't even miss sugar...okay well maybe I miss sugar a little bit but eliminating sugar from my diet would of been much more difficult if it weren't for stevia.One thing to be aware of is that many stevia products have an ingredient called xylitol which if you have a sensitive stomach it can give you belly aches from just ingesting a little bit.  I found this out the hard way, not a big deal because I was able to return the product without a hassle, great customer service on amazon.  I have learned that pure stevia powder, 30 Grams (1.06 Oz) Stevia 95% Steviosides Bulk Powder contains no xylitol and certain liquids do to but if they do not explicitily say it in the product description, you can be sure that it will contain xylitol since its cheaper to sell it that way.  I'm just glad that I have an alternative to sugar substitues like equal and splenda because for some reason my taste buds could never get use to those artifical sweeteners.
I make my own natural vanilla creme soda with this. Sparkling water and a few drops,very yummy. Doesnt spike by blood sugars like sodas made with artifical sweeteners or sugar. Great for diabetics.

I'm a bona fide fan of Stevia. I ordered this bottle after I read so many positive reviews, but I was disappointed in the distinct aftertaste of this product. I much prefer the unflavored Stevia granules I have been using for over a year.

I purchased liquid stevia in an effort to use more natural sugars in my baking. I tried simply replacing white sugar with liquid stevia in my favorite recipes. I went to Sweet Leaf's website and used their conversion chart. I found that 1 tsp of liquid stevia for every 1 cup of sugar was too much. The intial taste was ok but had a strong aftertaste that stayed in your mouth for awhile. I later tried recipes specifically calling for liquid stevia. These recipes tasted quite good and typically used less liquid stevia.

column9: Great natural replacement for sugar-free syrups
column10: I stopped using sugar-free coffee syrups and switched to naturally calorie-free flavored Stevia. I didn't want to use artificial sweeteners anymore, and this was a good option. Stevia does leave a slight after-taste, but it's not enough to not use this product. Try it!

column9: A little goes a long way
column10: I bought this to add to my protein shakes because I am eliminating artificial sweetners (Splenda, this means you) from my diet. I am very happy with my purchase. A few drops is all that I need, so the bottle should last a while.

column9: Got off my diet soda addiction
column10: I love this vanilla stevia.  I use it and other flavored stevias from the same company to flavor and sweeten naturally carbonated water (Perrier).  In fact it tastes good even in plain filtered water--not necessarily carbonated.  Also delicious in herbal teas.  These drinks with these flavored stevias really did get me off my soda addiction.  Previously I just couldn't give up the soda.  Now I love these stevia-flavored drinks so much I don't even miss the sodas.

My chiropractor recommended Stevia as an alternative to the artificial sweeteners I had been using.  I had been having chronic migraines, which he deduced were a result of my use of Aspartame.  Initially I was skeptical, but decided to give it a shot anyway.  I am happy to say that since I now use Stevia instead of any artificial sweeteners, I'm headache free!  Stevia comes in lots of flavors, even rootbeer, which I've used in sparkling water in place of diet soda - it's delicious and no headaches!  What could be better ...highly recommend! (PS this is the best price I've found anywhere ...)

I did a lot of research looking for the best reviewed stevia and chose this of the 2 (I like the liquid extract, I make a lot of cold drinks and didn't want to deal with dissolving anything). I have used stevia for 3 years now and have always had good, but not great stevia. Higher quality stevia, more pure that is, doesnt give that aftertaste of bitter liquorish. I didn't taste that at all in this stevia, and I definitely looked for it. Could be the flavoring they add to this, but either way the aftertaste isnt there. I bought this product for the first time 7 months ago.  I bought NOW Foods Stevia Liquid Extract Alcohol, 8 Ounce Bottle three months later.  My motive was to compare these products and see which one is best for me.I will try to be as detailed as possible.  So again I am evaluating "Sweet Leaf: Liquid Stevia Vanilla Creme" and "Now Foods: Better Stevia Original".At first, I expected Better Stevia to be what the packaging described, a better alternative to Stevia drinkers.  I expected it to be exactly what they advertised in its packaging:-Better tasting-Just as healthyetc.To compare them, I alternated an average of 6 drops into my morning coffee everyday.==Taste Evaluation==After everyday usage of these two products and after testing them extensively; I see no -significant- difference between the two in taste.  Please do take into consideration that I did not test these by serving suggestion amount (see Suggested Serving below).==Ingredients==Now let's talk about the ingredients.  Both products claim to be made with natural ingredients.  "Sweet Leaf: Liquid Stevia Vanilla Creme"  lists "natural flavors" apart from "Stevia extract".  "Now Foods Better Stevia Original" lists "water", "certified Organic Stevia extract" and "11% alcohol".Sweet Leaf has quite an advantage, since it does not list alcohol as an ingredient.I wanted more evidence about ingredients.  I thought that Sweet Leaf was trying to pull as fast one, by passing alcohol as a "natural flavor"; like many companies have done.So I visited the Sweet Leaf website and found this: "SweetLeaf Stevia® Sweetener does not use chemicals, alcohols, solvents or enzymes at any stage of the extraction and purification process."Bingo.  Sweet Leaf has -no alcohol-.==Suggested Serving and Packaging=="Sweet Leaf: Liquid Stevia Vanilla Creme" serving suggestion is 5 to 8 drops and contains a dropper for easier administration of the product.  You can count exactly how many drops you're serving.  As long as you don't go beyond 7-8 drops it should not be bitter at all."Now Foods Better Stevia Original" serving suggestion is 1 to 4 drops and has a split-open cap that it's very messy.  You can't count by drops, usually it spills to the body of the container.  It is very difficult to measure exactly how much you're administering.  I found that many times the bitterness was noticeable due to not knowing how much I was using.Final evaluation from 1 to 5.Taste:"Sweet Leaf: Liquid Stevia Vanilla Creme" = 5"Now Foods Better Stevia Original" = 5Ingredients:"Sweet Leaf: Liquid Stevia Vanilla Creme" = 5"Now Foods Better Stevia Original" = 4Suggested Serving and Packaging:"Sweet Leaf: Liquid Stevia Vanilla Creme" = 5"Now Foods Better Stevia Original" = 2All in all Sweet Leaf wins, for several reasons.  The packaging makes it very easy to serve the product properly. When I used the Sweet Leaf dropper with the Better Stevia I found that 4 drops weren't bitter.  But adding 8 drops of Better Stevia started to make my drink bitter.  So Better Stevia claims it tastes better, as long as you follow their serving suggestion.  Sweet Leaf tastes better otherwise.And to folks who really care about their alcohol intake for whatever reason; Sweet Leaf claims to have none.

I was so relieved to have found a great way to reduce the sugar in our diets and still have such a great sweet taste. It was perfect, I was happy. But then, strange symptoms started to surface. At first I got headaches, which became increasingly severe, and then backaches that felt like spinal 'brain freeze' (when you eat something too cold too fast.) It didn't occur to me at first that it could be at all related to the new Stevia. Then my toddler started telling me he was itchy all over. Then I got my menstrual cycle 2 weeks early. Finally it dawned on me that it could be related to the Stevia since this was the only thing at all that had changed in our diets. I googled 'adverse reactions to Stevia' and found several webpages where people described symptoms identical to mine. I was truly shocked. I stopped the Stevia... all the symptoms went away almost immediately. I realize now that there is a difference between the flavored liquid Stevia, which contains a 'proprietary blend' and 'natural flavors' (which could mean anything) and just the straight powder with nothing added (I haven't tried that, but won't now.) It also occurs to me that maybe the only Stevia that can truly be considered historically safe is the actual leaf itself, straight off the plant out of the garden. I still believe Stevia's safety record in the countries where it originated, but I think something has probably been lost in translation with the processing of it here in the US. Just my opinion. It should also be noted that anyone with allergies to ragweed should not take Stevia because it can cause asthma attacks. Hope this helps someone.

Long live Camper Van Beethoven!! This is a blessing for long time CVB fans who didn't have a chance to upgrade their collection to CD before most of this went out of print.  Wow, where to begin?  CVB was a band that matured on record, so to speak, so this is really a fascinating and entertaining listen from beginning to end.  Of course you get the endearing and humorous debut album with goofy anthems ala "Take the Skinheads Bowling" and various folk/ska instrumentals; the increasingly warped and psychedelic "II & III"; and this collections' centerpiece: the self titled 3rd album!!  Forget the editorial remark above about them "scratching their heads out loud" on this because there's nothing confused, unfocused, or tentative about this album.  I'd say it's a characteristically irreverent and eclectic psych-rock masterpiece.  The song writing has fully matured with the sarcastic humor still intact, and it seems to be intentionally conceived as an album that gets stranger and stranger as it goes on, with the group mastering every diverse style they apply themselves to.  I could go on and on about this album, but suffice it to say it's a classic.  "Camper Vantiquities", the 4th CD is a top notch odds and ends collection containing perhaps the best Camper song ever: "Seven Languages" and the Harrison/Starkey composition "Photograph."  Finally, the live CD is a competent but not revelatory live set from 1990 with 2 songs from 1988.  I would've prefered to hear an earlier and more chaotic live recording, but I'm sure the quality wouldn't have been as good.  All in all, you can't go wrong with this.  The packaging is quality: a thick , bright orange box with the 5 Cds in simple glossy slip cases, (well, the box is relatively thin but it's made of nice thick cardboard) and a full color booklet with 2 essays.  One is an entertaining first-hand account of what Santa Cruz was like when Camper formed; the other is a dry and factual journalists view on the Camper "phenomenon" MUCH LIKE THIS REVIEW.  I hope it was helpful.  Rock on Comrades!!!

column9: Camper van Beethoven is the greatest rock band ever
column10: Well, maybe not "the" greatest, but one of the best.  This set brings together the earlier stuff which is slightly more quirky than the two albums they did for Virgin.  Some of it is even sort of challenging, but mixed in are some songs as lovable as a soft fluffy kitten with a ball of yarn like "Take the Skinheads Bowling" and "Good Guys & Bad Guys".  There was this one story about them one time when they played in Philly and stayed with the Dead Milkmen for the night.  It's a great story, but probably shouldn't be repeated here.  When I first picked up a guitar (actually the first time I picked up a guitar after hearing the third album) I wanted to play "Good Guys & Bad Guys" but I was the only keyboard player in the band so I got stuck playing the keyboard part which is a lot more tasty after you play it a few times.  We can thank our lucky stars that these guys are touring again.  I was heartbroken when they broke up and Cracker always sounded a little too sanitized.  This set is almost like another album coming out, except that the songs came out before.  It's beautiful.

Finally, a collection of the best Camper Van Beethoven albums (I think there is one album missing from the band, a  major label release with intentionally clean over-production).  I had been waiting years for this dream CD, as I only possessed each one in vinyl.  Some people like to listen to a full album that has a recognizable identity in its sonic experience.  You will not get that from Camper, as they instead offer a faint, mysterious familiarity in musical pieces that can tweak your ears in two opposing directions, even during the simplist compositions.  If that sounds appealling, you can correctly guess that boredom cannot maintain a presence with this compilation.Categorizing this music is impossible, again due to so many style changes.  Psycho-country?  Unpretentious garage-rock with arena-sized talent?  Low-fi Hillbilly Jazz?  Spraycan Art-rock?  Gritty Underground Surf? Poor rich kids with Mischievous Aspirations transferring their energy into music? Kerouac whack?  How about calling it a "Flexible Soup".  It's anything but smooth, yet occassionally you find David Lowery's penchant for small club-guitar rock sneaking through (after CVB dismantled, he became the leader of the successful pop-rock group, Cracker).  It may be easier to instead think of the band as a group of hyper-static fellows whose medications are almost, but not quite at the right dosage.  They're simply possessed by friendly demons with a spiritual intent to entertain and cause wonder. Each album collectively draws numerous inspirations and styles, completely entertaining the listener through lyrics and musicianship on a variety of traditional and obscure instruments.  One can only imagine the pure enjoyment the band had while first writing then performing these before an audience.  For two decades now, I've held a relentless belief that CVB would make the most amusing backyard-party band -- sure to make Granmma Nelly dance alongside her pierced third generation of family one moment and then cover her bleeding ears when the next song begins.  However, I believe the band's intent is not to frighten or shock, but to instead expose the wealth of musical styles that one listener despises while another reaches a glee plateau.  Be sure that these same two listeners will switch positions when a later tune begins.  Are you prepared to enjoy the best of many worlds?Picturesque landscapes are lyrically drawn with a slacker-like intelligence in unimportant poignancy, the next moment you are drawn into a global hoe-down, followed then by crafty psychedelica mixed with raw instrumentals, closing with an guitar orchestra jamout with lead played by a screaming violin chant.  Add a half-tablespoon of sugar Wiseguy and serve.  Add this to your collection if you appreciate bands that are like no other.  Some tracks will prompt you to ask "Why?", yet with an immediate second thought you'll smile and say "Why hasn't Anyone Else?"[I noticed that CVB had recently made a handful of live performances after a long time apart.  I've caught several of their shows and recommend all to give your mind a jolt of electricity that is surprisingly pleasant.  You will walk away wide-eyed at the unrealized potential and wasted energy we swallow in 99% of today's music. ]

So for 10 possible different flavors I only received five and 50% was one flavor.  Furthermore they were all date stamped before the date I ordered. I certainly hope that is not a sell by date.  This is not what I expected.

I was very excited when i saw this product, i'm one of those people eager to try anything, and I've had exotic meats before in a number of ways, through friends that hunt I've enjoyed home made dishes made from a wide variety of game animals, and i've had less common animals like ostrich, kangaroo, and aligator that i ordered on like and cooked myself, and i've even had a few of these meats as jerky by other companies. I like the meats of the animals they made these jerkies from, i need to stress that point, because otherwise you may think that is what my problem is. it's not, this product was AWFUL!! these were some of the worst cured meat snacks I've ever had.  Is it possible to rate something and give it no stars? because that is what this product deserves. the meat managed somehow to be both bland and surprisingly foul, and coated with enough grease to lubricate an engine. I have tried several of the strips and sticks and found that to be a universal condition. I can only think that the people who wrote the rave reviews for this product did so without tasting it. this is dreadful stuff, suited only for those who simply want the novelty of claiming they ate strange animals and don't care what it tasted like. this meat was not fit for human consumption, in fact, i wouldn't even give it to my dog. I won't be buying anything else from buffalo bob.

Really excited when it got her today, then I opened it up! All but two were buffalo. One was wild boar and the last one was rotten moldy Elk. Yum. Thank you Amazon for refunding my money at least!! I selected two day shipping, so it got here fast. Please explain how something dehydrated goes putrid in two days? My guess is they didn't even attempt to look at it before throwing it into a box.
For some of the flavors, the beef (its mixed in with all flavors) it's overpowering. The venison is super tough to bite through too.
Bought this for my dad for fathers day. They're ok, I've tasted worse... and better. I have tried the honey ham one. Weird, tastes kind of like a hot dog.

I bought these for my boyfriend as part of his easter basket. I was hoping the variety would at least be close to what is shown, but it was lacking in aligator, had several doubles and once you look closely reads made with BEEF on almost all of them. So you aren't truly getting exotic jerky.I was displeased, but being the meat eating boy he is, HE LOVED THEM. Mentioned the spicy ones are SPICY though.He enjoyed them, but I don't think they were worth the price.

We liked this product a lot. It has a smooth text because it's mostly ground beef, i know that doesn't sound good, but it's not bad. The spice and seasoning level is good on all. A very good place to start for beginers, they're all the same cosistancy and texture. Suttle flavors, nothing too odd, or off putting.Enjoy!!

I figured I'd try this sampler pack after browsing around Amazon and coming across this product, and noting that there are varieties offered that aren't available from other retailers(duck, pheasant, antelope).  Unfortunately since they do note that what you receive from them is completely random, as you can guess I did not receive any of those.However, I did receive a good variety of different jerky and beef sticks that I can say that I enjoyed - for Jerky I received Wild Boar, Kangaroo, Alligator, Buffalo, and Elk.  For sticks I received Alligator, Elk, Wild Boar, Ostrich and Buffalo.  Each animal has their own unique flavor that you won't quite find anywhere else.Each of the regular sticks have a tendency to be a much sweeter flavor, while the jerky tends to have a flatter, more savory flavor.  I enjoyed the sticks more than the jerky due to that, but your mileage may vary.  The peppered variety forgoes the sweetness in flavor of a palpable peppery taste(especially if you bite into a peppercorn), so people who like a lot of pepper in their food would enjoy this.Be aware that spicy means *spicy*, and if you are turned off by spicy foods, I would suggest giving those to someone who likes spicy things without even opening the wrapper.All-in-all they were tasty, and are worth a buy if you want something 'a little different'.

I was hesitant to spend $20 on a batch of jerky.  But I'm glad I did.  The quality is great, all the different varieties are wonderful.  I love any type of jerky and have added this to my list.  The only one I didn't receive and haven't tried yet is the Wild Boar.  I plan on ordering some Wild Boar soon.  Will definitely purchase again.  It's nice to have variety.
Great item.  Bought this as a gift.  My friend started eating them about 20 minutes after opening the gift.  Loved them. Will buy from this supplier again.

column9: A perfect gift for a manly, man
column10: My husband is a jerky fanatic. Any meat that can be dehydrated and smoked he is all for. So, as a Christmas gift, I thought a wild game assortment would be perfect for him. Not only did my husband absolutely love this gift, but the quality of the jerky was exceptional. I would highly recommend for any jerky lover out there!
I bought this as a Christmas present for my husband.  The jerky came quickly and he absolutely loved the variety of jerky.  I would definitely order again!

Let me start by saying I HATE MUSTARD! I'm 42 and i've never liked it, won't even eat it in potato salads. My husband got a little jar of this in a salami/beef stick gift basket. It sat on the shelf for months and one day I was hungry for a bologna sandwich. For some odd reason I decided to put this on my sandwich and it was so good.
